Reflection – visualization

Challenge      & selection

When I started my new job as a business developer at e-Durable two months ago, I had a basic understanding of the cable industry, but no real customer experience. My first client was the owner of a restaurant who had just sent us the termination letter because our competitors' offers were 68% cheaper AND he was upset by the fact that our cable company had decided to no longer support his ISDN telephones, forcing him to replace all his ISDN equipments with IP telephones and call center at his own expense.

I decided to use the Vizualisation Thinking technique to start engaging with the client, show him that our solution was best for him and that the low price offered by the competition didn’t include all the options that were included in our offer (he had to compare apples with apples!)

Application

With the help of the client, I started to draw on a sheet of paper the building, the offices, the existing telecommunications and computer equipments, the staff and restaurant customers. Since the client is not a computer professional and the telephony installation was done 10 years ago, it took us several attempts to get a complete and accurate picture of the installation.

Then I used another sheet (see Appendix) to explain our proposed new setup and the advantages of our solution (less maintenance work for him as many functionalities were migrated to our cloud; a more robust service which was a key risk for him: a break in the phone line means a loss in the reservations and therefore a loss of revenues).

He realized that our price included interesting options that the competitor did not offer.

During the visualization reflection exercise, we tried different options (signal strength tests to locate the IP phone bases, looking for ways to connect the new IP phones without having to rewire the building), in order to save the client time and money.

Daycare Electronic Notification Board by Abul Polidori.

Challenge and Selection  WICASA requested the creation of an Electronic Notification Board to  besides broadcast emails to a mail list also provide the same notifications on a web page accessible by  the parents and caretakers.

The team (One-man Team, in the case I) saw an opportunity to reframe the request and expand the  scope creating a new form of communication between parents and daycare staff, not only caretakers,  mainly focusing on children daily follow up. An ethnographic research was put in place and a series of  interviews were conducted to gather information from parents, caretakers, and staff about their  technologic savviness, how comfortable they would be to have information about their children on the  web, what kind of info they would like to have from the daycare.

In possession of these data a combination of Visualization (Week 1 - video 6) and Storytelling (Week 2-  video 4) were used to convey that it would be beneficial to broaden the scope. The combination was a  key aspect of the strategy adopted. Visualization was used to get an alignment among the stakeholders,  helping to convey to the different audiences (mainly the staff) all the aspects of the problem and the line  of experimentation that was adopted later in the process. Storytelling gave a seamless description of  what was the pain points and concerns of the key stakeholders and how the solution would be  experienced in a daily basis by parent caretakers, making the data more “digestible”, softening the  learning curve, allowing stakeholders learn from each other and creating empathy across the board.

Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge:

The challenge was to launch and scale a business portfolio in a space which had no clear  adjacency to our current business line. This was to diversify revenue streams from the  current business, which had little scope of innovation and growth and, as per the BCG  growth/share matrix1, was indeed a cash cow.

Post ideation and evaluation of multiple alternatives, we decided to venture into creating a  platform for Hyperautomation of business systems. The key market that we decided to  target was our existing customer base in both the government and commercial space,  primarily in the business workflow heavy areas since this was the area we knew in depth.

Selection:

Since we were venturing out into a new area, the first thing that needed to be done was to  test key customer requirements and expectations. We also needed to test the defensibility  of our basic assumptions. Since we figured out that there might be a need to tweak our  assumptions or, indeed, pivot further, we wanted a method to quickly engage with the  customer base and test out our basic assumptions before scaling or discarding. Thus, a  learning launch was the best approach for our scenario.

Application:

In order to start the learning launch process, a set of hypotheses was created. These  hypotheses reflected the ideas and use-cases that we wanted to bring to the customers,  using our portfolio of services and tools. Each of these ideas was against a specific need of  our customer base and how we intended to meet these specific needs. These also  articulated how each of these ideas compared and stacked against alternatives.

Following the creation of hypotheses, we wanted to figure out from some of our deepest  engagements and customers if these assumptions were true against the use cases that we  had developed. Reflection Assignment  Design Thinking for Innovation MOOC  July 19th, 2018  Sjoerd Van Der Wal

1.  Challenge

The current Covid-19 pandemic is affecting healthcare, the economy, social and organizational wellbeing  around the world. This is also true for a small Island the one I live on. There is only one hospital with 11 ICU  beds on our Island of about 110.000 citizens, which makes the control of spreading and preventative  measures important. There are currently 9 patients who have tested positive. The government has urged  companies to let employees who have a high risk and employees who can work from home, stay home.  However, my employer, the hospital has not yet followed the advice of the government and let people work  from home, because it does not have experience with this and wants to have certain things like criteria and  policy in order before giving employees permission to work at home, thus minimalizing risk of further spread.  This situation is challenging on a national level, but also for businesses, organizations and individuals.

2.  Selection

The tool I have used to apply to the abovementioned challenge is Mind Mapping, because it provides  visualization and uncovering underlying patterns in a complex challenge/problem (reference lecture video  week 4. Mind Mapping). I have chosen to focus on the “What is” phase of Design Thinking to conceptualize  what the problem for employees are who are not being permitted to work from home and so create a  foundation of the transition to the following phases “What if”, “What wows” and “What works”. Hopefully with  this information my employer will be able to add this perspective to the “solution” and thus the policy that they  are working on to provide their employees safety at work or give them the possibility of working from home.

Design Thinking for Innovation – AIA  Student: Medo Uddin

FINAL ASSIGNMENT: DESIGN THINKING TOOL – STORYTELLING

CHALLENGE

I’m working as a Technology Enhanced Learning consultant in the Centre for Educational Innovation at a

Business School. One of our strategic goals as a department is assist teachers to introduce student

centred methodologies in the classroom. Many of them, although usually are working with method

case, mainly use a classic lecture approach in their courses. A year ago, we ran a pilot study with some

teachers particularly motivated and interested in innovation & technology that decide to participate in

the project. Each teacher had to select a little part (one session/topic/module) of his/her course and

introduce some innovations (a new student-centred methodology, renewed learning materials,

multimedia or storytelling based... etc.). That test worked reasonably well and resulted in many lessons

learned and many things to avoid as well, but, in the end, the main question was: It Will be possible to

transfer these experiences and learnings and involve all the teachers and entire institution

(stakeholders) into project?

SELECTION

We decided to try Storytelling tool, as we had amounts of audio-visual stuff, mostly interviews where

both teachers and students talk about their experiences on “innovative” courses.  We thought it would

be a good starting point to build a narrative around this project. Main issues, which could affect

implementation, were resistance to change and fear to step outside “Comfort Zone”. Therefore, this

narrative could help to pave the way, as to the first question, to implement the project.

APPLICATION

Because of aforementioned audio-visual material, we decided to make 4 video testimonials. The editing

and mixing process was made trying to answer some specific questions. On the part of faculty:

text:
LEARNING LAUNCH – FINAL ASSIGNEMENT – Diadie Singh

Challenge

The challenge I present is a real case in which we applied the method of Design Thinking in its

different phases. Our users are people in our sales department. This means, they carry a device

along the whole day, also to our customers. This device

has measures of 22 cm.x 10 cm. X 2.5 cm. (Length x width x

height) and weighs 500 g.

The challenge that we were proposed was to raise ways to bring the device as

functional, comfortable and aesthetic for the sales staff (men and women).

At the beginning of this phase of the project, we had 7 prototypes to test with them. Each

prototype was very different in terms of: handling,

type of fabric, accessory details.

With these 7 different prototypes, we should determine which worked and which did not, and

for those who worked, what and how they should be improved.

Selection

With the range of possible proposals, our objective at this stage was to determine which were

really valid and could finally be real solutions to carry the device. Because our sales staff can

be male / female and different age, we had to see if one product was

enough to give as a solution or we would validate different from them.

Learning Launch the tool is the best way to perform this test because we had groups of

sales staff to whom we could perform testing of prototypes.

Application

The first learning launch was made with a group of 8 people (5 men / 3 women) of different

Age.

We arranged a meeting in which each salesmen was provided with a kit with 7 different

prototypes models with detailed explanation - how to carry, instructions, etc. - In this phase,

our technical staff was with us, so questions or doubts could be solved.

This test phase lasted a month. At the end of the month we held a meeting with all salesmen to

obtain feedback from each of them. The conclusion of this first learning launch was to dismiss

2 prototypes and make improvements in the remaining 5.

C1 - Internal use

Design Thinking For Innovation

By: Sandra Gonzales

Reflection- Visualization

Challenge

I work as a risk and compliance officer in a start-up company. The business environment favours freedom,  entrepreneurial liberty, openness and empowerment within the employees, creating flexibility and  seamless work environment.  In the age of empowerment and flexibility, controls and procedures have  posed a great challenge. How can we ensure compliance with policies and procedures in the workplace  especially where procedures have not been reinforced before? The company already has existing policies  which employees are not very conversant with, at the same time, creating new procedures have been  resisted unless on a ‘putting out fire’ basis where a crisis occurs. This has posed a great risk in the business  and control failures.

With design thinking, we can be able to demystify the problem and come up with ideas and methods of  making controls embraced by employees especially in the said work environment. We will focus on trying  to uncover what our team members, as well as key stakeholders within, consider ineffective or  problematic then generate ideas and methods to help solve this.

Selection

Looking through design tools, we selected the Visualization tool, which is about visual thinking. It pushes  us beyond using words or language alone. It is a way of unlocking a different part of our brains that allows  us to think nonverbally and that managers might not normally use. This is as referenced by Flor Jackson  in the video lecture.

For the development of integrated and complex processes, it is often not enough to communicate  effectively through words and complex explanations. Employees need to understand the need of  observing certain procedures and to be able to see how that affects their day-to-day work. Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

Mind Mapping is a visual technique for structuring and organising thoughts and ideas. We can  use Mind Mapping in a general and wide-ranging fashion, whether generate Mind Maps with a  pen and paper or with special Mind Mapping software.

I attended a number of talks, lectures and presentations, and I am not remember much about  any of them. However, I have no doubt recall that some of them were very good and others  rather bad, and I have used the technique to prepare and structure lectures, talks and  presentations.

Application

An example of a lecture manuscript which I’ve already prepared is shows in Figure 1. It shows a  lecture manuscript for a talk lasting around 40 minutes on Lisbon (Portugal) about the Scrum  culture. Scrum is a framework that helps teams work together and encourages them to learn  through experiences, self-organize while working on a problem, and reflect on their wins and  losses to continuously improve.

I gave this lecture last week ago. The Mind Map contains only basic keywords, sufficient for  recalling content. As I have already some knowledge about this theme I didn’t need any  additional information. The Mind Map was drawn with Cloud micro software  (https://miro.com). text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

We innately like to tell and listen to stories. Our minds have evolved to decipher the patterns in stories.  They can be used to create signals amidst the din. It can be used to convey complex concepts  understandable to even an ordinary mind in both intellectually and emotionally engaging manner.  Science explains that stories activate the auditory cortex of the human brain stimulating the frontal and  parietal cortices and thus makes us engaged. So storytelling would serve as an ideal tool in training.

To train the new recruits who do technical work such as programming, has always been a challenge in an  Information Technology company. During the induction programme, the freshmen became bored and  disengaged quite easily and that too within the first few days. Though they were explained the do’s and  don’ts, they repeated the same mistakes that their seniors did after their training. The mistakes were  cyclical. Reading manuals about avoiding mistakes was boring to them as it did not connect to them and  it was also disengaging, therefore they reached their atrophy faster than expected.

It was decided to experiment with storytelling as a tool to explain the mistakes already committed by  employees who had surpassed this stage. It was believed this tool would make the freshman engaged,  involved, stay focused and learn from others experience.

Application

The training sessions to these freshmen were broken down to storytelling sessions. Jennifer Aaker, a  Marketing Professor from Stanford opines that stories are 22 times more memorable than mere  statement of facts.

The mistakes already committed during programming by the more experienced employees in the  company were asked to share it through storytelling. Each employee made an account of some of the  common mistakes they committed while working on their projects.

Yvonne Schmidt

DESIGN THINKING COURSE REFLECTION

I am a member of an engineering support team responsible for providing Design for Manufacturing  (DFM) input to mechanical design engineers during the design cycle for new products. Our team created  documents called Manufacturing Design Tenets, for use by design engineering during the product design  cycle to improve the manufacturability and reduce the cost of a mechanical component.  The  information in the design tenets was well received by the design engineering community. We have a  large design engineering community located in North America, Europe and Asia. Dissemination of the  information to all members of the community was an issue. We had a great product but not all of the  consumers were aware of its very existence. We tried several internal communication tools to help  familiarize the DEs with the tenets, but still could not reach all the potential customers.

We chose to create a training course for the design engineering(DE) personnel. We chose the Learning  Launch tool for this project. We used surveys and focus groups to determine the most appropriate  delivery method for the training. The data showed a preference for on online video training course  which could be viewed at the end users’ convenience.

Assignment Reflection – Visualisation |

Design Thinking for Innovation, BTECH)students)

Reflection – Visualisation

Challenge

One of my key assignments this year is an internal communications project I am currently running. The  project is nearing completion.

My campaign goals were as follows :

(a) to raise awareness among employees about social impact driven through our financial inclusion  programme Mein Pragati (I am progress)

(b) to create a platform so that social impact, whether at an individual or corporate level, becomes a  conversation starter, raising social consciousness and discourse about it.

Selection

The tools that I use most often are visualization and storytelling depending on the platform or medium I  have for awareness and recall. For instance, if it is an event or a presentation, I use story-telling. But for  a cause-based, campaign-specific internal communication, I use visualization.

To accurately depict the foundation’s journey, I referred to the 5Ws and 1H framework to form a set of  questions that would shape the narrative. The idea was to develop a visual story that all employees,  even those without context to our programme could comprehend.

I interviewed various stakeholders. Firstly, our employees, to understand what social impact means to  them. Based on 30 discussions, I created employee personas. I also spoke with my business leader to  understand what she’d like to convey as we were celebrating the foundation’s fifth anniversary. Finally, I  reached out to various external agencies to collaborate with, for ideation, and implementation, to  achieve our goals.

Based on these discussions, I identified three key associations with social impact. Firstly, a sense of  legacy, resulting from achieving milestones related to behavior change. DESIGN THINKING TOOL

VISUALISATION

1 | P a g e

DESIGN THINKING TOOL: VISUALIZATION

CHALLENGES AND SELECTION

Visualization is a technique for creating images, diagrams, or animations to communicate a

message. Visualization through visual imagery has been an effective way to communicate

both abstract and concrete ideas since the dawn of man. It is the first design thinking tool

used in this course.

It is a core component of the way that we communicate, whether we are aware of it or not.

When we are dealing with very complex problems, we are actually enacting a different kind

of problem. Visualization is really important in all fields and especially for the process of

design as it is a way of unlocking a different part of brain. It allows us to think in a nonverbal

way.  Visualization allows us to access parts of our brain, parts of our creativity, that we

might not normally be using in our conversation. Most people will tell you, especially those

who are in the field of management i.e from business world, that they are not artistic and

they cannot draw. Visualization isn't really about drawing  , though. It's actually about visual

thinking.

When we move on into pattern finding, that's where we start to think visually. When we get

to concept development or designing something visualization becomes incredibly key.

Because concepts are literally coming out of our imagination. And our brain is creating

pictures of something that doesn't yet exist.

APPLICATION

Visualization and expressing data is very mandatory thing to do while you represent your

idea. It is very important for the user to know what exactly you want to express. Visualization

today has ever-expanding applications in science, education, engineering (e.g., product

visualization), interactive multimedia, medicine, etc. Typical of a visualization application is

the field of computer graphics. The invention of computer graphics may be the most

Final Assignment

Frutos Orellana

CHALLENGE DESCRIPTION

I have formed an organizational consultant company called Institute of India® and as a manager I invited  7 colleagues to work with me in senior positions. We collaborate freely until we manage to sell  projects. Each project sold involves work for all of us. There are commissions for design and  sale of projects. Formally the consultancy was formed in January of this year. We have not yet  sold any projects although we have gone to several meetings to offer our services. We have the  great challenge of captivating the audience and selling projects.

TOOL SELECTION DESCRIPTION

To achieve our challenge, which is, to open up space in the market, we need to position our  Institute of India® brand. For this, we need to be an attractive brand and connect with people, as Andre  Martin said in week 2. To tell the story of our brand and services, we occupy the storytelling tool.  We want to create a good story, that is, to communicate a logical message, with emotional  connection and with a greater purpose, that encourages our audience (clients) to hire our  services.

VISUALIZATION TO TRANSFORM LIVES

Diana Alfonso – Engineer/Researcher

Colombia

Challenge

I work in a huge research program in my country, Colombia, regarding the development of  renewable energy to be used in the country by 2030. The program is divided in ten different  projects, I collaborate as a researcher in one of the projects that is related to the costumer  challenges within the adoption of these new technologies we are researching. We as  researchers, tend to be very quantitative so we first started with a marketplace research and  used only tools that were entirely related to the data we had and, because our team is mostly  compounded with engineers, they were oddly satisfied with the results of this first outlook of  the market. Yet, here is the challenge: The technologies that are being developed are (because  many scientific reasons) being designed to be used in country’s poorest zones, tending also to  transform lives and environments, so in the first marketplace research we did, we found that the  new technologies were indeed going to help this poor regions (quantitatively). But, there’s a  deeper challenge we didn’t notice: we didn’t really know our costumer, we didn’t gave a deep  thought about the fact that we were going to disrupt many communities way of living that have  had almost none contact with technology at all, and that they weren’t going be able to use it or  even understand it once they were installing it. So, we needed to study our market and costumer  in a deeper way, but this time using a different approach.

Challenge

I’m a member of the Digital Department of an international Company and my new challenge is  to implement a new tool in the Operations Department to improve the provider assignment  processes of their activity. The scope of the project consist in automatize the selection and  assignment of the providers of all the claims opened in the system. Agents (primary users)  often have problems with the IT tools because a lack of training or because they were not  involved in the building of the tool or understand the real benefit of it. The project duration is  estimated in 3 months and it includes the training session for all the stakeholders (agents and  providers).

Selection

We’ve decided to use visualization tools, starting with workflows to summarize the activity of  the assignment to jump to journey map and walkthrough to try the learning launch tool and  cover the main ressistances of the teams to the new it tools implemented in their activities.

Application

During the first two weeks we organize our first meetings we organize with agents and  providers to try to understand the high level process and depict it into basic workflows to  ensure the activity was clear.

After this sessions we spend 2 weeks to organize tours in the agents and providers offices to  see how is the daily activity and how their interact with the current tools.

Once the activity is clear, we went more in detail and we organize face to face meeting with  the agents and  providers to see how they manage their tasks, how they tackle their problems  and how they feel with the existing tools.

Design Thinking for Innovation

Final Assignment

Made by: Mario Markovic

Learning Launch

Challenge:   I am working I data analytic company as product manager. Due to the fact that we are  monetizing datasets we are always trying to find new ways of monetizing existing assets.  However, the main plan is to develop something that can be scalable internally as a products/  service but also a solution that can be scalable externally. One of our services is lead list/ b2b  selection services that provide our clients an exact list of potential clients to contact. In a  default way these lists are provided as hard copy lists in excel or some other legacy format.   We wanted to make one step further in our offer and provide to our clients not only list of  potential clients but also offer them a full-service product with capabilities to contact their  potential clients, online, contact them at social networks such as Facebook and LinkedIn.     Selections:  We decided to focus on that project for 4 weeks. We gathered a small team of people coming  from different departments (sales, IT, tech, product, customer care finance). We wanted  to ran this project as agile process knowing that our main hypothesis -“Clients want to have  capability for micro targeting of their niche potential clients at social networks“ need to be  verified. We wanted to prove each step in our product delivery process in order to spent time  and resources in a good and meaningful way. The challenge is to understand and give them what they want, keeping aside what we  know. My stakeholders are mostly automobile dealers and sales promoters for their product. I help them  build a marketing creative. I interpret their words and thoughts into illustrations and images to help in  their services which will be later delivered to their customer. I also suggest them opportunities for  improvements or solutions. This project was about Customer journey through a supermarket. How he  can use a single Contactless credit card for charging his car when parked at the parking lot, at the  supermarket premise  and how he can use the same card to do his shopping all at the same time, easily  cutting downtime. Earlier which was 10 steps process and by using 2 separate cards can now be  transformed to a single card and 4 easy steps process with the new customer card.

text:
Craig Gonzalez  Design Thinking for Innovation

Mind Mapping for Product Planning

Challenge & Selection

As part of my role, I am a business analyst who works very closely with the Product Owners in my organisation and  our customers are large corporates or big banks from across the world. A large part of product lines which our  customers consume will have 80% core product features which are globally common and 20% is either  customisation per geography or any other specific regional compliance obligations. Other than rolling out new  features into our core product globally, we keep on updating the customisation layer also. Whenever we get into  discussions with our customers, there are variety of issues which are brought on to the table by them which could  be either in the core product or the customised layer and we will have to collate all of those and analyse the  commonality between them and pick the items which qualify for enhancements, bug fixing and new features on  the core product and how it will impact the global customer base, which in fact is the trickiest part. Now, it is not  always the same problem which the customers bring forward and the result of fixing for one could result in  creating a new problem for another customer who was unaffected earlier. Therefore, in order to resolve this  efficiently and effectively I have been making use of mind mapping concept with the help of some real-life tools  e.g. XMind. I find mind mapping as very powerful as it looks for patterns and insights which comes really handy  when there is variety of data and stakeholders in the mix. It becomes very handy from my job perspective as if I  relay it back to the course would be the ‘What If’ phase. It helps me a lot in getting the stakeholders engaged and  also help them understanding my process with respect to other customers who are contesting to get a change  agreed and get rolled into the product roadmap.

1.  Challenge:

I am the general manager of a Music Record Label in Colombia. Our company has one  of the largest independent music catalogs in Latin America. Technological and cultural  changes have made people consume music digitally through mobile applications such  as Spotify, Deezer, Apple Music, etc. The sale of physical formats such as vinyl records  and compact discs has fallen to almost nothing. However, there is a musical product  that we want to keep as tangible, it is the "14 Dancing Cannon shots". This is a  compilation of the best musical themes during the year. This music compilation is highly  expected in the December season because they represent the arrival of the end of the  year holidays.  The challenge then is: Can the product be released in a different physical format from  CDs and vinyl records and at the same time incorporating a technological development  that also induces consumption on digital music platforms?

The chosen tool was Visualization. Since it was about making a creative proposal of a  musical format different from the traditional ones, it was important for the  communication that there be a non-verbal description of what the people involved in the  process   wanted    to    express. So this was a requirement  communicated to all project participants.

The Adventure Project

Allow me as a banker being a member of one of the most successful operational teams  in the banking sector, to share my own digital initiative idea "Adventure project".  My journey in the bank, as a head teller and a front liner enabled me for better  understanding of the customer journey, giving me the opportunity to come up with digital  innovative solutions.    Starting in 2017 after leading a team consisting of 7 employees in Sanstefano Br. one of  the most crowded branches and being one of the top three branches specified for tuition  fees payment for educational entities and universities and other schools in Alexandria  region.     Despite, the huge stress we have been through and the large number of operational  transaction that had been executed on daily basis all over the year. Behind every  obstacle lies a hidden opportunity.  The huge number of transactions executed to serve Non-bank customers specially  youth segment had negatively affect the AVG “Average waiting time” and may cause  customer dissatisfaction for banked and unbanked customers.     Therefore, I decided to take the advantage of such challenge and to go digital by  coming up with new innovative idea to migrate the traditional payments & fees to be  done through our digital channels, offering an exceptional digital experience " being  more efficient, quicker and cheaper" through our digital channels such as "Wallet,  Internet banking, ATM as well as the Mob App” offered to our bank customer and non-  bank customers, hence gaining their satisfaction and grabbing new to bank customers.     This will identify addition more opportunities for new products launch such as  educational loan and new type of accounts & services specifically tailored for the Youth  segment being the main source of NTB and Big Data. Design Thinking Course

Challenge and Selection      I selected Mind Mapping (Module 3) to develop a strategic vision, stimulate ideas, track  socio-cultural patterns and invisible connections, gain deep human centered insight and  detect the emotional needs of our audience to find a common thread between all the  different elements and activities proposed during the event, through mind mapping we  are looking to find solutions to enhance the atmosphere, the culinary experience and the  workshops proposed through out the event compared to the last 2 editions that took  place in Casablanca, Morocco during late fall season of 2014 and 2015.   Our challenge is to integrate a healthy vegetarian lifestyle in the community, build  bridges between our audience and the local organic farmers, yoga and music instructors  around a healthy meal with special flavors and recipes, while keeping in mind that  Moroccans used to eat very little meat and had a wider choice of vegetarian dishes  today eating meat is a lifestyle that leads to many diseases and environmental issues  but has increased significantly in the last 50 years, due to fear of malnutrition,  desertification of the land (Desert), the need for survival, however today, it is a sign of  wealth, power and belonging to a higher social class. text:
Design Thinking for Innovation  Learning Launch Reflection  Ravneet Williams  May 5, 2018

Challenge

I have worked as a Senior Project Manager in the engineering and construction industry for over fifteen  years. Most recently, my work has been managing large scale façade projects for skyscrapers and large- scale medical or commercial campuses. A typical project budget would average around $40M with a  project duration of roughly eighteen months. The three key phases of a project would, in order, include  1) design engineering (where our engineers would turn the architect’s vision into hundreds of detail  drawings), 2) production (where the detail drawings would be converted so the product could be  fabricated and assembled at one of our production facilities), and 3) field installation (where the  assembled product would be installed onto the building). A near constant that occurs once a project team  has been assembled is that many of the team members across departments have not worked together  before. Also, the mindset of individuals from each department is different simply because their job duties  are vastly diverse. The monetary scale of a given project, the risk that comes with such a long project  duration, and the possible issues within the project team makes, among many other things, the challenge  of fostering and constantly improving efficient communication of the utmost importance. For this  assignment, I am going to reflect on such a design thinking challenge I encountered while managing a 4- building biotech campus south of San Francisco, California.

Selection

After taking this course, I realized that I was using the “learning launch” tool on a regular basis. For the  reflection I am going to describe a situation where I encountered an appreciable communication challenge  at the forefront of a project. Visualization Tool for explaining Legal concepts

- Pushpalatha Bisht,

Legal Designer & Lawyer

Co-Founder &

Lead, Business Operations

Legal Design Arc

Visualization Challenge & Selection

Being a legal designer, we understand that law is complex and this slices it away from its effective application.  As a legal designer I decided to use visualization as a tool to develop legal courses for the acts to help students  better understand these concepts. I decided to use a storyboard to explain the Right to Information Act in  India. This will help the students achieve a practical understanding of the concepts and help their future clients  effectively.

Application

The following steps were taken by me to develop this storyboard: -

1. Deciding on the key elements required to make someone understand the Right to Education Act. This

required consideration of the frequently asked questions regarding this act.

2. Then I started deciding on the best manner of describing these elements, experimented with

characters, objects, icons, personifications to develop the flow.

3. Developed the elements like a woman who needed information regarding one of her job applications

with a government department.

4. I then went on to decide the flow of the story and the application of the elements.   5. There were three things that had to be kept in mind while developing it first, the conceptual

explanation of the Act; Second, the procedural understanding of the Act; Third the cases that are key  to the Act.

6. Then I went on to develop a storyline to explain all the three things to students.   7. After I had the narration and the storyline with me I started to develop the visual depiction of the

story.

Challenge:

When I was in college finishing a technical course, I remember very well the  exhibitions in which we had to present some information about, the teaching material  that the teacher gave us. Many of those times we had to express our thoughts through  speech with voice. Many were bored and they did not understand what we wanted to  express.   Expressing our ideas, became detestable and no one wanted to come forward to  expose any kind of information. After a little stress on the part of the students, it was  decided to change the way we worked.

We decided to investigate what were the methods in which you can get attention  without having to talk too much. We did not find studies that explained that words  could get attention for only 15 minutes, after it became monotonous but incredible  because between a word and an image, the image would be more attention or  between a video and an image, the video would win and position as number 1 for  catch the attention of participants.    Another thing that we developed was the games. Everyone decided to make people  laugh while they were learning as there was more chance to remember a specific  topic. If they were willing. Here we include materials that express drawings as the  game of guessing what I express in the drawing. Game finds the couple of words and  colors, among others.

January 2017

Design Thinking for Innovation

University of Virginia  Final Course Assignment

Reflection: Learning Launch

Challenge

I have offered support to a start-up company in the food business to take their venture to the next  level. Among all the areas that need to be covered in this process, we have decided to leverage  Design Thinking to take a step back and think again about the overall customer experience when  consuming the company products. The portfolio of products is composed of a set of high-quality  snacks based on Japanese cuisine that is intended to be consumed as quick meals mostly for  people who prioritizes a healthy and lean lifestyle. The challenge we have identified was that some  consumers were not figuring out how to open the meal package correctly, what was creating an  issue on the overall experience to consume the product. This fact would represent a problem in the  growth of the business as they plan the expansion to a more diverse audience for those snacks,

Selection

I have selected Learning Launch for this assignment because it brings a new perspective about how  important it is to avoid confirmation bias of project team members when trying to build real impactful  innovation to the business. Also, to test the concept of learning cycles to test assumptions in fast  and cheap ways, understanding that failures are also opportunities to get insights for the business.

I have been working for the last 15 years in leadership roles in the IT industry, and I have used  different methodologies to keep evolving my operation, most of them associated on shaping  behaviors of internal teams during innovation and planning cycles, using tools like Six Thinking Hats,  Instinctive Drives System and Future Based Planning. Reflection Design Thinking

Challenge & Selection    The challenge is to identify the problem of a process that has been carried out in the same way in  a company in different places and in which different departments are involved.    I selected the visualization tool, before defining and solving the problem, since it provides a shared  vision of the project and by using elements such as photographs, symbols and colors, they help to  have a single perspective of what is happening.    In this way we will seek to unify concepts and make evident the problems that have the greatest  impact to prioritize.    Using this technique in an all-day workshop helps people from different departments see the  problem also from the perspective of the other, thus finding a shared vision to define the impact,  scope, limits, actors and key elements .    In this case, the way of doing things has been the same for a long time and surprisingly we believe  that it is different in each city where the company operates and in many cases the reason why it is  done that way is not known. Using the visualization tool will add impressive value to the process  as it will allow us to understand the different realities and highlight the easily solvable problems  that exist today.    Application:    For the application, we consider building a process flow diagram together. For this diagram, symbols are  used that identify the action that is happening, who performs it, whether it is an operation, a record, or a  decision.  For this, apart from the usual identifiers, we use photographs of the people who do it.  As there are 5 different departments in 3 cities, we made 3 groups of 5 people randomly, to reach a general  consensus faster.  Questions of the type are asked, What actions do you take to obtain x result? How do you interact or  communicate with people in the other departments so that they understand what you need from them?For

Visualization

Peer-graded Assignment: Refection

Asif Khan

Design Thinking for Innovation

January 16, 2021

Challenge

We all love to eat good food. Cooking good food at home is not always feasible.  Sometimes we want to taste diferent good food from diferent sources. We visit our  nearest restaurants, food shops, travel to diferent regions, and taste diferent cuisine.  We also love to have good food delivered to their homes.

In the COVID-19 pandemic, the situation is changed. The demand for food delivery  services is geting higher. we use the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to  understand and know the users' pain points, come up with user-friendly and  functional solutions.

Selection

Visualization is one of the very important tools. It is a core component of the way to  communicate. It allows us to think in a nonverbal way. Designing a food delivery service  involves diferent groups of people. Food makers, delivery persons, and users of the  service are the indispensable parts of the service.

We will focus on trying to uncover what they think, speak and do. And also use  technology to ensure seamless food delivery service and experience. We take  inspiration from diferent resources. "The Good Kitchen" story mentioned at the very  beginning of the course is one of them.   (http://jacobs-fisher.com/listpost.html)

Application

Before diving down to the core we tried to understand the current scenario frst. We  identifed the targeted users and the stakeholders to fnd answers to some very  important questions.

Who they are? Where they live? What are the problems and how they face them now?  How they address and communicate? What solutions they currently have and how  they use them? What are the pain points and experiences? What are their  expectations?

Designing for Innovation Loredana Abidin

Reﬂection: Visualization Tool

Challenge + Selection

My challenge was how to create a year long content calendar for a wellness blog that I’m  launching. I needed to come up with interesting blog post titles for weekly posts and create a  content calendar that would help me plan content for the year.

I chose the visualization tool to help me get a big picture view of what I would be writing about  and to help me ensure that the content ﬂowed well together.

Application

I ﬁrst sketched out the 4 main topics that I would be writing about. These I called Life Wellbeing  areas. I also created symbols and colors for each area.

Next I created two customer personas for my target audience. I drew landscapes of their daily  life and what their problems and needs were. I created 4 life boards for the 4 main wellness  areas and I added stickies with ideas, problems, solutions, and inspiration. I shared with a  family member and gathered additional stickies of ideas.

I wrote list of books and research that I would be writing about and I drew where they  connected to the persona’s life.

I drew symbols for holidays, seasonal milestones and other important events throughout the  year. I sketched out where content ﬁt in throughout the year and where psychological shifts  would be for the customer.

I drew a visual calendar with weekly topic ideas and where it ﬁt in my customer persona’s life.

Insight + Approach

Using the visualization tool helped me get a better sense of my customer persona by visually  mapping out their life and how they transition throughout the year with seasons.

What I learned is that by laying out the four main topics that I will be writing about over a visual  map of the customer persona’s life and seasonal milestones, I was able to see better where  content would be most impactful. text:
Guayaquil, September 24, 2020.  Name: Adam Filip  Project: “Mirror Lake Laundry and Press Solutions”

Challenge:

My challenge was more complicated than what I thought at the beginning, to be honest I  believed that my group of problem solvers would finish this job in 1 or 2 weeks. However,  it was not. The problem we were assigned was a question from our employer: How can  he get more contracts and success in his micro-business with our help?

The person who hired us for this university problem solving project is called Saman Mojica, he is an excellent mechanical engineer. He has studied at recognized  universities in the United States and Argentina. Saman is dedicated to advising and  auditing metallic and mechanical structures and civil works in the national environment  (Ecuador) and abroad. Their main problem was not the quality of their work or the lack  of funding, their biggest problem is that not many people knew the usefulness of their  work and who could offer that service, that is, lack of advertising or marketing and  ignorance of the possible clients regarding the work offered by Saman Jaramillo and his  micro-company called “Bachpan NGO”.

Selection:

It is for this reason that we lean towards “Storytelling”, although we also use other tools  many times, such as: “Visualization” or “Learning Launch”. These additional tools and  steps were very helpful as we uncovered hidden issues that neither Hector nor we had  seen in the beginning. But we all create the same hypothesis. Our hypothesis was that, if  we were able to obtain the most efficient solution for all the problems that slowly came  to light, we could achieve our main objective, which was for Saman's micro-business to  expand. For this and many other reasons, it was very important that we integrate all these  tools and apply them in different processes, at different times, in order to obtain what we  wanted as a group.

has even affected lecturers’ performance in classes as well. As one of the experienced lecturers

meeting I tabled the discussion about this challenge; it became evident that every lecturer was

facing the same problem. I therefore volunteered to lead a team that was to find solutions to

this challenge.

an “essential human activity” for sharing experiences, explaining values, and deciding on

did use talk form of storytelling so as to be able to narrate the challenge as well as listen to the

students’ concerns. This will also give me the opportunity to discuss with the students the

negative impact of this current challenge on their academic work and why there is a need to

find solutions to resolve the challenge.  Listening engages people and empathy is an essential

and fundamental component in the process of solving the challenge.

by University of Virginia

Instructor:  Daniela Sangineto

Student:  Ruben Soria  matthew72@hotmail.com

Course Assignment - Mind Mapping – Integrating Solutions

Note:  The following is a true story with many of the details made generic in order to preserve privacy.

Challenge

Our firm recently acquired a technology company (TC) that built a suite of tools and services that serves  a niche market, opening up a new market for our firm.  Within that market, our firm has another  business unit (BU) that serves a segment of that niche market with a set of tools and services (some  similar and some exclusive), but within a smaller segmentation of that market.  I was selected to be part  of a team of 6 to evaluate the newly acquired TC to determine if there were tools and/or services that  could be integrated into the BU offering.  Goals include:

1. Keeping the various systems nimble.   2. Proving the efficacy of the front-end data reporting for existing business.  3. Exploring the feasibility of pursuing a larger segment of the market.

Selection

We conducted a dozen interviews with various stakeholders across both business units and other  technology experts.  We collected a large amount of data from those interviews, and chose as our  primary tool Mind Mapping to help aggregate and identify themes in the data.

Application

Each team member individually took notes from those interviews.  We then identified key terms and  themes from each interview and wrote them on sticky notes.  The team reconvened in a room with a  large white board and we drew a grid with 4 quadrants.  The top two quadrants were goals which were  separated by quotes/defining words and thoughts/beliefs.  The bottom two quadrants were pain points  separated by actions/behaviors and feelings/emotions.

Storytelling

Challenge

I work for a non-profit organization that provides quality education to under-privileged children.  My company adopts under-performing public schools in low-income communities. After adopting  those schools, we implement reforms that lead to positive student learning outcomes and increased  student enrollment.

In order to raise funds for our initiatives, we organize fundraising dinners. Guests pay an entry fee  to attend a musical performance followed by dinner. During the event, my company’s Fundraising  department used to highlight important facts about the shortcomings in the public school system  by displaying shocking facts about the low student enrollment, high drop-out rate, and abysmal  student achievement. The Fundraising Department personnel would then distribute donation forms  among the guests and ask them to make donation commitments to address the problems that they  were highlighting. At the end of the event, we would collect these firms. Very few people would  make any commitments and those who did, would not follow though by actually sending a  donation check. We were unable to identify why our guests were not making any donation  commitments when they clearly cared enough about the cause to attend our event.

Selection and Application

Last year, we all sat down to discuss ways to collect more donor commitments during our  fundraising dinner scheduled for December. We decided to interview guests and tried to place  ourselves in the shoes of our donors. We realized from our discussions that our fundraising pitches  during the events did not draw any interest from the guests. They would mostly tune out or start  talking among themselves when our Fundraising Manager would come on stage. The Fundraising  Manager would list out a number of facts and figures about the abysmal state of public schools but  it did not resonate with the guests.

Reflection — Learning Launch  Guiding a Digital-First Mindset Shift in an  Online Enterprise SaaS Business

By Santosh Kumar

Challenge    Enterprise businesses offering digital SaaS (Software-as-a-Service) products often rely heavily  on traditional Sales workflows. This means, the selling process is entirely manually driven with  individuals, or even whole teams of Sales and Pre-Sales professionals being involved in  helping a customer make a purchase decision and closing a deal. While this has worked  traditionally because of such digital products usually being expensive, high dollar-value items;  it comes at a great cost to the scalability of a business, especially when entering and capturing  newer or larger markets.    As a member of my organization’s marketing leadership, my team of cross-functional experts  and I were faced with the challenge of proving the market demand for a scalable, fully digital,  “try-before-you-buy” business model to our Executive leadership who had grown accustomed  to the traditional methods of doing business and reflected a fixed mindset1, convinced that  the market, or the customers, didn’t voice such a need for change.

We have also engaged in mind-mapping3 activities building alignment on the “What If”  scenario of our proposed solutions and we feel that a Learning Launch, being an  experimentation tool, will help us quickly gather valuable data4 in testing our hypotheses  and validating market-demand for a fully digital, instant “try-before-you-buy” experience of  our product as outlined in the “Challenge” section abov

Name: Bilal Sajid

Mind Mapping

Challenge:

Managing the starting up and opening of a restaurant business, all by myself.   (An appropriate title would be: ‘Project manager without a project team’)   Three years ago, I was hired as a project manager by a small businessman  to manage sales and inventory of a restaurant. Turns out, construction of the  restaurant has just begun. It was a long way from its first opening. Since, it was  a small business restaurant, I found it intriguing to see the whole process of the  start-up. So, I proposed to help manage the start-up by negotiating with the  business owner. The owner counted on me and handed over the entire project  for me handle. From exterior & interior designing to managing sales and  stocking kitchen & food supplies, I had to manage everything and time was  running out. I had been informed that only 8 months had been remaining in the  first opening. Knowing it was not a one-man job, I decided to take on the  challenge to gain experience.

Name: Bilal Sajid

Selection:   Given a vast variety of different tasks with dependencies related to restaurant  design and stocking inventory, I decided to use mind-mapping as a way to  organize all the work. The visualization aspect of mind-mapping helps to keep  track of tasks/activities and the order of completion for each of them.  (Mind mapping) I initiate by placing the main task in center and then divide it  into sub-tasks. Sub-tasks are ordered in hierarchically. I start working on the  lowest order activities and work my way up from there. Mind mapping is best  suited for me as it is a way to link key tasks using images, and lines to link them  according to their relations. text:
Reflection – Stakeholder Mind Mapping

By Melvin Lu

Challenge

As a Senior Manager of a Shared Service Center(SSC) I work with multiple stakeholders for multiple  countries across Asia Pacific region for an FMCG company. Challenge on hand was the Quality of  operations that I run. Stakeholder including business in the country were really not happy with the  Finance Services delivered and constantly saw SSC as a task oriented team which really impacted the  morale of the employees who felt too disengaged with what they did. With the dissatisfaction of the  business it really impacted future projects which had a lot of dependency on upstream processes to  achieve the larger Finance Strategies. Missing deadlines on implementing/executing Finance Strategies  was not an option and we as a team were given 2 Quarters only to turn it around. Hence it was decided  to come up with a Design Thinking strategy which is scientific and can provide results too.

Selection

With several tools at our disposal, we as a team felt Mind Mapping for our stakeholders would be the  key tool to understand the AS IS situation and current minds of our stakeholders. We also understood it  was a ‘what is’ phase and not a ‘what if’. And since we had multiple stakeholders it was important for us  as a team to look for patterns through this tool.

Application

I invited all of my Direct Reports who are SSC country managers and managed these stakeholders  directly day in day out. Since we were 16 of us so we formed 4 groups of 4 each. I took my team through  the broad Design Thinking process for the first 1 hour and then discussed the tool we specifically chose  for the same. We assigned a white board to each group and gave 45 minutes for them to list out what  feedback we received from our stakeholders in terms of what they think, what they feel, what they say  and what they do. Another 15 minutes for the group to summarize and structure their exercise for a  teach back to the other 3 groups.

Design Thinking Assignment - Reflection

Dieter Berger

Challenge

My challenge is to convince people to reduce their organic waste in their houses

by descomposting it. We are developing an electrical domestic composter which is able

to reduce the organic waste, generated in the kitchen, in between 60% and 80% and it

takes no more than 72 hours. The compost generated by our device has got a lot of

nutrients and can be used for growing plants and trees. Our challenge is to create the

habit of decomposting organic waste in every house we can, and show that it can be

extremely important for our planet and vey handful to use on gardens and organic food

growers.

Selection

Storytelling is the chosen tool. It is able to cause a really good impact on the

people, helping them to visualize the importance and benefits of decomposting their

organic waste at home. By adressing them individually they will be able to feel that they

are really important in this process and they are trully a part of it. We want every

individual to be inspired through the current scenario, making them feel that they are

contributing for the environment’s future by reducing their waste, and in exchange they

can get the best nutrients for their plants and maybe grow their own food. The chosen

tool can help to make everyone feel and understand the purpose of the product.

Application

By using the storytelling tool we were able to tell our customers what is the real

impact of organic waste to our planet. Showing the percentages of organic waste

generated in the last decade by humans caused a huge impact and could make them

feel responsible for it too. Bringing this responsability to them and making them to feel

as part of it gave us a big chance to introduce our product and consequently the habit

of decomposting their organic waste at home. Some of them got really excited to be

parto f something with a bigger purpose, other enjoyed a lot the idea of producing their

Reflection - Storytelling

Challenge & Selection:    I am currently working in a social service dedicated to helping women understand powerful  computer tools like coding. The girls I work with are usually from low-income families and do  not have access to many resources. It is also important that I connect and build a relationship with them in  order to motivate them and to better understand what’s the best method to teach them. It is  important for me to use the storytelling tool in order to accomplish the goals I have because it  helps me understand the girls and create a cause for which to work towards together. I then talked with them and told them to tell me  ways they could use these tools and resources to their advantage, after this they were more  excited about learning to code and use the resources, we would provide to them. It got them  thinking about all the possibilities, once we got to work, they finished all their work and lessons  before the deadlines. They finished early and worked hard because I had connected with them  and they understood how this could help them later on. text:
John Estrada

December 6, 2021

Design Thinking Reflection

Mind Mapping

Challenge:  Creating a comprehensive multi-year strategic plan that captures new value- driven company goals and objectives that allow for business growth and  innovation is a difficult task. The level of complexity increases when prioritizing  which objectives offer the most value while minimizing risk; based on stakeholder  input, market data, employee feedback, and past lessons learned.

Selection:  To better understand the individual business components (gaps, past targets, key  performance indicators, etc) and align them with the collective stakeholder input  (data, key lessons etc) I selected mind mapping as my preferred tool.

Application:  Mind mapping was instrumental in my ideation sessions held over several days  with stakeholders across my company. Each session was 2 hrs long (3 sessions  total) with key stakeholders participating in all 3 sessions. The goal of my  ideation exercises was to:   1. Level 0: Start with the organization’s mission, vision, value at the center circle

2. Level 1: Itemize the various departments/business units that are parts of the  organization as a whole

3. Level 2: Create the following groups for each department: 1. Staff 2.  Technology 3. Process

4. Level 3: Create the following categories: 1. Challenges 2. Successes 3.  Future Goals then place stakeholder input, data, insight within each bucket

5. Draw connector lines for all dependencies and/or similarities between  departments

Insight:  Having the ability to visualize the various components of my organization and  showing how each department and their challenges, successes, and goals were  directly connected gave all stakeholders that participated in the exercise much  more clarity on the current-state as well as where they needed to be for the  future-state. The mind map made prioritizing the future roadmap less complicated  since all stakeholders were onboard. We all knew we were on the same

Challenge and Selection

A key area of my job scope is to develop step-by-step digitalization guides for the  small and medium enterprises (SMEs) of various industries and sectors. The SMEs  are important to Singapore, collectively employing 70% of Singapore’s workforce and  account for almost half of Singapore’s GDP. Hence, digitalisation of SMEs can have  a profound impact on Singapore’s economy.

However, SMEs generally lack the technical know-how and find it difficult to divert  resources to digital transformation. Hence, it is important to develop a guide to make  going digital simple for the SMEs.

To develop a guide that is most suitable to the needs of the SMEs, I plan to conduct  a series of workshops with various SMEs, and use the Mind Mapping tool to  generate insights, collect information and create design criteria.

Application

In the first workshop that I conduct, I will gather information from the SMEs to  understand their experiences in digitalization. I will get each SME to fill up a form to  provide me with information regarding their digital transformation journey, such as:

-  Current mode business operations (manual vs digital)

-  Areas of improvement for business operations

-  Challenges that SMEs when digitalizing

-  Obstacles that are stopping them from digitalizing

In the second workshop, with the information consolidated, I will set up a room with  walls filled with the common problems faced by the SMEs in the industry and the  SMEs can go around the room to understand the problems and think about how  digitalization can come in to help solve the problems.

In the third workshop, SMEs will be put together in groups to share their experiences  and problems, and most importantly, how digitalization can help. The SMEs will then  work together, to discuss on how they want to digitally transform their businesses in  step-by-step manner.

Jorge Bernardo, 18.05.2021

Challenge

As a head of remote entry agency for clients using wallets for a popular Moroccan bank, my main  goal is to ensure that the services ordered by a client are successfully activated. However, successful  integration is only guaranteed if the customer carries out certain steps himself.

These steps are emailed to the customer after placing the order. Although these emails are very  personal and detailed, we noticed that customers often did not complete the steps and as a result  the onboarding did not always go as smoothly which also resulted in a drop in the customer  satisfaction.

Selection

Due to several possibilities to solve this problem, we decided to launch a learning launch. The  learning launch tool allowed us to test very quickly and at minimal cost if we were on the right track  or if we needed to completely change our thinking. Even if the result is not what you want, the loss is  minimal because the investment is low. A learning launch is indeed always beneficial: you quickly  know if you are on the right track with something or if you need to go back to the drawing board and  formulate a new or refined hypothesis based on the information gathered.

Application

Our guess was that the text of the mail might have been too long and people hadn't bothered to read  it. Based on this hypothesis, we decided to create a digital milestone plan. We were very excited  about the launch as we were hoping to see a lot of people click on the stage map. We did notice,  however, that the click-through rate was very low.

So we had to rephrase our hypothesis and realized that maybe the format was not the biggest  obstacle but maybe the channel! Our assumption was that customers viewed these emails as spam. Diana Palacios

Reflection: Visualization

Challenge and selection

I am a computer systems engineering student and as a thesis project, my team and I decided  that we wanted to focus our project on creating a useful tool aimed at visually impaired  people, after having carried out research on how in México there aren’t many accessible  tools that can help visually impaired people carry out the activities of their daily lives more  easily and also after having conducted a number of interviews with people that could help  us to have a better understanding of their needs.

Despite the fact that all team members have the same academic background, we all have  different interests in different areas of our major and therefore different approaches to  solving problems: a part of the team is more focused on software development, while the  rest is more interested on hardware development. This was a great area of opportunity for  our project, as it gave us the possibility of having a broader repertoire of possible solutions.

The limitations of our project were based on time: 9 months to complete the project and a  maximum budget of $ 500 usd.

After having done research on the tools that were within our reach to develop the project,  the next step was to think about the possibilities and to reach an agreement on the line that  we were going to follow. “Innovation and experimentation of creative processes” is to design furniture made

out of cardboard. This sustainable furniture must help the elderly to carry out

different activities, such as putting on shoes, cutting their toenails, moving around,

doing flexibility exercises, and other simple activities that may be difficult for them

due to their age. Thanks to the different steps of the design thinking process, I will be

able to successfully create these innovative cardboard furniture and empathize with

the user in the best possible way.

I believe that using the visualization tool allowed me to get to the main purpose of

the project, to empathize with the user through innovation. As Angela Weyes said in

the team were from different careers, so having different points of view on how to

Questionnaire

(INPUT REQUIRED)  ❖ Electricity

➢ Does it work at home based output voltage?

■ Yes, it works on normal input current present at home.

➢ Would it also work on a dc input current?

■ No, as we have given the option of working on chargable batteries, dc

input current wont work.

❖ Battery

➢ Is it rechargeable or one time battery ?

■ We have given the option of rechargeable batteries.

(DRYING MODES)

❖ Hot

➢ Is the hot mode safe?

■ Yes, we have taken into consideration of the damage, thereby giving a

lower temperature .

➢ What is hot mode for?

■ It is for fast drying.

❖ Cold

➢ What is cold mode for?

■ It is to set your hair in the style you wanted it to be.

➢ Can it dry my hair?

■ The main purpose is sor styling and not for drying.

(PERFORMANCE)

❖ Fast dry

➢ What is exactly fast dry?

■ This feature is mainly for the people with long hair , for whom drying the

hair takes alot of time.

➢ How is that carried out?

■ There is a separate clip available to ensure more air outlet.

❖ Styling

➢ Why is there a separate feature for styling?

■ We wanted to give a wide range of styling features for different kinds of

hair styles.

➢ How is this carried out?

■ For different kinds of hair we have given hair clips to style accordingly.

(VARIANTS)

❖ Colour

➢ How many colors are available?

■ There are a total of 5 available right now.

➢ Are there different models for men and women?

■ Yes, according to their needs we have.

❖ Price

➢ What is the price range?

■ Price varies from 3Thousand to 8Thousand rupees.

➢ Y the difference in the price ?

■ Different models have different output power levels, accordingly the

variations have been given.

Using Storytelling Tool for Student Counseling

 Challenge:

I am a faculty of a university and I have to deal with many types of psycho-social problems of the  students. Though my job is mostly academic, still being a mentor and adviser, I need to address  these issues. Students often do not open up at their first interaction. Their symptoms of disturbance  are usually expressed through their attitude in the classroom and other interactions. Some students  are irregular and remain unmindful in the class, others are ill mannered or rough in conduct. Some  students seems stressful and tired and even suffer from psychosomatic physical sickness. The  university has appointed a full time psychologist, with a separate office and facilities, who provides  Psycho-Social Counseling services for the students. But the students have some stigma regarding  communicating the psychologist as they think it will isolate them from others and they will be  considered mentally ill. Hence they sometimes share their problems with teachers and course  advisers. But the problem is teachers can listen to them with empathy and suggest some general  solutions, but they are not expert person for professional counseling. So, the challenge for the  teachers are to detect the students who need help and convince them to communicate the psycho  social counselor.

 Selection:

Just as this course resources mentioned, - through a good story, we could simply convey a message  that has logic. And also that a good story creates a cause and it ignites and unites people to solve  a bigger problem. text:
Design Thinking for Innovation - Week 5 Peer Graded Assignment

Done by Ahmed Figo

Tool that applied : Storytelling

▪  Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a powerful tool that are applicable in various situation of our daily life,  ergo it is the tool that I applied all the times. As Team leader in Media Player of Digital Dialogues, I sometimes face some obstacles in how to deliver the training to the  whole team because of the 24hours shifts that won’t allow me to meet all of them in the  same time. Besides, I also faced challenges of how to align all these messages and  make sure that all updates are well received and applied on our daily work.

I choose to apply storytelling as it can get insight into users, build empathy and reach  them effectively. I often create personas to represent target users and add conflict to  stories that reflect their user journeys and problems.

One of the reasons is through crafting stories, we can better understand what users  want from a solution. Good stories always captivate the team. In user experience   design, if all management team use storytelling throughout the design process to  ensure that all work focuses on the teams’ needs and the value that company want to  give those users. After completing design research to understand your users’ needs and  desires, you use your insights to tell a story about who your users are, what they need  and how you’ll provide that. This story makes it easy for everyone involved in the project  to empathize with the users and ensure that their work matches the story. Having a story  throughout your project means visualizing the design at the end of the launching  process is also straightforward, as you already know exactly which story to tell to show  how your training and updates provides value.

My storytelling will involve all my team in my section and my mission is to reach all of  them and deliver the same message to all my team.

Guddu Singh Reflection of Design Tool Application

Challenge and Selection:

I was working on a project and needed to communicate the magnitude of the discrepancy  between men and women in consulting. I needed to show how gender representation numbers  change over time as you progress into the higher levels of consulting. This was going to do into a  powerpoint deck that later made the case for offering unique networking opportunities for  women. I knew that, in order for the Ask later to be strongest, the audience really needed to feel  the disparity that exists at the highest levels of consulting.

I was deciding between using visualization and story-telling as a means of really connecting with  the audience and making this part of the presentation impactful. Ultimately, I decided to focus on  the Visualization tool. I chose this for a couple reasons: firstly, I thought of the saying “a picture  speaks a thousand words.” I knew that if people saw not just the numbers but the numbers  reflected in visual form, that would be more impactful. Secondly, I this tools is one I am less  comfortable with, so this also felt like a prime opportunity or practice.

Application and Approach

I ended up taking the data in Microsoft excel and spent time thinking about different ways to  visualize the data. I ended up deciding to start with showing a pie that starts out showing 50%  men and 50% women at entry level roles. I then removed respective parts of the pie as we moved  up the ranks to finally leave just 17% of the Partners were women. At the same time, the portion  of the pie that represented men keeps growing at each level up the ranks. So we start out with  parity and end up showing how the disparity looks by the end.

Insights and Future Application/Approach

Design Thinking for Innovation Final Project 1/26/2017

Fabio Sameh

Challenge and Selection: The challenge I would like to review has to do with recruiting potential students to a graduate  advertising program where I work.  We are a small program, only 200 students, and we have a  different way of funding as compared to most graduate programs at public institutions.  Our  operating funds are directly related to the students we can recruit to our program, meaning if we  don’t get 100 students each year, we might not be able to make certain purchases, hold events  or hire new staff or faculty.  Interestingly enough, while our students are highly successful after  graduation (we have a 99% placement rate after 6 months and hold a recruiter fair where almost  300 recruiters come to interview and hire 100 students) we always had a difﬁcult time getting  enough qualiﬁed recruits each year to ﬁll the tracks.  Many times we would only get 190  completed applications where our goal was at least 300.

Clearly there was a disconnect and we were certainly missing something important.  In this  case, we used a form of visualization to try and ﬁgure out what was going on.  We needed a  global view of our data and see the “what is” before we moved to the next steps (of course I did  not know these steps in the names that this course has given them at the time).

Application: As mentioned above, we can get plenty of data from our application process and qualitative  data from our current students as well.  We pulled data from the start of the application  download process where students tell us about themselves, how they heard about us, where  they lived, etc.

We also did a poll of our current students gathering other data that included questions of the  application and acceptance process and their impression of the number of students that apply  versus the 100 that get in. We use stories to better understand their  fears, needs and interests.
