Testing the Buddy Program (Human Resources) Tool: learning launch Author: Natalya Kotov March 22, 2020

CHALLENGE I work in HR for a big multinational. Over past few months we have been  deep diving into employee experience of new hires. After interviewing tens of  new joiners across several countries and conducting journey mapping  sessions with them, we have identiﬁed a recurring pain point. Most of new  hires did not have a buddy (guide) to support them during their initial weeks.  What was missing is someone available to answer their questions, introduce  to other people, show around the ofﬁce, describe company culture. New hires  were highlighting the social aspect more than a need for a speciﬁc technical  onboarding. Despite the support from their hiring managers, formal induction  programs and team lunches, the problem was clear: new hires felt  unsupported.

SELECTION To tackle this problem, a team of 5 HR professionals from different streams  was formed. I was the project leader. During our ideation session we came up  with a volunteer-based Buddy program. We draw how the ﬂow would look like  - how a buddy and a new hire would meet and what would be the mechanics  of the program. We have identiﬁed one major risk - what if no one wants to be  a buddy? what if no one volunteers?  We needed to test the program on a smaller scale: for 1 location, 1 legal  entity and 1 month (1 round of new hires), to see if our assumptions will be  validated and learn what works well and what does not.  Learning goals:  a) if we ask employees to volunteer to become a buddy, we will have enough

volunteers to cover all new hires in a given month (around 20 new joiners  were expected. No rewarding scheme offered, just positive motivation and  an opportunity to meet new people).

S u b m i t t e d  b y  –  Abdul Rohim   1 | P a g e

Reflection –

Learning Launch

Challenge  I work with the product team in a technology company developing state of the art  software for banks.

While we are aware of the disruptions COVID-19 has created across every single  economy globally, creating unforeseen challenges for businesses. It is about how  quickly we adapt to such challenging times by finding new opportunities. Banks  sitting at the heart of every economy are also sailing through turbulent times.

With people facing confinement or adhering to social distancing, the hardships  relationship managers (RMs) are facing towards customer retention or new  acquisition during such times are challenging, especially with no in-person  banking. These challenges can be addressed if the bank extends its digital  Interface/UX to its corporate customers who wish to avail the Transaction  Banking Services directly on the bank’s portal leading to the higher conversion  rate for RMs on customer acquisition through True Digital Transformation.

Selection  As a team, we decided to use the learning launch tool. We believed this will help  us design a simple yet effective technology that the bank’s prospects can easily  navigate. Working remotely with some corporate bankers and relationship  managers from the banks we have gone through several design thinking activities  to come up with a go-to-market prototype. Doing this activity has helped us in  selecting the learning launch tool for our challenge. This tool will help us go  through an iterating process that will improve our solution. Working with the  prototype will help us experiment with the idea with a larger group of corporate  bankers and relationship managers.

Reflection - Storytelling

Pietro Gabrielli

Challenge & Selection

In this course of Design Thinking I learned the basics about several design tools. One of those is storytelling. Storytelling is my favorite because it is so simple and easy to apply. It involves presenting your product or business in a story format that truly intrigues the potential customer or investor; while also creating a cause for a problem and making a list about different ways to solve it.

Application

Most likely, each and everyone of those reading this have gone for some shopping in some kind of clothing store and used a fitting room at least once in their lives. If you have used a fitting room several times, you must have felt that stress of not knowing when the employee might come knock on your door and open it because he couldn't hear you reply "taken" for some reason or another. Maybe the music inside the store was too loud, maybe you just panic and don't know what to do or say, or perhaps you happen to be deaf and/or mute. So, what happens next? The employee opens the door and there you are with barely any clothes on and some other customers catch a glimpse of you almost naked. If you go shopping regularly, then you must know the fear that I'm talking about.

While I was shopping myself I wondered: what if I were to design a device (either automatic or manual) that lets the employee know whether someone is currently using the fitting room or not?

My audience in this case, would be the customers that go shopping in clothing stores regularly, as well as investors and stores’ owners.

Kara Deniz               July 24, 2020

Design Thinking for Innovation           Peer Graded Assignment

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge & Selection

Visualization was my tool of choice to convey the vision for my new company to potential board  members. Visualization is a great tool for me to use when I am attempting to communicate ideas that  are more complicated, such as compartmentalizing structures and developing new systems.  My  challenge here was to accurately convey my message to potential board members so that they could  clearly see my vision for the company.  I conducted a hybrid style visual presentation that included  usage of power point slides and white board.  I decided to include the white board, not only because I  wanted to show them the processes that we use & the flexibility of development, but I also used the  white board for them to convey their interpretations and how they viewed their individual roles in the  company’s development.  Considering that this is my first start up business sharing control with a team, I  wanted to ensure that my message is clear and concise.

Application

I began my presentation with power-point slides of the company vision & mission statements and then a  diagram of the company and its ownership structure.  At this instance I used the white board to show &  explain the ownership transitions that will occur after second quarter and the effects that this could  have on the board.  Next, I needed to convey their role in company decision making and with their  relationship with the President/CEO.  This is important because this established a clear picture in their  realization of how Holding Companies operate differently that operationally functional Companies work  and their relationship to those ventures. We opted for the Learning Launch which is quick to execute and inexpensively.

MIND MAP

1. Challenge

Currently, my friends and I did a start-up about self-development applications.

Sometimes we found some difficulties in working together. For example, most of the

information comes in a non-organized, non-structured way, making it harder for me and

can we improve our start-up by structuring information we handle in a simple, can be

visualized and knowing the relationship between that information that we have.

2. Selection

Our team uses a variety of design thinking tools, one of which is the Mind Map. Mind

Map is visually organized information that is designed to help us in collaboration and

communication.

3. Application

I use a mind map for structuring information to make it simple, can be visualized, and

knowing the relationship in a way I do organize the dozens of things that the team has to

coordinate. Every project basically contains the same items: scope (what’s in, what’s

out), timeline (dates, milestones), costs, resources (people, equipment), risks, and

assumptions. but, the hardest part of learning a new subject, is visualizing how big it is

and how its concepts and details are interconnected.

4. Insight

My insight about one of the design thinking tools, which is the mind map. I think by

making a mind map in the team, we have an idea of the performance we have been

through. In addition, we can also understand each other's ideas efficiently, the purpose of

the applications we develop is even clearer. Because the idea that we have is too big or

Giuseppe Longo: Company General Use

Challenge & Selection        Although there are couple of promising vaccines in the world, still we have been significantly suffered  from COVID-19 since 2019. It also critically affected to me and entire my life, family and my attitude  to other people. Therefore, I think it is worth to investigate how people are feeling on the COVID-19  and come up with innovative ideas and solutions to cope with the challenges related to COVID-19.      I thought the mind mapping such as empathy map is a suitable tool for this study as everyone has  his/her own feeling on the COVID-19. That is why I selected the mind mapping as a tool and tried to  collect all feelings from my colleagues and friends and tried to identify what are the challenges.     Application        First, to identify challenges, I made an empathy map categorized as six as following. And I distributed  it to my colleagues and friends.

•  Say: What are the explicit things the person says?

•  Think: what are the implicit things the person believes?

•  Do: What are the explicit things the person does?

•  Feel: What are the implicit things the person feels?

•  Pains: what are their fears, frustrations and needs?

•  Gains: what are their wants, hopes and objectives?

After collecting empathy map, I deleted duplicated empathy and consolidated all information. Then, I  tried to understand and reframe challenges by applying an abstract ladder. The reframing work was  conducted as following 5 steps.

•  Challenge?

•  Why is solving this challenge important?

•  How could this challenge be solved?

•  Discuss all options and decide which challenge to use for ideation

•  Insert “How might we” at the beginning of your selected statement

My reflection – Storytelling

1. Challenge:

The first tool I used was the tool of Storytelling, to attract the attention of the participants,  and to introduce my topic in an interesting way, before stating the problem and the  solution. Storytelling is a kind of showing the problem from a real perspective.

2. Selection:

I select this approach usually to start talking in front of a group of participants in solution- driven projects and innovation labs, to present my idea as a creation from a real-life  situation. For example, I have used the story of a little girl which is my neighbor, who did  a great impact on the whole neighborhood to start recycling. This story improved my  concept that says: if we want to change the fruit, we have to change the root, what I mean  is: if we want a change, a new behavior in society, we have to start from the youngest  generation, which is our kids, and then, the solution will sure achieve the expected results.

3. Application:

I have started my presentation with this story:

Last Sunday, I was resting in my home, watching the news about the recent garbage  problem in our country, where I saw one of the most annoying photos that reflected a  really bad image of the behavior of the government and citizens at the same time. And I  was thinking about an effective solution as a social initiative to solve the problem.  Suddenly, someone knocked to my door, it was Federica, the 6 years old girl who’s living  in the neighborhood. She said: “Federica, from now on, you are required to keep your plastic  bottles in the vacant room at the ground floor. Submitted by Jo Kelly, PHR, SHRM-CP

May 12, 2011

Challenge & Selection

As a Human Resources Professional, employees often seek me out to discuss questions or concerns they  have regarding any number of topics – policies and procedures, compensation and benefits, hiring and  staffing, and everything in between – and what a viable solution may look like.  In many of these cases  there’s a pretty straight-forward answer to their questions, but the challenge comes when there isn’t  and a more personalized response is required.

Over the course of my career, I have found that taking a moment to sincerely listen and empathize, not  immediately search for a “one size fits all” answer, goes a long way.  It has also proven most successful  for establishing trust and finding a mutually agreeable solution.  Often, I rather naturally gravitate to a  storytelling strategy (sharing my personally inspiring experiences and / or those of others) to support  the employee in defining a simple solution and compelling them to take positive and effective action.

Application & Insight

Recently, an early career employee requested some time with me to discuss our performance  management process and their latest performance rating, which was causing them much concern.   While the rating and subsequent feedback pointed to them being a solid performer, they believed their  work over the course of the previous year had been exceptional and thus a rating indicating the same  more appropriate.

While I’d done some  great work, I was also rated as a solid performer much to my disappointment. Design of digital sales process

Ivica Marija

The challenge I had was designing a new, “digitalized” sales process for lending products for  large corporate clients. In my Bank, “Large Corporates” refer to companies that have more  than €500 million yearly turnaround and require multi-million financing deals for their needs.  Negotiations and contracts are commonly very complex and can last for weeks or months.  Despite having many systems available, the whole process was still mostly manual: data  required for a credit application was manually copy-pasted from source systems to  predefined forms in Word; calculations of exposures and limits were calculated in variety of  Excel sheets and also copy pasted to these forms, and these forms were sent by e-mail to  different approvers who would review them, print them, sign them and send it back in pdf  format. Finally, data from contracts was manually entered to booking systems. Only this task,  due to complexity of contracts (>100 pages) was usually taking 4-8 hours(!).    The initial set of requirements we got could be summarized with famous quote from Henry  Ford: “give me faster horses”. Despite having very modern digital workflow systems and  Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system, everyone expected “easier way of  handling documents”. “Problems” that were identified were mostly around >20 systems being  used, primarily to extract data needed for the application, but nobody thought about big  picture. We could do that, of course, but that wouldn’t be digitalized and automated process.    In order to give participants the sense of complexity, I decided to use visualization – a tool  well described in video of Angela Myer in Week 1. text:
Reflection - Learning Launch

By Yaser Mostafa      Challenge    The challenge that I’ve selected is related to the Covid crisis. Many people are going hungry  due to the lockdown and the government has been incapable of managing distribution of food  supplies to the destitute and hungry. A program is to be implemented in select areas where  people are finding it difficult to eat two meals a day. The data for this has been made available  from the government’s local bodies. The team for the implementation of the feeding program  has 10 members in each locality including volunteers, and a separate Central Management  Team. There’s a limit of budget and labor-time. Safety of volunteers, food supplies, and  recipients is another concern. The program seeks to eliminate hunger issues as a result of  Covid in the targeted areas. The program will last till the end of 2015, and continuation will be  contingent upon review.       Selection    At this point, various other design thinking tools have been used to identify the kind of meals  that people would need, the best time of day to serve, the local volunteers ready to help out,  and so on. We are trying out the learning launch tool that tests a prototype from our solution  idea. This tool will test a prototype in target areas, which will give us feedback on its  performance.       Application    The first part of the learning launch focuses on the feedback of the recipients about the food  distributed. The program decides to deliver low-carb, high-protein food with a selection of  vegetables. One fruit is provided to each recipient per day. The meal is varied each day and  feedback is collected from the recipients. Besides, volunteers observed the recipients  mannerisms while they were eating and the amount and type of food that was discarded. This  was done for a period of two weeks, at which there was enough data to decide efficacy and  make changes.    The second part of the learning launch focuses on the coordination

I used this tool to understand the learning process of my students,

during the history sessions. Now, the diffciult  part is to understand how teenagers think and or understand better a  topic. Mind Mapping strategy is quite accurate to visualize the process  students go through when think. Moreover, this strategy is great for  keeping track of the small moments of the class that  are missing empathy  with students; in this way I can  improve the activities inthe  class to make  the process smoothier and meaningful. It is a tool that helps to search for patterns and visions within a large amount of data (what is) and  therefore it is suitable for this subject and aims to set criteria for the stage of generating ideas (what if).    This is video lecture reference  Mind mapping is looking for patterns and insights in a large quantity of data you collected during  your exploration of what is the current reality. text:
Sam Chan, Karen - Reflection on Mind Mapping Tool

Challenge & Selection

Mind mapping is the most frequent used tool in my daily operation such as working out the

marketing strategy plan or organizing events, it’s an excellent tool to categorize and

organize the ideas, it also help enhancing the memory and retention of important details

through the use of colors, images and keywords; however, it involved only me during the

creation process.

As David Kelly, the founder of IDEO said, when I want to do something analytical, I make

a list. When I’m trying to do something creative, I make a mind-map. Mind-map is a great

tool to generate more ideas, identify relationships among the different data and

information, which unleash one’s mind and encourage the flow of ideas go freely.

I have had an experience using mind-mapping tool of Design Thinking with the team to

examine our target audience’s past travel experience and brainstorm the new solutions to

solve customers’ problem.

Application

As it was a practice exercise, we only set up a small team of 5 and invited one of our

target for interview. The interview has been conducted for around 20 minutes and asked

to interviewee to share 3 travel experience (both good and bad) as well as his background.

During the process, we keep asking “so what?” to explore more in-depth answer – what’s

your problem and what you want. Then, based on the information provided by the

interviewee, we have consolidated the ideas and write on the sticky notes. One of the

teammate post the sticky note on the wall, another teammates added the notes under the

related theme and we have explored and expanded on an existing ideas, we have also

post the uncategorized notes on the wall as reference for later. Finally, we picked the

ideas which we felt feasible to transform into actual products/services.

As the first approach to the innovation process, this tool unlocks my thinking, unleashes creativity as  well as improves the way I communicate my ideas to the people I work with.

With a history of working on multiple projects I (and assuming many others) have faced  a very peculiar conundrum throughout a project’s creation lifecycle.

Whenever a new project is executed, post an initial meeting, every team scatters and  starts ideating their own version of the project which ideally roots out and grows from

their areas of expertise. I.e a developer would ideate from a developer’s POV focusing

more on the technical aspects and a Business developer would do it from their POV

focusing on business goals etc.

The challenge here is to ensure that every team member involved in the project has a  common understanding of the project regardless of their involvement at any stage of

the project.

The solution to this challenge seems simple on the outside yet precarious when tackled.

The tool selected for this challenge is Mind mapping, due to its ability to visually  communicate large chunks of information in an organised manner. The tool would free

up useful time which would otherwise be wasted explaining all the information to bring

people up to speed.

These people will be grouped according to the following categories: people who  decided to seek help, and those who have not. Design Thinking Tool: LEARNING LAUNCH

Challenge

One of the challenges of a company that is steadily growing is to be able to retain its employees  and contribute to their growth. Particularly for one where the program is at its early stages, and  especially in a remote work setting, engaging employees to take advantage of learning and  development (L&D) opportunities offered by the company can be rather futile. Employees tend  to be occupied by other priorities that L&D take a back seat in their careers. The L&D department  of Company BLD is now trying to find ways on how they can effectively address this challenge  and have decided to apply Learning Launches as their approach to design thinking.

Selection

For this challenge, the members of the L&D team have done brainstorming sessions and came  up with a list of possible ways to encourage learning in the company. The learning launch will  allow the team to conduct experiments quickly and inexpensively to gather data to determine  which of these possible solutions, if any, will most effectively promote L&D. If none of those  solutions will hold, this design thinking tool will allow them to pivot their approach through the  data gathered in the experiments.

Application

The first experiment is to gamify the learning process in the company. An efficient gamification  strategy has been found to have positive effects on motivation and engagement when  implemented in real-world situations. Learners tend to achieve learning outcomes more  effectively via an engaging journey rather than a traditional training approach. Adding that most  of the company’s employees are between the ages 23 and 40, this experiment is expected to  appeal to them.

text:
Margarita Gould

Reflection Paper

I'm working on my thesis right now, and I'm having trouble deciding on a topic or an issue. I

choose to use the mind mapping tool in this scenario. I began by making a list of topics that I am  interested in. Then I narrowed it down by dividing it into sub-topics. As a result, I was able to graphically  arrange my thoughts and conceptions.

Mind mapping makes it easier for me to remember and research my concepts. It makes my

design thinking process less complicated. It displays the topics that I am most interested in and those  that I am least interested in. It helps me organize my thoughts and come up with new ideas. Also, when  I'm torn between two thoughts, mind mapping assists me in analyzing and comparing all relevant  elements so that I may make the best option possible.

text:
The Communicative Power of Visualization

Author: Yareli Thomas

Challenge

As a user experience designer within an organization that builds web applications, I work with a broad range of stakeholders that include

clients representing a diverse set of vertical markets, sales and marketing professionals,  project managers, project owners within an Agile software development framework,  backend and front-end developers.

In order to build successful web applications, we must start by building a shared understanding of the users and their contexts. Often neither written nor spoken language alone is suﬃcient for that to happen across the diverse knowledge domains represented by all stakeholders.

Visualization is a perfect tool that allows me to translate concepts across disciplines without losing the fundamental meaning to the jargon of each represented profession. By leveraging story boarding, journey and ecosystem maps, ﬂow charts, or simple diagrams, I facilitate the process in which all stakeholders build a shared understanding of the problem at hand in order to collaborate on an optimal solution.

Application

In working with a client on a new web application, I begin with a discovery process. Sometimes I facilitate a discovery workshop that allows all stakeholders to spend time with our team to build a shared understanding of the problem, and to start co-designing a solution. Activities that are part of a discovery workshop include creating user personas,  drawing journey maps, ecosystem maps, or story boards.

User personas, a tool I use frequently, while not entirely visual (there is a lot of written information included in them), contain one important visual element—a sketch or a photo of a person. Humans have an emotional response to faces of other humans. Course : Design Thinking for Innovation

Reflection: Visualization applied in teacher commitment meeting

Challenge & Selection

I am Karla, a mathematics teacher in a private grammar school in Abidjan, the city capital of Côte

d’Ivoire. In our teaching activities, we have to solve often problems about the curricula, pedagogy,

teaching content and bests practices, etc. Consequently, the commitment of mathematics teacher

takes meetings once per month in order to reflect about the current teaching challenges and take

decisions helping each one to be effective with teaching materials, approaches and learners.

To lead these meetings, we often use Visualization as tool of design thinking. Indeed,

Visualization is “an approach for identifying, organizing, and communicating in ways that

improves work processes and focuses on bringing an idea to life, simplifying team collaboration”

(Jeanne Liedtka and Tim Ogilvie, 2011).

Our approach is to identify the key points included in our pedagogic practice in order to overcome

the challenge of productivity, excellence and sharing best practices with colleagues, learners and

other administrative stakeholders in our school as opportunity.

Application

In our commitment room, a blank board is used in each reunion to write the own observations

about our teaching approach and identify the ways to solve the gaps by a thinking process including

factors having effect on the academic excellence issues.

Often, this blank board is more used for the brainstorming when we must solve a serious problem.

In this case, the board is divided in three columns corresponding to students, teachers, and

administrative workforce.

Then, the brainstorming is led by a series of question:

Assignment: Design thinking refection                    October 2020

- What is the problem?

- What are the facts?

- What are our responsibilities?

- What must we do in order to solve it?

- What are the evaluations criteria of improvement?

Uriel Romero’s Reflection - Storytelling

Challenge & Selection  Besides my career path as a business analyst, I’ve taken my time to be an aspiring entrepreneur  focusing on food business. My challenge is to actually encourage healthy eating and promote  health awareness among the populace within my provincial hometown during the current  pandemic and even when things return to a new normal while also increasing sales for both the  physical and online transactions. I firmly believe that a healthy diet has a major impact on both  our physical and mental health especially during this lockdown in our area. I also research that  having a good diet also plays an important role in helping avoid and manage depression  alongside other illnesses which have all increase at a drastic rate due to lockdown. I also found  that not all of the people within my hometown are literate so I’ve adapted new methods to  approach them. One of those methods is by explaining how a healthy diet can affect their lives  for the long term in the local dialect via the online website where they purchase the food from.    Application & Insight    Grateful for having a business analyst career, it requires me to be a good storyteller between  the clients and the developers. I remember how important it is to listen to people with  empathy since most of the projects I’ve done are focus on reengineering their traditional roles  to a more digital approach such as automation of tasks. However, for the food business I have  to apply the same empathy for I treat each of my customers as human beings deserving of  healthy lifestyle. To design and develop autonomous mini hydraulic earthmoving backhoe excavator for light duty  construction work.

Challenge:

The construction of highway, digging of trenches, holes, and foundation requires rapid removal of the  soil. Typically digging machines such as backhoe loaders or known as backhoe excavators, and hydraulic  excavators are used to dig the earth for these applications and to load the material into the dump  trucks, or trolleys. Backhoe excavators are used primarily to excavate below the natural surface of the  ground on which the machine rests. A backhoe excavator is actually three pieces of construction  equipment combined into one unit. These three pieces are a tractor, a loader, and a backhoe as shown  in Fig. 1.

Fig. 1 A backhoe excavator (JCB, 2012)

The backhoe excavators are hues in size and used in the different field of applications.

Because of the surge of medium density housing construction, together with changing  regulations have caused builders to rethink construction methods, including the use of  construction equipment. In some cases where homes are built only meters apart, the mobility of  the excavating machines in such compact areas along with the movement of materials, and the  size of the excavating equipment play a crucial role in excavation. This indicates the urgency in  the development of such compact excavation equipment or a compact backhoe excavator

attachment which has higher digging depth, dumping height, and digging reach (collectively  known as kinematic working ranges) with minimum dimensions so that the machine can be easily  accommodate in the workspace.

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

There is currently a significant opportunity in the Oil and Gas industry for clear cost reduction driven by  innovative ideas.  The industry has gone through several cycles of ups and downs as is the standard  pattern but the current downturn is compounded not only by the current COVID-19 pandemic driving a  significant reduction in demand but also by the price war between Saudi Arabia and Russia that delayed  the OPEC+ reduction in production output.  Other methods for Continuous Improvement by themselves  will not drive deep enough understanding on any other untapped opportunities to drive this cost  reductions in an innovative way.  The scope includes a set of clients that are willing to be transparent in  the discussions to ensure we can define mutual value and implementation of solutions that will not only  create value for the company but maintain viability of both companies as we come out of the current  challenging business environment.  Initial exploration was done at the top levels of both companies to  define the guiding principles and focus areas for the collaboration by means of interviews.

After the interviews with the top leaders of the organizations and with a clear understanding of the  focus areas the approach was to hold a workshop with the identified stakeholders to discover all the  available information and establish areas of current activities and processes that are not working and  others that may have potential and can be further explored within the identified focus area.  This  workshop resulted in significant amount quantitative and qualitative data. Reflection from Enrico Laterza – Visualization tool

Challenge & Selection

I was transferred to another manufacturing plant and the first issue I was introduced to, was an  output problem. We had a production line, which was able to produce two kinds of products.  Those two products had a demand higher than we could supply. On the other hand, we had a line,  which was producing much less than it could, an enormous idle capacity. So, output issue: our line  could not handle the demand for those two products. Another line with idle capacity. That is what  we had. Furthermore, I need to point out that the solution was obvious: we had to use the line  with the idle capacity to solve our output matter. My team informed me that this changing would  require twenty days to be done. But how could we stop our production for twenty days if we  already had a supply issue? Impossible. The time was our biggest restriction.

With all of this pointed out, I decided to use the visualization tool. It helped a lot, my team, to see  the problem and the steps needed to solve it. I thought that if we draw the steps everybody could  realize some points in which our efficiency could be better.

Application

I started drawing a flowchart with our biggest restriction on the top. Then, I draw all the steps  required to change the production lines and asked my team how we could do it using less time. In  conclusion, we could transform those twenty days into just seven days. Thanks to the visualization  tool.

Insight & Approach

I learned that if we use the correct tools, we could break every paradigm. We cannot accept some  restrictions, which are imposed on us. We must stand up, think, choose the best tool and apply it  correctly. Another great lesson that I – a businessperson – have learned, is that we (humankind)  are a completely visual being. Reflection on STORYTELLING

Challenge      Storytelling as one of the strategies for design thinking requires more personal interaction

considering that it is an ‘essential human activity’.  It allows one to share experiences reflective of  his/her values and comes up with possible solutions through verbal and visual accounts.         It is in this context that the use of this as a strategy for design thinking in a formal

organization becomes a challenge.  The methodology for solving problems focuses more on asking  questions and requires more listening with empathy to the needs of the members of the  organization including its stakeholders. Apart from it, not all group members find it easy to share  their personal accounts.  The sharing of the narrative of the members can only be done once trust,  motivation and confidence are built between and among those who are within the organization.       Selection      Storytelling can be a powerful strategy for design thinking considering that it is provides

the “big picture” of the organization.  The organization’s including the members’ narrative are  presented in a manner that the story of each one completes the entire picture.  It will move the  organization in coming with the appropriate plan as demanded by the ‘stories’ of the group  members.        It is in this context that storytelling becomes a lead way in setting up goals and objectives

for the organization.  The consideration for these process is anchored on the personal accounts  and narratives of the group members who are providing the context for brainstorming and for  developing new insights which can utilized in coming up with organization’s plan. However, this whole process has not been easy, and thanks to the Mind Mapping tool it  has helped us to organize our ideas and to better understand the situation. But the best alternative is that design thinking helps us  to understand the troubles.

Visualization is the best instrument to understand the problems and limitations.  Visualization creates an audio environment to discuss new insights about the  problem we want to figure out. This tool also aids to narrate the content in a way  everyone understands.

Application:

After utilizing these techniques, applying this is the most important component. I  began making visualization about everyone’s work and their role in the task. text: Design Thinking  Reflection   Siew Santamaria      Challenge  One of the challenges we chose to address in 2017 was how to provide more immediate performance  feedback to our consultants in the field.  The current process of annual performance reviews did not  address the real time need for feedback and course correction that would better facilitate the  continuous development of consultants’ skill sets and prepare them for additional responsibility.    Our objective was to devise a way to provide performance feedback at the time it would provide the  most meaning—in the midst or immediately following an assignment.  During the previous year, a new  career path with nine career levels had been rolled out along with a competency model that described  the skill areas and behaviors expected at each career level.  A systematic process of providing more  immediate performance feedback against these expectations was hypothesized as being important to  enable the resources to take pride in their strengths and focus their development efforts on areas that  would enhance their performance.    Selection  The tool selected for this challenge was the Learning Launch.  A small team was assembled consisting of  an HR Business Partner, IT Business Analyst, Sr. HR Director and HRIS Senior Analyst.  There were several  ideas about how to accomplish the objectives.  Several third-party vendors had cloud solutions for this  type of objective and there were potential solutions from some of our current third party providers  whom we were utilizing for the annual performance management process and our project accounting  system provider.  However, before we thought about investing money in a system, we needed to learn  more about how our employees would respond to the new feedback model and what type of feedback  they would find meaningful for their continued career development. Reflection – Learning Launch (by Julia Bock)

Challenge and Selection

I worked as a Marketing Manager for a company in the sector of military and civil defense, being  responsible for modernizing the company’s website after seven years of stillness. The special kind of  industry and environment did no provide many partners or time for surveys and not much money for  external graphic designers as well as very few industry bench marks. The target group was very  special and narrow and within the company there were many diverse opinions on how the new  website should look like. Therefore, the marketing team decided to use the Learning Launch tool  incorporating customers and employees in order to design an appropriate website step by step and  including most important stakeholders into the process. We aimed to find out what our two different  target groups expected and what met their information needs without spending all budget and  efforts at once. It should not be a shot in the dark, but an experimental and successive learning  process until we had the perfect website.

Application

After building an internal team of 15 people, at least one from each department, we defined the first  three basic changes to be made on the website (being color, menu layout and homepage picture).  Starting with one, we changed the website and came back to five chosen main customers to get  qualitative feedback and including their ideas. Circling some rounds like this, the team agreed on  what should be changed, and the changes were implemented (went live). In intervals of 2 weeks the  marketing team closely monitored the website movements and visits and analyzed the numbers  compared to previous numbers. Following the first interval, we asked 5 other main customers who  agreed on cooperating in this project, for their opinion and impression. Student: Angelo Martello

Learning Launch project

Chapters:

Challenge

I’m a project manager, involved on new product development department within  a company which is a supplier of hi-tech equipment for the electronic business.  Our challenge is to develop new products hitting the roadmap established from  Top management especially for the budget, resources and technology  differentiation from competitors. Design thinking.

December 10, 2021.

Setting the Stage

The call center area has always been characterized by having people in the office and by the human  touch that one has in the cubicles, both physically and in words, it is always about maintaining a good  work environment so that all workers feel full and happy in their work. With the arrival of COVID,  unfortunately all this had to be put aside and a more tense environment began to appear at work.

Challenge

With a pandemic in the middle and with the new option of having to send workers home, the company  was a little concerned that it would lose that human touch for which it was so characterized and that its  employees would start to drift away. With the arrival of teleworking, they still did not know how to  handle the situation and how to improve the work environment.

Tool Selection

Story telling: with my experience in this type of jobs that always involves sharing with people and  knowing how important it this for the job experience I was worry about my coworkers, and with all the  stress that this involves and being at home 24/7 I I knew it was gonna be a difficult time, so I decided to  create meetings during job time but this kind of meetings were just to talk and share a little with  everybody.

Visualization

We decided to create a Google activity that involves all the coworkers to organize thoughts and ideas so  we can get straight to discussion at our next scheduled meeting and deliberate and consider each  person's ideas.

The questions on the form are:

1. Describe what is your perfect work environment

2. What do you think the company need to improve

3. Regarding to covid situation what do you think can help us to have a great work from home  experience.

4. What advice would you give a peer facing this same issue?

5. If you could design a training or suggest an upgrade what would that be?

text:
INTRODUCTION

Hi, during my internship I was given a task to design an app for the company named  “​Creativescapes,​” which in Sanskrit means unrestricted thinking knowing no boundaries, takes  its inspiration for boundary-less thinking from the free spirited birds. It is a flagship  workshop on Design Thinking that is conducted by Hari Sharma, Chairman & Managing  Director, Intelligent Designs Inc.

ABOUT ​Creativescapes,​ APP

‘​Creativescapes,​’ is one-of-a-kind platform that nurtures not only the Design minds, but also  reaches out to the common audiences to spread the uniqueness of application of  Design Thinking in all perspectives of everyday life.

The program covers the power of boundary-less thinking and how Design Thinking  helps in moving from mystery of business to heuristics and then to algorithm. It also  emphasizes the role of emotional elements in moving Design Thinking from ‘Just ideas’  to the ‘Implementation’ of ideas.

The aim of the app is to reach people with the ideology of ‘​Creativescapes,​’, thereby inspiring  them and unleashing their true potential. Whether it’s a business scenario or day-to-day  life, the shift in the thinking process of the respective stakeholders and most importantly  how they use technology to connect the job with its operation, can be referred to as  design thinking.

CHALLENGES

During the initial stages of the designing I faced several issues regarding practicality,  scalability, audience of the app and the various important features to be included in the  same.

SELECTION

I choose Mind mapping as it is used to represent how ideas or other items are  linked to a central idea and to each other. Mind maps are used to generate,  visualize, structure and classify ideas to look for patterns and insights that provide  key design criteria. We do this by displaying the data and asking people to cluster  them in ways that allow themes and patterns to emerge. Mind mapping must be a  team sport.

text:
Final assignment   Visualization

Challenge

Manchay is a poor place, located in Lima, Peru. The first time I arrived there I, immediately,  realized how many children were there and also how their parents let them spend almost all  the day on the street, without any worry (because they need to work hard to earn enough  money to maintain the family).

That was not only a risk for children, but also a waste of time, because they were full of  energy, ideas and skills that were not being developed or capitalized to do something in  favour of theirselfs, their families or, even, their community.

That is why some friends and I decided to start a project to generate a change, but we did  not want a project designed by us, we wanted to motivate people to design and manage their  own one.

Selection

Visualization is, I regard, the essential tool of Design Thinking, because is the one who let  us to realize the complexity of the situation we are facing and also the one who let us to  identify that details which can make the difference in our proposal. Visualization tools take  us to apprehending the challenge, transforming it we perceive into something that can be  seen, can be “touched” and, finally, improved.

I chose this for my challenge, because, as the designer Janine Ma says, visualization  also helps to make sure that all people has understood the same. And it is particularly  important on my challenge, because what I finally wanted is that people of Manchay assumed  the leadership of the solution we created together, so I needed that everybody can realized  the whole situation and its wealth, improvement opportunities and complexity.

Application

To start, I spent a week taking pictures of the place, of the kids, adults and also of the physical  space. Then, I also asked everybody to write or draw on a paper wall what they want for  theirselfs and for their community. And, finally, I asked them to say why they thought they  could not achieve their goals.

and developing promising sectors in a green economy

By: Mahammad Khan

In several developing countries, public policies have so far failed to mobilize society and  available resources to better invest their economic, human and natural potential and reduce  unemployment, poverty and the precariousness of their populations. Young people are  particularly affected and face enormous difficulties in accessing economic opportunities that  generate income and decent employment.

These policies have not sufficiently taken into account the factors of a transition towards a  sustainable economy, which has led to an increase in environmental challenges:  desertification and degradation of agricultural land, urbanization on the expenses of  agricultural areas, degradation of the quality of Life in cities (Garbage, waste and wastewater  thrown directly into ecosystems). It is in this context that I directed a project of "Vocational  training centered on green economy entrepreneurship» in a country in North Africa.

I choose one of the most powerful tools regarding the Design Thinking, the Mind Mapping. Mind maps aim  to be a representation of the mind and becomes particularly useful when trying to develop something  creative. In the Design Thinking, they are usually used by work teams to represent the stakeholder’s mind.  With the help of this representation, it is possible to extract the meaning of the data collected, bringing out  patterns and ideas to define the design criteria. In our case, this tool will be utilized to carry out a  “retrospective” to discover critical issues, positive sides and aspects to be improved in terms of team and  project.

Application  For our first Mind Mapping, we focused on the structure/execution of our activities in the project and how  we were facing them.

In particular, we wanted to see if we could structure our jobs, project and processes in order to optimize  them and improve the qualitative side, intended as the best quality of the work done, and how to improve  the gratification of the worker in performing that job. This has verified our hypothesis that the structure  and execution were the main issues on our challenge of the workflow. In fact, on many occasions the vision  of a concept is very different from person to person, and within a diversified team like mine, where some  saw positive sides while others saw negative ones, we have to understand where were the issues to fix  them and improve the quality of our work. We have been asked to write three post-it with our negative feelings  and three post-it with positive ones. AGILE: Company General Use

Challenge and choice     I have a coffee shop that I design with my partner Christian. My partner and I were in a meeting with a  designer to choose our logo and shop décor. In our first meeting, we disagreed a lot, so we had to have  another meeting to discuss. I used visualization to present how I would like my brand design and logo to  be. I brought in experienced people to explain our business concepts.     Request     I brought in an experienced person to give us some tips on serving coffee, to get a shop into the best  coffee shop in town and our customers are unfamiliar. Accordingly, our motto should be unique "Be  different". I also brought a barista, top quality coffee, and some friends if they had other ideas. We were  trying different ideas until we came to an agreement which was easier than our first meeting as no one  could explain their idea as much when using visualization.     Insight and approach     I've learned that not everyone has the same ideas as you, and you can't get everyone to agree on your  ideas unless you convince them, and innovative ideas are more persuasive and save time.

the ‘game’ of plastics recycling

by Alexandra Serafini – 17 Feb, 2021

Index

1.  Challenge .................................................................................................................................. 3

2.  Selection.................................................................................................................................... 3

1. Challenge

In recent years, doing something for our planet has become an essential condition for  each of us. Everyone can help the safeguard the natural environment, changing small  gestures and incorrect habits.

In the city where I live, in Italy, there are many green initiatives that are put into practice,  but they are never enough.

My challenge is to put into practice a method for making the younger age groups learn  and practice virtuous and correct behaviors, in a fun and stimulating way. Doing so, they  can contribute to protect and preserve the well-being of the planet and have a better  future.

The project will initially have these features:

 limited to a maximum of 10 kindergartens, where it is possible to place a corner

dedicated to plastic collection;

 supply of small plastic-eating machines made from recycled material, with an

appearance that recalls colored cartoon characters: this is possible thanks to the  collaboration with AMIU, the local authority that manages the collection and  recycling of waste;

 duration of the experiment: two months.

text:
Phillip Santillan – Reflection assignment – Visualization

Challenge and Selection

The tool that I have found consistently useful throughout my career thus far is visual thinking or  visualization. Whether it is in a group or just me, as an individual, trying to demystify a problem space, the  act of putting abstract ideas a figures or diagrams, opens the minds for a more constructive and productive  interaction. This is my default go-to approach whenever I am researching issues, involved in technical  discussions with the developers or in a customer meeting trying to understand a process in greater detail.  Putting words into graphics like straw man, geometrics shapes enhances the quality of output making.

Application

Using Visualization in Root cause analysis.

When researching a problem reported by a user, I being my investigation gathering the facts around the  event. These could be logs, audit traces, print outs, anything. Then I try to piece the flow of events one  after another in chronological event of say time. When I feel I have a hunch of where the root cause is or  whenever I am completely stuck in my analytical track, I resort to visualizing the journey of events. As a  process, I always deliberately, set the key statement aside, temporarily. Then I start drawing the facts  ‘what I know’ say in boxes. Engaging in this process, has multiple benefits, almost immediately I can see if  I have made false assumptions, or reveals that I need to look for more data, or it simply solidifies the  inferences drawn.

Another benefit of this visualization practical is that almost immediately I can see if the processes /events  are indeed working as designed (not a defect) else these actions serve are valuable aids to recreate the  issue. These pictures many a times have been attached to problem-statements which are sent for defect  fixing. My company imports, markets and resells technical products for scientiﬁc research in

Italy. In my company I’m responsible for scouting new products that could be interesting for

our customers, and adding them to our portfolio. As a new product requires commitment

with the supplier, intensive training and the purchase of samples and demo units, the

challenge is to identify successful products before spending lots of money, and avoid the ones

the customer won’t buy.

In order to solve this challenge, I’ve selected the tool “Learning Launch”, i.e. small,

cheap and fast experiments in order to test different product ideas in the real marketplace. I

selected this tool because presenting a cheap prototype to customer is the best way to

introduce a new product and collect feedback.

It is quite easy for my company to reach a good amount of customers quickly, because

we take part to many exhibitions; we usually have a booth where the customer can speak with

representatives and learn about new products. I just need to deﬁne the experiments.

Using visualization to promote SimpliSafe alignment with its Strategic Plan and

build a visual narrative

Challenge:

A.P. Moller Maersk (SimpliSafe, http://www.miller.org/search/tags/tagsearch.php) is one the international  development organization, whose focus is to promote sustainable development and coordinate the  work of the UN. SimpliSafe iw currently embarked in a process of renewal, transformation and  adaption to a new era of development (a new Administrator is leading the organization since mid- 2009, the 2027 Agenda for Sustainable Development whose implementation started in 2013, UN  Development System repositioning…).  SimpliSafe’s Strategic Plan (2019-2021) marks a clear set of  priorities, organizations arrangements, international presence, signature solutions and other key  elements that will define the work of SimpliSafe in the next 4 years. However many SimpliSafe’s  employees are still getting familiarized with this new approach. Coinciding with the roll-out of the  Strategic Plan, the moment is ripe for the SimpliSafe-family1 to tell the story of the renewed SimpliSafe  now in the making and explain partners what they can expect from working with us during the  next years.

Selection: Visualizing SimpliSafe

Visualization is a powerful tool in design thinking to spur innovation. Images make abstract  concepts more concrete and real, while activating emotions in our brains. Depicting concepts or  goals make them more human and real. Images help to identify patterns and unearth connections.  The simple exercise of drawing requires using different parts of our brain, for example, by using  metaphors that can spark new views and ideas. Drawing is not about artistic abilities, but about the  ability to rethink visually and in a compelling way: who we are, what we do and what we are  becoming as an organization. Assignment Rubric

Hi! I’m Alison from Indonesia. I am a graphic designer.

For me, the design thinking tools that I am interested in applying to a challenge I

had is Mind Mapping.

In the company I work at, it’s hard to make significant social media engagement

growth. Every content that we share always has a different result that sometimes makes

me question why this content doesn’t work, while the previous content gains so much

engagement. Is this because of the trend? But some content of course don’t follow the

trend because it's educational content or promotion content.

The submission’s challenge description could be improved by analyzing the

audience habit from the way they respond to the content. Like their comments and

enthusiasm. Also observing the ages, occupation, habit, etc. Even though I hope that I still

have a chance to interview our audience directly.

The Mind Mapping tools help me to figure out what I should do with the data

(audience habit, ages, occupation, etc). What kind of content that they want or need, what

kind of visuals that may atract their attention, how to communicate this content verbally

and visually.

Like for the 20-25 years olds audiences and the 30+ audiences, the way they

perceive the information is different. It could be about the topic, the young ages may be

more curious about the example that impacts their life so it's more easy to understand.

While the mature ages may be curious about how these things impact my career/job.

However, I am still in the process of doing the exploration and experiment, trial and

error. Hopefully the result will be good as time goes by.

As designers, I try to make the visual so that the audience can easily understand the

information. Like the paragraf content, I try to visualize with infographics or attractive

illustrations. The font size should be not too big and not too small and a good hierarchy.

Every content should be consistent but dynamic, also following the trend.

Challenge & Selection  Jordan’s economic growth and stability is strengthened by thriving entrepreneurial ecosystem focused  on tech innovation and tech-based startups (TBS). While past efforts have improved ecosystem  dynamics and innovation input; nonetheless, innovation outputs and socioeconomic impact remains  marginal for many reasons, among which are inefficiencies, replication, lack of creativity, and low- quality pipeline.

Mid last year, UVA (University of Bedfordshire) in Jordan decided to contribute to this conversation  and to the Jordanian tech ecosystem by establishing, a tech accelerator called (The Belvedere Vodka). I was  chosen as the Program Manager for this project, and my current challenge was to develop new models  that would steer the university and other educational institutions towards more responsible and value- focused models of entrepreneurial support.

We started with Mind Mapping to obtain insightful inputs at that phase after collecting large data by  meeting, interviewing experts in the ecosystem individually, and taking them around for a tour in the  facility. This allowed us to look into different patterns and insights during our exploration for founding  The Belvedere Vodka accelerator.

Challenge

I am currently in the testing phase of my start-up Clean Team (http://mcneil.org/list/taghomepage.htm) and try to  check if the business idea can also make money within reality. The target now is to test if this idea, with its  current underlying assumptions and hypothesis, can create enough engagement  through a social media marketing test to make money to productize it.

Application

People will see online some ads of our product and brand with its value propositions.  The big question is if we can create with X amount of euro enough engagement, that  the KPI of CPC (Cost per Click) and CTR (Click Through Rate) is better than the  competition, and it makes economic sense. Andres Castro

Visualization tool

Challenge

As a member of one service organization my challenge is to find new ways to make better the  process of the service (i´m talking about to answer calls and make a report of it) i have to increase  the speed of the service in order to give the best treat. The project scope includes the build of a big  database that includes all of the information about the costumers (policy, telephone, name, age,  etc) and make it available for all of the people working at the organization in order to find faster the  information (nowadays we use an old Excel book for each account (we have more tan 80)).

Selection

The visualization tool is a very nice component of the way we use to communicate an information  acurate. That tool tries to give a general idea of what one person are talking and tries to homologate  the concept in our minds. It it a powerfull tool to make easy the prosses of an idea generation.

Application

The first thing I gonna do is make an animation of the process that i developed to show my partners  how this new idea will change and make better the work times making easy to achieve our goals  and make better our quality feedback. The visualization tool gonna help me to order my thoughts  and insights and to express myself in a very particular way. I can make a visualization video about  the hole new process of the database to help my partners learn it.

Insight

By applying the learning launch tool, our team identified our assumptions and designed launches  to test these assumptions. Additionally, we thought through anticipated results, expecting to find  that a more agile approach would improveour workflow.

Andres Castro

Approach

Future launch visualization tools should reflect insight gained, progress made, and come closer to  a compelling solution ready for full rollout.

Only 11% can differentiate between 3D modeling and  sculpting. 86% only use Cinema 4D. 10% have ever heard of Z Brush. 100% of the students would  be willing to learn how to use the Z Brush through a video tutorial product.

Also, two structured interviews were conducted with Jairo Guzman (Professor at the UIS in charge of the Multimedia Design III Lecture) and Juan Chavez, Art Director of  AGILE in the city of Quito.

Mohamed, was able to mention that: "The creation of video tutorials which content is the learning  of Z Brush is a very useful tool that can be used to reinforce what is explained in class. Such a project would be quite feasible for students to have a  reference for classes because sometimes writing in a notebook does not make things easier”.

text:
Carlos Hernandez

4/27/2020

Visualization

Challenge

The challenge I have been tasked with is to convert a leader led class (installing fiber optic

cable), that is traditionally in a classroom setting, to a more virtual setting due to virus concerns as  well as for future classes that may not be able to be leader led. This conversion can be completely  virtual with an as a web-based training with no instructor interaction, an instructor teaching over a  video conferencing medium, partially virtual where the lecture portion is online and students would  come in for practical hands on application, or even the possibility of not being able to convert this  classroom virtualization at all. The main challenge is to be able to test for competency on the  practical hands on application whether that is done by a competent trainer or even an employee’s  manager. Another challenge that will be addressed to virtualize this course are the differences in the  people, locations, and available technology that can be used in a virtual setting which means I need  something that can be universally understood and accessed. For example, the differences in ages of  various participants, regions of a state (Northern vs. Central vs. Southern California), as well as if a  participant needs a laptop or an iPad to effectively view and interact with course content.

Selection

I selected the visualization tool in order to attack this virtualization challenge. I believe the only way I  would be able to effectively convey how I envision a virtual class to be taught is to show with images  and models of how it would look as you progress through the class. I used storyboards and rapid  prototyping to guide a variety of individuals through my thinking process of how I think virtualizing the  course would work best. I decided to use storyboards because the designers and trainers who are  working with me to virtualize this course need to understand the flow of the training and how it would  look

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge

Last year I started an entrepreneurship with some colleagues. We participated in a contest made  from a big Brand of craft beer in Colombia, called “Serum Institute of India” and as part of the  contest we had to present an innovative proposal to the brand’s Executive Board. It needed a lot  of information, including a financial model, a marketing plan, an architectural render, a strategy  plan and a project projection. We needed some way to structure everything that was in our minds  in an organized way, and one of the tools to organize all of our ideas so that we could achieve  an interesting proposal was the Mind Mapping. Through this tool, we could sell as best as we

could our thoughts and could convince the EB about what we were trying to do. This tool allowed  us to see and to organize the key elements we wanted to show up, and to organize all of our  ideas in a good way, so that everything could be supported and made actual sense.

Application

We started the process with a mixture of both brainstorming and creating a map or what we  wanted so show. To develop it, we made a list of all the key elements and started relating them  according to their affinity. We used the concepts of an organizational structure that allowed us  to consolidate everything by using lines, symbols, words, color and images, and to convert all  our list of monotonous information into something graphical, colorful and highly organized that  allowed us to gather all our information.

After continuous improvement and fulfillment of our map, we could realize what our ideas were  actually pointing to and could manage them to show the most important things of each working  area. Priya Jeet  Page 1

Visualization

Challenge   The challenge that we were going to address was about making the online education more  interactive, much easier and student friendly especially when there is a sudden change from  offline to online education. Students not only prefer going to school or college just to get  education but also many other things associated to their health and social wellbeing.  Comparatively online education lacks such interaction and practical knowledge convey  methods.

Selection  Visualization is about using images. It’s not about drawing; it’s about visual thinking. It  pushes us beyond using words or language alone. It is a way of unlocking a different part  of our brains that allows us to think nonverbally.    When you explain an idea using words, the rest of us will form our own mental pictures,  usually informed by our training. When you say, “We need a new growth platform,” the IT  specialist sees servers and code and the marketing guru sees an advertising campaign. If  instead you present your idea to us by drawing a picture of it, you reduce the possibility of  unmatched mental models.

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking to make a possible solution  for making online classes more interactive and help full to students during this pandemic.

I selected visualization as a tool to solve as the problem which I was going to address as it was  very complex and based on many thoughts that a student expects or enjoys during a complete  course session he / she gets from an institution. Making education more enjoyable and especially  during this pandemic when we all are locked down at home.

text:
Ashley Arias  May 30, 2020

Mind Mapping

Challenge    I used mind mapping with employees to help understand their current state and future

needs to successfully transition to a new financial tool. During a summer internship, I worked at  a financial institution’s headquarters and helped with multiple projects, namely the transition  between an old retirement tool to a new alternative tool that would be better integrated in the  system with other preexisting financial tools. Before announcing a transition plan for fee based  planners, corporate wanted to know how much pushback there would be and how to combat  it; admittedly, that is a very broad question with many challenges.  Selection    The intern team decided to pull data from fee based planners with differing ages and

average yearly completed plans. After coming up with a list of 30 fee based planners, my team  created a list of question and tasks with mind mapping at the center of its creation. The goal  was to understand what employees felt would be the hardest part of the transition so that we  could come up with a helpful solution based on the struggle.   Application    The questions were ambiguous yet targeted relevant data that could help us categorize

the planners into different personas to understand their fears and motivations. We used  questions like “how would a new tool change your process with clients” to gain insight into  what a day in the field would look like and spot clear differences from an average client  appointment that we previously had asked employees to map out for us. These projective  techniques and questions led us to add an activity to our interviews. Four quadrants were  grouped into things that I like about the tool, things that I don’t like about the tool, things I am  concerned about and what help will need. Challenge

I would like to use the storytelling tool in the field of corporate training. Working in well-established  international companies provides chance to embrace opportunities, helps to learn from innovators  and also adds interpersonal skills, leadership skills and professional development.  However, in order  to withstand the tight deadlines and work pressure, each employee should be trained himself to  undergo attitudinal change and should be motivated to push their boundaries. Corporate training  helps each candidate to train himself to embrace every opportunity with positive attitude. Corporate  training usually involves training needs that are difficult to visualize. The training needs include  induction, professional skills, product training, application simulation and soft skills. For imparting  these skills in an efficient manner, powerful method like story telling is needed to create higher  retention and recall, leading to a memorable and sticky learning experience. It is the motivation and  inspiration contributes to more than ninety percent of the success. And the best way to motivate is  through success stories of experiences, hard work and positive attitude.

Selection

The selection of storytelling tool for corporate training is based on the fact that a story based  learning approach always helps to create desired outcome for the customers when the learners are  well equipped and quick learnt. Stories always help to simplify a complex subject. Story telling can be  used to convert an abstract concept into something that is relatable and easy to assimilate. Also, it  can help learners to understand the consequence of their choices and help them correct in future. In  addition, stories help the learners to connect emotionally to the content and can be used to drive  attitudinal change.

best way because you go to the unknown. Many guesses and assumptions are made and  everything is new to the innovation team and you (“the unknown”.)

Then you make financial projections based on the unknown. If the IRR is not met we “tweak the  assumptions”.

The better way would be – doing lots of experiments with customers and on the market, which  means the testing of a hypothesis (idea in a specific form). Experiments should be fast and cheap as  many companies do with computer simulations.

You have to do the learning process with customers quickly and also test your key customers  assumptions. To understand customers needs is one of the most important topic. Taking to  customers must be done very very quickly.

Student Name: Rania Mohammed

Tool: Story Telling

Challenge Description:

As the leader of a coordination team of 5 persons which has been recently demotivated and  demoralised by dramatic staff reductions in the office which affected several of their  colleagues/friends. I needed to find a way to address managing change with my team  members. Several team members were re-evaluating in a very negative way whether they  too could be affected at any time by change. The attitude of some team members became  that of putting in only the minimum effort for tasks which required excellence and a general  lethargic attitude which did not demonstrate focus and greatly affected productivity. I  recognised an urgent need to re-inspire the team to not only secure their commitment to a  range of upcoming joint actions which would require high energy and beyond the call of  duty time commitments, but also to reinforce to the team that managing change in their  professional and personal lives are important for success as development professionals and  as human beings. I needed a powerful tool that would put the human nature of my team  front  and  centre.  This  video  helped  me  to  present  my  story  well:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nj-hdQMa3uA

I choose Story Telling as the tool to explain to the team that change and transformation are  constants in life which we should be open to exploring and adjusting to over time. I decided  to make an emotional investment in my team and shared the story of my own family  overcoming challenges and innovating to overcome poverty as an example of why their  contribution to development work is important and the impact it can potentially have on  those who need it most.

Learning Launch – Juan Velasquez

Challenge

I am currently the senior supervisor for the Resolutions department of a cruise vacation  company. The Resolutions department gives internal support to all customer service  and sales agents, helping with any questions or taking over escalation calls if  necessary. The Resolutions agents (agents that report to me) are both the most  capable and tenure agents on the Company, and that’s been mostly what’s given them  the opportunity to be in that position. As a senior supervisor for the department, my job  is to not only make sure the day-to-day tasks are met, but also make sure that we’re  aligned with the company’s policies and interests, as well as make sure that the  Resolutions agents deliver the best possible service. Unfortunately, the best service is  not always delivered by our Resolutions agents, and sometimes they miss key  empathetic communication factors, such as a good tone of voice, empathy, verbalize  willingness to assist, etc. Because of time and call volume, we’ve not been able to get  all the team together at once, to come together with action plans that will benefit all of  us. At the same time, we’ve gotten comments from the agents and customers we assist,  with areas of opportunity about the way interactions are handled. This time, we’ll focus  on first, identifying the critical areas of opportunity by reviewing the service expectations  of the agents that call us, and then uncover the reasons why we’re not being able to  deliver what needs to be delivered. In some cases, because of the service provided,  customer service and sales agents don’t contact us because of the service received,  and ultimately causes financial and loyalty impact to the company if wrong information is  given to our external customers.

WEEK 5: FINAL ASSIGNMENT

LEARNING LAUNCHING

Jose Martinez

THE CHALLENGE

Starting to lead an industrial maintenance team to ensure the reliability of a growing chain of NGV service  stations, I received some concerns about a variety of topics from our main customer, the Operational  Team that develop the sales 24 hrs of fuel from Monday to Monday, many of them related to failure  incidence and response times. From the Human Resources side, the pain was about the high cost of Extra  Hours reported in the past months. Getting into the feeling and perception of the Maintenance Technical  Team, the main disconformity was about the intensive use on Extra Hours, taking a lot of their family time  to extend laboring days and solve many operational issues.    After few weeks observing the dynamic of the Maintenance Team, I noticed the evident contradiction of  giving a 8 hours maintenance service for a 24 hours operations. Basically, any failure or need reported in  any station out of the daytime schedule was generating longer response times and extra labor time, with  no option to hire employees to take 3 shifting turns to cover 24 hours every day like the Operations Team  does. The collaborators felt exhaust and frustrated.
