text: Design Thinking for Innovation: Reflection     Author:  Surya Mohamad ©      Title: The Power of Storytelling for a Start-up Pitch    Challenge:  My team and I are in the pre-start-up phase of incorporating our own BioTech Start-up company. We  are currently working on the first prove of concept on a new drug delivery system against a specific  cancer type. Already in this early phase of development, we are dependent on financial support as  BioTech require a lot of resources from a financial and people point of view. A huge challenge is to  bring business angles, private equity investors or venture capitalists on board at this very early stage  of high risk. How to convince them to support such innovation although “everything” remains  unclear at the beginning of this journey (Piero Vicari; module 1)? In a pitch the biggest challenge is  the limited time window (5-7 minutes) for convincing the right investors. Hence a short, simple and  compelling story has to attract them to invest into you and the team.    Selection:  I was choosing the Storytelling tool to address our challenge. According to Elroy Ford’s analysis  (Global Leadership Development Director @ Mars; Module 2) most business leaders are bored 90%  of the conversation. But he showed a great way to change that. In order to draw their attention  towards the prime goal of inspiring them!  In my view a very good example of storytelling is how Apple managers sell their new creations during  Apple’s Keynotes. They are able to connect emotions, characters and values of people that live that  product every day (see following video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tQSdE32O5KE). They  don’t only present a list of things but rather a connection of emotions and actions of what people can  do with their products.  Storytelling encompasses logics, emotional connection and a larger purpose. That’s why “The- Storytelling-Tool” is the ideal instrument to sell innovation in pitch and get the right people inspired.    App

Reflection Storytelling

(Nathan Kumar)

Context  I work for a government agency that promote a culture and holistic system of lifelong learning  through the pursuit of skills mastery, and strengthen the ecosystem of quality education and  training. The challenge is a lot of our initiatives and programmes are through an individual- targeted strategy (think B2C model) and we’re now developing a enterprise-targeted strategy  (think B2B model).    Challenge  I chose to use the tool storytelling to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space  among a diverse group of stakeholders who view the challenge of skills mastery from very  different starting points.     The first step I took was to define who are stakeholders are. Our stakeholders inside the  agency included the various departments such as the middle and back offices and critically  the policy owners who had to understand a new mode of engaging with enterprise. Whereas  our stakeholders outside the agency include the training providers, the educational institutes  and the individuals who now have to be viewed as employees instead of individuals.     The second step I took was to identify, articulate and define the ‘what is’ existing state of the  problem. I articulated 2 key points in my story: the emotional reason why we needed to have  employees pursue skills master and the larger purpose of workforce development. In the  context of a retail business owner, I painted a situation where we continued on our individual- targeted strategy (i.e. the individual learns e-commerce skills) but the employer is not in  support of training the staff as they believe in the traditional means of doing their work (i.e. via  a brick-and-mortar business model) and there’s conflict as the individual doesn’t feel motivated,  valued or supported to execute their job.     Selection  I chose to use the tool storytelling as it has the ability to connects the stakeholders to the  emotions, the characters, the values that we want

text:
Reflection Tiago Borges about Mind Mapping

Challenge    The challenge chosen was around and Onboarding process in an IT Company. The idea  was apply the design thinking tools to understand how the process happened and  improve the processes using the tools. Mind mapping is a great tool inside the Design  thinking and was used to understand the gaps that the process had and how was the  things that could be improved.   The case is that when an It company hired new employees to work as analysts for  different customers, there was no an onboarding process. That process was done  thought the project culture, generating a lot of none equalizes in the answers to the  end users.    Selection    I chose the mind mapping because we haven’t sure about the process like happened  that moment and We would need to understand how was the things that could be  improved. Using the ideas learned at the course, I started the exercise with 10  employees, mapping the process like happened.   After this, we had more 2 phases, to get the pain points and the improvement ideas. In  the end of the exercise, we used the periodization matrix to choice the best  improvement ideas.    Application    The application happened using one session, with 10 employees of the company,  working as managers (different level). We had 3 hours to run the 3 phases of the  exercise, covering the process, pain point and improvement ideas.   In the end of the processes, we had 15 steps of the process like was running, 23 pain  points and 15 improvement ideas. We chose 11 ideas as measure ideas to apply in the  process. Analyzing this numbers, I believe that the process was a success, effective.     Insight      When the exercise started, I think that all participants don’t know about the  simulation, the exercise and about the ways that Design Thinking can improve the  process. I had to show how the things would work.   The presentation of Design Thinking changed the mind of the participants and I believe  that.

When we are thinking of an idea, suppose,  we taste a specific food or visit a place, on that time our mind starts to link this action with  our old memories and previous experience using a relevant model. Our brain starts to think  with one centre action, colour, taste or image and builds branches of thoughts that are used as  a base for other multiplied ideas. Our thinking process is very similar to tree branches.   Basically, this concept is used as the basis for all Visualisation systems and approaches also.

We are especially blessed with this digital age where we are getting different visual input that

text:
Danielle West	 ‘Listening	for	improvement’

1. Challenge: describe your challenge, including all of the relevant

information

I work for a large healthcare organisation. I am in the role of Organisational  Development manager. My main responsibility at the moment is to design a  behavioural framework to support the launch of a new set of organisational values.  The output, (a new set of organisational values) has been decided by our board.  However, how I go about creating this has been left with me.  I believe that the Design-thinking process and tools will help to work through this  challenge in a way that the outcome will be more meaningful to all of our  stakeholders.    I believe this framework needed to encompass the expectations of our customers  (patients and their families) and our staff in order for it to be supportive of the cultural  transformation we are seeking.    I enlisted a small team of people from a range of disciplines to support me in this work.

2. Selection: In your own words briefly describe the tool you selected

(eg. What is it and why did you select it for your challenge – include  any appropriate video lecture references)

The Storytelling tool was the one that resonated strongly with me when considering  the challenge I was working on.     We have received a lot of feedback (complaints) from patients, describing that they  felt dehumanised in the care process that we provide and that they are an input to the  system, rather than a human being in need of care and support.  It seemed important that we understand the actual experiences of our patients, in their  words and through their eyes.    We also felt that it was important for staff to be able to share their experiences of  working in our organisation. I used a story-telling method (modified) for this part also.

Vinod Baker

Our Challenge

I work in an operational environment; the purpose of our business unit is to ensure the circulation  of money. Our staffs’ primary job is to handle the monies that is coming into the bank (deposits)  and the monies that is leaving the bank’s premises and transported to clients’ premises  (withdrawals). Dealing with clients’ money is an important job however quite stressful for our  staff. All our clients rely on our service offerings for them to continue with their business.

The staff morale and motivation is not at a desirable level for optimal productivity. Our challenge  is to change how our employees feel about working for this business unit. To create an  environment that employees find pleasant and a place that encourages growth and learning.  Furthermore, we want our staff to feel motivated and encouraged to improve how they work.  Having motivated and determined staff will have a positive implication on our productivity.  Therefore, as part of our People Program we need initiatives that assist in changing how our  people feel about their work. We also need initiatives that are cost efficient.

Our Selection

We started our design thinking journey by using multiple tools such as: interviews and personas  to understand why our employees came to work and how they felt at work. More importantly we  wanted to find out how we can make their lives better and what is important for them. Majority of  our people work an 8-hour shift, this means that they spend more time at work with colleagues  than they do with their families. Hence it is important that we improve this environment.

The team and I are now at a phase where we would like to test our hypothesis and assumption  by running small experiments and prototypes, learning launches. But it is important to give equal importance  to both physical and mental health which is lacking in the society.

So, I came up with an idea of mental health app with professionals like  psychologists, psychotherapists, counsellors. Along with professionals we also  include caregivers because they play an important role in the treatment  process. The app also includes personality tests, mood trackers, positive  quotes and many more features. Through the app we can reach out to large  group of people with 24/7 availability at their comfort level.

Challenge & Selection

In 2009 my friend Luca came to me wanting to launch a brand of clothes that spoke about Maranhão (a region of northeastern Brazil). However, historically, there were only two brands that did very well in .  has a facility of exporting lifestyle and fashion for being one of the main postcards of Brazil. In Maranhão, the clothes that were manufactured were usually destined for tourists and did not have a personality. They were just "souvenirs" of the city. Knowing this I talked with Luca and suggested the application of some techniques of Design Thinking. Initially, we needed to understand the problem from the point of view of our consumer (empathy), and for this we began to look at which brands our target public most liked to use and interact with them to delve into the motives that made them buy these products. We realized that our target audience looked a lot like us and we consumed the same brands from other locations in Brazil. Knowing this we already had an idea of  how to start to validate the idea by doing a benchmarking with these brands that we consumed.

Application

As the goal was to launch a brand that spoke of Maranhao, it was natural to start talking about how Maranhão came about, who we were colonized, what people invaded us, and what heritage these people left us. After a very deep research on the history of Maranhão, the ﬁrst collection of the brand with prints of some postcards of the state appeared in stylized form, taking as references the type of design of the brands that we used and put to sell. It was a success!!!

Insight & Approach

With this we discovered that people loved to wear clothes that showed pride in being from the region and still did not do it because they did not have a more fashionable option. Design Thinking Reflection: Storytelling

Challenge

In my organization, I am responsible for business development in the EMEA region, but apart from my  core role and responsibilities, I “wear many hats”, e.g. organize business conferences and events,  manage alliances and accounts, create collateral, etc. I work with clients, partners, internal teams,  external teams and various stakeholders, day in, day out and addressing diverse groups with different  goals, backgrounds, challenges, needs and wants has always been a known challenge, not only for me. I  needed to communicate more efficiently with different stakeholder groups, structure messages and key  takeaways better, create build up and align meeting participants, regardless if they are from Marketing  or IT, around a single vision of the problem we are trying to solve.

Selection

Unfortunately, I have limited opportunities under the circumstances of COVID-19 global pandemic and  lockdown to practice my new design thinking knowledge acquired during the course, however, luckily,  storytelling is a design tool I can practice every day on infinite Zoom meetings and it can be applied to  multiple contexts. Apart from the reason mentioned above, we learned from both Barry and  the Chief Learning Officer of Mars Inc. how storytelling is an important design tool and a tool that has  been increasingly leveraged in the business world as every product, service, solution and institution has a  story behind it. A good story in a nutshell is more than just conveying a message that has logic, it has a  larger emotional connection and purpose or i.e. it creates a cause that according to the CLO of Mars Inc.  “ignites people and unites people”. text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge      My name is Karen Gonzalez. I am ICT Director of a school in South Africa. Some fifteen years ago I co- wrote some software to manage the internal venue bookings at our school. Being a software  developer was and is still not part of my role at the school, but integrating technology into the  curriculum and empowering staff and children to become responsible and capable adults in a  technology rich world, certainly is. We developed the software because there was nothing  commercially available at that stage that suited our needs and pocket. Another reason was that, in  those early years, when we were trying to get staff to use technology to improve the learning and  teaching experience, we reasoned that giving teachers (and administrators) tools to do their daily jobs  would improve literacy and have positive educational spin offs. The software has lived on and is used  extensively by an increasing number of people and for more than the original, quite simplistic,  purpose. The software in function and form is very much end of life but the tool(s) is so interwoven in  the fabric of how we manage events, sports practices, and classroom activities that we simply can’t  manage without it for any time at all. The software is buggy and is written in a language that is no  longer supported. Our challenge is to seamlessly replace the software with something that will meet  the new needs of the school, without disrupting daily activities, on a very tight budget and at the  same time win the buy in of the various managers who will very likely need to change their process. REFLECTION - STORYTELLING

Challenge and selection

I teach at the Faculty of Engineering of the Pesto Pizza and one of the  challenges is to train future research students, as well as to develop the research skills of the students.  At the Beescoop a system of formative research was implemented  through three programs. The first program involves students from the first to the third cycle in which  research habits are developed. The second program involves from the 4th to the 7th cycle where  scientific thought is developed in the selected courses of the specialty. Finally, program III from the  8th to the 10th cycle in which contact and visibility of the research is achieved through the final  development of the research work and its publication in various congresses and academic events.

Storytelling or the creation of stories is a tool that connects from the beginning with the student and  inspires creativity and is one of the educational techniques that allows teachers and students to learn  and innovate. A story will impact differently on each student, as said in the previous paragraph at the  University we train student researchers through a system of formative research so that they through  creativity, research and the use of technologies can provide solutions to the problems of their  community. Many of these students to begin to develop their formative research work have to identify  a real problem and most of them begin with a question: what problem can I solve and investigate?  and this is where storytelling is applied to identify themselves and create meaning through a story,  inspire them to connect in the story, identify with the character, link the context by determining the  problems in their family or social environment and propose solutions using knowledge and applying  technologies.

rendered​ ​U.S.​ ​History​ ​curriculum​ ​and​ ​thus​ ​the​ ​skill-set​ ​to​ ​be​ ​successful.​ ​However,​ ​thinking

creativity​ ​and​ ​divergent​ ​thinking.

text:
John Yates Design Thinking for Innovation Carolina Chavez May 3, 2020

Reflection: The Mind Mapping Tool

1. Challenge

My consulting firm was tasked by our client, a health-care foundation board, to help them design an organizational strategy in light of all the rapidly moving developments in health-care. The board was at an impasse, uncertain on where to place its bets to best support health-care in this country without being able to predict where a number of current trends might lead. We used design thinking to present a few high-level, flexible, iterative, strategic options for the board that the foundation could pursue within the 2021-2024 time-frame.

2. Selection

This reflection will focus on the mind mapping tool, which was the most important phase of the project as it moved the process from the What Is? stage of ascertaining the current state of the organization and of health-care in the U.S., to the crucial What If? stage of beginning to draft new, possible realities for the foundation. This fulfilled the purpose of the board in hiring my firm.

I am defining mind mapping as the collective visualization by the board members of the sum of their knowledge, experiences, insights, interests, and visions of health-care, thereby establishing a snapshot or base upon which to build a series of possible strategic options for the foundation to pursue. As Lopez said in the Module 3 video:

“In the first phase of the design thinking process, we take a look at the current reality, at What Is? In doing so, we amass a huge amount of data. Before moving to the next phase, What If?, we need to distill all that data into information and insights that can be easily communicated. This is just what mind mapping does well.”

Following the completion of extensive health-care industry research and in-depth interviews with members of the board to collect data on the current reality in the What Is? stage of the design thinking approach, we started the mind mapping

text: Mauro Zizza, DESIGN THINKING ASSIGNMENT    DT for psychotherapy: The role of story telling    I am an engineer and I became an specialist in Machine Design and Design Methods. For  reasons out of the scope of this essay, I became a psychotherapist in several approaches,  one of them being existential therapy.     In some point last year, I realized that I operated sometimes in therapy under the scope of  design stages and thought of having a method based on that. This is not the method itself  but a reflection on the coincidences and how a DT is affected by the method itself and, if  seen correctly, it is also a healing process for some.    What is?    When I have a new client or a regular one, I alway ask: what do you want to work with? So  they begin telling me a story. At the first stages I use the phenomenological method to keep  asking what is? Just the data, no judgements -for now. Sometimes this is enough since the  person can change his/her story by clearing the facts and is able to separate his/her own  judgements or prejudices.     What if?    In a second stage we begin to explore what others would think. So first I ask: What do you  think I think about it? Some times they are very close and others not. So I continue to ask:  What if you see things like I do? Then we can ask: what do he/she/they think about our  session? What if you ask them? What if you propose/suggest/explore what you found out  today about yourself?    What wows?    A regular question to clients is: what are your options, your wishes, alternatives? text:
REFLECTION

VISUALIZATION

By Melissa Martinez

Challenge

I am a university student in the last semesters of Administration. Last semester I took a course on  Development of Creative Potential. Throughout this class we addressed different creativity  techniques and for the final evaluation we were asked to do a work as a team in which it was  necessary to design a creativity development program as if we were going to implement it in a real  company.

My team and I develop the points of the work and prepare it for a first review. Our teacher put  particular emphasis on that our projects looked 100% school-based and that we should make them  look professional, like a formal company would present a program in real life. My colleagues seemed  quite disoriented, they didn't know how to make our work look professional. I offered to do it and  tried to explain the idea to them.

Selection

I am not a professional nor do I have much experience in the business world of work. However, I am  a mostly visual person and I like to work with these elements.

As mentioned in the video conference that talks about this tool, visualization is quite important in  our way of communicating. By having to use the right side of our brain (often ignored) we can think  non-verbally and be more creative. That is why I chose this tool, because the impact that an element  has on our view is what will influence it to attract our attention or go unnoticed.

Application

The first thing I did was a quick evaluation of the job we had, it was pretty ugly and it didn't attract  attention at all. Right away, I myself visualized in my mind how I would like it to look and feel  professional, creative, and impactful.

Then I looked for graphic elements of all kinds to highlight my document and applied them:  headings, images, graphics and figures, color combination, letters, emphasis and distribution of the  text, etc. The result was amazing even for me, it was truly professional and eye-catching work.

Example Reflection-Mind Mapping

By Karina Duque

Challenge and Selection

Mindmapping is a tool I used in my office; however, I was not aware that I was specifically  applying it although with a limited approach. It came to me first by instinct. I mean, I gathered  with my four-member team and we used to brainstorm ideas purposefully to solve an issue.  I  work in an International Organization in the Environment field. I am responsible for the  financial and administrative monitoring of environment projects according to the  organization’s and donor’s rules and regulations. These projects have their management units,  we call them PMU. Sometimes we forget that in those PMU, real people are working. We don’t  see these people we only see financial and administrative processes and requests coming from  them. The challenge we face is that these processes are not smooth and do not represent our  vision of “impeccable administration”. Therefore, project’s targets are delayed due to paper  work, bureaucracy, errors and long time processing.

Application

After learning what mind mapping really is, I decided to get close to my PMU colleagues. I’ve  been generally “judging” what they do from my supervision role rather than having a more  empathetic approach. First, I organized monthly meetings with my team to motivate them to  be more people centered when providing a course of action. Then, we started to interview, to  talk to people. This time, we made it with a different approach, using the invitation to “the  garage sale” event. We offered this time questions: ¿What makes your daily work difficult?  ¿What would you need to improve the processes you send to our Unit? ¿ From 1 to 10, how  empowered do you feel in your position to deliver a high-quality work? What do you want to  share? Well, we got surprised discovering that many of the challenges they have come from a  poor understanding of the reasons behind a regulation. Challenge & Selection

As a manager in a global consulting firm focused on assisting companies manage their  global workforce, I interact daily with a multitude of stakeholders. These include client  HR Mobility professionals and expatriate employees, third party relocation and  immigration vendors, colleagues across 100+ countries, my own direct team as well as  our offshore compliance team. All of which with different perspectives and reality  leading to different inputs and expectations throughout the entire process.

Although moving employees abroad isn’t a new phenomenon, the globalization that  started in the early 90’s and the advancements in technology created opportunities for  companies of all sizes to venture into new markets, therefore increasing exponentially  the need for employee relocations in traditional and new locations. This brings me to the  challenge we faced – our 15 year-old system became outdated and inefficient despite a  few ad-hoc attempts over the years to fix it and integrate it. It was clear to me that the  conventional linear analysis would neither properly identify the underlying problems nor  arrive at a solution that would resolve it effectively and wow all of us.

I used the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to gain a deep understanding of the  current system’s capabilities and shortfalls and the possible solutions. I knew I needed a  compelling story to gain support at all levels of my organization and secure resources  and the team was key.

The initial phase consisted of reaching out to senior leadership and request the  nomination of potential candidates from the various business units and service lines.  These were all top performers with proven records, different background and expertise.

Lucas Medina

Application

In my town there is a small shop of many years to which we want to lend a hand.  The owner is Rob, a friendly guy who knows the whole town and likes talking to the  neighbors very much and it seems that they do too. He and two other employees run  the store where they sell many types of products. However, in recent years his sales  have fallen because new companies have arrived and Rob does not know how to  adapt to the new competition. Rob is a tough nut to crack to deal with changes. It has  too many products, many of them sell poorly because they are not current, but Rob  does not want to get rid of them. He says “they are slow selling, but people like it.”

Another problem that Rob has and why sales have fallen is when it comes to charging  because he stays talking to customers for a long time and slows down work, and  some customers who want a quick purchase become desperate. Plus, it’s so chaotic  and disorganized that a new customer always has to call an employee to find the  product he’s looking for.

In addition, Rob must be relocated, to speed up customer  charges.

We are currently faced with the challenge of shifting the way we do projects within our organization as we  stand up a new digital strategy. Some background information: we are one of the country’s largest energy  producers and have been going through a transformation over the past 5 years. Along with the downturn, our focus has shifted from production growth at any cost to a sustainability mindset.  We realize that we can be part of the solution as the world has turned its attention to reducing GHG emissions,  reducing our carbon footprint and becoming more aware of how the products we use daily are manufactured,  distributed and disposed of.

As the technology leaders for the company, we have recently combined business process management with  innovation and solution design to develop projects in a more responsible and planful manner. The challenge is really to shift how  our group approaches design and development right from the beginning of a project, rather than  fundamentally changing the activities of our experts – the what. It was important to successfully use the newly launched product to attract new customers as  well as ensure stickiness of existing customers. There was a national campaign around the same, but  since in India, as per a famous saying, the language changes every 100 KM, so to cater to this diversity,  we decided to come up with a communication plan very specific to the geographic scope of my unit in  Punjab state.

Visualization – Antonio Coppola

Challenge: Change Management on a proposed process change within the claims organization of a large  US based P&C insurer which will greatly modify how First Notice of Loss (FNOL) submissions are  processed. Change of process will introduce Robotic Process Automation (RPA) functionality and  significantly modify work content and responsibilities for Contact Center associates.

Selection: Selected Visualization, or visual thinking to create a shared understanding of the problem the  change of process was attempting to solve. The approach used leverages pictures to help visualize  painpoints and desired future state in a brainstorming format. The pictures are intended to evoke an  emotional response to real life issues, frustrations and ideals that the associates are feeling.

Application: I conducted several focus group sessions with customers to obtain Voice of the Customer  (VOC) and several focus groups with associates to obtain Voice of the Associate (VOA). The sessions  were held over several weeks to ensure we had a good representation of customers and associates. I  began the VOC sessions with a high-level process map to represent the customers experience as they  traveled along the process of filing an auto damage claim. I then asked the customers to select pictures  that best represented how they felt through the process. Pictures selected ranged from feelings of  frustration, fear, uncertainty, anger, etc.. which were not surprising. In most cases the claimant has just  been in a car accident, not saavy of the insurance process, and is flustered. Name: Gurwinder Singh

Challenge

I am hired as a change specialist of my organisation to change the existing silo culture into more  collaborative culture to increase customer satisfaction score by 30 percent . There are currently 5  teams with each has 9 members working on five different products that release features  to address  the rapid needs of customers during the COVID period. The existing culture is teams operate in a silo  manner and also product features are selected based on product owners knowledge that is  fragmented about the product and not customer driven.

Selection

As I do have digital product and agile cultural transformation experience and coached the team  members on Agile culture and Scrum framework of complex product development, I am going to try  learning launch tool to test the agile operating model of complex product development.

Application

For our learning launch, I focussed on implementing collaborative culture between three teams first  to ensure that team members can follow Agile Scrum framework in working together. All the three  teams share a common goal of working towards customer centric features identified through mind  mapping tool techniques. I setup a timeboxed, iterative and incremental culture for these teams and  every week, the individual team leaders share the lessons learnt and action required to further  improvement. In this way of experimentation, learning and action on continuous improvements  made the team working collaboratively towards a common goal. After two months of  experimentation, fine tuning and aligning all the team members to work collaboratively, then  implemented the same for the remaining three teams successfully.

text:
MIND MAPPING TO HELP A TRAINING COMPANY TRANSFORM THEIR BUSINESS MODEL

1. Challenge

I run my own marketing consultancy specializing in commercial acceleration. My clients are  large Life Sciences corporates. Exceptionally, a friend who owns a medium-size,  international training company asked me to help facilitate a process to define a new,  digitally-enabled business model for his company, including a roadmap on how to achieve  the end-to-end digital transformation of the business as soon as possible.

The high urgency is due to the coronavirus crisis. While the training company has a strong  proposition and a long, successful track record, it’s fairly ‘old-school’ in its content,  approach and methods; it relies almost entirely on large face-to-face classroom trainings to  get the job done for clients. This no longer works in the era of social distancing and remote  work and must be urgently evolved.

The expectation is to upgrade content, ways of working and customer experience using  technology with the overall goal of step-changing growth. This company not only wants to  survive the crisis but also thrive in the new post-covid19 reality. I will be working amidst  internal and external uncertainty, with a small team who worries about their current  situation and manages budgets tightly. I want to use the Design Thinking approach to  address the challenge. This paper will focus on how I will use MIND MAPPING to bridge the  path from What Is to What if.

2. Selection

I have used mind mapping formally and informally in the past but never as part of the  rigorous yet flexible process Design Thinking provides. In the context of Design Thinking  mind mapping is an incredibly powerful tool which allows its users to translate tons of  disparate data into meaningful, communicable insights which deliver criteria on which to  build innovation.

text:
Cristino Ramirez

29 May 2020

Challenge & Selection:

Our government customer was used to relying on proprietary data collection and analysis tools  specifically tailored for the government operating environment.  Over time, the government customer  realized that commercial solutions offerings existed that could provide highly accurate data analysis to  enhance their knowledge and awareness of their operating environment at a very affordable cost.   When compared to designing and acquiring their own proprietary system, the government customer  realized that our commercial solution could have the potential to enhance their capabilities, but were  interested in understanding how our data analysis system could be integrated into their normal daily  operations.

Selection:

I chose the “Learning Launch” tool for this customer, because it allowed our team to work very closely  and collaboratively with the customer in an environment that closely mimicked how the system would  be deployed if the project proved to be a viable prototype that should be scaled.

Application:   Since the customer was already a receiver of raw data from my company, we were able to  generate a high number of data sets over a 6-week period to include disconfirming data in our test  batches.  The cost of the “Learning Launch” was largely limited to labor costs associated with two of our  analysts and software engineers that supported the active contract with the customer for data  collection.  The individuals chosen to support the “Learning Launch” were very disciplined in their  approach, but also had a history of listening very well to customer and tailoring the response to best  meet the customer’s needs.  Since the nature of the project was leveraging real world data that  generated potentially hundreds of datasets daily, we were able to both develop fast feedback cycles and  present real world examples to our customer to garner their feedback.

Amritpal’s Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge  Being a member of my company’s innovation department, I was called along with my team for an urgent  meeting. Based on our latest monthly report, a big number of our newly employed engineers have  complained about an unpleasant and boring working environment; an unfortunate fact for a company  that relies on young and fresh minds to keep aiming forward. My challenge is to create an environment  in which our employees can perform and endure their daily challenges agreeably and more pleasantly.   The project scope includes our team’s department and the new employees of other departments, with a  limited period of thirty business days. We will focus on trying to uncover and pin point the effective  solutions with regard to a pleasant environment.

Selection  “When I want to do something analytical, I make a list. When I’m trying to do something creative, I make  a mind-map.” David Kelley-Founder, IDEO.  With the problem already in hand, I selected the Mind-Mapping tool at this stage of my design. I believe  it illustrates the minds of our employees to finally create a common mind amongst them regarding the  reality of our challenge.      Application  Mind Mapping is great way to brainstorm. In order to turn their ideas into reality, we had to collect data  from our employees.  My colleagues and I have prepared a reunion for all the concerned members of  the company; at first, we have demanded answers from each employee on a survey that tackled their  vision of a pleasant environment. The survey contained many types of questions, some were closed,  other were open and loaded questions that required a deeper thinking; for example: 1)Would you like a  cup of coffee every few hours? text:
Challenge

I think that all tools are important and have a lot of challenges, because everything in  the world it’s change all the time, then we have to towards this movement, through  studying, understanding the best way to do it. Also, I truly believe that companies begin  understanding that the quickly evolution is made for people, then we have to specialize  to understand the people, describe what they want? What they dream? What they  need? What can we do to be better for them? After these answers, we can offer right  solutions of them, that’s why I chose Visualization, because it’s a good way to know  these answers.    In my mind, it’s really simple to understand and accept that we have to focus in human,  in their life’s, their needs. This is the gap that we can work and increase value.

Select

For me, I would like to start my challenge with Visualization, because in my opinion when  we begin to analyze any problem, we have to break down the first barrier if exist, it’s to  get a start a good relationship with stakeholders and users (if are not the same person),  because these people give us all the information that we need, through your mindsets,  your feelings, your emotions, your behaviors, your life and your knowledge, but we have  to search other information’s to complete our job too.    In my career, I had opportunities to do this job to understand the people, using empathy,  but I always think that I can learn more how to do better that I know, that’s why I think  Visualization it’s a great way. Another thing is I think that Visualization tools provide to  show what we are talking, because we can use resources to materialize the  conversation, the understanding, search, even the stakeholders doesn’t know the right  way or what’s the real problem, and we can help them to do this. There is guy who works as a Talent acquisition professional in a multinational organization, his day to day  activity revolves around interacting with different level of professionals, He get involved into the process  of human resource starting from recruitment till separation. He regularly meets with different  stakeholders like hiring managers, head of departments, chief officers of my company also with the  representative of recruitment agencies.   But, why are we discussing about a day to day life of an employee, any clue?  Well, to answer your question this is the story of mine where I tried to show a glimpse of how my days  looks like any fine day. Meeting with various stakeholders require some data, bullets or facts to present  or to provide them update on day to day activities, SLA, projections, selections, forecasting and many  more data and figures. Using sTOYrytelling by Roberto Pink

http://www.frederick-curtis.net/posts/wp-content/categoryauthor.php

Challenge & Selection    The purpose of this challenge was to discuss how the communication between users and  developers influence the outcome of a process of developing a software. Specifically  contextualized from the agile development perspective the proposal was to discuss how  narrations of history could enhance and improve elicitation process requirements. So the idea  was to adopt the storytelling paradigm directing the focus of studies for application in  software engineering processes. The storytelling is closely linked to the development of  mankind, and use techniques and strategies they use narratives to capture the audience's  attention and lead to certain actions of subtle and natural way has become quite effective.

Application

These photos are bottom of the page, we were discussing how to innovate in products created  in technology companies, using design thinking. Was applied storytelling using toys,  participants rode on the scene and with it we can see that the focus should always be on  customers / users. Before the process within the company for software creation was  bureaucratic, we thought only within the time limit and agreed financial values. But now  processes have changed and customer satisfaction comes first.

Insight & Approach

It is often necessary to teach your client some things, from instructions on how to use products  or services, to strategies and best practices in the use of tools. Normally, manuals and step by  step guides are boring and too long to fulfill the role of teaching what is needed.

Use characters (who are also representing the consumers themselves) within a story is the  best way to teach something more absorbing content, illustrating situations and desired  solutions.

Every client has a history and it can be good enough to promote your product or service.  revolutionary ideas usually solve old problems.

text:
Reflections on Visualization

by Gonzalo Wong

Challenge: The Fuzzy Mess

I choose Visualization to see how it would help me resolve a problem in our support escalation process.

I had a bad experience escalating a service outage to the correct people at our company.  Several of my  peers who should have known about the outage were not made aware of the problem. We discovered  customers were not aware of the solution when it was put in place.  These breakdowns in  communication left me wondering where our process was broken and what we need to do to fix it.  I  gathered our team to walk through the process and experiences of different people to see if we could  identify the source of the communication breakdown.

Selection: Helping Others See the Same Challenge

I chose to draw out the events that revealed the problem in a visualization.  The visual representation of the communication flow overcame the complexity of the issue and the likelihood of confusion in our  conversation.  How could I keep the group on the same place as we reviewed the escalation events was  the challenge.  Because visualization supports congruent understanding I thought it would help keep  the group together as we reviewed the escalation process.

Application: Draw, Discuss, Repeat

I drew a representation of each of events in the escalation sequence as it was reviewed and discussed.  Once all the events were in the visualization the team was able to reflect on places where things went  wrong.  This led to proposed fixes being added to the visual. We were able to keep the discussion  focused by reference to parts of the process in the visualization.

Insight: Point of View

The use of visualization helped the entire team see the problems in the process from a number of  perspectives at the same time.  The discussion was focused. We were able to jump to new topics  quickly by pointing a place in the visualization.  The team stayed with the different aspects of the  conversation quickly.

Final Assignment by Anna Russo

Challenge

I am an HRBP & OD Manager at a desalination and water treatment  organization. we are spread over 5 different geographies. Within my  responsibilities are the complete training and development of our ~450  employees worldwide. Organizational development holds many different areas.  For this assignment I focused on the managers development program, which I  build based on my own agenda, OD trends that I collect, and statements  regarding performance from managers in our routine meetings, or from the  performance management review process.

Managers Development programs usually try to gather the employees and not  only teach them techniques but to become a group of associates, that opens  about managerial issues and dilemmas. In the current state that gathering is  banned creating a 6 meetings program seems unreal.

Selection

I decided to try a learning launch. with all the data I collected, after my team  gathered and thought together what our possibilities are, I decided to try a first  session for our Team Leaders that will be on-line and will try to achieve our  managers development goals.

Application

I set a date and scheduled the meeting. Found a sales and marketing manager  to share a case study regarding decision making. We built the presentation  together by colliding the theoretical background with the actual way decisions are  made in my company. Exploring our GO-NO-GO procedure.

Instead of a serious of meetings I built just the learning launch. Tried to set  specific slides for queries so that people will not be silent during this session and  they will have to participate.

Challenge

I was working for a Consulting Firm and was on an assignment/project to reduce operational costs from  an IT Infrastructure department. The client Infrastructure had many aspects like Power Distribution, Cooling, Disaster Recovery, Test and  Production Environment, Virtual / Cloud Appliances etc. that were contributing in a large carbon foot  print of the data center.  The steering committee were more concerned about the Production  Environment as it supported 21 Airline Companies’ Reservation Systems across Europe and Asia and for  them their customer impact could cause a huge loss in credibility and market share.

Example Reflection: Visualization.

Challenge and selection.

The first tool I used was the visualization of other team members, because it was

necessary to understand the needs of the people and have a common idea, and then I

was able to start planning possible solutions to the problems that could arise in the

development of the event.

The scope and limitations are other aspects that we want to develop, what kind of people

we will attract and how many people we can improve, so that people feel more

comfortable than when they compete.

Application.

Initially, the brainstorming process began, and then the information and information

gathered by customers' employees was used to create charts and sketches of the

company's new organization. This is very useful because customers are part of the

change, they allow us to improve and they warn us of the reasons for the failure of our

company.

We chose to add a template to this method to divide the customer's suppliers in order to

incorporate detailed company information so that we can work more efficiently.

Insight and Approach

What I have learned from this knowledge is to broaden my horizons and to be able to

see more clearly. Many tools that I think are temporarily not essential, but, on the

contrary, are essential for the correct development of thought. Sharing ideas is a good

way to create a unified environment, as other team members have the confidence to

participate and can analyze the data together to reach an agreement and specify the

most appropriate conditions for the company.

Ever since I discovered the visualization tool, I have realized that it cannot open its eyes,

but concentrates on daily work. Visualization allows us to open our minds to understand

the needs of those around us, so that we can use it to provide services that can benefit

them.

text:
REFLECTION – LEARNING LAUNCH    Abdo Cortes

January 9, 2021   UNIVERSITY OF VIRGINIA – DARDEN SCHOOL OF BUSINESS

Challenge:

I founded a watch company in the Philippines a few years back with the aim of becoming the first Filipino- owned watch company that assembled its timepieces locally.  Being a physicist and a technical watch  enthusiast, I wanted to plant the seeds on developing watchmaking in the Philippines.  So, without having  any business background, I decided to conduct a Learning Launch to test my idea through an experiment.   With the gap in my business acumen, I was fortunate enough to come across a book called The Physics of  Business Growth which happened to be written by Tom Garza and Rosa Cortes.  By coming  up with an analogy of putting up a business or an idea through the scientific method, I was able to grasp  the process.  The analogy was very helpful.

At the very beginning, the main task was to decide on the kind timepiece that will be launched as a test.  The test would be to test the brand’s name recall and retention, targeted market acceptance, and, of  course, sales.

Selection:

I gathered three of my friends who were from different industries to join me in developing the initial  model and asked them for their insights.  Apart from this, I also held a separate brainstorming session  with my lead technician.  I believed that through the product ideation, we had a good product to test.

Application:

During our learning launch, we focused on the creation of the brand and in properly sending out the  message about us and the product that we launched.  Given the limited financial resources we had then,  we decided to launch a high-quality basic dress timepiece as it aligns with the brand’s image.  We launched  the timepiece in a boutique hotel’s restaurant and invited friends from the press and some showbiz  personalities.  We wanted to get feedback through different streams so that we can properly address  possible points for improvement

Mind Mapping

By: Charlotte Jones

Challenge and Selection

At the National School of Arts and Crafts Casablanca, I am a member of the EAP Student Committee. The Student Advisory Board assists the Business School with improving the student  experience by providing a student perspective on issues facing academics, communication, and  career development opportunities. To better understand the student population’s wants and needs  we conducted a large in-depth interview at the Business School. All 15 board members,  including myself, each interviewed 10 business students with a range of grade levels and  degrees. We covered the main focuses of the admission process, academics, career preparation,  and overall communication.

Once we completed the interviews we were left with a massive amount of information.

Our challenge became decoding patterns in the data to discover where to focus our efforts. The  challenge promoted our selection of the Mind Mapping Tool. Mind Mapping is a term used for  the process of discovering patterns within the information you collected during the beginning of  exploration or the ‘What is?’ phase. As noted in the Mind Mapping Video, with Wendy Lopez,  mind mapping is a visual process of capturing the perspectives of customers, or students in this  scenario. The tool guides the team through a process of laying out all of your information,  observing trends, and noting clusters. The Mind Mapping process is a way for the student board  to narrow down issues for consideration.

the interviews. On giant sticky notes, we all creatively wrote down the things that are working  and the things that are not working, based on conversations with students. DARDEN BUSINESS SCHOOL – COURSERA

OFF-GRID REFRIGERATION CHALLENGE IN ABUJA-NIGERIA

Habibu George

Abuja, October 30, 2016

CONTENTS

1. CHALLENGE; Market penetration  ……………………………………………  3

2. TOOL SELECTED; Learning Launches …………………………………..........  3

3. APPLICATION and INSIGHTS ……………………………………………………..  3

4. APPROACH  ………………………………………………………………..….. ..  4

CHALLENGE; Market penetration

Power is a significant challenge in Nigeria. In about two decades this nation has expended  over twenty billion U.S. Dollars yet our total power output is about Five thousand  megawatts. This is a country with a population of about a hundred and seventy million  people occupying about a million square kilometres of land. Many people need power to  run their fridges, freezers, air conditioning etc but this lack of it created a challenge and an  opportunity. So we set up a factory to produce blocks of ice that we could provide the  people in our state to use in meeting some of their refrigeration needs. Because of the  burning nature of the need and huge population we believed this would be a no brainer  and would hit the market in a huge wave. This did not happen. As a matter of fact, we  struggled to make sales of 20 blocks a day from a 1000 block a day factory. This was not  sustainable and we had to take significant action and fast if were not going to shelve the  business.    This way we would get hard facts on why the market was reacting with such poor reception  to a product that was designed (as we thought) to meet an ardent refrigeration need.

TOOL SELECTED; Learning Launches

Lucky for us I had this challenge in mind while taking the course and it seemed sensible  to use the learning launches. This would keep is in the market experimenting to get to the  truth we required to take a decision on our current business and or, model. The whole idea  was that we would get the true market feel and information we would use. From the videos  Estela Perez

text:
Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge

I am a member of the organization’s product development team. We are a multinational company from  the textile industry, and our challenge is to grow the sales of our line products. P&D works closely with  the Sales team, which brings us the feedback from our B2B customers, with our Trade Marketing  department, which brings us the feedback and information from the market, and the industrial  development team at the industrial plant.    The company spent a few months in a process of mind set and cultural change, when the employees  were trained in agile methodologies, to use them as new tools for the developments of the new product  process, and also solve problems in which the company has found difficulty.

Selection    After the training our team has already followed up with some parts of the "What Is" (Journey  Mapping, Value Chain Analysis), and now we have reached the stage of Mind Mapping, which is why I  choose this tool for reflection.    Application    First, we chose a large room in the office. Then we paste all the data that we collected during the  previous phases on the walls. We gathered a group of twenty people from the areas of sales, trade  marketing, product development and industrial, so they could look at it. Gradually everyone made  observations, and we followed the processes of insights formation and clustered the data so we could  proceed with brainstorming.    Insight    After the use of mind mapping, we could perceive a series of links and patterns among the interviewees,  and in this way, it was possible to observe some problems and feelings of the consumers that we didn’t  know before. Because of this process it was possible to reach the stage of brainstorming much more  prepared to develop a solution that fits the consumer better and adds more financial value to the  company. Linda Moore REFLECTION – VISUALIZATION

CHALLENGE

While working for my previous employer, a large defense contractor offering products and services from undersea  to outer space, I managed all tradeshow and sponsorship activity for a sector headquartered in Herndon, Virginia.  Before I arrived, each business unit was managing their own pool of funds, deciding which shows and sponsorships  in which to participate/contribute and there was no overall structure as to the total sector spend. Decisions were  being made with no regard to sector priorities, large contract bids or future bid considerations. Additionally, there  was no alignment on any of the branding and marketing material, and more than once different business units  from the same sector were appearing at trade shows, without knowledge the other was participating. There was  an immediate need to align the funds under one umbrella and to develop a unified approach to spend, messaging  and participation at tradeshows and with sponsorships.

SELECTION

For this exercise, I opted to apply the design thinking tool of visualization to first uncover the issue at hand. To help  with our fight to align the budget under one umbrella (managed by me), I first needed to shine a light on just how  many unnecessary (from a business perspective) trade shows the business units were attending, how much in  sponsorship money was being dispersed, as well as the total sector spend in these areas. as part of the peer-review section of the Design Thinking For Innovation course offered by University of Virginia.

CROWDSOURCING A CHURCH FUNDRAISING ACTIVITY

1. Challenge:

I am leading the youth community at my church, and I proposed we hold a fundraising activity to raise funds to  support the education of a few students from the underprivileged society nearby. The proceeds were to go towards  helping the children with new uniforms, getting them school supplies (like a school bag, notebooks, textbooks,  stationery, etc) and paying their tuition fees.    The church members are used to donating money for church-associated charity organizations, reconstruction and  remodelling of the church, construction of new projects, tithe and several other avenues. They sometimes feel that  the youth does not have their priorities in the right place, and so, the adults are not likely to want to invest time and  money into a youth-led programme, regardless of the value it provides and to who.

2. Selection & Application:

Several design thinking tools like Visualization, Story Telling, Mind Mapping and Learning Launch came into play –  albeit in a mixed blend.    Surveys & Data Gathering  I spoke to the students I intended to help, to understand what it is they need the most and stands in the way of their  education. I spoke to the church leaders to understand who the major donors were and what kind of causes they  tended to contribute to. I interviewed several donors to understand what attracts them to want to donate to a cause,  and how that experience could be improved. I spoke to the school the children attended, to NGOs and to social  workers, to understand the school’s fee structure and how much it would cost to sponsor a child for a month. Design Thinking Tool

Learning Launch

Challenge:

I’m Patrick, from Port Said, Egypt. I work with a charitable  foundation (Life Makers Foundation). Last year we had an annual  objective to empower 100 in need families with 100 micro  enterprises, to make them able to gain their own money rather  than keep getting money from people/donors.    To achieve this objective, our strategy was to raise money through  a one-month street/public fundraising campaign. The challenge  we’ve faced included both: 1) how to attract people to donate, 2)  where to locate our donations booths. In other words, as we had  some limited resources (volunteers, booths, budget, etc..), we  wanted to figure out how to raise money with the most effective  and efficient way.     Selection:

The selected tool is Learning Launch as we wanted to examine our  hypotheses in the real world and to get field data in which we can  rely on during our campaigns. Learning Launch is the tenth design  thinking tool, it allows us to make an affordable experiment to test  the impact of a new solution on the customers. The purpose of  Learning Launch is to get a truthful set of data and insights that  either confirm or disconfirm our assumptions, which lead to either  continue developing your idea or pivot/eliminate your idea.

Application:

Port Said city is divided into five districts, so we placed a donations  booth in the hottest spot of each district all day long, to test where  are the best places to raise money from, in addition to determining  what time of the day is better to talk to people at. The second thing  we did was collecting information and insights about the potential  donors’ behavior when we talk to them about our foundation and  its objectives and strategies    Insights:

Therefore, I had to convince people in my college that it was a good idea and I would gain their

companies and college management.

When it comes to affecting and influencing people under your organization, in my opinion, there is no

better choice then storytelling. I have a story to tell them about why the existing societies are not as

good as they should be, and there is no society that would excel students’ soft skills. If you want to

create, you need to create. You cannot just listen to people who create and then become a creator

yourself. This idea led to turn my thoughts to a story then to tell people. Some say storytelling have

four P’s: People, Place, Plot, and Purpose. Therefore, I chose storytelling to be able to show these

aspects.

Application

Before assembling people together for the board of this society, I have took them one by one and spoke

privately with each. Emotional branding is the key point in here for society and I have tried that. Each

individual was from different disciplines, because this society is a multidisciplinary one. Hence, I aimed

for their needs and how this society can have benefits for their faculty as well. Apart from that, our

collaborative companies had their needs as well. After all, it must be a win-win relationship and I told

our story according to that. I explained the benefits of cooperation with telling stories. People had to

chance to show empathy with this storytelling applications and were all eager to participate in it.

Insight

text:
Giuseppe Alberti – Design thinking for innovation

Challenge

I’m a professional photographer, based in Brazil, and weddings are my

main niche. Through this course I’ve learned some tools and methods, and now

I’m able to put in practice some ideas that lived in my mind for the last year.

As I talk to my clients, I hear some frequent problems that brides go

through, when planning their weddings – things that go from finding the right

professionals to the way that a ceremony must happen.

Selection/Application/Insight/Approach

Based on that, my idea was to develop a course, so that the brides can be

more prepared to the problems that appear during a wedding plan.

And here enters the design thinking: I’ve interviewed some brides, being

or not my clients, to have a deeper understand of the issues that they go and

gone by.

Focusing on the problems of them, I’ve learned about the core pain they

face, and confirmed my assumption, that the course will solve some serious

problems. I will now proceed and test ways to do. If it becomes necessary,

pivoting and looking for alternative paths to solve the problems I hear about so

often.

I’m already using the knowledge acquired in the course classes.

text:
USING MIND MAPPING TO UNCOVER CLIENT INSIGHTS

CHALLENGE The big challenge in my project is extracting the most signiﬁcant insights from the important quantity of information gathered from  quantitative research and qualitative consumer interviews. These insights will be used both to structure our offers to clients and prioritize mass  communication messaging in a new market.

SELECTION I chose to use mind mapping to help us develop a common understanding of the challenge and agree on the most signiﬁcant insights.

APPLICATION We invited 20 stakeholders in the project to a full-day session. In the ﬁrst part of the session, participants were invited to visit our  « gallery ». All the information, quotes, statistics, pictures from consumer homes, were put up on the walls. The room was covered in information  (picture 1).

Participants captured on post-it notes the information that felt most signiﬁcant to them as they wandered throughout the room.

We then divided participants in teams of 4 and asked them to share the information they had found signiﬁcant to ﬁnd overarching themes (picture  2). We asked them to look for patterns in the information they had collected but also to be mindful of anything that stood out as being particularly  different. Their overarching themes were noted and developed on large ﬂip charts (picture 3).

In the second part of the session, each team presented its themes to all the participants for discussion and comparison. We were then able to ﬁnd a  common understanding of the « So whats? » and start working together on the design conditions as the project moves forward.

Regina Parker — November 2016

INSIGHT Most participants in the Mind Mapping exercise never truly experience our destination as our clients do. Their visits are carefully orchestrated and mapped-out.  Mind Mapping was truly enlightening for them as an occasion to understand the client experience without the ﬁlter of a report or analysis.  Mind Mapping opened many  eyes.

Isabel Pardal

Challenge       I work in a multinational pharma as an intern of talent acquisition area and one of my biggest challenge is to develop  our Internship Program to attract young talents for our opportunities. The project of developing a complex program  like this, involves many target internal areas in the company like Communication, Marketing, Talent Management and  Human Resources. So, to think about what we are going to promote for the students in the market, all of these parts  for the insights and decision-making must be involved. There is also a consulter supporting us in this project by  promoting and doing the recruitment and selection of the internship vacancies that show up in our company.  For the Internship Program´s development we have to study and decide some very essential points: Target public (who  we want to attract), market competition, visibility and attractiveness, benefits, design and content shown on the hot  site.      Selection      Thinking about the challenge of involving different areas for structuring the project, Mind mapping was chosen as a  Design Thinking tool, in this case. Mind mapping is a highly effective way of getting information in and out of our brain  and it is a creative and logical means of note-taking and note-making that literally "maps out" the ideas. In addition,  this tool of Design Thinking can be used for all the levels in a company with the goal to establish criteria for the what- if idea generation phase.    The use of the Mind Map allows a strategic view of all the processes and interconnected points of something, because  it is a visual tool, allowing the generation of more structured insights. TOOL:  Visualization

Diego Campo

Challenge & Selection

I work as a bodywork quality engineer at an automobile assembly company. The factory where I  work has a low percentage of automation and the welding processes are manual by operators.  Because of this there are many quality problems associated with poor welding application. We have  resorted to all kinds of strategies to find root causes, we have changed machines, installed aids in  the stalls and nothing worked. At that time, we realized that we were not really understanding the  needs of welders for them to apply welding well. They also did not understand the reasons why we  made so many changes in the factory, there was no effective communication. At that time, we  decided to use the visualization tool. As we saw in the first week of the course, this tool allows us to  activate different areas of the brain to understand information differently.

Application

To better understand the difficulties and problems of the operators, we decided to create  personalized meeting spaces. We formed groups of 4 workers together with 2 engineers from our  quality problem solving team. The first step in the meetings was to ensure that we all understood  the quality defects that we had in the same way, for this we used visual tools such as photos of the  defects, videos showing incorrectly applied welding beads and some cartoons that showed the basic  rules to follow. The second step in the meeting was the opposite situation, now the operators taught  us visually in the workplaces the difficulties they had in doing their job well, each worker went to  his post, carried out the operation and taught us his problems so that together we could find a  solution. Eman Rahaman Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection     Coming from an English Literature background putting things into a story seems second nature  to me. Storytelling is one of those things about humans that makes us drawn to one another and  feeds into our curiosity.   I work in a media agency with numerous diverse clients that all belong in different industries,  and i’m challenged constantly when tapping into the client’s mentality and making sure that our  creative content stays relevant to the brand’s guidelines and still maintains a creative standard.     Application    Working in an agency that has client fluidity has multiple creative challenges, you are faced with  numerous creative blocks having to steer from one client to another. However, applying the  storytelling tool clears away a lot of confusion in the sense that it narrows your creative thinking  into a smaller scale, not by limiting the possibilities, but by focusing on what makes every client  unique by centering on its key points.   For example, one of our clients is a tongue scraping product that wanted a campaign to raise  more awareness into the products’ sales. First thing I suggested was to know more about the  product itself and all of it’s characteristics, what makes it stand out? Why isn't it selling? Who is  it targeted to? Basically create an entire character list customized for that product.   The more we knew about the product and who they wanted to target the easier it was for us to  cultivate a campaign suited for it. Design Thinking for Innovation (Jan – Feb 2018)  Final Assignment - Learning Launch     Submitted by Jyoti Ward – 2 February 2018    1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

My company has in invested in Microsoft Office 365 – a suite of software services and apps to aid  collaboration, document access and productivity. Whilst adoption is gradually increasing, our staff  are not yet taking full advantage of these tools (and so not harnessing savings and benefits to the  company). Some people are relying on ways of creating and sharing documents that they have  become familiar with over many years, but which don’t have the benefits new functionality offers –  e.g. they will email a document to colleagues rather than collaborate online through the enterprise  social network, Yammer.

We want to foster a mindset and skills base across our workforce where the digital tools offered  by O365 are routinely used, providing demonstrable benefits to the way people work.

Using a ‘design thinking’ approach, we carried out some ‘skills insight interviews’ in November.  Assisted by a group of around 15 Office365 (O365) champions (individuals who have taken on a  role to support colleagues in the use of the Microsoft Office 365 suite) we sought to understand  what’s holding people back. We have used these insights to formulate hypotheses that we can  test. This covers the ‘What is?’ and ‘What if?’ steps described in the Design Thinking for  Innovation course.

The next step is to test some of the ideas we generated using experimentation. The ‘Learning  Launch’ tool provides the means to do this in a practical setting with real end-users. This will allow  us to test whether the action taken meets our requirements: namely to increase the skills and  capability of end users in using O365.

The present-day society outwardly overemphasizes and  overplays Filipinos’ resilient trait. The very same resiliency is the one conjuring up the dismissal  of risks in an advent of another insignificant event. text: Carlos Pereira: Reflection on Mind Mapping    Challenge:  My problem was related to the high incidence of clinical depression in a nursing  home. This situation came to me through a request for help from one of the  health professionals, a nurse, from the institution; referring to the high number  of polymedicated patients, both for chronic conditions, with cardiovascular,  metabolic and respiratory disease, as well as medication aimed at mental health  – causing high financial and personal costs for the elderly.    Selection:  My first thought was to apply "What is?" to clarify the situation, trying to find the  real problem, or cause, for depression in this group of elderly people.  In this way, I carried out a set of interviews (ethnographic research) in an  attempt to understand what these people felt, what their days were like, what  problems they perceived, what they liked to see improved in their lives.  Given the above, I chose to use the Mind Mapping technique, in order to  gather all relevant feelings and perceptions, so I can gain insight knowledge  from what was really keeping those people from being happy and have better  quality of life.    Application:  In order to carry out the proposal to use the Mind Mapping technique, several  visits were made during 1 month, in order to be able to speak with all the  residents of the home, as well as with the providers.  During these visits, the problems of both parties were heard, which was felt and  perceived by patients as problematic and subject to improvement (subjective);  as well as evaluation feedback from home providers (objective).  We were able to notice that the absence of playful moments as well as limited  family visits in the post-COVID-19 era; accentuated by dissatisfaction with the  food in the canteen, were a problem for these elderly people. text:
Wilma Dekker – Design Thinking for Business Innovation    February 5 2017

Reflection – Visualisation      Challenge  In my work as a leadership consultant, my team and I help companies that need change but don’t know  how to lead it; the journey into the unknown. I work for clients and their high-educated young professionals  in the professional services sector; i.e. consultants, lawyers, accountants, sales professionals and  marketeers. They are often not used to be asked what could be the ‘what if situation’, they are more likely to  be conditioned to know the ‘right’ answer.     Selection  I was working for a client, a big consultancy agency and I coached a young woman; let’s call her Alice. She  and the rest of her peers got the order from management to set goals for the year and the goals had to  contribute to a more business development focused office. I was asked to help each of them. Alice had a  hard time in knowing how she wanted to grow in the coming year, develop goals accordingly, and make  them business aligned. I choose to help her with using the Visualisation tool (module 1 video 6). I first  helped her set the ‘what is situation’ and than help her through the ‘What if situation”. Finding your own  person in goals to set is very important for intrinsic motivation reasons; people that set goals that align with  them personal are more likely to succeed.

Alice  Alice is around 28 years old, pretty, a smart woman and we sat down in the conference room for  her first meeting with me, she got me some water and we got started. She asked if this  conversation was confidential and I told her yes. Than she talked for 20 straight minutes about  what she didn’t wanted this year, what she hated about her job, it felt like she really needed this to  get of her chest. She told me that she was tired. We really established the ‘What is situation’ at that  point. Getting into the ‘What if situation’ was harder for her. That’s where I used the visualisation.

Juan Bakker Group - Confidential

Peer-graded Assignment: Reflection – Visualization    Challenge and selection.    One of the tools I have used in problem solving/idea generation is the tool of visualization or visual  thinking, to understand a research problem and areas to work on before attempting to come up with  different solutions to the problem. In order to design the solution, first we must build a good  understanding of the problem that we are trying to solve. Visualization tool helps to build connections  between different findings and understand the bigger picture. I have used the technique of using a  research wall to display all the relevant research outputs, in one place. The visual aspect of the wall  triggers idea generation and enables project members to better understand research insights.    Application    I start the process by creating a graphic of the problem domain. To develop the graphic, I will draw from  any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing material may be existing  research data, manufacturing methods, market data and/or customer feedback.     For the activity, I will divide the researchers into groups of 2-3 participants each specialized in a different  area of study, such as chemistry, engineering and biology. Each group receives a copy of the graphic of  the problem domain that they can write on directly. They will get following questions to answer,

1. What are the customer pains and weaknesses of the existing problem?  2. What are the improvements you would make to eliminate existing pains and weaknesses?

Each group gets 30 minutes to discuss and answer the questions on the graphic. Then each group gets to  display their answers on a white board which helps to identify the commonalities of different solutions.
