our daily life follows a sequence like we will visualize it first and then we will frame it into a

structure.  By using mind mapping we can divide the entire session into sub divisions like main

branches and then to sub branches. So I have selected mind mapping as a tool to my challenge

because I can remember it forever by creating a branch like structure in my mind and then

recollect and retrieve it whenever required.

Application: I have applied it by dividing the main components and sub systems in the engine.

How the power transmission takes place and how to identify them through some visual effects

like drawing a flow chart and dividing into sub systems and then remembering. I have started

creating a flowchart or a cycle in my mind through different variations like how the flow takes

place and are there any alternative ways to that.

Insights: It helped me to think more creative and out of the box. It helped me to create some

short cuts in a clear cut way. One can even find out the solutions using mind mapping because I

can identify the bottlenecks in the process due to which I was unable to say the process and

Reflection "Mind Mapping"

Challenge & Selection

One of my favorite tools is Mind Mapping. Generally, I use it when I feel that  we have collected a lot of different data from different stakeholders:  customers, partners, participants and so on. For me, Mind Mapping is a sort  of the bridge between what is and what if  phase: we use it when we are  eager to begin generating ideas.     I’m a Product Designer for a consulting company so I use this tool often with  my clients while exploring different opportunities to innovate within their  company. I love this tool because it lets a lot of place to the imagination and  helps participants to understand the context of the customers lives instead  of seeing only business context.

Application

I start this exercise by laying all the data we have collected for everybody to  see it: for example, the good idea is to use a big light room. Visualize this  information helps to display the key components of what we have learned  during what is phase. Then, I invite different people and seat them at small

teams. I try to select very different people for this exercises. The only criteria is  to take curious and open-minded people, who are really interesting in what  you are doing.     Once everybody arrived, I distribute paper, stickers, markers, and  whiteboards to teams and explain the exercise. The important thing to do  here is to explain that they are here to help us to move forward and that  there are no good or wrong answers. Sometimes, I ask them to take off their  jackets and ties because it helps to put everyone on the same level and to be  more open-minded while working together.     Then, I ask everybody to make a tour of the room. Sometimes, I can give  them some additional explications about the information they can see. We believe that all kids are naturally creative and that every classroom should be filled with  creativity and wonder.

We want to see teachers unleash the creative potential in all of their students so that kids can  be makers, designers, artists, and engineers.

We know that school can be busy. Materials can be scarce. The creative process can seem  confusing, especially when you have a tight curriculum map. So creativity becomes a side  project, an enrichment activity you get to when you have time for it. But the thing is, there’s  never enough time.

We can do better.

We believe that creative thinking is as vital as math or reading or writing. There’s power in  problem-solving and experimenting and taking things from questions to ideas to authentic  products that you launch to the world. Something happens in students when they define  themselves as makers and inventors and creators.

That’s the power of design thinking. It provides a flexible framework for creative work. It’s  used in engineering, publishing, business, the humanities, in non-profit and community work.  And yes, it can be used in education! You can use it in every subject with every age group.  Although there are many versions of the design thinking model, we have developed the  LAUNCH Cycle as a student-friendly way to engage in design thinking.

We believe all students deserve the opportunity to be their best creative selves, both in and out  of school. We believe all kids are unique, authentic, and destined to be original.

Most importantly, we believe this is not an all-encompassing solution, but a start. We believe  our role is to empower kids to make an impact on the world around them and fully believe in  themselves.

The  project is limited to internal resources (i.e., budget and employee time). The project  should not exceed 25 business days and the solution should include an even distribution  of working hours amongst the team members. We will focus on trying to uncover what  our team members, as well as key stakeholders within the larger marketing department  and IT department, consider to be ineffective or problematic with regard to the workflow.

Since I am an event designer-visualizer, I think the “visualization” tool will be  corresponding.

To sell visuals to customers, you need to convey the atmosphere and idea in an

understandable and better visual way.

What are the problems with this?

1.  Time

2.  Explanation of the technical part. Advantages and disadvantages.

3.  Budget

Selection

It is all about the chain. The chain of the work process and the way it usually goes:

•  Breaking down RFP,

•  Strategy,

•  Creative idea,

•  Sketching,

•  Mood boards,

•  Layout,

•  3D modeling,

•  Rendering,

•  Post – work

1. Time. In this chain, you cannot remove any phase and save

time. Since everything is interconnected with each other. By removing at

least one chain, can disrupt the smooth transition from idea to

the final visualization and lose more time.

The time problem is that assigned to this complete chain.

2. Technical. We must explain to the client that this beautiful picture will be

executed one-to-one. How? Technical document. The technical part has its

own chain, and when the client changes something there, the domino

effect is triggered. Not only in the technical part, but in the whole initial

idea. But why a client change something in the technical document or in

the whole chain? Budget.

3. For instance, we strengthened the structure with metal supports, and when

the client reduces a budget, we have to reduce the weight of all the

structure and strengthen it with wood instead of metal.

(visuals) and reduce time. Since this saves a lot of time, you can return without

changing the entire chain, but just ask the right question.

text:
Visualization

Challenge

When I worked as a Management Consultant in my previous Job, I faced the recurring  challenge of being exposed to very complex situations. In one case we were brought in  because a company wanted to optimize their output of one production line. The Problem  was that they could not oversee the complex connection of the variating production times  in their value stream. They buried themselves in data and could not ﬁnd an solution.

Selection

For me the selection of a tool was very clear. Since there was no way to see through the  complexity of the situation simply by accumulation data in a spreadsheet the decision was  made to use visualization to gain understanding of the challenge. Visualization would help  us to one the one hand to create a workﬂow which allowed to oversee process as a whole  and on the other hand to create something that the involved people could actually touch  and feel. This would reduce the overall complexity tremendously because all the people  involved hat a common understanding of the status quo without any room for  interpretations and misunderstandings. Just as Angela Meyer described in the video  „Visualization tool“ in week 1 mapping out the process would help us commonly  understand the situation.

Application

When we started we can to crawl our way through data to initially gain understanding of  how the pieces ﬁt together. Given the available software nowadays to create visualization  we ﬁrst thought we could utilize them for presenting a set and done visual map of how  thing where going right now and how things could actually work. Having prepared such a  map on the computer we approached the meeting and presented our work. A few minutes  into the presentation I realized our fully prepared visual map would confuse the  participants just as much as the data in a spreadsheet. text: Visualizations are one of the important parts of the job.  We see the result of our work in our pictures. There are  many advantages to this tool. It shows what should  turn out, and it will be easier for people who work with  you to understand what we want to receive. The second  important plus is that visualization shows all your  mistakes in work. That you are allowed to correct your  mistakes.  But there are also disadvantages to this tool. There are  good visualizations and there are bad ones. Such  visualizations do not convey the naturalness that exists.  Such work will clearly differ from implementation.  And the second less important disadvantage is that  visualization takes up most of the time from work. To  achieve the best result, you need to sit for many hours.  For me, visualization is an important part of my job. It  is very closely related to my future profession. It is  partly one of the important tools.

text:
Reflection – MIND MAPPING

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of MIND MAPPING to achieve a shared understanding of a problem  space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define possible  solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers, who are government  agencies working to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their  services to their customer, which may be INDIAN citizens, businesses, and non-citizens. I have used  the technique of using a straw man MIND MAPPING of a problem domain with a set of questions or  prompts for discussion to allow a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the  process of defining the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to  consider when identifying pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.

Application

I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw  man graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The  existing material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing  materials or other auditing reports. If materials are not available, then I conduct informal interviews  with one-three of the stakeholders who serve as my main points of contact on the initiative. If  appropriate to the situation, I will borrow the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from previous  research, The front-stage/back-stage approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service –  even an internal service – has customers with whom the service provider interacts and internal  processes that enable the organization to provide the service. text:
MIND MAPPING

INTRODUCTION:

Mind mapping is a way to link key concepts in an organized manner to a specific central  concept using branches lines and links. It describes the concept in a way creative way and  helps in better understanding the idea behind the concept instead of paragraphs.

CHALLENGE:

The challenge in Mind Mapping is compiling and segregating all relevant information and  deciding key points and their position. The mind map created must be clean and  understandable, so simple key words needs to be added.

SELECTION:

Mind mapping describes the concept in a way creative way and helps in better  understanding the idea behind the concept instead of paragraphs, this improves the minds  capacity to remember and apply these concepts and ideas easily. The colours added will  help organize the idea better and there will be a clarified explanation for people who need a  quick review or insight of the concept.

APPLICATIONS:

Mind Mapping has various applications, it is colourful so it is captivating and helps us  remember concepts easily. It is organized to a central idea and gives you a quick refresh on  what the whole concept is about with just a few key words. Mind mapping helps you create  new connections between ideas that may be not visible in paragraph format.

The few things a mind map should contain are:

1.Central Idea

2.Branches

3.Keywords

4.Colurs

APPROACH and INSIGHT:

Mind Mapping should be neat with as less words as possible with more creativity and  organization. Make it more colourful so that the one who looks gets a quick grasp or what  you are trying to convey.

I will make my mind maps more colourful and add clean key points that describe the  whole idea.

text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I work with minors at risk who come from Africa to Spain in search of work, they have no  resources and are mistreated by society as there is the bad concept that they come to hurt and  not in search of opportunities, or out of need to survive already because in their countries of  origin they cannot subsist. I spend most of my time advising minors so that they can find a job  and a proper future. I teach them Spanish ,Catalan, Math and English, I think that the more are  the best qualified and skilled labor will find opportunities and be better prepared to enter into  the labor market. Many times we exchange knowledge and most children know many trades  such as carpentry or crafts that most young Spaniards do not know, together we share stories  that make me realize the great inequality that these young people have, and the luck we have  those who we live in a developed country, where we have many options and facilities that for  them mean a lot of effort to achieve.

I often use their stories to show that their knowledge is very valuable and that if they have  been able to learn a trade, they have the ability to train today and fight for a future, as they  are winners and have a lot of merit.

Application

VISUALIZATION

Challenge and selection

I work in the central office of the institutional training department of non-profit NGO

whose purpose is to promote personal responsibility and social awareness in order to achieve  a model of a just, equal and sustainable society. We have branches in fifty countries on six  continents, with very different cultures and socio-economic conditions. Some branches have  been up and running for over fifty years, and others have been opened only recently. The  central office is responsible for creating products that are regularly distributed national offices,  and for providing annual training sessions for national managers. Each local office has its own  teachers and adapts the contents they receive to local needs.

Some countries have small offices with a maximum or one or two people who are

responsible for promoting institutional training. This training is given to managers, employees  and also to volunteers who collaborate in the different initiatives that the institution promotes  to fulfill its mission. This formation needs to be up to date, in order to effectively face the  challenges presented in the social environment. These challenges concern not only concrete  issues that need to be faced, but also effective communication with different types of   audiences.

Data has been collected, in personal interviews, with the people in charge of offices in

the smaller countries, to better understand their difficulties and their training needs. The  trainers of these smaller locations are convinced and highly motivated regarding the value of  their role. Learning Launch    by Melvin Alfaro

Challenge and Selection

In the last time I used the Learning Launch tool to determine the essential aspects of a problem in  the area of construction and recovery of waste generated by this industry in my country Chile and  to be able to define and identify possible solutions. I am a member of a modular construction  product development team and for this we carried out a project in order to generate a new  construction system. We will carry out a market analysis, execute it for a period of 90 days, and we  will work on the solution based on the necessary technical background and the experience that  the team has with the implementation of the Uniblocksystem construction system. We focus on  discovering the necessary technical characteristics so that the work team has a basis to start  organizing marketing, production, distribution and sales plans in a collaborative way, encouraging  a continuous work flow to avoid obstacles in the development and launch of the new product to  market.

Our team has worked on accompanying activities with a construction engineering faculty of one of  the most prestigious universities in our country, which added to the experience of the team has  been able to achieve an understanding of the learning launch tool. Reflection – Mind mapping

Challenge

I work in a company as a sales manager, which is responsible for manufacturing  and marketing computers with the following characteristics: a 1.5 Ghz processor,  512 MB RAM, a 20 GB hard drive, and an internet connection of at least 256 Kbps  which until a few months ago fulfilled the needs of the clients' clients, but with the  great offer of this product in the market, a sales deficit has been identified in the  company; In the first months it was not relevant, but little by little it has increased  significantly, this has forced the company to rethink staff cuts, leaving many  families without support, for this reason it is essential to create a strategic plan to  solve this problem and increase sales ensuring the economic stability of the  company and therefore of the owners and employees.

Selection

To solve this problem, mind maps will be used, which are a fundamental tool when  generating ideas, it helps to translate data into information that can be easily  communicated, it is also used to give solutions in an ingenious and creative way.  With this tool we try to look for patterns and perceptions to find what the reality of  the problem is, it aims to generate hypothetical ideas of what is coming; The mind  map is the alternative to a report written with graphs and spreadsheets, this is a  didactic, creative, intuitive and eye-catching summary of everything that report  should have.

Application

For the application of the mental map regarding the solution of this problem  referred to, studies were first carried out to analyze what may be the cause of the  decrease in sales by surveying our customers in which questions such as: What  can we do? do to improve our product? Why do you prefer to buy other brands?  What has been your experience with our products? To which the general response  was obtained that our products did not fully meet the needs of customers, since  other companies sold computers with better features.

Reflection - Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I work for a large company. We have offices in 10 different countries and hundreds of

workers. I am in charge of the development of the tool most of them use for work every

day.

As you may imagine, communication in an environment with so many different people,

languages and different cultural backgrounds is not easy.  We had  problems before

developing the tool in the right direction because of misunderstandings between the

different offices and us, or even between the developers and me.

I decided to try Storytelling as a way to improve the communication. Storytelling would

help everyone understand each other, being more empathic, and bring context at every

stage of communication.

Application

Briefly, my work consist in talking to the countries, gathering their problems and needs,

then, communicating these to developers that will build tools for them.

I used storytelling in 2 different ways:

When I talk to the local offices:

Before, they used to tell me: “Hey Felice, next to the car information, we need a button

that sends an email to the previous owner.”

Now, I ask them more questions, and force them to build a story. They will go for

something like: “When the worker finish the inspection of a car and save the report, he

usually goes to the list. Then he needs to send an email to the previous owner of the car to

confirm the transaction.”

When I define the task for the team of developers:

Before, I will just communicate: “We need a new button next to the car information that

sends an email to the previous owner.”

Now, I will explain the entire story to the developers. We will go through the task together

and, usually, we find better solutions. E.g. In the previous case, one of the developers

proposed to automate the email delivery, as it always needed to happen.

In this case, storytelling improved the communication, brought more context and made

everyone understand each other’s needs.

text: Sign-in experiments – Learning Launch      Challenge  I am the owner of a mobile application which is a free application and has features which  can work without login and also some features which require login. Even though a lot of  features in the App can work without login (sign-in) but we still wanted to get users logged  in into our App. My challenge was to get maximum number of users signed in into the App  but without impacting the App’s play store ratings. After getting users signed in, there’s a lot  product management can do by tracking the users behaviors and interests. We had about a  period of 3 months to come up with the best optimal of way of driving sign-ins. The intent  was to present user with the Sign in screen on App launch itself but which design and which  behavior would work the best was still unknown.      Selection  Since we were doing sign in on launch for the first time and also we had to keep the App  ratings also intact, learning launch via experiments became an obvious choice for us. The  learning launch is an experiment meant to quickly test and prototype.      Application  We came up with different variants of the Sign in screen – mandatory sign-in, optional sign- in, optional sign-in with a more subtle cancel option and variants of all these with and  without social sign in options. Over a period of 3 months, we rolled out each experiment for  about a week to funnel the path users are taking till they eventually sign in and to see how  many sign in success and failures are there. Also, which type of sign in options users are  using the most – corporate login, Google login or Facebook login.     Each of these experiments were run in exclusion to get clear idea about which variant  results in maximum success. App rating was another factor. text:
Mind Mapping

Challenge >>

Mind Mapping is a great tool that I used many times in my daily life. In some or  the other ways I talk with many people. Everyone is filled with a Unique  Mindset. So each time I’m supposed to talk to a completely new person. It’s  delightful to know how a person thinks. Also, It’s challenging to deal with their  mindset. At some aspects it’s confusing to know a person at the very instant.  So, I start  up with some warm welcome to break the ice and head towards a  steady deep conversation. This makes the Client feel safe. Now, the best part is  Mapping Client Minds. The great thing about mind mapping is that you can put  your ideas down in any order, as soon as they pop into your head. You are not  constrained by thinking in order. Simply, throw out any and all ideas, then  worry about reorganizing them later.

Application >>

Using a mind map allows Subject Matter Experts or your audience to make  cross references. It can easily function as an instrument for collaboration  during a kick-off meeting. It’s also an excellent tool for free writing while  brainstorming ideas. Whether you’re categorizing ideas, or simply negotiating  the big topics with a Subject Matter Expert, mind mapping provides an easy  platform to classify ideas and move them around. Some mind mapping tools  even offer the ability to embed notes, links, attachments, images and even  connect multiple mind-maps within a single map, making it a one stop-shop for  collaboration. This tool is a visual representation during a project kick-off  meeting or the front end analysis phase. Gathering requirements, negotiating  broad ideas and transforming them into learning objectives become smoother  with this tool. It means making sense of how ideas, content, concepts and  objectives fit together. It also provides a platform to prioritize workflows or  procedures that need focus. Example Reflection – Visualization

Challenge:

I am a Third-year engineering student at a renowned university in India. I have always found out that  expressing my ideas and methodologies to my teachers just through vocal communication is very  difficult and many a time this happened that some of my ideas started getting rejected, but a similar  idea from one of my classmates was appreciated. I started feeling that I lacked speaking skills or maybe  had some issue with interacting with my teachers. But that wasn't the case! I already had received so  many prizes in debates, literature competitions and was a good orator. Then I thought why not find out  what was so special in that classmate of mine who was always successful in this. I understood that more  than the information, efficiently conveying them and to make others easily understand the thing was  the trick!

Selection:

The lack of creative content in my delivery of the thoughts made me try out the visualization design tool.  I felt that there couldn't be anything more apt than practically implementing this in everyday life. As I  selected visualization as my design thinking tool slowly and steadily, I started getting the positive results.

Application:

I tried making impressive PPTs, some project prototypes, drawings, 3D models, illustrations and much  more to explain my ideas to the class. It turned out that I was pretty good at making designs. Slowly I got  a hold on the aesthetics and started excelling in it. The second semester had just begun and as expected  the class teacher had asked us for a topic and idea for the semester project. I took 3 days to research  and finally came on a conclusion to do a project on "Hand gesture recognition for the deaf people." Challenge

I work in the education sector in my country and recently we had been  experiencing challenges in the online learning programs. This challenges include  access to internet by students who come from a less than average family, for  example some parents do not have smart phones to access online platforms,  others have the smart phones but cannot afford to purchase bundles every day to  facilitate the students learning, some have more than one child hence online  learning becomes difficult when the students are many and the phone is only one  in the family. Another challenge was lack of textbooks. This is because textbooks  are very expensive to purchase especially if you have more than one child and  none of them is in the same grade. There also lacked a connection between  teachers and their students making it difficult for the teachers to follow up on the  progress of their students.

Selection

I selected a learning launch which is a carefully designed experiment or prototype  designed to test the key underlying value-generating assumptions of a potential  new-growth initiative. It is a learning experiment conducted quickly and  inexpensively to gather market-driven data to determine whether a growth idea  has enough merit to warrant detailed investigation with the commitment of  further time, people and resources. I came up with a solution of an application  and I needed a quick and cheap way of testing it against my assumptions that it  would work so as to qualify or disqualify my assumptions.

I first came up with the idea of an application that would be accessible to all via  USSD, SMS, smartphones, tablets or laptops. Reflection –Visualization

Challenge & Selection

Visualization is a tool that I commonly use as it provides a variety of  benefits for both individual and collective problem solving.

As a strategy consultant, I often work with senior management that are  very numbers-driven and place emphasis on macro-economic factors such  as interest rates and overall market developments. Using visualization has  two key benefits with regards to this target group. First, it enables me to  empathize with the managers and display very complex insights with visual  tools such as charts, processes, driver trees etc. which enables them to  absorb a lot of information in short time which is crucial given their packed  schedules.

The second benefit, where I would like to focus on, is the ability of using  visualization to spur the creativity of senior executives and develop creative  solutions together.  Very often, the focus on macro trends and numbers  does not cater for the volatility in today's business. Nowadays, a deep  understanding of customers' needs and an effectual logic is more important  than data-driven analysis. Using visualization cultivates using the right side  of the brain and allows the managers to empathize and truly understand  hidden customer needs and develop tangible solutions for the existing  problems.

Application

Usually, I start the process by drawing the current customer journey of the  problem domain. In order to lay out the customer journey, I will combine  ethnographic research methods such as observation and ethnographic  interviews with secondary research sources such as our consulting firm- internal knowledge and insights from the client. Reflection: Storytelling

Challenge & Selection:

Being able to present and persuade why a company, business unit or joint venture needs to be  merged or acquired is of paramount importance and sometimes it goes beyond the financial returns  this investment opportunity may offer. My line of work – mergers and acquisitions – strongly depend  on our competency to present what makes an opportunity unique. In today’s environment where  there is an excess of companies and start-ups looking for investors, there is a myriad of opportunities  of where to grow and/or place financial resources in.

Storytelling is critical to maintain the attention of different stakeholders. When I work with buyers,  you have to be able to present and persuade sellers to transact with clients. Same when I work with  sellers. In addition to the much-needed ability to be able to persuade, equally important is the ability  to listen to others stories so we can thoroughly understand their motives and incentives to transact  (or not). Active listening turns out to be equally powerful as we are able later on to weed-out those  buyers or sellers who are mostly looking to gain access to privileged information and lack the right  priorities when starting a transaction process.

Application:

When we are engaged to sell a business, the first thing we typically do is spend a great deal of time  brainstorming what makes this opportunity unique and special. We reflect on the company’s value  proposition, their place in the industry and its competitive landscape, we think about how strong the  management team is vis-à-vis others, and also make sure we identify -early on- the key investment  opportunities or traits for every business. The project is limited to internal  resources (i.e., budget and employee time). The project should not exceed 30 business days  and the solution should include an even distribution of working hours amongst the team  members. We will focus on trying to uncover what our team members, as well as key  stakeholders within the larger marketing department and IT department, consider to be  ineffective or problematic with regard to the workflow.     Selection     Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools, so we are ready to  try the learning launch tool. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment meant to  quickly test an idea and prototype. Design Thinking for innovation Assignment - Reﬂection

Nothing in the world is heavier than an   empty heart.

( S p e n d  s o m e  t i m e  w i t h  t h e  e l d e r l y . )

Challenge: How to engage the elderly in a way that ensures they feel productive & not lonely?

Loneliness is a killer. This is even more true for the elderly who are living alone. It  not only leads to frustration but is a root cause of spiralling mental as well as  physical health issues. The elderly, retired from their days jobs often “feel  useless” because society offers very few avenues to engage them thoughtfully /  meaningfully. Naturally they love their kids and grandkids, but their interaction  with the family is often reduced to occasional phone calls or video calls. They see  their grandkid’s growing up from a distance and cannot wait for that once a year  trip that will bring their whole family under one roof. The elderly have a whole lot  of knowledge, wisdom and pure affection to offer. The ideal way to engage them  is productively, so that it doesn’t seem like charity or sympathy but rather a  reinforcement of their dignity and self belief. In a social construct that has already  determined a “retirement age” irrespective of the individual capabilities (mental &  physical) of person, this is a tricky challenge.

Challenge

Visualization is one of the powerful tool which allows us to think in a non verbal way. Anywhere it is not  specified that while explaining something to someone it’s necessary to draw some emojis or cliparts.  Visualization through visual imagery has been an effective way to communicate both abstract and concrete ideas since  the dawn of humanity. Data visualization is the graphical representation of information and data. By using visual  elements like charts, graphs, and maps, data visualization tools provide an accessible way to see and understand  trends, outliers, and patterns in data. At first this might go tough but if practice is done it goes smoothly.

Selection

There are various tools that can be utilized for drawing the images, charts, digraphs, etc. As we had studied  in 1st Week about visualization technique it seems that it helps bringing ideas to life. We’re thinking about  possibilities that we haven’t yet seen. At first I was explaining to develop online food home delivery services  to my aunt and ms.Manuela (Aunt’s friend). Initially, they were not being able to analyze the things as per my  perspective and opinion. This eventually dawned me and only miscommunication was happening.

Application

There are lots and lots of things happening around us. Gradually, we learn everyday. But just learning is not  the overall achievement. Whatever we have learned we must apply it somewhere. So, I decided to re- introduce my topic to Manuela and my aunt. But this time I introduced a small clip that contained some  characters and a story based upon my topic. The story include the start of our project, what can we do in  that, what will be the benefits of it, and all the effects that will happen if we provide an online services. Visualization

Challenge and Selection

I am a content developer in which I develop study materials for kids from class 5th to 12th.  Basically, the final product is a type of an animated video where I am the narrator and the  videos are based on the script that I write. I joined the company few months back and I was not  experienced in the teaching field. Following the process of script writing to the final video was  a tough job. So, the process is that, after I write the script, I have a conversation with the editors  of my company who makes the video. Earlier I had a hard time in making them understand  verbally what I want in my final video. Finally, visualization tool came to the rescue. This tool  helps me in conveying my needs to the editors very easily. I have used various flowcharts,  diagrammatic representation, basically a 2D form of the video.

Application

Once I was having a conversation with my editor regarding a video to be made about  digestive system. I made him understand the script that I wrote and the stepwise output that I  desire. He said that he understood but somehow, I was feeling that he didn’t. Well, I waited  for the final video. Next day I saw the video and it was not at all understandable, there was no  link between concepts and I myself had hard time in understanding the concept which was  taught by me only. Then I thought that there is some communication gap between me and my  editors because the editors where all skilled up and they did exactly what was told to them.  This process continued for many videos and I was not satisfied with any of them. Even the  feedbacks from the kids for these published videos were bad. text:
VISUALIZATION

Effective people used visualization tools to imagine their desired outcomes for years.

The exercise has also produced high performers who seem to be super power to help develop a dream  life by completing one target or mission in a hyper-focused and confidential manner.

We all do have this tremendous strength, but most of us were never taught to use it effectively.

Elite sportsmen use it. This is used by the super-rich. And peak performers are now using it in all fields.  That is what visualization is called.

The daily practice of visualizing your dreams as already complete can quickly speed up your  achievement.

Four important advantages are provided with visualisation techniques to focus on your objectives and  wishes.

1.) It activates your creative subconscious that begins creative ideas for your purpose.

2.) It enables the brain to perceive and recognize more easily the resources that are necessary to  achieve your dreams.

3.) It activates the law of attraction and draws people , resources, and circumstances into your life in  order to reach your goals.

4.) It strengthens the drive internally to take the appropriate steps to achieve your dreams.

Visualize with the ‘Mental Rehearsal’ Technique:

Creating goal shots

A further powerful technique of visualization is to create a photo or picture of yourself as if it was

finished already. If one of your goals is to have a new car, bring a picture of yourself behind the wheel of  your dream car down to your local car dealer. If you wish to visit Paris, find a picture or poster of the  Eiffel Tower and take an image of yourself.

Create a Visual Picture and an Affirmation for Each Goal

We advise you to find or to make an impression of every aspect of your dream life. Build an image or a  view for every target – economy, job, leisure, new skills and potential, what you want to buy, etc.

text: Challenge & Selection     Youssef Schneider, who has muscular discomfort, is one of the biggest fans of Trabzonspor. His  biggest dream was to score a goal for Trabzonspor one day. I wanted to realize Youssef's dreams  to show how 5G technology will remove the limits. In order to introduce such technology, I  wanted to make a little kid's dreams come true. Then I planned all our work and infrastructure  accordingly.    Application    For this, I used storytelling tool which I believe is the most appropriate one for this case. I  used VR glasses and microphones so that Youssef can direct the football player instantly. Youssef  instantly saw the camera attached to the football player and directed him and scored his dream  goal. Thus, I realized Youssef's dream of scoring beautiful goals like Trabzonspor players, one of  his biggest dreams.   Before the 3 December Disabled Day, all work was done in the Trabzonspor training field,  preparations were completed. Thanks to 5G technology, Youssef saw the field with VR glasses  at a delay rate of only 1-10 milliseconds through Sörloth's eyes, and he scored Erce Kardeşler  with the commands he gave!    Insight & Approach    Beginning from the moment it was released, my ad film got supported by every football club  and their fans alongside Trabzonspor. On TV and digital we reached 10,3 million people in  total, with 689 thousand impressions and 2,5 million views. Our #PeopleHaveNoBoundaries  hashtag became TT on Twitter and shared for 3.6 thousand times.  Turkey’s most prominent  TV channels, 19 newspapers and 144 news sites announced Youssef’s goal on their news  broadcasts. What I might do differently next time is that I would plan my mind mapping in a  more specific way. But I am sure I’d use storytelling tool again.

Challenge

Agriculture is the backbone of India and in my country India it provides more than 65% of its  GDP. Even though this is quite impressive but, the Farmers on the ground level behind this  still live in below poverty conditions. This is because lack information on where to get market  for their products, they lack information on market prices they must depend on exploitative  middlemen who take advantage of their ignorance. There is also a long distribution  consist  of middle level chain that dilutes their revenue.

Selection

Working with some farmers have gone  through several design thinking activities to come up with a go-to-market prototype learning launch  tool for our challenge. This tool will help us go through an iterating process that will improve on our  solution. Working with the prototype will help us experiment the idea with a larger group of farmers.

Application

we focused on providing a mobile application that runs on a smartphone, with  incredible features like image capture, chat and location. This is to ensure we capture quality  information about farm products farmers would like to sell. Our focus was to observe how farmers  interact with the mobile platform. text:
Selfcare Application Learning Launch

Challenge  I work as a software development manager at a telecommunications company which is seeking  to go beyond its traditional services, such as voice calls and value-added services. To establish  this vision, the company created a new division, called Digital, aimed at creating new digital  revenue streams. This division then started a series of design thinking activities that resulted in  several promising ideas. One of these ideas, for which I was in charge, was to transform our  Selfcare mobile application into a SuperApp that would enable our users to enjoy digital services  as well. These services could range from e-governmental (such as utility bill and toll payment) to  e-tourism (such as ticket and hotel reservation) and even entertainment (such as watching live  TV channels). Our ultimate goal was to provides almost every service that the users need. In this  way, the users could use our application for most of their day to day activities, and the company  could establish new digital revenue streams it envisioned. However, around 30% of the  company’s revenue was generated through traditional services sold on the Selfcare application,  and we needed to ensure that introducing digital services will not detract current loyal users.

Selection  To overcome this challenge, we used Learning Launch tool because we had no idea how  customers would react to this huge transformation, and we needed validated insight. In other  words, we needed a way to measure the enthusiasm of our users towards new digital services,  and which services in particular they are interested in, if any. In this way, we expected to prevent  huge investments in a new application that might fail, prevent detraction of current loyal users,  and delivering an application that our users will fall in love with. This experiment had to be done  quickly and with limited budget spending.

Challenge & Selection

The main instrument I utilized was the method of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to accomplish a mutual comprehension of an issue among a different gathering of partners before striving to recognize and characterize potential answers for the issue. Through visual thinking, we can visualise the problem which opens up all the possible challenges that we can discuss to find out the solution. In this technique, we draw a picture and write down all the possibilities in a pictorial way to make the discussion easier. This methodology has been admired and used regularly by the government offices attempting to apply innovation advancements to modernize the passage of their administrations to their client, which might be U.S. residents, organizations, and non-residents.

To start the process, we create a picture of the problem domain. We draw the picture from any existing material available to understand the environment. The picture drawn is simple and made by using simple shapes & icons available on the internet. The existing material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, GAO or other auditing reports. Visualisation

Challenge and Selection

The tool that I chose to apply is the tool of visualization to showcase to my members the possible  implications of their decisions regarding the outcome of the project. I often use this method to show the  possible project outcomes a few terms later so that my members, especially those in the executive  committee will be able to make more informed decisions, since their decisions can greatly influence the  way the project will move in. Most of the time, I use the technique of a timeline with different humans  in it, and attach a set of conditions and trade-offs with each decision that can be made along the way.  This has helped us identify and understand the entire project from a big picture and consider the  opportunity cost of certain decisions that may only be clear later in the project.

Application

The way that I carry out the visualization tool is as such:

I often gather the executive committee into a room, and get them to project their desired project  outcome. Once they have an image of how they would like to project to turn out, they will be required  to classify them into the following time frames: 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or towards the end of the  project, depending on which one comes earlier first. This helps us break the daunting project into  smaller and more manageable steps for us to plan solutions for it.

From then, we will zoom into the particular details of the project, and that is when we will use the  technique of timeline with different images of human interactions in them. For instance, when we  decide to adopt project A with an external vendor, we would like to consider the flow 1 year from now,  especially the best case and worst case scenarios. Reflection on visualization

Challenge and selection

I get the help of the tool of visualization and visual thinking because it is the easiest and the  way that I am mostly talented in. I can get a shared and diverse idea of stakeholders and it  helps me to plan it overall. I usually use this on customers who are in an interest of developing  a software for their companies to make it efficient and so that they can provide their services  too using these programs. I use strawman technique for the questions that I ask from them  prior to start of the software development process which is the requirement gathering process.  Helps me to define the scope, boundaries relationship between the entities and the key  elements.

Application

Usually start the process with a straw man graphic of the problem domain. Ill draw from the  requirements which the client provides. The materials are voice records, use case scenarios, various  documentations of the requirements, and user stories. Plus the interviews.

If needed I might have to use various approaches like “front-stage/back-stage” and etc. The template I  often start with also has a column on the left to identify Partners and Value Chain Providers and a  column on the right to identify requirements, such as , the things what the client need in order to get  this project a success. So that I can map the users and what they want from this system to be developed.  Also I will have a column which specifies the propriety level of the requirement. So that I can inform the  developers what requirements are most crucial in the system. The straw man graphic is simple, using  simple shapes and icons available in Visio or on the Internet. If the front-stage/back-stage view doesn’t  work, then I will create a different type of visual, either based on a high-level process flow with swim  lanes for different stakeholders, or another format for example (Activity diagram with swim lanes).

Design Thinking for Innovation - Week 5  Peer Graded Assignment

Tool that applied: Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a powerful tool that are applicable in various situation of our daily life, ergo it is the tool  that I applied all the times. As a marketers of a shampoo company, I always faced the challenges of  how to attract more customers to try and fall in love with our new launched products. Besides, I also  faced challenges of how to ensure the phenomena of decreasing brand loyalty towards our products  being happened as there are variety of choices for customers to choose in the markets nowadays.

I choose to apply storytelling as it is able to get insight into users, build empathy and reach them  emotionally. I often create personas to represent target users and add conflict to stories that reflect  their user journeys and problems. One of the reason is through crafting stories, we can better  understand what users want from a solution. Good stories always captivate audiences. In user  experience (UX) design, if designers use storytelling throughout the design process to ensure that all  work focuses on the users’ needs and the value that company want to give those users. After  completing design research to understand your users’ needs and desires, you use your insights to tell  a story about who your users are, what they need and how you’ll provide that. This story makes it  easy for everyone involved in the project to empathize with the users and ensure that their work  matches the story. Having a story throughout your project means marketing the design at the end of  the design process is also straightforward, as you already know exactly which story to tell to show  how your product provides value.

text:
Reflection - Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

The shopping center has information desks where administrators work. Administrators help customers  find their way to the desired store, help if someone is lost, answer incoming phone calls, and answer  other questions from visitors to the shopping center.

Objective: to improve service at information desks.

At the start of the project, the following problems existed:

• Information desk staff are overwhelmed with work, unable to answer calls and questions from suitable  visitors.

• Employees do not pay due attention to visitors and respond formally. Lack of well-trained voice and  empathy. The staff don't smile.

To solve the problem, a design thinking approach was required, since problems could not be solved in  obvious ways, such as increasing wages, introducing financial motivation, expanding the staff.

To solve the problem, a mind-map tool was chosen based on in-depth interviews with line employees of  the shopping center, top managers, middle managers, as well as visitors to the shopping center.  Drawing up a mind-map will allow you to calculate the main pains that employees of different levels and  visitors of the shopping center are talking about and collect insights on the main sections.

https://www.coursera.org/learn/uva-darden-design-thinking-innovation/lecture/lsFRa/mind-mapping- tool

Application

Interviews of visitors and interviews of employees were analyzed separately, then a mind map of visitors  and employees were compiled. Then the team of experts analyzed both maps and made a general mind  map, forming a number of insights based on it.

This design thinking tool was really effective as it helped:

• Organize information by dividing it into main blocks

• Find points of contact of opinion of buyers and employees, as well as points of contact of opinion of  employees of top and line positions

• Highlight the main and additional insights, the implementation of which is important for the success

Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I was working with an organic farm in Pondicherry, South India. The farm uses permaculture methods  and follows the teachings of the great Japanese farmer and philosopher Masanobu Fukuoka. They were  trying to make a direct impact on the people lives around and the visitors of the farm.  The farm  primarily targeted in two things. The first was to make people understand the value of local food and  the second was the practice of organic farming with permaculture methods. But the communication  materials created to meet these requirements were highly philosophical and technical because the farm  wants to have a philosophical bond with the target audience.  Unfortunately, this storytelling model  created a huge communication gap between the farm and the audience.  The working class couldn’t  resonate themselves with these stories.  Ignorance about the permaculture farming models and direct  impact on the consumers were really big issues.  Thus the need for a better storytelling was realized.

Application

After deconstructing the ideas to be conveyed, I decided to construct stories which will touch the  audience in a personal level. I asked the farmer about the positive changes he experienced during  farming. From the conversation, I made few codes (variables) which common man will also be able to  relate.  Few of them were:  happiness, abundance, honoring mother Earth, back to nature. Then I  decided to create stories with these elements as a centric theme and then connecting it to  permaculture. The first video story featured the farmer explaining how the farm made him happy! He  used the term Happy multiple times in the video. Journey mapping tool was used to create the agenda as per the largest number of similar wishes and  usefulness. We wanted to enhance the agenda through inclusiveness of empathy to connect better.

The targeted groups for this meeting are mostly engineering employees with different levels of technical  expertise and their managers. Challenge

During this pandemic, and the consequential lockdown has resulted in kids doing online schooling. It  was fun in start, but soon we realized that this is not the best way for kids to study, not at least now.   There are pros and cons, but without the proper transition to the online education as norm, both kids  and parents and teachers did not know how to cope with it. One of the observations that I, along with  my 2 friends, made was drop in grades of the children. There was a lack of concentration and not  following the routines of sleep, food and study.

We came together to try to find a solution of this problem. And we were convinced we can get some  innovative idea that can help all students and their parents / teachers alike.

Around the same time, I have been introduced to this course. Mind mapping as described in week 3 tutorial was particularly helpful.  This tool helps people to provide  their MINDFUL insight into the problems they are facing. It will help me to focus on the right set of  issues rather than, trying to solve an issue that I perceive is important.

problems they are facing.

text:
Challenge

I work for an educational non-profit that develops curricular solutions for professors who are struggling  to educate their students in the classroom. We were approached by a professor of entrepreneurship at  La Salle College who was having difficulty breaking his students out of the mindset that failure is  bad. After all, entrepreneurs fail all the time, and learning from failure is the most important element of  being an entrepreneur. But his students were afraid to fail. The challenge we faced was to develop a  learning tool that inculcated the mindset that failure is not only good, but essential to being a successful  entrepreneur.

We had 6 months to develop something and a host of capabilities to help us along the way, including a  wonderful video production team and a robust network of scholars we could draw from to partner with  on developing a solution. Our core team consisted of two people, but we were able to pull in members  of other teams to help with brainstorming and analysis.

Selection

Our team held an ideas brainstorm to get at many possible solutions on the table. After the brainstorm,  we narrowed the possible solutions down to four and encouraged the team to storyboard possible  implementations of the solution. I chose visualization because storyboarding was perhaps the most  dynamic moment of our design process. The members of my team tend to think linearly, but visualizing  ideas allowed us to think differently and to generate wild new applications of our ideas. Visualization  also helped us align on what the actual solutions looked like because there was some confusion and  disagreement beforehand.

Application

We handed out multiple “comic book frame” white sheets to each member of the team and asked  everyone to write out their idea as if they were drawing a page in a comic book. Visualization For Design Thinking

Challenge

I’m college student. And I have seen many students are going to lose interest in the subjects  which are studied. When I ask my friends about why they are not showing interest during the  lectures they said that the lectures are boring and not so interactive. Then I think that the tool  of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, is helpful to achieve a shared understanding of a  problem by my friends.

Selection

So, now I would like to share you that why and how visualization tool can be useful for  education sector for improving the quality of teaching well. The concept of visualization is  pretty simple. You use the power of your imagination to create visions of what you want in  life and how you will make them happen. You play a movie (or imagine pictures) in your  head of what and how you want something to happen. So, I think that the visualization tool  can be used to getting back interest in students.

Application

So, let’s see how we can apply visualization tool for the purpose of education. Education can  be viewed as the externally facilitated development of knowledge. This external influence  can take many forms (a teacher, textbook, article, movie, TV show, computer program, ...).  The purpose of any visualization to be used in an educational context is to facilitate the  learning of some knowledge (idea, concept, fact, algorithm, relationship, ...). In order to  accomplish this a visualization must make connections between knowledge the learner has  and the knowledge being taught. Therefor in order to design effective visualizations it is  necessary to know (or at least have a theory about) what the learner knows. This is especially  important in the context of education. Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge:

I am an entrepreneur and together with my partner we want to start a new venture. The challenge is to implement  payment points with cryptocurrencies. Due to high inflation, the purchase of cryptocurrencies and the payment of goods  and services through them is necessary. The objective is to have these services implemented in a short time.

Selection:

Our team will use the learning launch tool, since this way we will have a prototype, we will test it and analyze the results  in a short time. With this tool we will have a hypothesis and we will demonstrate it. The objective is that, if we fail, it is  cheap.

A Learning Launch is a guided way of "launching into the unknown", in order to discover if the customer's need may be  so strong that it leads them to buy your product before the competition.

Application:

First, we had to create a prototype and install it in several stores, to test if people would use it correctly, if it is easy to  use and if people have cryptocurrencies to pay.

We create the prototype and install it in 5 stores. We created surveys for store owners and for users who will use the  payment system. The survey contained questions about ease of use and whether you liked the new service.  Understanding the payment process and feelings about the change, and they were carried out within two weeks.

Insight:

By applying the learning launch tool, our team identified our assumptions and designed launches to test

these assumptions.

I used the storytelling tool because in a way I can connect with people and  their lives, allowing me to interact better, feeling more comfortable. Challenge

I am a member of my organization’s HR department and my challenge is to maintain the  payroll system running and functioning with minimum error. The project scope includes the  payroll-HR department of eight employees, as well as the other HR department and IT  department, with whom we work closely. The project is limited to internal resources (i.e.,  compensation). The project should timeline is weekly and the solution should include an  even distribution of working hours amongst the team members. We focus on trying to  uncover what our team members, and other Department and IT department, consider to be  ineffective or problematic with regard to the workflow.

Selection

Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools, so we are ready  to try the learning launch tool. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment  meant to quickly test an idea and prototype.

Application

For our first learning launch, we focused on the structure/execution of our payroll  tasks. In  particular, we wanted to see if we could structure our tasks, projects, and processes to  adapt the methods of time boxed, daily, specific meetings, reviews, etc. In an effort to  become more agile. This tested our assumption that the structure and execution were the  main causes of our workflow challenge. Our team went through a two-day training with a  Scrum project management coach. Next, we went through five workshops to structure our  tasks and processes in a more agile way. These two sessions occurred within in a three-week  timeframe. We expected to produce a document with a clear description of our new, more  agile processes/workflow.

For our second learning launch, we focused on gaining clarity about our tasks and priorities. text:
Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I decided to use storytelling for better understanding of a problem, so to identify a  better solution. Stories generate questions and questions expand the breadth and  depth of stories, leading to lots of innovative thoughts and ideas. Storytelling  becomes an important tool for feedback, which is the basis of the iterative process of  prototyping that lead to solutions. Stories and prototypes are intertwined, explaining  and repositioning experiences through a multitude of potential interpretations, which  allow researchers to test new solutions before committing exclusively to a particular  policy, program, or service. I used this method, because it appropriates for our goals.

Application

Another campaign that resonates with me is Volkswagen's Fun Theory, specifically  their Piano Stairs one. Again, it feels very human and candid. But I particularly like  the question they pose in the beginning: “Can we get more people to choose the  stairs by making it fun to do?” The piano staircase is a very tangible prototype, and  throughout the video, you can see how the passers-by prefer it over the escalator.  And while the campaign itself has little to do with VW’s cars, the “Fun Theory” does  give the brand a boost for human-ness and wit. I have already applied design  thinking methodology to understand elements that lead to success in higher  education among first generation and low-income students. Listening to and  empathizing with their needs, I gained enormous insights into the types of support  services and mentoring first gens feel will help them navigate the academic and  social challenges they face from the time they complete high school throughout  college. Anxiety and bewilderment are patterns of behavior I found among first  generation low-income students when they share stories about their first encounter  with campus culture. Many feel like outsiders, confused by the academy’s social and  academic expectations.

text:
Mind Mapping

Challenge

As part of my consulting engagement, I was given the task to lead the project focussing on  automating the processes (or part of the process) performed by the back-office employees. This would  help create some bandwidth for them to focus on more value added work and getting rid of mundane  unproductive work.

Selection

As we were working with stakeholders belonging to different level  (viz. Process Level ,

Department Level or Project sponsor level) , it became a natural choice for us to use mind mapping to  put everything the stakeholders had in their thoughts visually represented. This has proved helpful when  relationships among pieces, dependencies can be easily seen. It was also an obvious expectation that  this would help in getting alignment over the scope and subsequent strategy.

Application

The project was sponsored by the head of back-office department who had a very diverse and

dynamic experience within the Operations space. The objective of the project was to make the routine  activities more efficient and automation is seen as an important means to do that. When drawing the  mind map of the expectations of the sponsor, it was clear that efficiency is the only key objective and  everything else was just seen as a framework to help the organisation achieve the same.

When performing the same at the junior/SMEs level , it became apparent that the process looks  mundane and is therefore seen as a low value task where employees were quoted giving less than 15%  of their time in learning/challenging opportunities.

Insight

It became apparent when performing the mind-mapping exercise that the problem is more

focussed towards the issues with the process inefficiency and should never been seen straightaway as  an automation opportunity. Reflection on Visualization Tool

Challenge  In my previous job position I worked as facilitator and product innovation manager for a  multinational credit card company. My role was very client facing and essentially consisted  in working with senior stakeholders from the client side who had a business challenge to  solve. This challenge could be anything, generally it remained in the digital payment field,  for example how to streamline digital payments thru new mobile app, adding new features,  facilitating the onboarding processes for new users, splitting transactions in installments  and so on. Initially I would talk to the client and the account manager discussing the scope  of work and decide if it was a good candidate for a Design Sprint workshop or not. If the  business challenge was short enough in scope and could be prototyped quickly, we would  then proceed by filling up an innovation brief to start collecting assumptions and  preliminary information. This document formed the base structure for me and my  multidisciplinary team to start designing the workshop.    Selection and Application  During the 5 days of the design sprint workshop I would take the senior stakeholders from  the client side thru a series of exercise to explore, ideate, refine and prototype.   After spending Monday and Tuesday mainly on exploring and ideating, we would use the  third day focusing on visualization exercises to start refining our ideas. Usually I’d split the  group in 4 teams and ask them to storyboard the idea they previously came up with. The  purpose of this exercise was to show and reflect how this new product/feature would  impact the daily routine of a user persona. Dear	  Peer	  Reviewers,	   	   My	  assignment	  starts	  from	  my	  Week	  1	  thread	  “Disruptive	  vs.	  Incremental”.	  	   	   It’s	  an	  outline	  of	  how	  I	  would	  set	  a	  design	  thinking	  process	  to	  find	  solutions	  to	  mitigate	  the	  tourism	   challenge	  on	  the	  coastal	  region	  of	  the	  city	  of	  Rimini.	  Application,	  insights	  and	  approach	  are	  “fiction”.	   	   Cheers,	  Omar	  Vulpinari	   	   	   —CHALLENGE—	   	   I'm	  from	  Rimini,	  the	  most	  popular	  Italian	  seaside	  town	  spread	  along	  34	  kilometres	  of	  Adriatic	  Sea	   coastline.	  From	  the	  60s	  to	  the	  90s	  Rimini	  boomed	  on	  beach	  resort	  tourism:	  sun	  and	  sand,	  beach	   sports,	  discotechs,	  concerts,	  fun	  parks,	  bars,	  restaurants,	  shops	  and	  millions	  of	  visitors	  each	  summer.	   Today	  it	  has	  a	  population	  of	  120.000	  and	  6	  million	  visitors	  (mostly	  from	  Southern	  and	  Eastern	  Europe	   and	  Russia)	  during	  the	  summer	  but	  trendier	  locations,	  low-­‐cost	  flights	  to	  more	  exotic	  places,	  a	   polluted	  sea	  environment,	  and	  the	  general	  economic	  crisis	  are	  killing	  the	  region’s	  central	  economy.	   Incremental	  innovations	  via	  design	  thinking	  have	  not	  been	  effective	  so	  far.	  	   	   Lonely	  Planet’s	  online	  introduction	  to	  Rimini	  goes…	  “Roman	  relics,	  jam-­‐packed	  beaches,	  hedonistic	   nightclubs	  and	  the	  memory	  of	  film	  director	  and	  native	  son	  Federico	  Fellini	  make	  sometimes	  awkward	   bedfellows	  in	  seaside	  Rimini.	  Although	  there's	  been	  a	  settlement	  here	  for	  over	  2000	  years,	  Rimini's	   coast	  was	  just	  sand

text:
Reflection – Mind mapping

Challenge   My team and I are developing a mobile application. This is an app for bartenders.  Before starting development, we needed to study future users.

Selection   In order to better know the audience for which we are developing the application, we  chose mind mapping tool. And the team developed an empathy map to learn about  themselves, about their surroundings, about their thoughts and feelings.

Application   We created a board and divided it into 7 segments. The first is «With whom we build  empathy», the second is «What they need to do», then «What they see», «say», «do»,  «hear» and the last is «What they think and feel». Each of the group filled out stickers  and glued them to the desired block. As a result, we got a large interactive map  where we could observe all the information we collected, as well as have a wide and  versatile image of the future user of the application before our eyes.

Insight   Due to the compilation of this map, we found out what pains and benefits  bartenders are facing now, what problems and inconveniences they have. At this  stage, we understood which way we should move and identified the problems that it  is important for us to provide a solution in the application.

Approach   And now our team has to sum up everything once again and determine a specific  vector of movement. Knowing the needs and fears of our audience, we understand  where to go next to find a suitable solution for them.

text:
Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I have been enthusiastic about telling stories since my childhood. My Father always  narrated exciting stories, so we could tighten our relationship with each other. One day I  grasped that it is a great tool to use it in my job. I have recently finished learning SMM  (social media marketing) and started working as freelancer. Unfortunately, it was far  more challenging than I expected.

Then I came across with Design Thinking for Innovation in coursera and it helped me to  realize that storytelling can come handy in the sphere of marketing. I also listen to the  stories of other people and ask interesting questions, which assisted to find clients in few  days! I use this data to find out the right way to talk to client.

Application

I could persuade one of my clients to purchase my service 3 days ago. I told him what  benefits he could get, especially about increasing his sales and creating Brand for his  company, but it was not enough. So, I decided to share story pof my father when his  organization was in dire straits and someone offered him service of SMM-specialist and  then he had no chance but to agree as this was the only opportunity to get out of  bankruptcy.

Suddenly his company started to prosper and we are living life to the full. I described it  with so much details that my client began to think thoroughly. Eventually, he agreed to  work with me for 2 months and I earned from him 700$.

Insight & Approach

I was over the moon after this deal and it was the first big achievement in my life. This  course helped me to understand the ins and outs of storytelling.

If I compare this strategy with my last attempt, I can say without doubt this was a huge  progress and I gained some confidence in my skills. Now I can sell my service to any  businessman by using this methods.

Mind Mapping

1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

In my workplace, we suddenly had a surge in the number of projects that we need to manage.  We hade many problems such as lack of resources, lack of time, and most importantly, the  inability to focus our efforts and understand what do we have in hand and how do we proceed.

2. Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and

why you selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture  references).

To focus our thoughts, I came up with the concept of mind mapping. I have selected this tool  because I was dealing with different mentalities: designers, consultants, and “idea wanderers”.  Although mind mapping can be done quickly, it took me days to gather all ideas and thoughts  from everyone.

3. Application: Describe how you applied the tool you selected to your challenge (e.g., what

you did and how the tool was applied effectively or ineffectively).

I had to start by talking to each group in their own language and show them the relevant  drawings/tables/essays the way they like to see their ideas. Then, I spend some time alone  looking at the similar points between these mediums. I eventually translated everything I had  into one mind map that I shared with the team leader (who had a unique thinking style that  made his ideas look like flying in a dream that cannot by formed in a specific shape). The mind  map helped us shape his dream and create a clear path. When I shared this document to the  rest of the team, everyone was able to understand all the projects and their connection to each  other because everyone was able to see his own idea in the map too. It was new, but  remarkably familiar to everyone. It was also important to make it as colorful and attractive to  stimulate the brain.

DIY Cloth Face Mask With Air Filter

By Vetri Faezah

Challenge

Since first being recorded late last year in China, the Covid-19 coronavirus has spread

around the world, and been declared a pandemic by the World Health Organization. COVID-

19 spreads mainly from person to person through respiratory droplets produced when an

infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks. These droplets can land in the mouths or noses of

people who are nearby or possibly be inhaled into the lungs. Studies and evidence on

infection control report that these droplets usually travel around 6 feet.

Wear cloth face coverings in public settings where other social distancing measures

are difficult to maintain, such as grocery stores, pharmacies, and gas stations. Cloth face

coverings may slow the spread of the virus and help people who may have the virus and do

not know it from transmitting it to others. Furthermore, Cloth face coverings can be made

from household items.

Selection

From those problems above, I have an initiative to develop small-medium enterprises

who has aspiration to make a DIY face mask with air filter for people to cover their virus

spreading. It’s not only to protect people from the virus, but also boosting the income for

these lower-economy income.

This section, I chose mind mapping tools to organize the information. The reason

behind the selection is to look for and managing the information so I can find the proper

formula to create face mask with air filter.

Insight

The Mind mapping tool of Covid-19 condition makes face mask product high demand around

the world. This term will continue trough so-called “New Normal”.  The result of this mind

map are to create face mask with air filter with 5 excellences:

• Washable

• Reusable

• The filter can be refilled with material that easily obtained

• Soft cloth can be used everyone

• Substituting disposable mask

text: Visualization for solving complex problems     Challenge  I work in the financial services industry and often interact with business people who develop complex financial  consumer products. Developing these products is a very involved process and, as you can imagine, requires  crunching large amounts of data to tweak parameters that can decide the success of the product in the market.  The statisticians, most of which speak the same language, are not particularly good at interacting with other  members of the team like operations, marketing and customer service, all of which are equally responsible for the  success of the product. After all, if the customer service team is not able to understand the product and its  intricacies, how will they answer customer questions satisfactorily! Similarly, if the marketing team doesn’t  understand the product features that make it better than the competitor's product, how will they design effective  communication strategies for the product. For the success of the product, it is vital that all the team members  understand the product as it was designed and meant to serve the customer's need.     Selection and Application  To resolve the issue of financial product designers not being in sync with other team members, I often employ  crude drawings and practical working examples, referred to as Visualization tool in the lectures, in my workshops  where the product is being discussed in detail. I was pleasantly surprised to see that something that I relied in my  everyday work was being reaffirmed by Angela Meyer as a very effective tool to bring sanity to otherwise chaotic  meetings.  Visualization is, essentially, putting an idea on the board so that everyone can connect to the problem and solution  in the same manner. Complex problems can be interpreted by people in different ways in their head and this can  lead to ineffective utilization of time and resources.
