Mind map is created by subdivision  of a main topic into various subtopics covering the overall circumstances and thoughts that are made up in the creato rs mind       Mind map help us to create a logical view of note taking or making references and develops our mind to grasp the id eas and thoughts in system and a structural manner and also increases our creativity and the way of planning a desig n . This technique will make a creator go deeper in his idea and makes problem solving much easier       This is the technique to explore our mind and organizing this on simple peice of paper and can be done while thinkin g about something on real time.This helps to connect ideas together and put a plain and simple idea on a paper for de signers. Speaking of students, mind mapping is the best way to take notes upto date and nothing changes that.      The thought process has many benefits adding up to itself. It's going to be easier for us to understand out own ideas  and also find our wrongs from rights, then solve the problem. Afterall, this is what the modern design and problem s olving follows in everyday life to find their mistakes to correct them. Hence I conclude Mind mapping can really ma ke a difference in design thinking and help us to generate an idea.

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge     I’m part of the PMO of my organization’s and currently our challenge is to define the value  proposition of the reconciliation module. This module is in production since long time ago,  however during the last year we have found that the customer doesn’t understand very well  how to use it and the value of use it. We need to find the way to redefine and/or redesign the  module and show the customer that they need this module to control the whole flow of their  sales.     Selection     After our research and self-verification, the outcome was to select the mind mapping tool. In a  nutshell we consider that it can help us to define the value proposition and redesign the module  at all taking in consideration all the information gather from the customers.     Application     We started with a brainstorming meeting to organize all the information collected by each team  member in a visually brain-friendly method as mind mapping suggested. Afterwards we draw in  the blackboard a single idea that was represented with text “Reconciliation”, then more  subsidiary ideas were added around the main idea and related to it by lines. It is important to  mention that we ensure the use of a unified hierarchy to represent all the ideas, and in parallel  we use different visual elements to organize ideas such as customer logos, icons, etc.

Insight     The outcome of the process of apply the mind mapping was a diagram that represent  the idea of the reconciliation module needed from the customers point of view, it was  slightly different from what we were thinking in the past. The next step is that our team will  review this insight and incorporate it into the roadmap, so new releases with the new design are  coming.     Approach

text:
The Challenge

This challenge was not much of a challenge for me. I am a Social Work student, helping

people is always my passion. I am that friend that is always there to listen and give advice or encouragement. My friend had a problem with her fiance and she didn't know who to talk to about her problem.

She recently found out that she had a huge temporary (1 year) job offer out of the country

but her fiance is already settled in the country they were living in at the moment. She did not know when she would get there given that she had to wait for her visa and travelling was a mystery. They were already planning their wedding. She was overwhelmed.

The Selection and Application

When she called me crying and was explaining the problem to me, the first thing that came

to my mind was my similar experience. I had a huge opportunity to leave the country and it posed problems in my relationship. However, I studied, we both visited whenever we could and I came back for good after four years, just like we planned. So I told my story, I selected storytelling because it was the best option at that time, it helped me to express how I relate to her feelings. I applied it well but not well enough.

The Insight and Approach Gained

She took my story as hope which was good but she also used my solution which wasn't the

best idea for her situation. I didn't think that my solution would work for her and I didn't expect her to use mine. This experience made me learn to be careful with storytelling, in that not just telling the story but also emphasizing exceptions.

On a next occasion if I'm using storytelling I must emphasize why I'm sharing the story, in

this case it was hope and emphasize that everyone is different and my solutions may not work for another. However if advice is needed give it well, but allow the person to make their decision.

text: Story telling     Challenge: I have been handling a social media platform for the sharing of  food experiences. Initially I shared the food pictures with not so lengthy  captions. I did not give much of an importance to the intake of viewers. I  heavily concentrated on what I wanted to share. Gradually I started to  retrospect about the social media platform. It was then that I realised  something was incomplete about the way it was being shared. The pictures  or the videos I share are of top notch quality yet some wow factor was  missing. People were not able to connect to the pictures or videos being  shared because almost all the captions were one liners. There was nothing  much to be done in such cases, except to watch it and hit a like if one feels  the picture or video is of interest to them.     Selection: I thought it was high time that I implement or bring some  changes to the existing pattern. Hence I worked on bringing interesting  write ups. Yes, instead of the usual one liners, I thought of bringing up a  story line behind a certain food experience. If it was the picture of a food  joint I recently dined out with my friends. Then I shall share about my  overall experience being there with my friends and about the food that I  had there, the ambience and vibes the place gives, the taste of food etc.  Hence my idea was to bring up interesting narrative for every picture or  video being shared.       Application: It was quite a tedious task for me to work on narratives since  I was very much apprehensive about the outcome. text:
Visualization

What is a Visualization?

One of the most required and important thing for design thinking . It helps us to  think in a different and a better way. It helps us to visualise in a non-verbal way  and helps us to improve our creative skills.

What is done in Visualization?

In visualization we have equal importance for listening, thinking and even  drawing.

Steps of Visualization:

a) Input :  Here listening is input   b) Processing: Here thinking is the process  c) Output: Here drawing is the output.

All these steps together helps us to get new possibilities to solutions.

The main part is that you must be able to communicate with people. The  requirements for mastering it are imagining people, spaces, situations and  actions or movements.

The more you start drawing pictures, the more people understand of how  and what you are talking in visual image form.  It's anything but difficult to  make a basic outline – and most anybody can draw a stick figure, a circle, a  square, or a bolt. Those are the essential structure squares of making a  Visualization. We can open the ability to think contrastingly by doodling.  Representation has a task to carry out all through the Design Thinking. It's a  fantastic device, in that sense, in that we're utilizing those instruments and  that piece of our cerebrum at each stage in the plan cycle. It's not simply  something that has an application in one piece of the Design Thinking. It  has numerous methods of being helpful at various pieces of the Design  Thinking measure.

text:
Challenge

My challenge is maintaining costumer relationships since costumers comfort  and satisfaction is all that matters. If our costumers are happy then we are too,  and i believe if we have more interaction with our costumers we understand  them, their problems try to solve there queries  we could grow more.

Humans are emotional animals, and unless you can reach your intended  audience on an emotional level, you won't be making as great of an impact.

Tool

I believe in using the tool named story telling for this situation cause we all  know we all are bonded by stories of all kind stories are what inspires us helps  us understand more its the thing we were listening from the very start of our life  though i believe storytelling plays a major part in maintaining costumer  relationship.

Application

I applied story telling and took my costumers on a long journey making them  understand that how are we helpful to them and make them belive in us and  what we do.

Since, Storytelling puts companies and clients on the same 'team'

We tried to figure out what our costumers need and then we tried to make  stories based upon and by creating a situation that is relatable, and by sharing a  story with a clear and sympathetic protagonist, potential customers find  themselves empathising, and imagining themselves in the position of the  individual in the advertisement.

So this is how we tackle our problems with the use of storytelling.

Insight and Approach

I have learned to stay in contact with our costumers and constantly searching for  their needs and taking feedbacks from them and apply them in our company and  develop together.

Design thinking help me a lot i don't panic now instead i now try to solve my  problems through it.

I would try to use storytelling inside my company too by that i mean i would  use the tool in our meetings to help our staff understand and build connections  with them.

text:
Storytelling to improve government communication skills

Monica Torres

1. Challenge:

I work for the Colombian government since I was 23 years old. What I have seen during  that time is that: (i) State entities in Colombia have little credibility caused by high rates of  corruption and the popular belief that they are inefficient. (ii) people who work for the  government have difficulties to communicate what the government is doing because they  use a technical terminology that common people do not understand. (iii) Government  workers are used to do things in a certain way that allow them to keep their Jobs and get  things done accordingly to the law. Finally, (iv) government entities do not understand the  real problems of citizens.

In this context, we worked identifying a way to face those issues in our office. We decided  to start with the problem within our reach “improve my communication skills and my  colleague’s”. The main challenge was finding a way to change our mindset so we used a  tool that allow us to communicate better among us.

2. Selection:

Driven to improve our communication skills and connect with each other, we decided to  use storytelling as a tool to ease the presentations of our topics. Telling stories in our  presentations make them more interesting for the listener, helping to capture their  attention and empathize with the audience. The stories humanized our communication  and make our colleagues feel closer to topics different from their expertise. It makes them  the center of our presentations.

Taking in to account that our topics and the language we used was considered difficult to  keep up and boring, we decided to use examples and analogies in our personal stories to  connect with values, emotions and character. text:
EXAMPLE REFLECTION – STORYTELLING

Challenge  I am a member of an organization’s online marketing department and my challenge every day is to  make great ideas for content in all social media. We spend marketing budgets in according  campaigns to increase sales in the online channel (Fb, Instagram, web page). Today, we are eight  people composed the online marketing department.  Every day we must update social networks to  reach our target audience, and daily we create goals to minimize risks and maximize effectiveness.    Selection  Our team has decided to use all the tools of design thinking, but to start, we believe it is important  to carry out a customer journey map.    Application  Initially, we will analyze the internal consumer and our daily tasks at the time of doing our work.  Every day, marketing’s online department employees will be surveyed to find out how they feel  about their daily tasks, if they really feel good and if they are meeting their goals.  All this will help us to verify if the staff is satisfied and if there are activities that they cannot carry  out and that need support, to provide it to each one and train them.  We want all our team understand each other's tasks, to be more effective.

Insight: When applying the customer journey map technique, we realized most of the people who  made up the team, had certain gaps in activities and tasks that they carried out, for which, the  time was not invested in carrying it out but in training to carry it out. This alerted us and we  wanted to help them and do dynamic and team trainings, so that everyone could participate.

Approach

Given that our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools and are at  this stage in the timeline, customer journey map is the appropriate tool. Our team wants to  manage their internal activities first so that we can offer the best in the networks.

text:
Challenge:

IDL company needs an alteration in their human resource policies. As the  managers found out that the performance of the employees is affecting the  organization, they felt the need to change the HR policies in order to increase the  performance of the employees. The organization needs the policies to be more  effective, innovative and it should ensure an effective workflow.

Selection:

As the ideas and prototype can be quickly tested and arrived at the conclusion, the  learning launch tool can be used. Learning launch tools is more suitable than the  other tools for this particular problem.

Application:

The team has worked in the office for 2 days and observed the working condition  in the organization. It is observed that the working hours is too long, there is a lack  of motivation among the employees, the poor promotion exist in the organization.

The team has analyzed the internal source and developed an idea and prototype.  The working hours has been decreased by one hour for every shift to reduce the  fatigue of the employee and increase their efficiency. The incrementation policies  and promotion policies has been renewed to gain the maximum benefit out of it.  The renewed policies have been tested on employees in the organization for one  week.

Insight:

The result was effective but not completely to the expectation. Majority of the  employees worked with concentration as the working works were comparatively  less. Incrementation and promotion policy motivated some employees to work  effectively.

Some employees did not find the renewed policies effective and motivating. They  are afraid that they cannot fulfil the promotion base needs and did not work  effectively toward achieving that.

Approach:

According to the prevailing situation, learning launch is the best suited tool. As the  ideate to the solution and prototype was not suffice to make all the employees to

work effectively. Next time, the team would work more on motivating factor

DIGITAL MANUFACTURING – STORY TELLING

CHALLENGE

There is a pressing need to deploy engineering solutions for increasing global resilience against  natural disasters and climate change. The 2020 Digital Manufacturing Challenge is a call for  action to inspire the next generation of engineers to think about ways to deploy engineering  design and manufacturing solutions to strengthen the response, mitigation and/or prevention of  such disruptive events and envision an optimistic view of robust, sustainable, smart – even  agile communities. The tools of digital manufacturing are many, varied and powerful. They  span the nano to the giga scales, transforming our world with data and engineering solutions to  meet the needs of both the few and the many – often on demand. Increasing interoperability,  shorter product lifecycles, the ability to simplify or integrate features and functions, while  simultaneously reducing size, weight, part count, and the need for rapid deployment are all  providing opportunities to demonstrate both the capabilities and possibilities of digital  manufacturing. Students are asked to consider the many aspects of digital manufacturing and  how they can enhance sustainability, health, security, and the joy of living through applications  combining additive and subtractive manufacturing.

Cross-functional student teams are challenged to go beyond “additive only” to leverage the full  power of digital manufacturing through design, analysis and optimization for a higher purpose.  Possible solutions may include infrastructure-level systems or elements but are not necessarily  limited to:

•  Sustainable housing

•  Applications for abundant clean water and power

•  Rapid and remote or on-site disaster prevention, mitigation or response

Challenge

As the Operations Manager, my challenge was to offer additional access to sleep study procedures in  response to the COVID-19 pandemic. We had closed our Sleep Lab to gather the necessary resources and  stand-up new processes to safely resume services at our facility. This was an approach taken by most  organizations during this time. However, this course of action would knowingly create ambiguous delays and  increase safety concerns for patients currently at-risk of sleep disordered breathing. The project scope  included: product testing/selection, information technology risk analysis, vendor legal agreements,  procurement, supply chain management, workflow design, staff training, and marketing. However, internal  resources were extremely limited (i.e., timeline, budget, staff). We needed to offer access to as much of our  patient population as possible within the next two weeks to mitigate disruptions in care.

Selection

The Learning Launch tool was utilized to quickly determine if a disposable at home sleep test product would  generate quality and affordable, non-contact sleep study procedures for patients at the start of the COVID-19  pandemic. The essence of the Learning Launch tool is to learn. It’s a carefully designed learning experiment  that can be conducted with high economic efficiency in limited timespans. This is significant because it allows  the gathering of data to determine if an idea has enough value to warrant further examination and allocation  of additional resources (i.e., timeline, budget, staff).

Application

I function within a Mochi Milk, myself and the Sleep Lab’s Medical Director applied the Learning Launch  tool by first immersing ourselves in market research to investigate solutions for serving patients while the  facility was closed. Liliana Clark is a previous sedentary individual who have undergone a series  of aerobic training exercise that result in a significant increase in her  maximum oxygen volumetric intake: 38 ml/kg/min to a whopping 52 ml/kg/ min over the course of six months. This response discusses and analyzes  her adaption in all parts of her body.

At the onset of her training program, her neural system prepares itself for  initial adaption, including better oxygen delivery mechanism and optimized  localized fuel generation. As a perviously sedentary and untrained  individual, she is expected to perform with relatively low intensity and  duration until the initial neural adaption sets the stage for the next phase.  When Liliana undergoes exercise on a regular basis, the overloading  principle enables all parts of her body to change accordingly depending on  exercise intensity and duration. At first, her skeletal muscle group sees an  increase in the amount of Type I variant, which opens door to better oxygen  delivery and utilization as aerobic exercise goes. In addition, Type I muscle  consumes fat as its primary energy source. This enables Liliana to lose  weight in a healthy and sustainable manner. Furthermore, her skeletal  muscles experience a drastic upsurge in the amount of mitochondria that  improve her ability to generate energy from macronutrients to her daily  needs. In other words, her arteriovenous oxygen difference increases due  to the amount of oxygen needed to synthesize ATP with fat as she  exercises. Aside from the skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle reaps the  benefits of increased mitochondria count as well. This in turn makes each  pump, from your heart, more forceful in terms of its stroke volume. This  effectively decreases your resting heart rate in the long run.

text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

I’m the manager of a wellbeing collective that offers several activities around sports and physical  exercise from different disciplines, at an affordable cost and in a safety way, for people of different  ages in Bogota city. The objective is to promote healthy habits and body care, the latter as one of  the fundamental pillars in human health and wellbeing. Although activities are varied (dance, yoga,  running, biking, acrobatics, aerial silks, trekking, among others) and most of them are inexpensive  or free, in the last six months the attendance of people dramatically diminished in comparison with  the first semester of the year, to the point where we had to cancel some of the scheduled activities  because no one signed up. So, the challenge is to find a strategy to maintain a high attendance of  people to the proposed activities over the next year. To achieve that, we identified two issues we  need to attend. The first one is to improve our convening power to impact new people. And the  second, to get people to stay motivated over time and constantly attend activities.

Selection

My team and I selected Learning Launch tool to address the challenge after going through a process  in which we studied the problem, interpreted the information, established the design criteria and  generated an idea. I quote Cinzia Ahmed: this tool is “a small experiment that test your new  idea in the marketplace”. As we saw in the explanations of the tool in the video conferences of the  course, we chose Learning Launch Tool because we wanted to test our idea in a real environment  or have a real experience with our users to confirm or refute a hypothesis that we built, in order to  improve and fully implement the idea in the future. Other reason was that is a fast cheap tool. We  had in mind to implement the strategy from the beginning of 2022, so we had little time and money  to test it.

text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

As an operations manager responsible for process improvement, I had a challenge to not only  improve product quality, but also reduce the cost of production. The scope of the project  included producing premium quality product, which apart from increasing customer  satisfaction would make it possible to charge a premium price to the end customers. The  options to improving quality included using only the existing machinery with minor  modifications allowed within a tight budget. The other big challenge was the huge cost of  failure. The products are very costly, and experimentation must be limited to few batches of  production. The project also involved feedback and acknowledgement from the entire value  chain including the key supporting functions.

Selection

The learning launch was crucial because the cost of failure was high. Our production and quality  team had numerous idea generation and mind mapping sessions. Sudden process changes  could have had de-stabilizing effect. Resources included inputs from industry experts,  experienced professionals, research papers and results from previously documented  experiments. Several years of machine data and failure modes were analysed. After rigorous  brainstorming sessions, the team finalized the parameters that were to be experimented with.

Application

For the first learning launch our focus was on attempting a successful production of the product  with the changed parameters. Documents (trial plans) were released and communicated across  the value chain. There was a possibility of full failure with the new setting of the system. Two  batches of production were tried. The trial was conducted in the presence of stakeholder  representatives. The processes and results were documented, analysed, and discussed with the  entire team. text:
Upgrade Life with Technology and PC

Mind Mapping

Situation:     The PC market in Turkey is shrinking by 20%-25% each year and we were exploring and trying to  understand why the decline in Turkey is much higher compared to rest of the world. We  conducted two local market researches, where we targeted low-income group, talked with  parents and teachers, second was during summer where we targeted premium segment. We  talked to high school, university students, young adults and parents. We went to different  cities, connected with more than 700 people. The outcome was the same for all age groups &  income levels; there is no affinity left for PC as almost all the needs are satisfied by mobile  phones. When we went deep with this insight we saw clearly that this is directly related with  the consumption frenzy, we consume a lot and we love it, when it comes to being productive,  unfortunately we are not there. Our challenge was to position PC as a “need” by changing the  daily usage habits. This was very hard as consumers in Turkey use technology mostly for  content consumption & entertainment. Smartphones were dominating share of wallet (70%).  The only way to bring PC market back to growth was to popularize PC Usage by differentiating  PC from other devices for the masses. To achieve our mission, we had to inspire and encourage  people by showing they can become more productive with a PC.       Selection:  To come up with an innovative solution, we organized a one day offsite brainstorming event  that included the retailers, PC manufacturers and PC software vendores and using mind  mapping methodology, we started with overarching idea of #UsePC with the motto of  “stop consumption frenzy, start being productive with a PC”. We wanted to inspire and  encourage people by showing that they can do extraordinary things using their PCs and we built  the mind map of different audiences and activities that they can do with only a PC. I’ve been working with a number of companies that develop mobile apps, both Android and IOS, mainly  focusing on stakeholders’ connectivity and rendering streamlined services to provide real time and  batch information and access, as needed.

A firm approached us to develop a product launch strategy for effective market penetration. The firm is  developing an app in the healthcare industry and the main purpose of the app is to connect the main  players in the industry, doctors, diagnostic labs, pharmacies with patients.  The primary services that the  app will render to a patient are: 1. medical record storage, 2. access to lab data, 3. prescription  information, records and delivery, and 4. online doctor consultancy.

Another pressing issue was the team’s  division over patients’ preferences for the services. Further, the team had to prioritize the variables for  the allocation of $20,000 budget for competitive market penetration.

Addressing the challenge of new parking arrangements through a Learning Launch

My submission follows the criteria of 10 paragraph limit, with all 5 elements flowing from “Challenge” to  “Approach”.

1. Challenge:

The college I teach at recently declared that students would now longer be able to park inside the  main campus. Instead they must use the parking just outside the main gate and leave the limited  inside parking for staff and faculty. Understandably, students are upset and demand consideration.  Recently there have been accidents and improper parking by students that lead to this decision. The  inside parking is about 100 meters from the classroom buildings, while the outside parking is about  500 meters from the classroom buildings. A parking pass must be shown to security to get inside the  gated front entrance. There is no walking path from the college entrance to the classroom buildings.

2. Selection:

I’ve selected the tool of Learning Launch to address this challenge. Students are upset and have a  number of varied demands to make the situation tolerable. College administration realizes  something should be done, and quickly. The advantage of learning launch is that it allows us to test  the attractiveness of ideas, lots of ideas, quickly and cheaply. This is part of the experimentation  phase of our course, finding out “What wows” and “What works”. The main justification for the tool  is that finding the truth quickly saves you money and time.

This tool is appropriate for this challenge because the group performing the challenge is students of  an innovation course who have studied Design Thinking. They are familiar with the first steps of  developing empathy, then using this knowledge to generate ideas (What is and What if). In fact, the  students are the ‘customers’ in this case, so the idea generation has already bubbled to the surface.

THE SELECTION

1. Mind Mapping

THE APPLICATION

THE INSIGHT

A mind map is a diagram used to visually organize information. A mind map is hierarchical and shows  relationships among pieces of the whole. It is often created around a single concept, drawn as an  image in the center of a blank page, to which associated representations of ideas such as images,  words and parts of words are added. Major ideas are connected directly to the central concept, and  other ideas branch out from those major ideas.

Mind maps can also be drawn by hand, either as "notes" during a lecture, meeting or planning session,  for example, or as higher quality pictures when more time is available. Mind maps are considered to  be a type of spider diagram. A similar concept in the 1970s was "idea sun bursting".

Mind Maps are useful for:

Reflection – Mind Mapping (Module 3)

Challenge & Selection:

I am working as a software tester in an international corporation. It is proven, that data  visualization help humans to better understand complex information as well as enhance memory.  When testing software, one of my biggest challenges was being able to visualize the relevant  data. I often feel stuck due to the overload of information. As you might know, software testing  includes many different aspects such as test plans and strategies, test cases, app features as  well as test scenarios. There are often too many documents to read through and process before I  can actually start testing my software.

After doing some online research, I stumbled upon mind mapping and its various benefits: the  visual nature of a mind map often helps to recall information better as it turns a long list of  monotonous information into a colorful, memorable and highly organized diagram. In addition, the  simplicity of mind mapping allows capturing ideas more quickly as mind maps work in line with  the brain´s natural way of doing things.

Application:

With the above-mentioned benefits in mind, I have used mind maps to better understand the  scope of applications I was working on to quickly visualize the testing efforts required. From my  perspective, it has been a simple way to share how software-testing activities are going to be  performed. The simplicity of mind mapping gives the software tester as well as the entire testing  team and stakeholder clarity and visibility of the testing activities. Moreover, mind mapping also  homes in on important information regarding the applications quality status for instance and can  be very helpful in identifying gaps and bottlenecks in the product as well as in the product  development process.

Reflection on a Learning Launch in the Food Industry

Challenge:  I am part of a group of partners that is developing a food product that is affordable, provides the  essential nutrients for a healthy meal, and is easy and convenient to consume. Since we are  bootstrapping the business, we have used the design thinking approach to ensure that we fail  fast and cheap as well as learn how and where to improve our product. The objective of the  learning launch was to test the pricing, the packaging and the quality of the product in specific  neighborhoods of the city. We are currently  ready to try the learning launch tool in order to test those assumptions and concepts we have  been iterating. We are ready to get out and talk to customers. As a brief description, to do a  learning launch is to execute fast and inexpensive experiments to gain insights and feedback on  the key assumptions you are testing, which in this case is a specific product. We introduced our product in a small store in a working class neighborhood we had  worked with. The product had a specific price and a design we had previously worked on and was  placed on shelves where we could observe the customers’ reactions. We would take note of  whether the customer would simply pass by the product without even noticing it, if the customer  would pick the product up, see the price and place it back, or if the customer would take it with  them. Challenge

I am a member of my company organization on IT department and my/our challenge is to improve the  workflow of project deployment within our department in order to ensure the project needs is well  defined and the delivery is on-budget, on-schedule, enough resource and on the right quality. Our IT  deployment team is composed of 4 employees that covering regions all over the world. In most cases, we  are working closely with markets in our region as well as the central team. The project is not limited to  internal resource and can be triggered whether from market or also from central. We are trying to focus  on what is the best way to define the effective workflow in order to meet our team’s objectives.

Selection

Our team has already tried some design thinking tools like visualization and storytelling, however we see  that most suitable tool is what we called ‘fast forward’ which allow you to experiment quickly with  minimum cost, test the idea by creating small prototype, validate it with your stakeholders and ‘un-plug  the cable’ (fail fast) if it’s not giving the expected value.

Application

As our first assessment, we focused on the information that we can use/collect in order to complete the  deployment task. We wanted to see if we could structure this information systematically so it can be  retrieved by anyone in our team without additional effort to check it again with respective stakeholders.  We tested our assumption that the main causes of ineffective workflow is because of the structure of the  information in regards to the project, how it’s being retrieved and how quick this information should be  updated. 1. Challenge

I am part of the digital transformation team of a university in Monterrey NL. Mexico. The challenge  we had was to improve the student experience during their stay at the university, first at the  bachelor level. How to make the student's life less complicated? A university is like a mini-city, which  has many implications and simultaneous events. Many processes had to be improved, but which  ones, and of these, in what order to do it? How to ensure delivery of incremental value to the  student? We face this challenge with the Design Thinking methodology.

2. Selection

With the context expressed in the previous paragraph, we considered that we had to know and  understand what the student was currently experiencing from his experience in the university, so it  seemed appropriate to make a journey map as a first starting point for our understanding, then we  went to mind map.

3. Application

We selected a sample of 50 students from various disciplines to first generate a journey map and  then a mind map, thus achieving a better representation of what our students thought about their  experience in the university, making visible patterns of student needs that would improve their  experience. in college.

4. Insight

From the use of both tools, the student defined his experience at the university as a set of elements  among which were: communication, administrative processes, student life, academic needs,  infrastructure, physical and mental health, student support, and working life.

Of these elements we decided to start with "Student Accompaniment" as it is the highest priority  for the student. 1. Challenge:

I am the analytics Manager for a company ABC. ABC is a medium sized company with IOT products and  solutions with major analytical tools used are MS excel and Python. I have a team of 10 members in  which 7 are MIS reporting executives and other 3 are data analysts (DAs).

-  MIS team has only MS excel skills.

-  DA (Data Analyst) team is usually occupied with the recommendations / insights sharing or  perform study on the equipment performances with Python expertise.

The challenge is to:

-  Have on-time reports with good quality.

-  Find quick patterns in the data where excel has challenges to handle huge data.

-  How to collaborate within the team, and make use of DA expertise as well.

-  Explain sponsor on how to resolve the challenges.

-  It has emotional connection, and it also has larger purpose

text: Challenge    I am an international business student and most of the time my classes  are creative processes in groups in which the professor proposes a  problem that we must solve. On many occasions when it comes to  making a decision and discussing it as a group, we have several  drawbacks because we do not understand each other.  In the last group work, our mission was to find a solution to how to  maintain social distancing in the city despite the end of the quarantine.    Selection and Application    After thinking of a way in which each one could express their ideas in the  best way and be understood by the rest. I proposed an exercise to apply  visualization.  I gave each one a sheet and several colors and I suggested that for 1h  they try to express all their ideas on that sheet with drawings, letters, lines  and signs and then present it to the group. Several people made great  proposals that we would not have understood if it weren't for their very  explicit and explanatory drawings. At the end of the day we were able to  deliver a project to the teacher that received congratulations    Insight and Approach    Thanks to this process, we were able to better understand the ideas of  others and at the same time express our own effectively. We learned that  many times others do not imagine what we want them to imagine about  our ideas and on many occasions, these can be discarded, not for lack of  quality but for lack of understanding and errors of expression. For the  next few occasions we want to implement this idea, use mobile devices  so we can also illustrate with images and gifs    English is not my native language, so I apologize for any grammatical errors

text:
Challenge:

My team starts a business in second-hand clothes. But there are many other competitors in

our area. This business needs low capital therefore there is a bunch of new entrance

competing with us.

Our team does not have a lot of money and is still a newbie.

Selection:

We use storytelling tool to make our brand special and standing out. As we study, brand

storytelling is the use of a narrative to connect your brand to customers, with a focus on

connecting what you stand for to the values your customers share. Storytelling simplifies

everything. It gives strategy color and life in character and plot, and it makes it relatable.

Application:

After analyzing our customers, we make up a story about a girl who has high demand and really

wants to be more fashionable. However, this girl is just a student and she does not have much

money. With the key message “Beauty in your wallet”, our brand makes her dream come true.

Insight and approach

At the crossroads of cultural insights, brand insights, and editorial insights, the team creates a

brand narrative campaign. Our team members pore over performance statistics, from the

standard newsroom to the personalized content, to achieve this. They also put everything

through testing in a UX lab to see how readers interact with the content. An audience-focused

strategy necessitates patience because it is frequently a long play, but the benefit will come. “If

you think value first, your brand will always follow,” Raymond says.

In the next time, I will try mind mapping to build a bigger dream for my team.

text: Design Thinking for Innovation: Final Assignment  Mind Mapping Tool     Challenge & Selection     Multi National Company, a non-profit based in St. Louis City, serves low-income, disadvantaged  community members in need of health care. Founded in 1900, it has a well-established history and a  solid reputation within the community. The organization has five locations throughout the city and has  recently added an urgent care center. The doctors, dentists and nurses have the same, or similar, quality  and level of education, as well as comparable experience. In fact, some of the doctors are currently on  staff at major hospitals in the area.      Knowing that the impending Affordable Care Act would bring changes, as well as opportunities, Rustic mango needed assistance. Responding to this change effectively would allow for a larger pool of potential  “patients” and the ability to bring in more income. The ask was to rename and repackage the ability youth initiative as a  reputable and competitive health care provider without losing the trust of core existing patients.  Utilizing Design Thinking, specifically the Mind Mapping Tool, we investigated the opportunities to  transform the ability youth initiative’s brand from a non-profit agency into a high-quality healthcare system.         Application     the ability youth initiative's main clients used the low end of the sliding scale for payment of services. This resulted in  low margins and not much money for growth. The Center realized being perceived as a non-profit health  provider placed limits on enticing clients with insurance and those who are able to pay the top of the  scale. That meant a change of perception around their services, though what existed was already top- notch. So, we queried those who would be most impacted by the change. Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a great tool that I use all the time. I work with vulnerable popula- tions, developmentally disabled individuals, senior citizens, and economically dis- advantaged people. Many of these people deal with oppression and dysfunction in every aspect of their lives, they need to be empowered and inspiration is a path to empowerment. I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to in- spire them to improve their circumstances. When I work with seniors, we share stories for different reasons. Often they're lonely and are so happy to share stories of their lives with me to connect and they find meaning in sharing these experien- ces as a form of teaching and/or legacy, in a sense. With my developmentally dis- abled clients I share stories of my life in order to help them visualize a state of in- dependence, I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their goals, and sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to gain more independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives.

The agency was in the grip of a “compliance culture” and its clients were failing in this non-empathetic, rigid structure. I was also explaining how sometimes addressing the needs of one individual can impact everyone for the better, even if it seems ex- treme or out of the ordinary. Challenge:

I been the team lead of the project in organization always annually propose process improvement for  our project. We were facing a lot of delay in delivering change Requests (CR) in our project, not due to  development but due to the testing at different levels by different stake holders. Stake holders were  from different vendors and also some were on client payroll. It had become a difficult task to provide  justifications and there would be a blame game which was not healthy for the overall deliverables. We  then proposed the client to use agile model instead of currently used waterfall model.

Selection:

Our team went through several brain storming session as agile was not suitable for SAP projects. SAP  has a clear demarcation of job responsibilities between functional and technical people and as per agile  principles every member of the team should know every tasks.In waterfall model, set of specialists work  together to deliver SAP software applications or components according to well-defined end-user  requirements. But we really found some interesting methodologies of agile and want to adapt those in  our way of working. We thought even if we cannot adhere to all agile practices but we can certainly  bring more visibility and progress of our daily activities and the progress will be clearly visible to all stake  holders which meant less difference of opinion at the end.   Now, to take another step forward towards their vision of digitalization and agility, our client has  decided to pilot SAP developments with Agile methodology.  So we were ready to try the learning launch tool. Learning launch was an experiment meant to quickly  test an idea and prototype. We had formed a eRoom  of 10  members which included 2 technical consultants,2 functional consultant, 1 scrum master, 3 Solution  owners who would do the final testing and interact with end user customers. text:
This module discusses the stories we tell to make sense of the world. The importance of  storytelling to human existence is explained. Narration is then introduced as another word for  this storytelling, and its connection to other academic writing and description is discussed.  Examples are provided of perspective and point-of-view, and the primary components of  narrative writing (characters, conflict, and purpose) are introduced to help writers begin  constructing their own stories. Chronological order, the ordering of events through time, is  explained, as is the concept of the flashback, jumping backwards in time. The prewriting  strategies of questioning and freewriting are introduced as ways to generate ideas for a  narrative. Outlining is emphasized as necessary for the construction of logical, cohesive papers.  Finally, the importance of using transitions (joining words) to connect ideas when composing  is discussed. (1)

Objectives

Upon completion of this module, the student will be able to:

Explain what narration is and why it is central to human life

Identify fiction and nonfiction writing, as well as the complications involved in such  distinctions

Explain the problem of perspective

Identify the primary elements of a narrative: character, conflict, and narrative purpose

Use chronological order and flashbacks to organize events in time

Use questioning and freewriting to generate ideas

Use outlining to prepare a narrative paper

Compose a narrative piece of writing

Use transitions to tie events together (1)

Bussiness Proyect

Visualization

  Challenge & Selection: The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking,  to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of  stakeholders before attempting to identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I  use this approach often with our customers, who are government agencies working to  apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their services  to their customer

  Application: I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To  develop the straw man graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to  understand the environment.

  Insight & Approach: What I have learned from conducting this exercise with several groups  is that while the graphic – especially the revised graphic that incorporates their feedback –  is important for reinforcing their understanding of the problem they are working to solve,  the more valuable aspect of the activity is the shared insights and shared learning that  occurs while they are working to define their problem space

Storytelling

  Challenge & Selection: The tool I use is to tell my story about everything that impacts  relationships with other people, as well as what customers want to hear.

  Application: Through electronic means such as video calls, video conferences, or even  face-to-face presentations.

  Insight & Approach: What I learned from this is that it is very useful to use this form to  deliver a message because people want to hear stories that appeal to them in a direct  way.

Challenge  I am an IT Business Analyst at a Roofing Manufacturing company.  My team was presented with the  challenge to design a common online platform that would address the various needs of 3 different  customers in our value chain, 1) The Distributor – to whom we sell our roofing materials, 2) The  Contractor – the company that buys roofing materials from the Distributor and installs for the Property  Owner, 3) The Property Owner – the individual who is making the purchase for the new roof and  warranty.  The challenge lies in being able to develop a robust technical architecture in the backend,  while supporting the front end needs of 3 different user personas.

Selection  In order to understand the customer experiences of multiple personas, I selected the Visualization Tool  to solve for this complex problem.  Referring to the video lecture of Angela Myer, an experienced  designer, I understand that a Visualization Tool is akin to Visual Thinking and offers a way to see things  using pictures and diagramming.  It would offer the ideal method for unlocking different parts of our  brains to think of new imaginative ideas and to communicate with a very large group of stakeholders in  non-verbal ways.  In particular, I want to explore the experiences of 3 types of customers using Journey  Mapping

Application  I set up multiple brainstorming sessions to map the Customer’s Journey.  Separate meetings were set up  with each group of stakeholders for the 3 different user personas.  In other words, there were a set of  meetings exclusively for the Distributor stakeholders, and then another set of meetings exclusively for  the Contractor stakeholders and then finally a 3rd set of meetings exclusively for the Property Owner  stakeholders.  Within these groups of stakeholders, we had a diverse group of people, ranging from IT to  sales to marketing to customer support.  By holding 3 different sets of exclusive brainstorming sessions,  we were able to focus on the journey

1_ Challenge and Selection :

Mind mapping is a greet tool that I used every time , it has many uses to solve problems . and I will talk

about an  very important challenge  of this tool this is “ make smarter decisions “ .if you are  facing a

problem and not sure which option to take to overcome it ?  try using the main branches of a mind map

to identify the different options available and explore the possibilities of each option . Mapping out your

options using keywords will trigger associations in your brain and spark further ideas . this will enable

you to analyse each option thoroughly and set yourself up for making the best decision based on all of

the facts . as your brain works creatively towards a solution , drawing out new ideas , you will start to

look at your problem from different angles . we often face problems in thinking about design and

In the past, this has been a difficult problem to solve because there’s no one right answer, and if  one listens to anecdotes from others, there are a multitude of directions to take ecommerce videos.     Selection  I selected mind mapping, which is a design tool that allows someone to take all the data that they have,  distill it into usable data, look for patterns and insights, and translate those into design criteria. I thought  this was appropriate for the challenge of what younger audiences want from ecommerce video because  we have a wealth of data available on this topic – best practices, user-testing, focus groups, years of  analytics, interviews, and more – but we haven’t been able to take all of this data and turn it into  something useful. Mind mapping and its insights should allow us to better visualize and engage with the  data and turn it into useful information that can influence future experiments.     Application  I applied the tool by gathering all the data that we have available at this point – best practices from  experts, user-testing, focus groups, years of analytics, and interviews – and laying it all out. I then invited  a small group of co-workers from my company to help with this project. We picked out nuggets of data  that we each found interesting, then we talked through those interesting points and combined like  points into groups, and then saw what conclusions or insights we could draw. This seemed to be an  effective way to approach a large amount of data that might have otherwise been unwieldy. Ajayi Azubuike Reflection

Challenge & Selection

I am the cofounder and CEO of a new social entrepreneurship called USCG hair care and  extensions. USCG is a hair company that not only sells hair extensions, but also uses products as  a platform to promote breast health awareness to the population of African American women. After  finding out that African American woman face a 40% higher mortality rate due to breast cancer than any  other racial or ethnic group, even though they are not the highest diagnosed group, my cofounder and I  wanted to do something to help lower the rate. We learned that factors like late detection, improper  follow up care, and general access to health resources were a few reasons for the high mortality rate.  We decided to create USCG and use it to spread breast health information to other black  women. This is how USCG was born, we use hair products to serve as an unconventional  avenue of exposure to inform women about breast cancer and breast health information. For every  order that is purchased from USCG, a portion of the proceeds goes to creating better access to  breast health services for African American women. As a new startup, our challenge is spreading the  importance of our message and the value of our mission not only to our consumers, but also to  investors. The hair extension industry is a billion-dollar industry, but it is also a saturated industry with  many hair extension companies already in existence. Our challenge is communicating to investors that  our product is profitable and that our unique business concept will make USCG stand out from  our competitors.

The tool we employed to help us with this challenge was storytelling. MIND MAPPING

Challenge

I am a member of marketing team of my organisation and we are primarily one of the major

dealers of smart phone and mobile accessories. Our challenge is to improve sales as earlier it

was good. We have to identify the probable reasons regarding the sales decline. The project

scope includes competitors, various brands, pricing strategy, etc. We have a good team of

eight (08) salesmen responsible for sales and distribution of different brands of smart phone

and mobile accessories at district, state, and national level.

Selection

Our team has already gone through 10 different tools of Design Thinking, so we are ready to

adopt Mind Mapping tool for addressing the challenge mentioned above. Broadly speaking,

the Mind mapping is an experiential tool which will bring creative ideas from all the team

members to solve the challenge.

Application:

Initially, we have arranged a group activity i.e. brainstorming. We invited all the salesmen

and other team members of marketing department. The aim of this session was to identify

different factors regarding the sales decline.

In the second stage, we filtered all the factors/reasons identified through brainstorming with

the help of strategic marketing team. The team concluded best fitted reasons for the

challenge mentioned above.

Later, each member of the strategic marketing team gave a deep thought and decided to

conduct a customer survey to validate the identified factors. The survey was including

various questions related to brand preference, price affordability, features, VAS, etc. and

conducted within 15 days time duration.

Insight

By applying the Mind Mapping, it was found that the customer’s view were 80% common

with the factors identified during brainstorming activity. It also resulted in change of

preferences as major factor for the sales decline. It is found from the survey data analysis

that most of the customers have started preferring the new smartphones and related

Visualization

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding

of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define

possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers, who are government

agencies working to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their

services to their customer, which may be U.S. citizens, businesses, and non-citizens. I have used the

technique of using a straw man visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for

discussion to allow a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining

the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying

pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.

Application

I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw man

graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing

material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, GAO or

other auditing reports. If materials are not available, then I conduct informal interviews with one-three

of the stakeholders who serve as my main points of contact on the initiative.

If appropriate to the situation, I will borrow the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from previous

research, and discussed in David Gray’s book, “The Connected Company”. The front-stage/back-stage

approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service – even an internal service – has customers

with whom the service provider interacts and internal processes that enable the organization to provide

Sensitivity: Internal & Restricted

Challenge

The organization, for which I work, is an IT service provider, but apart from services, lately one of the  strategic focusses is creating more IPs. IPs can be source of non-linear revenue for the growth for the  organization. The challenge in front of my team was to utilize a technology platform to create new IP  products. Hence, the immediate problem was to identify the use cases, which can be conceptualized on  the platform.

To achieve that, our team conducted a 2 day long workshop, where we invited people of different  domains – healthcare, energy & utilities, banking & finance, retail etc under one roof. The group had to  discuss the problems in their domain. By the end of day 2, the group was to identify a few indicative use  cases, which can be developed.

Selection

I selected Visualization tool for facilitating the discussion. Visualization tool is one the simplest and most  intuitive tools for design thinking. It is about putting thoughts in form of simple visuals, which can be as  simple as a hand-drawn circle. Visualization tool is well explained in the Visualisation tool video at link  https://www.coursera.org/learn/uva-darden-design-thinking-innovation/home/week/1.

I used this tool as we were at the preliminary stage of the engagement. People had gathered from  diverse domains and varied technical expertise. They had different ways of expressing themselves.  Everyone was expressing same ideas in different manner, so visualization tool was required to give  discussion a direction.

Application

At the start of the workshop, I reiterated the objectives and deliverables of the workshop. I wrote them  on a chart paper and pasted in the conference room, so that people can go back to the agenda  whenever, there is a deviation.

text:
Embedding Learning Launch in Online Pedagogy

Challenge:

COVID 19 pandemic has forced us to bring some substantial changes in our life and one such  change is in the way we teach and learn in schools. Normal classes were suspended in most of  the educational institutes across India from March 2020. Since we started the new academic  session in April 2020, classes are held on online platforms due to lockdown and social  distancing norms. As everyone was caught unawares by this pandemic, no school was prepared  with an e-learning pedagogy. The result is, everyone is in the race to transform and convert a  conventional pedagogy designed for an on-campus physical classroom to the virtual mode using  various online platforms. This poses a major challenge in imparting effective learning keeping in  mind the holistic development of the child. This is also aggravated by the digital divide that  exists in our society.

As an educator, in addition to teaching my subject, I have to keep in mind the co-scholastic and  other learning outcomes which are imparted to the students through co- curricular and extra- curricular activities in the campus in pre-COVID 19 era. Both scholastic as well as co-scholastic  development of a learner in online mode of teaching and learning process requires not only a  pedagogy suitable for the e-learning ecosystem, but also a paradigm shift in our approach to  learn virtually. This would take time for all the stakeholders. Students and teachers alike are  making an earnest effort and it is pertinent at this point of time not to ignore the holistic  development of the child. Time will only unfold whether our efforts have been well directed  towards overcoming these hurdles to the desired extent. Could Learning Launch be the  panacea? Let us find out.

VISUALIZATION

CHALLENGE AND SELECTION

Visualization has always been my first step in tackling a problem. My father always told me to sit back  and think with a calm mind before acting upon a situation. Clam and collected mind leads to  visualization of solution one wouldn’t come up with if the situation is thought up with stress and tension  to find a solution ASAP. First idea is not always the best. I use visualization in most of the task I’m given,  it makes my thoughts more organize and doesn’t leave space for doubt in my decision making.

APPLICATION

I got admission in a design college amidst covid, and being an extroverted person, I got in contact with  my college mentors online as soon as I could. After making a name for myself in their eyes, they started  including me in certain problems relating to interaction among mentors and freshmen, freshmen and  seniors and even among batchmates themselves. Since everything was virtual and there was no way for  us to get to know our batchmates and seniors, it became an issue. They asked for my opinion on this and  told me to come up some ideas that could bridge the gap between our college students. This gave me a  perfect platform to apply visualization on a much larger scale, so far I had only made decision  individually and just for myself.

INSIGHT

The challenge in hand needed a wider perspective of communication, it would have been easy to get  make a group online and let students interact, but that’s just futile on so many levels. One, having the  whole batch or the whole department student in one or two groups would not lead to any beneficial  interaction, there would be 500+ messages on group every hour and it would probably be just the same  kids talking. It would also become difficult to segregate useful information from casual information. text:
Challenge & Selection

I work in the energy industry in the area of billing. We have many different customers who  send us their electricity consumption. Sometimes digital, sometimes by letter or phone, or  sometimes we send employees over to read the electricity meter. It is a multitude of linear  and rigid processes. Customers can be industrial customers, families or older people who can  hardly hear or move. We need the correct data from all these customers as quickly as  possible. Unfortunately, this often doesn't work. Delays, incorrect readings, incorrect  invoices occur or communication fails. In order to modernize this entire accounting process,  you first need a deep and comprehensive understanding of the problem. Which customer  groups have which problems where? When? Which process steps can you revise? What are  the customers' needs?

First of all, the entire process must be recorded here. With all the steps and customers. An  overview is required to define the relationships and interfaces. That is why the visualization  tool is used here. The customer groups and their relationships and the associated problems  and needs are identified here using diagrams, mind maps and post-actual customers and  arrows.

Application

To understand where the problems lie and where the customers' needs are, I paint the  entire process on the board. The beginning is a small drawing of an electricity meter. The  various customer groups are already divided here with arrows. Household customers (single,  family, pensioners), industry and trade. Various arrows lead to the absence here. This takes  care of the readings, which in turn come to us for billing. Two columns are created under  each intersection and each customer group. One for the problem, one for the need.

REFLECTION - LEARNING LAUNCH

CHALLENGE:

I am a Loan Officer and a Marketing Representive at a rural branch for one of the largest commercial banks  in my country. My challenge is marketing our Cash Secured loan product to customers who have existing  savings accounts with balances that qualifies them for the product and we decided that the best way to do  this was via the telephone. This product entails lending customers for any specific purpose by holding the  cash in their account as collateral. There has been a decline in this product and management has requested  that more emphasis be placed on it since there is little to no risk involved in this type of lending. The scope  of the project includes the Loan Department which consist of four (4) staff who are also the Marketing  Representatives of the branch and also the IT Department who will be gathering the data (e.g. name of  customers, account balance, occupation and telephone numbers) from the core banking system. The project  should not exceed more that 10 days and is limited to internal resources. We will try to reach out to as many  eligible customers as possible and try to perceive how effective this method has proved to be.

SELECTION:

Our team has unanimously decided that the best design thinking tool to use for this project is the learning  launch tool since this is an experiment meant to quickly and inexpensively test an idea and prototype so as  to gather market-driven data to determine whether a growth idea has enough merit to warrant detailed  investigation with the commitment of further time, people and resources.

APPLICATION:

Using the learning launch tool, our team allocated two hours each day to contact customers via the telephone  using the data gathered by the IT Department. The  challenge is to create a unified process for all these departments, which is not only employee-friendly  but also effective in bringing expected outcomes with utmost accuracy.

To bring the best solution for all the departments, I have opted for the visualization tool, which includes  creating a task process for all the departments. Visualization is the key to think rethink and rearrange  ideas/imagination at the same time, which is essential to deliver the best result.

with the accuracy of the result.

A Marketing Company was owned by an emergent Electrical Distribution Company, the  company assigned marketing managers to lift up the sales of the forth factory on a  specific project “Smart Home Utilities”, The problem was that by creating new campaigns,  they found out that it had already been used before (on discounts, maintenance offers and  contracts expansions), and still the linear drop of sales continuous. The Unclear problem identification (is it the Product? Market? Competitors dominance?)  led up to brainstorming many possibilities and solutions mapped with the greater goal -  Sales Acceleration. In the short amount of time that was assigned to this project there  was only Facts and User Centred Guesses ( User needs focused and NOT Product/User  Opinions on a product). No Market/Product Research Conducted.

text:
Mind Mapping to solve online rural education during COVID 19 in Peru

Challenge

In Perú we have a rural population almost entirely disconnected of the world. Almost 90% of rural  population does not have access to Wi-Fi: this due to the plains, mountains and difficult access  accompanied by the neglection of the government. During the pandemic, all schools closed and the  only alternative to continue all children´s education was through TV or online classes.

Peruvian public education is low quality, so the scarce quantity of families in poor areas who had  smartphones or TV received 3-4 hours of class in only two subjects: math and communication. This  classes were not personalized, and children ended up with many questions and were unable to  understand nor learn at all.

A group of young university students, including me, had the idea to create a program to give tutoring  sessions to kids in really poor areas through our smartphones. “Por un Perú Mejor”- (For a better  Peru, in English) At first, we thought the whole organization would be easy, but after a few weeks  we created a page in Facebook and Instagram hundreds of parents contacted us for free tutoring  lessons on many subjects. We needed to create a new way to manage all this information of children  entering to the program and, we needed to include more tutor volunteers and manage them  correctly, like a real NGO.

Selection

As we learned at Unit 3 of this course, Mind Mapping is a useful tool to find patterns among wide  amounts of data. Having many inputs on the educative problems many Peruvian children were  having during online classes, making mind maps within the organizational leaders of our  organization, we were able to group ideas and solutions to manage better the children and  volunteers to better help children learn adequately.

text:
Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge:

My challenge was one that fit perfectly within the criteria for one of the tools.  I work for an  organization that is building a new software for our industry.  It is a very complex and in-depth tool,  which looks to streamline the profession while providing an overall more effective product.  This project  has around 40 different people working on it, all in different capacities.  My role is designing much of the  methodology around the specific items which will make this tool “cutting-edge”.  As such, the elements  that my team and I design do not exist in any other tool today, therefore we must solve problems that  no other tool has been able to do.  One module in particular has plagued the industry for years, and has  effectively been set aside for the past year because of the complexity.  It was my job to figure it out.

Since  there were so many different elements, I chose the Mind Map as a way to gather all of my thoughts and  used it to identify patterns and themes.

text:
VISUALIZATION TOOL FOR DESIGNING A MAGAZINE

CHALLENGE-

The tool I used was the Visualization, or also known as Visual Thinking, to achieve a similar  thought process among a group of my college-mates. I use this approach often with my college  staffs and friends to make them understand my vision and to help me for creating something  extraordinary. I was appointed as the department head for the editorial team for the  department magazine. The challenge I was given was to deliver a magazine in 13 days with a  team consisting of 8 members. With the given short period of time, I had to make each and  every one of them to understand the problem and start working towards our common vision.

SELECTION-

Visualization  is any technique for creating images, diagrams, or animations to communicate a  message or to describe a vision. Visualization through visual imagery has been an effective way  to communicate between a group of individuals. It can be a drawing created by hand or digitally  showing what something will look like when created. They are used to plan for still images or  products and can be a rough sketch or a detailed final design.

APPLICATION-

I decided to gather the group around and made them sit in pair of two. To each pair I gave them  a sheet of paper with the problem and the thing that needed to be done. They responded by  adding their points. After getting their feedbacks and suggestions, I presented them few  pictures, videos and diagrams on board to make them understand the plan to finish the work in  such short duration.

INSIGHT-

The use of verbal communication or posting texts would have made it almost impossible for my  team to completely understand my vision and plan and finish the work in such short span of  time. By using the Visualization technique I was able to make them clearly understand the  situation and start working towards the plan, and within the short span of time, we completed  the magazine and were able to present it. So, the challenge is how to overcome this and  figure out what really matters to the client beforehand.

In the lesson on the Mind Mapping  tool from week three, Angelica Martinez showed what Mind Mapping is all about. And I learned that it’s  a great tool take all the information available and collaboratively shape an understanding of the  current reality and, as a team, deep dive into what the essence of the problem is. I believe that Mind  Mapping could help in specifying the current state at the beginning of an engagement and would  therefore solve my challenge.

text:
Storytelling

Challenge & Selection    I had no idea why people fail although they have a valid, let say “working” projects till I explore  the power of storytelling. As an entrepreneur, I spend most of my time by telling our project to  people in social events. The more I speak about the project, the less convincing it gets. The  reason behind it, I’m telling the details and I assume (unintentionally) that people are already  aware of the problem and the solution that we are working on. After a while, it’s beginning to be  like a lecture that people are checking their watches hoping it finishes. As Elias Ramirez states,  storytelling ​is about the connection that we give to people about a piece of information that we're  trying to share. It’s all different from giving a formula but rather it touches the feeling which you are  trying to solve.Storytelling is a big part of the product not a side dish so one can reach to more  people with a less functional product with a good story. Therefore I decided to use storytelling as a  strategy to gather people to share the same passion for our project and our solution.    Application    As I stated before, I’m an entrepreneur and our main goal is to reach a fund to be able to  continue product development and let the company survive. In addition to that, since we have a  final product, our other targets are customers. Both investors and customers need to  understand the product first. However, it’s not sufficient, customers should feel that they need  our product and investors should be convinced that society needs our product.     As a vertical farming company, we were talking about the technology behind our home type  vertical farming units. How it makes you grow vegetables, what’s automated and how all of  these things are possible in your living room. We have pages of documents, lots of slides and  scripts to tell. text: Challenge:   Working to champion a number of innovative ICT based solutions to tackle gender based violence, I was  tasked to achieve the unison among a myriad of stakeholders to select some of distinctly themed ideas for  learn launching.    Selection:  The first tool that I used was mind mapping. The tool inevitability links up with visual thinking. It is always  better than using words when brainstorming, asking questions and connecting ideas. Mind mapping makes  visual thinking come alive, that is why I chose it. The tool also allows a smooth fusion of other great design  thinking tools; I was able to fuse in ethnography via storytelling, and journey mapping.    It starts with a single idea that is represented with text, colour or image. Each idea presented with one single  word or any visual elements to categorize it. More subsidiary ideas are added around the main idea and  interconnected by lines. Unified hierarchy styles are then able to be easily implemented through the mind  map.     Application:   During the brainstorming meetings we had held with developers about the general problem of GBV, many  outputs were shared and presented in fractals. These ideas were prepared into a portfolio of napkin pitches.  The intent was to allow for co creation by joining a two dozen team representing diverse demographics and  introduce them to this portfolio in order to champion the best ideas for prototyping and eventually learn  launching.  The stakeholder team was given some homework that involved them reflecting about some of  their GBV experiences to prepare them for a story telling session later on.    We organised a simple exhibition for the stakeholders. This was without much attention to how the  exhibition’s physical set up would influence the human engagement. We did brief the exhibitors on how to  interact with the stakeholders without imposing their ideas. We allowed our stakeholders to wander  through the exhibition at their own pace and pick out the ideas
