text: Student: Maria Amin  Coursera: Design Thinking for Innovation, Maria Amin, UVA    Challenge:  The design thinking tool I chose from the Design Thinking course was storytelling.  This is a  skill I have wanted to improve as some of the most successful consultants I work with are great  storytellers.  Traditionally, the way we sell consulting within our service line is to identify the client's  current issues and demonstrate our group’s capabilities to address them.  We needed to change the way  we told our group's consulting story.  A story that moves from a capabilities to character-driven  approach that all team members could tell and customers wanted to hear.     Selection: Our consulting sales practice is based on developing relationships based on high value and  trust.  As a result, I chose storytelling as a tool to build on connecting with clients in the way Design  Thinking week 2 lecture described it “as a way to make a strategy relate-able, to give it color, life,  through character and plot." The lecture finally gave me a framework to build a story, develop suspense,  and create a seemingly simple answer.  I believe this simplicity is a key to building trust and developing  relationships with clients.       Application:  I began with white-boarding the steps of storytelling with a colleague in a two-hour design  thinking session. We sectioned off parts of the walls with the 5 areas:  main character, sell the challenge,  fellowship, tensions, and a path to move forward.  From a host of different characters, we started with  our main character as Valerie, a high level executive and a potential customer, tasked by her CEO with a  new annual goal to create a digital strategy to increase revenue for her business unit. We brainstormed  all the different ways Valerie could try to achieve this goal utilizing different colored sticky notes. text:
I used storytelling to try and get my idea across to a group of people I wanted to  help me start a food pantry for pets.  As a writer, I’ve used stories my whole life  and so that technique is most natural to me when I’m trying to influence or  simply communicate.  I used the stories of animals and their down-and-out  caregivers to try tug on the heartstrings of prospective stakeholders.

There were many times I tried to use storytelling – some with success and some  without.  I used one story about my own dog coming from a woman in the  south who had to give him up because she could no longer afford him.  This  worked on a few of the people I spoke with and they donated to the program.

One thing I learned is that some people are not interested in stories – only facts  and profits.  Those types of people are too hard to me to communicate with.

For things I’d change next time, the first would be practicing emotional  detachment, for one.  I can’t understand how people don’t want to help others  in their community keep their animals – especially if they are well off.  I would  also try and pick the tool according to my audience and know my audience well  before speaking with them.

text:
Stephanie Gonzalez

Storytelling Reflection

Challenge

I work at a Transnational huge company where Design Thinking is now part of the business  strategy; the company has managed to adapt Design Thinking to its own business so it can focus  in the users that really matter and in the type of business it offers. As this is a huge company  every center in each country had to start learning and applying Design Thinking and as change  is never easy but always good, in my country I was part of the leadership that was bringing Design  Thinking to everybody’s lives.

I started with education and it was naturally becoming known and used among my peers;  however, there was an important challenge in all the business processes when applying Design  Thinking as the framework it is; and the challenge was: How can we engage with our clients so  we can also design better experiences in the solutions we offer to them, including team  involvement, workshop management, projects and more.

Selection

I selected then Storytelling because I think telling a story is the best approach to get someone not  only to pay attention to something, but to understand and act with purpose and it was just what  was needed. This tool allowed every client real or potential and every person interested in  applying Design Thinking with their clients to actually had a guide on how to really engage.

Application

I got together with a group of other four Design Thinkers as passionate as me and with their  support a Playbook was created. This Playbook is a document that is now available for all of the  employees of the company I work for and intends to help any other team in the world that wants  to use Design Thinking to achieve a great engagement with their clients. In the playbook it is first  specified that a group of people working together is always necessary and that in our case we  received also guidance and strategic support from an Executive of the company. We also defined  the tasks of this team.

Challenge

In my organization, I work within IT helping tie together IT strategy with Business strategy to deliver  results.  I am often challenged with the role of “translator” by making clear to sales associates what  capabilities are offered on an IT side and making business goals clear to more technical IT resources that  are charged with delivering technical solutions.

In a recent example that occurred while I was taking this course, we were tasked with reimagining what  some of our financial reporting could look like.  The challenge was to allow business to clearly articulate  the problem while also working within the constraints of what is possible while also showing what is  additionally available outside of standard table like reporting that has historically been done at our  company in this space.

Selection

For this particular problem we chose Visualization.  While we used multiple tools throughout the  process, I feel the most helpful tool was visualization.  We chose this because from the start we could  work with our business stakeholders to document user journeys.  It was important for us to visualize  form the beginning what kinds of users were going to be using this financial dashboard and what were  their expected results.

Application

We started by mapping a flow chart that visualized multiple user types accessing the same legacy  financial chart, exporting it to excel, and performing their own individual analysis to get their own value  out of the data.  Through this journey mapping visualization tool, we were able to visually map out each  of these journeys showing what each user type needed from the dashboard.

Visualization

Challenge & Selection

I am a researcher and within my group we gather a lot of scientific data which we deem as important.  Most of the time, scientific data from experiments turns out to be a lot of numbers, which includes  many complicated names and processes. Therefore, for many of the co-workers, this data can be very  confusing and consequently, the focus within the group gets lost easily. This poses a challenge, since  these stakeholders also should have a say of what the company should be going forward with, as well  as be informed of the company’s activity in a way that is understandable. This causes some challenge  when it comes to communication between parts of the company.

For this essay I have chosen the tool of Visualization. Visualization involves principals in which data  can be presented in clear visual representations to enhance the uptake of content. As Angela Myer  mentions in her visualization lecture from this course, you do not have artistic and drawing for  visualization, but visual thinking. Visualization is quite broad, and its purpose is to communicate  information or a message can be used in an infinite matter. These include animations, diagrams,  animations and pictures. Visualization is good for many different projects, for this specific project it  would be great due to the difficulty in the scientific content and large data that is involved, in which  you have to know a lot of the research to even understand much of the results. This is why we would  use visualization to make all our stakeholders understand how our current research is going.

text:
Learning Launch

Challenge

I work for the bank. Historically we have two schemes for serving clients in our branches. For retail  clients we have a big desk with 4-5 employees. But for corporate client we have only 1 person, who  serve them. It had done because corporate clients usually do their operations via Internet and couriers.  Our managers can go to their offices for discussing new products. We did not need a big space for them  in the branch. However, 3 years ago, we have started to work with small companies and entrepreneurs,  which need to go to the bank more often, than large corporate companies do. They have not couriers,  and they cannot pay money for collection of their cash from the shops to the bank. What happened?  We have started observing situation then we have a free staff on the retail desk, but there is a queue to  the corporate manager. Retail and corporate desks have different IT programs, and different products  and services, different learning processes for our stuff. Our bank has about 400 branches. We had not a  lot of money to find new offices for our branches. It was our challenge. What to do in this situation.

We have an idea to teach our retail staff to serve corporate clients. Therefore, when we have a free staff  on the retail desk he could serve a corporate client. Our hypothesis was that It will reduce queues.  However, we have a lot of technology limitations and fears about our staff – can they remember a lot of  things in their mind, may be they will do a lot of mistakes? And our corporate clients will complain about  it? Some members of our team want to make a big project about unification IT platform, which will  prompt to our staff what to do. We understand that it will be a big investment, and we really did not  know how we could create this new program (maybe we need to take retail program and upgrade it  with corporate functions or quite the contrary). What if our hypothesis is not right and our fears is true?

Reflection - Visualization

Challenge

I'm a student of bachelor program visual communication, that is why visualization is the most used tool of design thinking for me. This is a quite wide program and diversity of skills, which gives university for us limitlessly. To make up books and magazines I would like too much. Visualization can help to start thinking about the size of the book, content and fonts that I can use there and the emotion, which I want to hand over with my design. I have one example, I must do visual research and make it up like a multi-page edition, and this task was not easy for me, because at the start i didn’t imagine what book I would do as a result.

Selection

I decided to start with the common actions to find some references in verified Internet resources and in printed books in bookshops. By chance I found some interesting conceptual things, which inspired me.

Application

The topic of my visual research was comparison between monumental propaganda in the Soviet Union and the present time. This theme was quite specific, that was a problem to find suitable references at the start of the process. I don’t want to copy soviet encyclopedias, and the differences between materials didn’t allow me to do a clear catalog. Reflection – Man Man Kwok  Challenge and selection

I have once ran a workshop to help a church organization to understand the way Jesus taught about how  He means about His real family, the values he treasured and preached, and how He organized His disciples  to form the very first Christian Church. All the 8 participants were Christians, and they sought for a deeper  understanding on the teaching of Jesus and connect to their daily lives experiences. They were from  different backgrounds, including secondary school teacher, scientist at laboratory, clerical workers,  freelancers, student and a blind man.      Since concepts of family relationships, values and organizations are abstract ideas, I chose “visual thinking”  to gather the thoughts and insights of the participants, and make sure they are on the same page.

Application    I make use of “post-it” note (sticky note) to gather the thoughts of the participants. I asked them to write  (or draw) on each note one “character” in a family (i.e. “father”, “son”, “grandparent”, etc) in a general  perspective. The ideas were first clustered and then I ask them to organize the “characters” into a chart of  family tree on white board. It revealed that, in general perspective, Chinese people have an extended  family concept and think that there are at least three level of hierarchy in family (grandparents, parents and  kids). They also pointed out that the center of a family belongs to the parents, and the Father is always the

central commander who possesses most of the authority. So, we drew a set of concentric circle in which  parents is the center.

1. Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a useful tool in both industry and research. I used this tool to describe my Ph.D. research at  conferences and symposiums. Ph.D. students usually face challenges when presenting their research  because the research is usually based on a detailed problem or an abstract concept that could be difficult  to describe, especially if the presentation is addressed to an audience different than academia. The  success of research is based on identifying new knowledge that must contributed to the advances of  science. My research was titled “Framework addressed to financial analysis of solution architectures  considering uncertainty and flexibility”. When my audience read the thesis’s title, few people were  interested in hearing more about the research. Most of them ran away because it sounded complicated.  It was hard to describe my research during the first years of my Ph.D. until I learned about Storytelling.  Then, I used stories to illustrate the different steps of my research as well as the results of using the  proposed framework.

2. Application

To use Storytelling, I created stories based on real businesses that helped me to describe the problem,  objectives, strategy, and research proposal. I used a specific case of a Healthcare company that needed  to invest in a new Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system to achieve its business objectives  and maintain alignment with its business strategy. The stories were written with simple words and graphs  that were associated with the main concepts (solution architecture, financial analysis, uncertainty, and  flexibility). The stories were described step by step presenting the connections between the concepts. I  took my audience through a timeline, where the problems and risks were showed clearly. 1. Challenge

In order to shorten commutes, save gas, reduce emissions and enhance the mental well being of residents of  Virginia I would like to work with VDOT to better time traffic signals to maximize efficiency.  The ability to track  vehicle, pedestrian and bicycle traffic and adapt traffic control to increase traffic flow while ensuring multimodal  safety is critical and possible given the advancement in technology.  My cell phone hardware has the video and  processing power to easily solve this problem.    Why hasn’t it been done?

2. Selection

I chose Storytelling for the tool to convey the need for Smart Traffic Controls.  The section of the class describing  how executives sit in an office all day waiting to hear something that compels them motivated me to try an  approach which I have never used, but thought I could learn something from trying a new technique.  The  notion that presenters only get 20% of a person’s attention during their pitch impacted me to try using  storytelling to inspire, “to make this challenge a cause”.

3. Application

At the next Fairfax County Transportation Advisory Committee meeting, I would like to submit the following  (fictitious) story:

No one knew why Daniel Q Schneider killed himself in the early morning hours on July 10, 2020.  He was found  in his car with a bullet in his head, in his driveway after his work shift was over.  Daniel was a good man, honest  and hard-working.  What could have possibly driven him to this point?   He had always been interested in  technology, had lots of computers, electronic toys, video games, even a 3D printer.  The last was the catalyst for  his ultimate demise having produced the 3D gun that ended his life.  His family was aware of his mental  downward slide but had no idea of the depths of his despair. Example Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection  I work as a Global Marketing Manager and Creative Strategist for a South Korean tech company  and our mission is to market our group communication app in the US and generate an active  user community. Our product is a utility - something that is handy and solves the everyday small  problems of group communication. This is the challenge as we are not a super innovative  news-worthy product that is easier to get people’s attention and to market effectively. This is  where I selected ‘Storytelling’ as a tool to create marketing campaigns that worked.         Application   We advertise our app on social where content is king and people are there to be entertained or  to find knowledge that is useful to their lives. When we advertised with ad creatives that were  dry and simply explained the various features it had, the ad campaigns had very poor  performance. People are not computers that are just looking for information - they are emotional  beings who have jobs, families, beliefs, and values. This is why storytelling is so powerful. In  order to create better ad creatives, I first researched our target audience to understand what  they think, feel, and value in their lives - and also how they communicate with their group. With  these insights, I began to script and produce ad creatives that have a narrative element relevant  to the target audience’s lives. This could be a situation they faced in their daily lives or a strong  belief they held. Storytelling was carefully considered in both the visual and copywriting parts of  the ad. Visually, people can relate to the things and scenes that they see everyday, Also if those  things are portrayed in an intriguing visual style it will help to catch people’s attention while they  fast scroll through their social feed. We recognized that peoples’ shopping behavior in pharmaceutical stores are changing. In Hungary,  these stores are still following the old styles when the industry lacked advertisements and people  either purchased the prescribed medicine, or asked for a medicine telling his or her problem or sickness  and the competition was low. However, today we are being overwhelmed with TV advertisement,  billboards and so on, offering us a discount on medicines and brands competing heavily against each  other. Our challenge was to uncover peoples’ behavior and problems and align drugstores to these.

SELECTION

I selected the visualization tool. This tool is a way of visually representing somebody’s thought or idea.  It includes drawings itself, but also colors, charts, diagrams, contexts, interrelations, etc. Talking about  something can be misleading, as everybody has a slightly different way of understanding things. Visual  representation  of  an  idea  helps  participant  to  achieve  a  common  understanding.

I selected this tool to understand or customers’ problems. This is one of the first stages in the process.  As the video lecturer stated: “when the environment to solve problems is dependent on other people  being able to understand you and align their ideas to yours”. Mutual understanding on a problem is a  prerequisite to proceed on solving it.

The secondary stakeholders comprises of  Operations team, Estate Management, Deployment, Technology & Telecom operators. Hence  focus is required on increasing the Partner Satisfaction which is all time low in current situation.    Selection

Since Mind Mapping tool looks for patterns & insights in the large set of data, it generates creativity  between common minds, it helps generating new design criteria & creates insights before What if. Broadly  speaking, it shall help us to get an insight on low partner satisfaction index & shall help us to establish  criteria for What if Idea Generation Phase.

EXAM REFLECTION – STORYTELLING

Good Morning to One and All,

So I have decided to write my reflection on Storytelling.

CHALLENGE

Storytelling can be used as a method to teach ethics, values and cultural norms to  everyone. It is that one word which brings interest to everyone. I am a student  doing my Bachelors in Commerce, as an individual I am a person who is very  scared of speaking in front of huge gatherings but now as I have many challenges  in my college where I should not only speak in front of everyone but also be bold  enough to face it. In the beginning, that is when I was in my first year I was very  scared and stammered a lot and was very anxious. It took me a lot of time to  overcome this but I had to figure out something, that is when I came up with  storytelling. I feel this one is different from the others. The word ‘story’ only gives  people different kind of excitement. This type can be used by anyone, anywhere  because you can talk to your elders telling them a story which would even involve  them and make them feel that they have someone or even speak to your  classmates by giving them an example and making them understand what I would  like to say. This particular aspect “Storytelling” would make us stand apart from  the others.

“Storytelling is the most powerful way to put ideas into the world and in action  these days.”

SELECTION

The reason I chose “Storytelling” from the other design thinking tools is because I  feel that this would help any person and let them connect with the topic and  understand the content which we would like to express without any conflicts and  confusions. It would even help them involve and guide us if any changes are  needed. The story that I heard from my professor about IBM was very nice and  interesting and at the end while choosing my tool for reflection I didn’t have any  second thoughts because this was apt for my way of learning and conveying  things to others.

NEGOTIATION SKILLS VIA MOTIVATION

Challenge & Selection:  Motivate and involve team for better profitability and customer  understanding. As there was a lack of involvement and better knowledge on customer, team  was struggling to earn better profits. Need some tool to make them understand on learning  negotiation and customer. STORY TELLING as a tool which can solve this issue of understanding  and seriousness by better involvement. The same is used for this experiment.

Application:

I have used two common stories.

 First story is about learning of human attitude towards negotiation. Arrived from daily

experience of negotiation with vegetable vendor in India. Whenever we go for buying  vegetables, we always go for the fresh vegetable (Good product), while buying the same  we will cross check the price of the product with other vendors and will ask the ( Good  product) vendor to match the lowest price. Though effective saving with vegetable  vendor is not much but it’s more related to human behavior on negotiation. The  learning here is, the customer is likely to negotiate with us on our good quality services  with poor pricing and we need to find the way out. It’s on customer buying behavior.

 Second story is of two car salesman. One salesman has offered a better price, but have

not done any follow up with the client. He was not even bothered to know what is the  customer requirement and is happy to give the best price. Whereas second salesmen in  this story take complete input from customer about need, members in family involved,  who all will drive car, more likely parameters on customer empathy. That helped him in  suggesting best suited vehicle. He also gone extra mile to visit his home with the  suitable vehicle and make customer understood why he should go for the model which  will be more suitable. text: Challenge and Selection     I am currently pursuing my MBA in Human Resource Development and during the course, I  got an opportunity to work with Hobby Buddy, as a Learning and Development Intern for the Asia  Pacific Region. The challenge that I faced during this tenure was I had to prepare a case study  illustrating the recent cultural transformation that organization went through in a form of  case study which will also depict certain situations that rose from it. So, I chose Storytelling  as my method of choice, because I felt that it would be very convenient for the people on the  receiving end if they could get the entire content in a way which would be easy for them to  consume and understand. More importantly, I was going to make this Case for people across  18 Asian countries with varying cultures and backgrounds. Hence, Storytelling felt like the  most appropriate choice.     Application    I started my journey with drawing up a story that most of the employees would relate to in  the organization. But I was told by my manager to not use the company name or figures. So,  I created a fake organization and kept it in the similar businesses as ours to create a sense of  belongingness amongst the recipients. After that, I moved to creating the core values of the  organization and framed the general structure for the case study. I used certain aspects of  visualization in my approach as well. I took help from my team mates as I gave them roles to  play which corresponded to the main characters of my case.  This helped me in gathering a clear sense of what aspects I needed to keep in my case. And  not just that it had to be converted into an animation video before it was sent to the  employees.     I paid attention to how context operates in different cultures and incorporated that into my  final work. I feel that this project would not have turned out the way it did, if not for what  little I knew about design thinking and various techniques used for the same.

During this COVID-19 lockdown, it is obvious to avoid touch things by bare hands and maintaining  hygiene of washing hands frequently. With the help of Design thinking, during this lockdown, I came  out with an innovative solution for my office and home, to open the doors by a foot.

Challenge & Selection:

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a common  understanding of a problem among the group of users at home and my office before attempting to  identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often to find solutions to  various problems in day to day activities. Starting with innovations to modernize and invent new  product quality improvements and new products for business requirements.

I have used the technique of foot operated door opening using visualization of a problem with a set  of questions or prompts for discussion to allow my family members to learn from each other in the  process of defining the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to  consider when identifying pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.

In a scenario where a person walks in home from outside, he or she uses hands to open the door.  Assuming his/her hands are not safe to easily open the door handle. What to do? Perhaps, if the  door is already unlocked, they could press foot pedal under the door to open the door. This is a  spectacularly simple idea that for a number of people could be helpful. And no interface required!

text:
Example reflection-Visualisation

Challenge and Selection-

One challenge within an organization is to develop new innovative products and services and

present them to the market. These products must be developed in an economical and

sustainable way. They must also answer a desire or need on the market, be technologically

and organizationally feasible and financially viable (Brown, 2009). Design competency in

organizations can help to improve the processes of creating innovative, sustainable products

and services. A typical design process includes generic steps such as the identification of

needs, idea generation and conceptual design, detailed product design, the preparation of

production and design of production system, production, marketing and delivery. Defined

generic design phases include Idea and Concept Design, Product Design and System Design.

These phases often differ from each other in objectives and approaches but have the design

concept in common. Another aspect these phases share is the use and need of visual

communication.

Application-

Visualisation is a core component of the way that we communicate, whether we're aware of it

or not. When we're dealing with very complex problems, we're enacting a different kind of

problem solving that has to bring in more than just logic. Visualisation is really important for

the process of Design Thinking because it's actually a way of unlocking a different part of our

brain. It allows us to think in a non-verbal way and access parts of our brain, our creativity.

Most design thinkers call visualisation as “the mother of all design tools”, because they are

used in every stage of the design thinking process.

Visualisation is equal parts listening, thinking and drawing. Listening is the input, thinking is

the processing and drawing is the output. These three skills work together equally in

understanding complexity, visualising outcomes to create new possibilities.

1. 1. My Three Key Learnings froM Design thinking innovation: Don’t be afraid to fail. Failure makes you think about your ideas in a different way. It helps you to go on other paths of exploring. Empathy. I got a real understanding about how using empathy can aid in solving problems. Using empathy when interviewing someone made me focus in on the small aspects of solving things by talking to people and listening to what they had to say. Ideate. I learned how to brainstorm in a better and more fruitful way. Thinking about coming up with ideas from different vantage points was a real insight. Often, I rely on ideas that are the most obvious, but my prototype ideas came from thinking like a 5-year old.

3. reflection on how To apply Design Thinking To My workplace: I work in a creative services office composed of designers, writers, photographers, and videographers. While we do practice brainstorming, Design Thinking gave me insights on how to make those sessions more fruitful. We did have a brainstorm meeting during my second week of taking this class. I made everyone stand up and use post-it notes to help us with our ideas. And it worked! Standing provides a more interactive environment than sitting and posting ideas to a white board encouraged further interactivity among the team. Design Thinking made me want to share the ideas I learned in the course and how I could apply it to improve our problem-solving processes. text:
Design Thinking at Pixar and Disney

By Ashok Sharma

Challenge:

Creating stories that touch people’s hearts.

Selection:

The tool of and storytelling has been selected since this is about movies. Storytelling can be really  powerful and compelling. It can inspire many others with a proper message. It’s important to  understand the skill of persuasion and emotional intelligence which influence people. Every heart- touching story inspires others. Pixar and Disney are known for such heart-touching stories which  inspire people.

Application:

Ratatouille is a film about Remy, a small, rat with a blue coat. Remy dreams to be a big chef in  Paris. Ratatouille was a massive international commercial success because of its unique and heart- touching story. Pixar and Disney always come up with ingenious stories that touches people’s  hearts. How do they do it? It is through R&D in a collaborative and iterative environment.  However, the process isn’t as simple as is sounds.   All stories at Pixar and Disney start as a part of a 3-idea pitch. After spending almost five months  crafting pitches for all three separate project ideas, each director from the core team presents them  to the Chief Creative Officer (CCO). The CCO then is bound to select one of them to be the next  project, or asks the directors to reiterate the idea and pitch it again.   Once an idea is selected, it enters the R&D process which takes up to one year. The purpose of this  phase is to deepen the original story idea from the proposed pitch. Multi-disciplinary R&D groups  direct topical examination, making reels with cuts from a wide assortment of movies set up with a  good soundtrack. With time, the story rooms are filled with images and notes covering the walls for  the director and creative team to take inspiration from.

Reflection - Storytelling

Does not matter if you have to use embellished and  improvised stories, or just facts, it all depend on who will be your audience, and what is your  goals. I  am used to engage them to every activities we have to do, and also to stimulate their  imagination. But even that, sometimes still being a challenge to manage it. Every audience  have a different experience of life, a different goal, and especially, different perspective. So  for myself, the most important in this process, is to know and understand who is your  audience, learn about them and you will have success. VISION DEVELOPMENT

1. The challenge.

The problem I am looking to tackle is to do with parenting children in this modern age.  I am seeking to  uncover insights into what problems/challenges modern parents are facing and uncover truths about  what today’s parents believe about childhood, parenting, and what success looks like.  The reason I am  scratching at this area is because I have been contemplating opening a daycare/preschool, but am  unconvinced that this is the best action. I would like to use design thinking to gather deep insight into  some problems modern parents like myself are facing.

As an undergraduate student earning my degree in psychology, and from a background of working in  various children’s programs, I found the research around early childhood, notably the importance of  play in early childhood, particularly compelling.  Ten years later, as I was fully round with the  expectation of my first daughter and feverishly reading parenting books covering topics that ranged  from attachment parenting, sleep and sleep training, music for brain development, singing to the baby  in the womb, stress levels and the developing baby, sexual abuse and predators, the effects of marital  stress on children, language exposure and the brain, vaccinations, childhood disease, illness, SIDS,  breastfeeding, bottle feeding and on and on... and feeling utterly inundated with so much information  but having access to very little real life support.  The postpartum depression and isolation that I felt  following the birth of my little girl casts a dark shadow on what should have been a wonderful time in  my life (sans the utter lack of sleep of the first six months).  All of the good ideas, and theoretical  intentions of what my parenting was going to be went out the window as every day, in the early days,  we were just trying to survive the day and keep the little creature alive! Challenge:

-  Redesign Corporate procurement from decentralized processes throughout the firm to a  functionalization model with ‘center-led’ oversight and governance over the sourcing, risk  assessment, contracting, purchasing, approval and payment of good and services.

-  Additional Objectives/Challenges:

o Mandated Cost savings from:

▪  Establishing an environment of spend discipline

▪  Identifying duplicative services

▪  Reining in un-concentrated spend – too many vendors

▪  Establish competitive bidding

o Competing priorities

▪  Vendor Management – Risk assessment, accurate records, governance

▪  Internal Clients – mandated/goal is speed to market

Selection: Visualization

-  I chose the tool of visualization to inform the firm (specifically senior leadership, the business  owners of vendor relationships and users of procurement services) of our automated future state  with a ‘Procure to Pay’ solution.  The process will include a vetted catalog of goods and services,  automated approval workflows, centralized order management and streamlined invoice processing.    The vendor team will be taking work off the desk of everyone who engages with a 3rd party – from  contract services through fulfillment to billing.

Application:

-  I started by depicting a diagram of the existing, decentralized state of 3rd party Vendor management  with the gaps and inefficiencies evidenced.  The slides progressed to an ‘Amazon’ like purchasing  tool, whereby business owners will put desired objects in their ‘cart’ for purchase.  For certain  spend, such as office supplies or contract workers, the user will be directed to a preferred partner  website, such as Office Max or Staples or other internally managed tool for that particular category  spend. Reflection – Storytelling      Challenge

My name is Antonia Coelho and I study at the Ankara University, from Brazil. We

have a discipline in the school grade that is based on problem solving, where students

propose a common problem in their day to day profession. As my course is Obstetrics

(my country) in obstetric violence are bad, we decided to make a booklet to inform these

women on how to proceed in case they were victims of obstetric violence. This booklet

would obtain information such as government figures to report obstetric violence, as well as

how to identify cases of racism in the hospital that they were visiting. The purpose of these

booklets that would be distributed in the Brazilian public health system (SUS) was to

empower black women about their active role in society and how they themselves can be

instrumental in changing racism in the public health system. This action is justified because

we see from data exposed on Brazilian government websites, public data, that the women

who suffer the most obstetric violence are black women.    Selection

using an engaging narrative. As our group is composed only of black women, when we were

Challenge

Our learning programs are designed with a heavy faculty model. This structure ensures  senior individuals / leaders of the Firm are present for our learning programs and  allows for a faculty member to facilitate the small breakout group sessions. The breakout  group sessions have 5 participants each thereby creating a requirement for faculty to be  present for each group of 5 participants. This creates a requirement of 6 faculty to be  present for a group of 30 participants – our typical class size. As you can imagine,  scheduling this number of faculty for large numbers of programs throughout the year is  very challenging. Given this challenge, we developed a list of ideas to test reducing the  faculty number. These ideas included 1) increasing the size of the breakout groups, 2)  giving participants the responsibility to lead their own breakout groups and 3) rotating  faculty across multiple breakout groups.

Selection and Application

We selected the learning launch tool to test our ideas. We selected 20% of our programs  and tested the 3 ideas across the programs. We did not let the participants know there  was any change – hoping that they would not go into the program with any biases. We  implemented the guidance provided by Ed Hess in the Week 4 content. We thought  about

-  What we needed to confirm and disconfirm the idea and  -  The quantity and quality of the data.

We structured survey questions to understand the value and impact of the session in the  new format as compared to the old format. We tested for the impact on the participants’  ability to practice and develop the new skill at the end of the program. We also tested  the longer-term impact by surveying the group 100 days after the program. We  compared the results from the programs with the new faculty models with the results  from programs in the old format. text:
Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection    Mind mapping is a great way to explain thoughts visually and to help stakeholders represent  what’s on their mind about some challenge or idea. I work with clients from companies of all  sizes, from startups to large companies, and very often we are given challenges that come in  the form of requirements or a defined idea from someone, or some team, with little insights  from users or even from coworkers. We usually run workshops with all stakeholders to make  them see that writing down a list of requirements is not the first thing you should do to start  projects effectively. It’s obviously one way to scope the project, in order to get quotes from  providers, but clients should take a step back and start by thinking on the real needs first,  before diving in a technical approach. To get stakeholders started in thinking together in  possible solutions for their challenges, mind mapping is an easy tool that comes naturally for  them after seeing a couple of examples.    Application    An interesting project I’ve worked recently was the definition of an intranet for a large  company. As you can imagine, large companies have several departments and, therefore,  different needs for each one. Trying to understand what are each team needs for an intranet  is quite a challenge and, to get everyone on board in the definition process is crucial. So we  started by doing workshops with people from each department, getting them all together in  the same room so they could be aware of each others needs. Using meaningful customer stories to show the strengths of design thinking

Challenge

My challenge is to convince my team to approach a new project with the design-thinking

methodology. I work in a large technological company that has been using an experimental

approach based on quantitative data for years. This approach historically deﬁnes the

company's identity and has enabled it to achieve excellent results and operate as an industry

leader. Although this strategy still works well, it is increasingly clear that product innovation is

no longer suﬃcient, and that to maintain a leading position it is essential to innovate the

business model. The strategy used so far, based on convergent thinking and quantitative data,

begins to show its limits and, despite participating in the increase in revenue and market share,

has proved inadequate in generating revolutionary ideas, leaving the side of the company

discovered to the attacks of new younger and brave competitors.

telling a story to attract the attention of an audience, conveying the message that history wants

to tell and stimulate a speciﬁc desire in them, persuading them to perform a speciﬁc action.

The storytelling diﬀers from more traditional communication techniques because it puts at the

center of the story the feelings, and aims to involve and not to convince.

Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

I was working as an intern in the marketing department for a major FMCG company in India. The  brand I was working for was a premium biscuit brand, which was also the 2nd largest brand in terms  of Value. The task was to make this brand the biggest in India. To do that we had to beat a rival  biscuit brand, competing in the value/ low cost biscuit category. The gap over the years had reduced  and come down to INR 32 Cr (Thirty-two crores Indian Rupees) per month and this remaining gap  had to be reduced further by the end of the financial year. To do this, we analysed the monthly sales  across India and got to know two States where the biscuit consumption was the highest, including  the sales of the rival brand, but our sales were below the national average. So we devised a  marketing campaign to increase the sales in those two states.

After have used various design thinking concepts, including Secondary reseach, empathising with  distributors, retailers and consumers in those two states through In depth interviews, Focus group  discussions, shadowing them and ethnographic studies, we got to know that the distribution was  very poor in those areas, and the consumer were used to the taste of the rival brand. They also  thought the rival company to be an age-old company, and ours to be new, when in reality ours is a  100 year old one. The campaign therefore had to be two pronged; It had to make consumers try the  biscuit, and the distribution of the biscuit had also to be increased so that they are available near  consumers. This meant the task was to be a joint effort of both sales and the marketing team.

for regular day-to-day eating

Challenge

My challenge was to consider alternative work and career options - it's only natural to  wonder what else is out there from time to time. The challenge was also to determine  what approaches one could take, and do so in a relatively low risk and cost effective  manner.

Mid-career changes can sometimes be risky because of the time and expense needed to  execute and because the outcome can be difficult to foresee (for example, will I like  being a lawyer). By nature a pivot does not often does not lend itself easily to  quickly exploring and comparing different avenues. A career change is often a kind of  wicked problem... there may be several options and one may not know that a decision  taken is good (or bad!) until it is ‘too late’.

Selection

The tool selected to address the challenge was the Learning Launch Tool. It was  selected because as the Video described, this approach advocated the use of relatively  quick and cheap tests and experiments. Options could be drawn up and evaluated - after  trying one option - if not appealing, move on to the next, and find out in a relatively  short period of time. The hard part would be trying to find a medium that could serve  as a testing vehicle.

Application

The insight and key that helped enable and drive this approach was the proliferation of  courses offered online. The actual application of this technique would involve  participating in various courses as desired. There are many different courses online  that are relatively short and don’t require the commitment of a full degree program and  yet often still require the same degree of rigor as a graduate program. Taking  individual courses gives one the ability to sample and try out different areas of  potential interest.

text:
Reflection – Visualization of a New Process

Challenge   As a new member of this state-owned company, with a few disgruntled, unhappy and very  adverse to change employees from the IT department, I had the difficult challenge to design  and implement a new Change Procedure, with the mission of order the workflow and  eliminate some issues the auditors have been raising for ages.     Selection   Even though I was not familiar with design thinking techniques at the time, I thought the first  step would need to use the visualization tool.   I think that this is one of the best tools for this task, which facilitates both designing and  showing the way different groups of people interact with each other along the process flow.  The good thing is in this case you don’t need to be a very talented artist to implement this  technique, you just need to be able to draw lines, rectangles and rhomboids.    Application   We began by drawing a very basic process flow on a whiteboard, with a reduced group of  people.  Then we discussed about it, iterating over it, and continued to add more layers of  complexity, attaching post-it notes, to give more detailed explanations when necessary.   Then we organized different groups, to show all the participants how the steps of the  procedure could go, and allow them to make suggestions or changes, as long as some basic  compliance principles were to be preserved.    Insight   As I already mentioned, I didn’t know about design thinking at the time, but the experience  ratified our ideas about how this approach would be our best and maybe only chance to  success, which was using a visualization tool, besides getting all impacted people feel they  were on-board, participating of the design and implementation just from the beginning of the  project.     Approach   I think that I wouldn’t change the selected tool, which I continue to believe is the best for this  job, but I’d surely try to complement it with other techniques at an early stage.

text:
VISUALIZATION

The design process is a multi-layered process in which many mental, cognitive and perceptual  mechanisms come into play. Understanding of the process and design can only be possible with the  comprehension of the act of design that progresses as a complex pattern until the design product  emerges. An evaluation that develops solely on the design object may be incomplete in terms of how  the design was made or how to make a better design. For this reason, deciphering the design  process, which is defined as a poly-pattern in terms of its complex structure and synchronous  processes, will provide positive contributions to the field of design knowledge.

Visualization or visualization is any technique for creating images, diagrams or animations to convey  a message. Visualization through visual imagery has been an effective way of communicating both  abstract and concrete ideas since the dawn of humanity. Examples from history include cave  paintings, Egyptian hieroglyphs, Greek geometry, and Leonardo da Vinci's revolutionary technical  drawing methods for engineering and scientific purposes.

Today, visualization, science, education, engineering (eg product visualization), interactive  multimedia, medicine, etc. It has applications that are constantly expanding in fields. A typical  example of visualization applications is in the field of computer graphics. The invention of computer  graphics (and 3D computer graphics) may be the most important development in visualization since  the invention of central perspective in the Renaissance. The development of animation has also  helped improve visualization.

Assignment 1

Assignment

Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all  relevant information.

From employees perspective, there is no central location where all tasks and  activities in my organization (a division within a big company) are properly  tracked and monitored. Frequently people in the organization do not know who is  doing what, what are tasks they are responsible for and what are the  expectorations. For a manager perspective, it is very difficult to get birds-eye  view of the status of tasks and projects in the organization and getting any  details about any particular task or project requires distracting employees by  asking them to stop their work and generate reports to inform management and  decision makers of simple and trivial information about their tasks. Also there is  no way to know how much of the organization activities are aligned with actual  objectives. For information confidentiality reasons, we cannot use any of the  cloud-based task/project management tools.

Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool  you selected (e.g., what it is and why you selected it  for your challenge -- including any appropriate video  lecture references).

Used the internal Microsoft SharePoint system to develop central location where  all the organization activities (projects, tasks, meeting minutes, knowledge items  ... etc) would be stored and interlinked together. SharePoint allows non-technical  people to develop a wide variety of information structures which means that the  solution can be quickly and changed and adopted to the needs of users without  long change cycles. Also the flexibility of the SharePoint platform would allow for  changes as the operating model of the organization changes as incremental  improvements are made along the way. text:
Learning Launches for Creating a Sense of Ownership

Challenge

I currently work in a major transportation company that is regulated by the state. A few years  ago, an accident occurred on one of the routes. This has caused a lot of financial damage.  The company is required by law to be able to provide a report on all facilities and vehicles  involved in case of an accident. However, the recreation of the data needed was very costly  since the data required was not collected and stored on a central device.

I was instructed to build a workflow software together with a team of software developers to  track and support the construction of all new transportation facilities. By using this tool at  every step of the construction process, relevant data, that is necessary for generating a  report in case of an accident, can be collected and stored.

We have quickly found out that the major challenge was to create a tool that users would  want to use. It was hard to get them to provide information and to choose to adapt their way  of working by using a digital process. To them it came across as an additional responsibility  and a tool for enforcing control. Furthermore, it was extremely costly and demotivating to  map and implement a process tool that would not be used in the end.

Tool

We knew that we had to inspire the users somehow to ensure that the tool would be used in  the end and the necessary data would be collected consistently. We chose to organize  regular learning launches, where we would test possible scenarios with users by presenting  them with simple mockups of interfaces. Mockups are simple drawings of how an interface  could look like in the end. They are a cheap way of displaying possible features and  functionalities.

Through this approach we have hoped to include users in the whole development process  and to create a sense of ownership over the tool. Our goal was to decrease emotional  barriers by creating transparency and giving them a sense of co

Female employees are working with us who has come from rural background ,  less educated and are from far flung areas. Most of the girls have not come out of their  hometown earlier. Girls are not aware how to use toilet facilities or how to take care of  their hygiene & health. Girls get easily influenced with the lifestyle of the people around  and couldn’t manage to save money. The number of girls have increased rapidly in last two  years and hence the challenges to help them in acquainting with the culture has also  increased.

To face this challenge & coming up with the sustainable solution that can help in fulfilling  the objective of creating healthy environment for female employees and at the same time  guiding them to groom & develop, we adopted the storytelling  design thinking tool . I  really got impressed with the story of the George & the Geoff which was told in second  video of week 2 and hence chose to adopt this design thinking tool.

We identified female employees who are already associated with us and have come from  such background and are associated with us for more than 3 years. We organized forums  where the older employees can interact with the new one. We also displayed the stories  of girls and their achievements on the hostel and unit’s notice boards.

We asked the older employees to share their stories with new girls so that they can learn  how they can adjust in new environment. The challenges they face like hesitation,  inferiority complex or lack of confidence & shared how they learnt that change is law of  nature. Challenge

I work in a high-tech manufacturing environment. A few years ago, we were faced with escalations from  our customers about failures in shipped product. A small team was formed to investigate the issues and  implement corrective actions. The team analyzed all the issues in detail to see if there are any systemic  root causes. The findings were compiled and presented. It was noticed that there were inconsistencies  in the manufacturing and validation processes that were being used. We noticed that even experienced  personnel had a tough time to keep up with the complex requirements and specifications of building the  product. Newly hired personnel were struggling to follow instructions, calculating specifications,  interpreting results, and ensuring highest quality of shipped product.

We needed to build a tool that will help personnel, irrespective of their experience, to build complex  assemblies with ease. We had to change the way we were doing things. Change is not easy - we needed  buy in. We need to build something that both experienced and new people like. The solution should be  scalable and at the same time make economic sense.

Selection

Design is an Iterative process. It might take years to perfect a product. But in the high tech work we  need to be quick to market. We need to get buy in from all the stake holders fast. We need to convince  management to Invest based on reliable good data.

A colleague and I started to work on this problem. We both had a lot of experience (breadth) in the  manufacturing domain. We have worked in this area for years and were able to think through the  details. We also had decent programming skills that were needed to develop something that we could  test out. We decided to quickly build something and do a Learning Launch.

Reflection – Learning Launch  Leave Advisor

Ivan Tomac

Challenge

I am a senior UX designer for our organization and our challenge was to develop a decision  making application that helps employees pick the correct leave of absence (LOA) option which will  reduce the risk of taking an incorrect form of LOA and to help limit the time that a HR  representative would need walking an employee or manager through the decision making process.  This project would last two months and we would have an appropriate amount of budget to  support a 4 person design team with different backgrounds and skills. Our team will work to  develop the correct user experience and decision making guidance in the application so that the  overall experience would not last more than 5 minutes and the employee would be guaranteed in  taking the correct form of LOA.

Selection

We have already utilized journey mapping and empathy mapping so that we could best describe  our user personas. Based on our findings and understanding of the requirements and user needs,  we felt that a learning launch would be the method for us to test our design rapidly and give us the  opportunity to quickly refine our design.

Application

For our learning launch we set up a user experience test lab and relied on an agile design sprint  process. We conducted 2 test labs over a 3 day period. Each test had 20 users from our 3 primary  user group (Employees, Managers and HR Representatives).

As Thomas Koch stated in the training: “The key here is, is to do experiments that are  fast and cheap. Because you want to do lots of experiments. If they took a long  time you wouldn't ever get to a good idea. You would not ever get to a new  product that goes to market. If it was real expensive because you did lots of long  experiments, you'd run out of money before you found a new source of revenue.”

Reflection – Story telling

Challenge and Selection:

The tool I used was Story telling. We formed a team and I'm the technical head of the team. We design  and fabricate ATVs. As the oldest member of my team, I also had to motivate my team members during  this pandemic season. I used this tool often, with my team members and vendors and dealers who  supply materials and tools. I share stories of previous members of the team, and the team's legacy, to  my team members to make them realize that they are working in one of the best racing teams of our  country. Sometimes, we use stories to understand each other in a better way. I also check the way they  work before and after I share my stories, this tells me whether I have succeeded in doing what I should  be making them do.

Application:

I have a story about using story telling. One year ago, there was a dispute among 4 members of the  team. They argued about who would make a better driver of the vehicle. I had to intervene. I took them  to our evening snacks shop and I explained them why one was better than the other to drive the vehicle.  I told them there was a similar incident the previous year. I also let them share their views on who  should be a better driver. Finally, I concluded that the best among them has already been decided  during the team selection process, but as they are having a disbelief, I let them have a test and that  would prove the decision.

The test was an eye-opener. The four of them calmed down. I told them that the team members were  selected meticulously and each one of them were a valuable piece. This worked very well and they all  were back to being buddies.

text:
Use of Visualization on Workflow Optimization

Challenge & Selection

I am working for a cement production company which has traditional organisational culture. We  are currently using traditional methods for project management and  to follow operational  workflows. After failure on some projects in the initial phase we discovered some repetitive  patterns which create bottlenecks. As a members of digital transformation team, we wanted to  challenge our company’s teams to find more optimized methods to follow workflows; not only in  projects but in their daily business lifes (on their operational works).    First of all, in order to establish a sense of urgency we had to understand  if status-quo is more  risky than the unknown. We have spent time with engineers and technicians (ethnography) to  understand how they determine bottlenecks and solve them.  We empathized with the  employees and their issues .

Application

Since some of the issues are complex and have many layers, we have used visualization to  help managers to  understand patterns in the issues.    We used visualization to describe bottlenecks on 3 layers. In the first layer,  we have introduced  the personas we have created. It shows their passion, their abilities and their expectations from  the company,     Second layer presents personas’ daily routines and workflows. Here we used diagrams and  boards (like Kanban boards) to represent the flows and bottlenecks. We also showed how  bottlenecks block other flows, highlighting intersections with other flows. This eased for us to  see how a roadblock affects  different silos and projects and finally  affects the bigger picture.     In the third layer we presented detailed visualizations of  the bottlenecks. Challenge:

One friend of mine asked me for helping her with project for head of department of one

Government Ministry-to develop mechanism of effective interaction between government

structures in the framework of public procurement system. I work in this field but government

programs and their structure differs from things with which I work. But it was interesting for

me and some kind of level up. I agreed to help my friend.

The previous system was not effective and we need to explain all new which  we had

developed concept for a  person (head of department) who actually knows nothing about it and

can’t understand it. She has a very old and sophisticated work approach and rejected all ideas

and presentations of this project before. Project was not complicated for understanding for

specialists. We have described and repeated my friend speech several times for other experts

and they understand everything. I understand that the key problem was not in the project it was

in the order of project presentation to head of department. She  requires her subordinates to

describe everything in printed presentations or print papers for her and describe whole concept,

without the use of projectors or presentations on computer. It is easier for her to read and try by

herself get the idea, but long working day and huge flow of information had decreased reduced

her brain ability of perception of information from the text. I recommended my friend to use

visualization tool.

Selection:

Visualization is a way of unlocking a different part of your brain. Visualization is

anything from the picture which we has draw to the presentations and graphics that we create in

a presentation,or create an application.  Visualization, as like Storytelling tool, is really

important for explaining of idea or concept, but when you work with system where a lot of

elements it would be better to visualize it and how all elements are connected with each other.

was a deliberate attempt to revisit the concept of customer journey. One of the challenges my

organization faces is the management of its B2B retail prepaid card, previously customers have

to spend hours at the company head office to recharge or top-up their cards for future use. All

activities involved in the process were manually done at a designated customer service points.

Considering the inconveniences being created, for instance customers spending hours to be

attended to, management seeks to know what wows and what works.

SELECTION:  Being a member of the company’s digitalization team, we adopted “VISUALIZATION” as a design

thinking tool to find innovative ways to improve customer experience. The team was tasked to

employ visual thinking to offer innovative solutions to wow the customer.

what works. A group of twenty (20) cross-functional and diverse backgrounds, was inaugurated

to begin the journey of innovation.

data on the current condition. We wrote down what we observed to be the current customer

experience, these are in the form of sticky notes which are posted on a big board in a hall

dedicated to this exercise.

Then, the team moved to the ideation stage where the individual team members brainstorm to

find solutions to the problems identified at the observation stage. The solutions are mapped to

the individual problems posted on the board.

Whenever we start the progress, we would spend much amount of  time in brainstorming and come up with really good insights. The  outcomes were reflected in the form of degraded quality in the presentation slides. These things  cost us heavily and we couldn’t make up to the further rounds in many competitions. We are sure  that this has to be changed and we should go in a systematic approach while dealing with case  competitions.

Challenge:

To design and develop an idea for decreasing the rate of return owing to sizing issues for online clothing  retailing platforms. To meet the requirements, learning launch tool was implemented.

Hypothesis:

To provide the right fit clothing for consumers looking for online shopping.

Assumption:

Value creation

Customer perspective Data

1) Digital penetration is high; therefore, market has high potential for growth

o  Men does less online shopping but the market is increasing due to the increasing  awareness and customer satisfaction. More trendy sites are coming up catering to the  latest fashions trends which make it attractive for buyers these days

o  Women buyers are more frequent. Also, high sales per transaction

o  Children wear also holds substantial portfolio – buyers are mothers

2) Return rates are high which indicates customers dissatisfaction due to absence of trial mechanism

o In the men's segment the return rate is low, but sizing returns is the major issue  o In the women’s segment the return rate is high and sizing issue is the major issue, also

color is not same as the image, or fit is different, etc.

o In the Children’s segment the return rate owning to sizing is not a major issue, only

quality matters for the parent buyers

3) Sizing charts are not user friendly to provide right fit clothing

o Indian market does not have their own sizing chart and lends it from European, US or

other such markets which does not always fit the Indian body shape

o Alternate feasible methods are not available for digital market to cater sizing needs  o Current online market uses sizing chart and data analytics to give the best fit using user’s

past buying trends, since sizing chart is at default: the analytics is at default

Key assumption derived: Working on men’s collection will be easier to start with and enter the market.  Eventually women’s collection range can be taken up which is mire varied and rigorous

text:
Food Business Problem: Visualization

A large problem I have encountered in business is making the customer experience and

purchase convenient for them. The business in place is a food business that operates online.

The purchase cycle starts off with customers inquiring for a date for delivery, making a payment,

and booking their own delivery rider to pick up their orders. However, it has come to the

attention of the business owner that customers can likely be unsatisfied as their purchasing

experience is not so easy and there are inconveniences that occur. The first problem would be

not having a clear date on when orders will be ready. Second would involve the need for

customers to book their own delivery riders to pick up their orders.

To help me solve this problem, I used the visualization tool in order for me to see in all angles

and perspectives how this problem 1) affects the different parties involved 2) possible solutions

that can be implemented and satisfy all parties. I used the straw man visualization to help

generate discussions on this. I divided the stakeholders into three: 1) business owners 2)

employees and 3) customers. The main questions I asked was 1) to see how these problems

affect their place in the business 2) what possible solutions they would propose.

I have learned from the graphics created by each party that there are definitely stark differences

between each party as owners want to maximize profit, employees do not want to be

overworked and clients want the easiest way to purchase the products. However, the

visualization also helped shed light on the commonalities between these parties. Besides this,

the visualization also helped bring out possible solutions each party did not see or recognize

and also bring up more problems that can be solved along the way.

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation

Final assignment – Example reflection : Learning Launch

Challenge

As a market researcher dedicated to innovation processes, I handle various client projects, including  websites developments. The last project I was in charge for, was to imagine and test a new  governmental website to hire teachers. The challenge was to deliver an attractive image of the career  and provide an easy-to-understand information within a unique website, whatever the profile visitor.   The project scope includes three stages: an insight research stage nearby a student community, a test  of a first light website prototype (i.e. information architecture and themes only) and at last, the beta  version website test. Optimizations must be provided after each test stage in order to gradually meet  the website general goals. The student community was asked to produce ideas and propose  suggestions at each stage to associate them in a valuable co-creation process.      Selection     I have already gone through several pretest of various prototype in my career but I had never  experimented as formal approach as the learning launch tool. As this project begun with insight  exploration and ideation stages, I handled I was interested to use it for two reasons. First, to assess the  ideas developed by the web agency from the design criteria proposed at the end of the first stage; and  secondly be able to iterate and pivot with optimizations and new ideas.   In addition, I thought this tool could be a great opportunity to maintain the engagement of the  community student all along the project. text: 1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.    The idea comes from a national park resort plan while I was in my former architecture company.  The client wants to develop a 3.5-square-kilometer mountain land near a reservoir and makes it  into one of the best destination for family tourism in Eastern China. After a few rounds’  discussion with the client, we decided to plan a national park resort of campground, safari zoo  and most exciting, a kid zoo where a family can adopt a docile animal and live with them for a  couple of days everytime they visit the zoo. And in the strategy plan chapter, we came with an  idea to build an APP that those animal adopters, especially kids, can use to check their pet’s  everyday life and know more about all the animals live in the zoo.    To achieve these goals I have to design this system as a binding service for the animal adoption  program.    2. Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why  you selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).    As our main tool we decided to choose Visualization tool, which is described by many authors as  a “the mother of all design tools”. As a method it refers to any activity, which makes information  beyond text and numbers into images, maps and stories.    Visualization method is used to visualize our ideas to make them more convenient, simple and  real for the our audience and us because in fact, visualization is not about drawing. As a business consultant we also need to use “left brain” techniques, however, will  be used in further part of our project.    3. Challenge

I work with an institution that help the vulnerable targeting especially those affected with HIV &

Aids in the western part of the Country, we work together with the hospitals in the region to

provide them with finances and Mentorship & support for sustainability and Continuity of the

services to the affected persons. Our big problem in the finance department was on how we are

able to collect Finance documents within 87 facilities spread across the region with minimal

operation cost-This documents included Finance Reports, Support Documents Such Payment

Vouchers, Receipts Invoices, Timesheets and Pay slips in order to make work easier and donor

reporting smooth with efficiency.

The problem solutions entailed 10 Finance staff and 5 Management Staff to come up with an

efficient system to sort out the challenge within 3 Months. The team were to brainstorm on the

Storytelling

Challenge    As a project manager at a non-profit organization that provides psychological services to children and teens, my  organization was recently faced with what our course has referred to as a “wicked problem.” My organization was  confronted by a sharp rise (almost double compared to the previous year) in referrals from school counselors and  school-based juvenile probation officers for children and teens who had violated school policies to the extent that  expulsion was warranted. The spike in referrals was due to schools’ increasing adoption of “zero tolerance” policies  related to drugs, alcohol, and violence on school grounds—rather than discipline students individually, schools were  opting to expel students in large numbers after their first offense.    The challenge, then, was to develop a systematic and evidence-based approach to meet the psychological and social  needs of students who had recently been expelled, in order to decrease school expulsions overall throughout the  community school corporation. This challenge was “wicked,” however, because the students’ needs and backgrounds  were vastly different. A “one-size-fits-all” program was simply not going to resolve the challenge faced by the students,  schools, and our community as hundreds of students were expelled from area middle & high schools each semester. My  team and I were tasked with rolling out an outpatient psychological treatment program that would decrease the level of  school expulsions in the community by addressing the needs of the students who had been expelled for a variety of  offenses—drugs, alcohol, and violence. Challenge and Selection:

I have selected mind mapping as a tool ,mind map is a graphical way to represent ideas and concepts. It is a visual thinking tool that helps structuring information ,helping you to better analyze, comprehend, synthesize ,recall and generate new ideas. Just as in every idea , its power lies in its simplicity .Mind maps are used to help structure information to gain a better understanding. It is hierarchical and shows relationships among pieces of the whole. Mjor ideas are connected directly to the central concept, and other ideas branch out from those major ideas.

Applications:

I was having many applications of selecting mind mapping as a choice. Memorizing things,organizing ideas,brain storming sessions,attractive presentations,simplify complex ideas,problem solving,case study,project management,sourcing,summarizing.

Approach:

Organizing ideas:This usage overlaps with the memorizing to a certain point but it still

deserves a separate attention as it has a wide practical implementation that can not be deduced to the educational needs only.It has to do with how our brain functions.It works by creating associative connections between concepts,and this makes it much easier to see the interconnectedness between ideas by presenting them in a non-linear fashion.

Brain storming sessions: It looks easy to organize an idea,but you need a brain

storming session if you do not have one in the first place.Mind maps are dynamic and can follow up the fast changing tempo of the session.Mind maps can hold the sessions under control,for brainstorming and can easily go off topic with the limits of discussion are not clear cut.

Insight:

Attractive presentations: Mind maps are excellent for presentations because they

provide a well organized flow that it is easier to grasp.In this way my presentation will look more professional and easy to follow.

Organization:

Enhance productivity: Mind mapping enables me to learn faster communicate more efficiently
