text: Challenge: Get approval to create an innovative development experience for  new managers    I was tasked with coming up with a learning solution for new managers in our organization. Our current  approach to management development was to send managers out of the office to a workshop for several  days of full-day academic learning about how to lead and manage people. Our senior leadership believed this  approach was necessary so that managers weren’t distracted during training and they could receive a “brain  dump” of HR-related information all at one time. In my initial conversations with new managers, however, it  became clear that this approach was ineffective. Although they needed the HR information, they were  stressed out by the idea of being away from their jobs for the week and they couldn’t absorb so much  information at once – particularly when they had no chance to apply it in the moment. We were so focused  on the dissemination of processes and policies, we had lost sight of managers’ emotional needs, which our  training programs weren’t addressing at all. I had a vision for approaching the learning solution in a  completely different way but, before I could move forward with the idea, my immediate challenge was to  get several groups of senior leader stakeholders to embrace the concept. Without their support, I would  never be able to make such a large scale change.      Selection: Storytelling    I work for a very large financial services institution. The connotation is that there are lot of “stuffed shirt”  banker types…which isn’t too far off the mark! As I went through the Design Thinking for Innovation program,  I thought to myself that the technique I would use the least would be storytelling. I just couldn’t quite  envision a positive reaction from the stakeholders I work with, thinking they would find the technique too  “fluffy” and not sufficiently data-driven. After all, we are in the business of making money, not making  emotional connections!

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

I am working in IT industry and as a part of profile I am mainly handling AMS contracts to support  client IT application with our experts. My main challenge is to provide 24*7 IT support to our clients  and keep their applications running as per service level agreement with the help of my team. These  applications are integrated with each other and due to complexity of system and data flow I was  facing various issues of integration failure. To analyse root causes we have launched Failure mode  analysis tool to find issues in system and fix it permanently.

Application

To perform failure mode analysis, I have identified subject matter experts from my team, and we  have conducted sessions. I used mind mapping tool “Freehand” and identified repetitive issues first  to focus on fixing them. For each issue I have identified subject matter expert and discussed possible  reasons of failure, with detailed discussion I have reached on various points. At this level we had  concluded various points and now another challenge was lying with us to fix them permanently. This  level we all are gathered as a team and used sticky notes with two different colours, Yellow- Yellow  colour that is what we know about issue and Pink for possible solution of issue. This activity helps  me and the whole team to learn and explore new things

Insight & Approach

With the help of Mind mapping tool, I have reached on root causes of various issues and fixed them  permanently. But this activity helped us as a team in various ways

1) We have identified new ideas and suggestions to offer our clients   2) We have developed proof of concepts and ready with us to grab new opportunities and

clients

3) Whole team got cross functional knowledge about from various subject experts

With this experience we have started this practice in other areas and in various projects and started  including experts in other functions as well

   

Mind Mapping

Challenge

We were running a Youth Group Organization called LATAM (La Republica) in a refugee camp to empower youth, build their capacities for them to discover their potential. During our operation, our challenge was that, we couldn't get relevant information about what exactly the young people want to do that will help them. The youth were traumatized by their past experiences (some loss their parents, relatives, friends etc) in the war. When we ask questions to get their mind, no one participated in answering question. So, it became hard for us to get information on what could be done to youth (and we couldn't do anything different unless what youth want). We did some counseling and sensitization meetings for youth and local leaders.

Selection

Mind mapping is a great tool that I used at all times to easily collect hidden data from different people. So our team chose mind mapping tool. Providing sticky note to participants and ask a question, then each of them write as many answers as he/she can. This helps us gather more information about things on ground and what they think should be done.

Application

For our first Mind Mapping, we managed to collect more information from different people for our project of youth 4 change. Our team completed a survey with some few youth and local leaders. The surveys included questions about life standards, youth's needs, understanding to their roles and feelings about the change, that was within a two-week timeframe.I also explained how addressing the needs of one person can impact everyone for the better. Our organization selected 30 youth for three-day training on peace building and conflict resolution. In every after session, we ask two-three questions. We provide them with sticky notes for writing their answers. Through the process, we collected different informations that we could not get if we use other means e.g throwing question to audience. Reflection  –  Learning  Launch

Learning  Launch  is  the  Design  Thinking  tool  that  has  most  resonated  with  me  from  Patrizia’s   teachings.  The  idea  that  we  should  embrace  failure  and  learn  from  it  is  a  hard  concept  for  me  to   adopt.  In  a  world  where  successes  are  celebrated,  it’s  difficult  to  step  back  and  look  at  what  can   be  gained  from  trying  and  failing.      Because  Learning  Launches  are  quick  and  dirty—and  on  a  small  scale—this  provides  comfort   to  me  that  small  failures  can  lead  to  big  successes.

Challenge   A  recent  challenge  for  me  has  been  trying  to  implement  a  new  program  management  software   to  another  division  of  our  company.  Our  team  has  been  using  this  program  management   software  with  one  division  of  our  company  (mostly  successfully)  for  years.  We  are  trying  to   implement  this  same  software  with  our  team  of  Event  Planners.  The  work  that  our  Event   Planners  do  is  inherently  different  than  the  other  division  because  timelines  might  be  quicker,   budgets  might  be  smaller  and  clients  might  be  more  demanding.  This  is  on  top  of  the  specific   struggles  of  event  planning  based  on  destination  challenges  (safety,  weather,  customs,   disease),  travel  parameters,  and  the  event  planners  constantly  traveling  all  over  the  world  so   they  aren’t  in  the  office  to  learn  new  processes.     The  Management  Team  from  my  department  has  required  that  the  new  program  management   software  be  implemented  with  the  Event  Planners  by  the  new  fiscal  year.  The  Management   Team  of  the  Event  Planners  is  fickle  with  support  for  the  use  of  the  new  software. Challenge

I am a member of my organization’s online marketing department and my/our challenge is to improve  the workflow within the department in order to increase sales in the online channel and to spend  marketing budgets on the right campaigns. The project scope includes the online marketing department  composed of ten employees, as well as the larger marketing department . The project is limited to  internal resources (i.e., budget and employee time). The project should not exceed 30 business days and  the solution should include an even distribution of working hours amongst the team members. We will  focus on trying to uncover what our team members, as well as key stakeholders within the larger  marketing department and IT department, consider to be ineffective or problematic with regard to the  workflow.

Selection

Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools, so we are ready to try the  learning launch tool. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment meant to quickly test an  idea and prototype.

Application

For our first learning launch, we focused on the structure/execution of our online marketing tasks. In  particular, we wanted to see if we could structure our tasks, projects, and processes to adapt the  methods of Scrum project management for our work (e.g., time boxed, daily, specific meetings, reviews,  etc.) in an effort to become more agile. This tested our assumption that the structure and execution  were the main causes of our workflow challenge. Our team went through a two-day training with a  Scrum project management coach. Next, we went through five workshops to structure our tasks and  processes in a more agile way. These two sessions occurred within in a three-week timeframe. Challenge:

In my line of work, I find myself doing a lot of final product testing.  These tests can range from  characterization to reliability and even simple function testing.  One of the issues I run across frequently  is the results of testing often bring up more questions than they do answers.  As a result, after  continually iterated test plans, the end test plan can look way different then what was originally  requested. Thus, it becomes my challenge to return to the requester and explain the discrepancies  between how things started and where they ended up.  I began to think that maybe instead of the  constant iterations we could get a more complete picture from the beginning.

Selection:

To deal this this challenge, I have selected the tool of storytelling.  A lot of the times when I get an initial  request for testing it is something simple, such as “see if raising the temperate can increase  performance.”  Now this by itself is fairly vague.  For example, I do not know what the metric for  performance is.  Further, there are several variables that could change, and I am unaware of which  variable is the desired result.  The reason I picked storytelling is because there is obviously a larger  picture that is getting lost after it was reduced to a single problem statement.  Secondly, the data I am  returning with is lacking the context to make it really meaningful.

Application:

The first thing I did was go to the requesting manager and find out exactly what they were looking for in  term of performance.  Often in the case in the semiconductor industry, there is many steps in a process  and certain changes upstream can have major effects down the line.  I had him bring together various  stakeholders from the different steps so we could create a fuller picture of what was exactly the  performance they were looking to improve. Design thinking final assignment

1. Akash Singh Final assignment design. Thinking. Action. Lab

2. 3 key takeaways 1. Assumptions are a part of everything we do. Design thinking is about

working with those assumptions as a starting point for creativity. Often, assumptions are taken  for granted and can lead to errors in judgement. Design thinking encourages empathizing with  the subjects of a challenge or issue that invariably challenge those assumptions. So the design  thinking approach for me, is about checking assumptions and incorporating multiple  perspectives into an idea. 2. Fail Early and often – success is not built on one idea that is an  instant 100% solution. Rather, success is built on many iterations, tries and failures. We often  just remember the success and forget all of the incremental steps that fostered that success.  Design thinking encourages prototyping of ideas, to force testing, feedback and failure early so  that ideas can naturally grow and mature. Thus the power of design thinking is to let the ideas  evolve on their own, outside of any one’s ego or attachment to any one solution. 3. Take the  other’s perspective – too often we get confined into our work processes and doing things ‘the  way they were done before’ – Design thinking encourages actively taking on the ‘other’s’  perspective, to feel their experience of a problem or challenge so that you can relate and think  of ideas that come from their perspective, not just your own

text: CHALLENGE AND SELECTION:  The challenge that I have chosen is to widen the availability of products to the  middle class consumers. I have always seen that imported products especially  aren’t being advertised abundantly or marketed in a proper manner. The  common consumers do not have access to certain products even if they are  able to pay for it.   The tool i have chosen is Mind-Mapping.This tool will not only let me know the  reasons for the consumer gap but will also help clear out certain aspects of  marketing for the stakeholders.    APPLICATION:  I start the process by defining my design issue and explaining the issue and  the consumer gap in the form of graphics and maps. I draw out various  flowcharts to demonstrate the market flow of these products to the  stakeholders to give them a clear picture. The stakeholders then think about  the reasons for the gap by looking over the flowcharts and the maps and then  find out conclusive solutions for the same.   I keep on reminding them about what the reality is and what the constraints  are. They each come up with different solutions like more digital  access,importation of more popular and more relevant products,selling of the  products more freely so that they can be more available to the consumers,etc.    INSIGHT AND APPROACH:  It was an exhilarating experience. This made a lot of opportunities available to  the job seekers and entrepreneurs who think of accelerating a business or  starting one. The response we got was massive and plausible. This technique  helped many marketers to market their products in a streamlined manner and  increased their product accessibility.  The graphic gives the diverse group of stakeholders a focal point for  discussion that allows them to share their perspectives and develop insights  into potential root causes of their problems. text:
From Waste to Worth

Reflection : Visualisation

Challenge and Selection

Waste management has been a  daunting  task especially in developing and under developed  countries. Dumping of waste in large scale as well as small scale results in environment  pollution, health hazards and ecological imbalances. Air, water and soil are dangerously  polluted .It has also contributed significantly to the increase of incurable diseases  and   spreading of  diseases like dengue, malaria etc. For example, dengue fever is spread by  mosquito, which breeds in stagnant water. Carelessly dumped  containers, tubes etc are the  home ground for their breeding. According to the statistics of WHO 390 million dengue  infections are reported per year. Also biomagnifications has disrupted the food chain leading   to extinction of a number of species.

Why should we not use the same scrape for constructive purposes? How to convert the  garbage to gain ?Scientific solutions and massive machineries are already available. Still it  does not act as the  problem solver. Improper  management, installation as well as  maintenance expenses,  inaccessibility and lack of awareness  catalyses the pollution process.  It is human tendency to feel happier with steadfast  outcomes  rather than a long term benefits  and community welfare. We need an easily convincible, simple but powerful  tool that would   wreck the mind set  of people and align their thoughts to our imagination.

Visualisation is the representation of facts and ideas  for easy understanding of stake holder.  It has a wide variety of techniques ranging from pencil drawing to video playback. It helps to  lay out abstract idea in simple figures. After attending  video lecture by  Angela Myer, on  Visualization felt that it is tailor made for the requirement. Challenge

I am an HR manager part of a team responsible for policy and strategy in my organization. Our  organization (about 7000 employees) did not have a work from home (WFH) policy before the  COVID-19 pandemic forced us to close our Corporate Headquarters. Our HR team was tasked to  prepare a WFH policy keeping in mind all pros and cons. The policy required the collection of  opinion from stakeholders such as employees at all levels, top management and customers who were  regular visitors to the office. The important aspect was to get the daily work done through a policy  that allowed virtual means of communication through structured rules of WFH to ensure business  continuity and smooth customer experience. This required close coordination between all the  departments of our organization including our IT team.

Selection

The approach consisted of three phases i.e. Phase I: developing a questionnaire for obtaining  responses of stakeholders; Phase II:  formulation of a draft policy based on responses and best  practices followed by other organizations and, Phase III: testing the draft policy amongst a small  random group of employees. We selected the learning launch tool to quickly test the actual  implementation issues related to the proposed policy. Moreover, this tool was best suited under the  difficult circumstances of the pandemic.

Application

After formulation of the policy and obtaining nod (from the Director-HR) for conducting the learning  launch of the WFH policy, our team conducted a series of mock sessions by engaging employees of  different departments. The draft policy was distributed in advance to the participants and the online  meetings were held during office hours with specific agendas. Better work place – mind mapping

Challenge My challenge has to do with people management in a large multilocation team. Our group is very diverse, with people located in 4 different sites around the world of at least 10 different  nationalities. Working virtually is difficult, sometime time and energy consuming. During the last year a  peak in number of people leaving have been registered. As our is a young team with salaries at the low end  of the agreed fork, the first actions did focus on salaries revision for selected individuals and the possible  need of more frequent discussions around career progression as the immediate needs.

Selection of tool The first tool selected to act on the problem had actually identified those as primary needs, but that tool  was a short survey with predetermined themes and seemed to give wrong direction. In fact, by answering  to the question ‘do you have frequent conversations about your career’ with a mean score, the partecipants lead the management think they wanted more. But career discussions are already happening twice a year  for everybody, hence the question was probably not the right one to be asked.  We decided therefore to use mind mapping, involving more closely with the teams and providing safe  environment and time for discussion.

Application Teams were gathered in small groups and asked to come up with their own insight on people engagement  improvement or the lack thereof. Partecipant were given time to come up with some individual reflections, then gathered on a board on  sticky note by themes. Those themes were the same familiar themes of reward and recognition, work life  balance and career progression, but as the discussion went on and many ‘why’ and ‘so what’ were asked, a  more precise picture came through. Challenge & Selection I work as part of the sales strategy team for a newspaper publishing organisation in India. The  regional sales teams here work on selling advertising space to various clients. The clients are  segmented by their overall advertising value into three segments: Key Accounts, Mid-tier Accounts  & Long-tail Accounts. Each sales team is given a mix of accounts from each group to target. While  working on optimising the sales process I found that the current model resulted in limited focus on  the long-tail accounts due to a perceived lack of business potential. I leveraged visualisation tool to  present my analysis to the management and highlight the missed opportunity under the current  sales model.

The reason for choosing visualisation as the tool was because I felt that it would help present the  scale of the problem and also to develop a common understanding. I was inspired by the video  from Angela Myer, where she talks about how visualisation can be a powerful tool to develop  consensus among a diverse group and to communicate ideas very clearly. This was of prime  importance to me as without a common understanding we cannot even begin to identify possible  solutions.

The number of clients called in each segment was compared against the  segment’s overall client list to capture the % of clients being actively targeted (coverage ratio). text:
MINDMAPPING TO IMPROVE EMPLOYEE EXPERIENCE

CHALLENGE

As part of my studies in Corporate Communications we regularly receive group assignments,  simulating real-life agency-client relationships and projects. The groups of 5-7 students per group  are randomly assigned each semester, pointing us to assume new team structures quickly. Within  this dynamic set of influences on team structures, our school requires us to use a quite rigid  structure when developing campaign concepts, providing regular coaching sessions to check on  our progress and making sure we use certain tools at the correct point of time throughout our  semester: the main challenge is to be creative and innovative within a rather rigid set of rules.

In this particular project we received the brief to create a new employer branding concept for a  large infrastructure client. The client’s employee base provides a diverse cross section through my  country’s society, covering all classes, educational levels, ages and genders (albeit having a  percentage of female employees of less than 12%), located both in urban and rural areas. The  client asked us to create a selection of activities that will reach all, or at least most of the employees  and will provide a solution for both the thinning knowledge base in lieu of the approaching  generational gap with about 1/3 of the current staff set to be retired in the next 10 years and make  the company more attractive for female employees without alienating the mostly male staff.

SELECTION

text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge    I work in an organisation that carries out maintenance on military vehicles. Many of our  employees are ex-military technicians who have served for a reasonable time in the military and  are keen to keep using their technical skills without being subject to the more military side of  their previous career such as deploying overseas. Many of these technicians have the mindset  they are still in the military and getting the equipment serviceable at all costs is the most  important task they must accomplish each day. Their ‘mission’ is to get the equipment  serviceable to enable the military to achieve its mission.     Unfortunately, the technicians often expose themselves to risky situations while undertaking  maintenance and do not realise they are significantly older than when they in the military. They  still bend and twist and climb and lift heavy objects because they have always done things that  way. The workers were being injured, mainly from soft-tissue injuries such as muscle sprains and  strains. Some technicians also had pre-existing medical conditions as a result of their previous  military service (e.g. bad backs, weak joints). I had to find a method of reducing the number of  injuries.

Selection and Application    I had tried providing lifting aids and correct instruction in lifting techniques. I had arranged for  Army physical training instructors to give demonstrations of correct handling and lifting  techniques. I had arranged for ex-champion weightlifters to show how to correctly lift objects but  our injury rate just kept increasing. An obvious insight to the current situation was the previous  ‘usual’ methods of application to get people to use correct lifting techniques were not working. I  decided to apply design thinking knowledge and employ storytelling as a different approach to  change behaviour.     Storytelling makes strategy accessible and brings a different (personal) perspective to the  problem. I

As part of an organization that is in the process of turning its “Training Area” into a “Change  Management Area”. We are constantly looking forward to improving our clients experience  with collaborative tools and services for their business. Right now we are facing a problem  with long time relationship customers. They are no longer satisfied with our current training  programs and their contents, because as they say: “We already had all the training you can  offer … ¿what else do you have?.  The current “pandemia” issue that our world is living, presented an even more challenging  scenario. Because some of our ideas to manage this challenge would demand presential  activities with our clients. Now we can only use remote tools to accomplish this. We are  forced to experiment with our ideas. So we decided to go with a Learning Launch process.  The problem was that we couldn't “just Try” with sensitive and complicated clients. So we  targeted some of our clients with strong, friendly relationships with us. And also with a strong  focus on innovation, so they could understand what we were trying to do, with them as a  “Learning partner” to try, experiment and iterate some of our training ideas directly with their  users. Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

I am an entrepreneur who likes to invest in small low risk businesses. Recently, I started a new business  venture for providing accommodation for women who live away from their family either to pursue  their education or their career. The place was designed to accommodate close to 30 people, giving  them a flexibility to either live individually or share a room with another person. But the main  challenge I would encounter here would be to deliver a homely atmosphere – a place where they feel  safe, secure and most importantly healthy food and hygienic living conditions. These variables actually  summarize the whole vision of my business. To deliver to the needs of my customers, it was important  for me to reflect on my assumptions and also improvise my approach by getting constructive feedback  from my customers. This would prove to be a crucial aspect to make it a successful business.

Selection

Since I stepped into this venture with minimum experience and exposure, I chose to put my instincts  and the whole idea to test by adopting the Learning Launch tool. I launched my business and marketed  it through social networks, newspaper ads and brochures.

text: Challenge:   In 2019, I was trying to find out how to promote online tutoring to tutors, parents and students in Singapore.  Online tutoring in Singapore had not really taken off yet at that time. In fact, everybody had different ideas of  what online tutoring was. Parents were generally skeptical about its usefulness, students mostly did not have a  clear idea of what online tutoring looked like, and most tutors were adopting a “wait-and-see” approach  towards this emerging technology.    There were also multiple factors that affected the adoption rate of online tutoring. Among these are: maturity of  online tutoring software, availability of on-boarding training, cost of subscription of online tutoring software,  effectiveness of learning through online tutoring, cyber security concerns, etc.    My team conducted training for approximately 150 freelance tutors who showed interest in online tutoring but  only a handful of them really adopted online tutoring as part of their offer. We tried to engage parents in a few  parents workshops; they produced only a few customers.    Due to our limited resources, a multi-pronged approach like that was very hard and slow work. The challenge  was really to identify a few critical factors that had maximum impact on the adoption rate of online tutoring in  Singapore, and to act upon them. Reﬂection - Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection  I have worked in shared services for most of my professional career within the same  organization. Regardless of what objectives management come up with it always come down  to how can we bring the cost of a transaction down.

Our shared service organization covers close to 2000 team players spread across 4 regional  service-centers as well a multitude of in-country teams covering several areas such as payroll  Our objective was to reduce payroll processing costs by several million dollars over 5 years.

The challenge is linked to the selection of a single payroll provider to cover close to 50000  active and retired personnel in 30 countries. Example Reflection – Visualization

Challenge

I was working as an Inventory Analyst in the Logistics Department of a natural gas distribution  company, and together with my boss, we were designing a project that intended to replace our  current inventory management system (which was based on the use of spreadsheets) for the  MRP (Materials Requirement Planning) module that was included in our SAP ERP system, but  has never been used before. After doing some analysis, we concluded that it would allow us to  enhance our materials requirement planification time and precision. However, we had to  convince our manager about that.

Selection

In order to efficiently communicate our idea, I selected the Visualization tool (though in that  time I was not aware of it as a Design Thinking tool) to convey a clear understanding of the  inventory related problems we would be tackling by implementing the MRP module: reducing  planning time and being able to execute it more often, and reducing the probability of incurring  in a stock-out or an over stock. This would be the best way to get our manager approval.

Application

Using bar graphs and intuitive pictures (such as empty shelves or accumulated materials due to  imprecise purchasing), through a classic PowerPoint presentation, we presented our project to  the manager. We focused on the current situation (what is?) and the potential situation to which  we would arrive in the event of correctly executing the project (what if?).

Insight

Despite the presentation went well, we realized we haven’t fully considered the impact this  project would have in the Procurement Department (on which our department depended on),  as they workload would have suffered a considerable increase. This was, as I can see now,  because we weren’t empathetic enough and didn’t consider an important stakeholder the way  we were supposed to. Assignment-  Learning Launch

Challenge

As a product manager for a company which makes chips for cordless phones, my challenge was to  improve the user experience in terms of voice quality and reception at the end of the usable range of  the phone. The target was to provide a better quality than our competition while reducing product  returns due to low perceived quality. The main challenge was to improve the quality, while controlling  the very sensitive cost structure of the product. All of this had to be done within the next product launch  cycle in 90 days.

Selection

The learning launch tool was used to select between 3 different ideas which have been suggested by the  engineers to improve the quality. This tool was selected since consumer voice quality experience is  extremely subjective and cannot be predicted by engineering simulations and measurements. The early  launch tool was the best way to get early unbiased feedback without spending too much resources and  be able to “fail early” on nonproductive approaches which would be “tabled” .

Application

Early launch was done to a group of 20 students, who would serve as consumers. The consumers were  given 3 different prototype products utilizing different engineering solutions (antenna design, noise  muting and advanced signal processing) for assessment. The students were then asked what solution  sounded best to them.  This provided early subjective feedback without confirmation bias.

Based on the student feedback, we concluded that a combination of two of the ideas (noise muting and  improved antenna) seemed to provide a better solution.  As a result, repivoting was done, and a  prototype utilizing the combined solution was put to the test of the student group   to confirm that the  combined solution was superior to the individual solutions.

text: Reflection on Design Thinking for Business Innovation  University of Virginia Darden School of Business    Challenge    Every teenager that has attended high school probably knows that there are students that  have difficulties making friends, and end up eating lunch alone. Eating lunch alone due to a  lack of friends can have serious effects on a person’s well-being, and eventually on mental  health. According to an article by Kira Asatryan that has appeared in Psychology Today,  loneliness can cause mental health disorders such as depression and addiction.     Such situations do not only occur in high schools, but can be observed at universities across  the globe as well. While attending a U.S. college for a semester during my undergraduate  degree, I started to realize that there are several students eating lunch alone, not because  they choose to, but because they lack social connections on campus. This was a situation I  wanted to change. To do so, I wanted to permanently reserve a table in the college’s dining  hall, where I would place small cards with topics that foster conversation among the people  sitting there. By decorating the table in a special way (e.g. by using a yellow tablecloth), and  establishing a poster explaining the cause and the idea, the table should become well known  across the whole campus, foster sharing a table with unfamiliar people, and ultimately  facilitate making new friends.     My plans called for the support of the college’s administration since a table would need to be  assigned to the cause permanently. However, the challenge I faced was the transmission of  the underlying problem to people that probably never thought of it and/or never experienced  the problem of loneliness in the dining hall themselves. text: Reflection – Story Telling:    Challenge:  I’m currently an undergrad student in my senior here at a business school, I will soon be  applying for jobs or for my masters. All we are ever repeatedly told to do is sell ourselves to  professionals, businesses and corporations. In that sense, it is really important for us to know  who we are, explain our background and interests with clarity and also show how we will add  value to the corporations we’re applying. This sounds easy enough on paper. However, as  students we are usually lost on how to market ourselves the best way.     Selection:  I’ve chosen the story telling tool because its fundamental idea is to be able to tell your own  story. Liberal art college students suffer with this question the most as very few of us have  some sort of direction on where we belong or what we want to. Branding our story  innovatively not only helps us keep our options open but also gives a holistic approach to  professionals and professors on the kind of people we are.     Application:   I utilized the story telling tool in my emails to instructors on how I learnt from their course. I  know this isn’t much, though it was a good start. Rather than telling them I simply enjoyed  the course, I now told them a more individual and personal story on how the course helped  me grow. This helped me form deeper personal relationships with my instructors and made  me understand and value the course more than before.     Insight:   Story telling helps you be in charge and in control of your life. By telling myself and  convincing my instructors that their course did benefit me in some way, I was able to  internalize this added value and be more positive about my learning experiences. The project is limited to internal resources (i.e., budget and  employee time). The project should not exceed 20 business days and the solution should include an  even distribution of working hours amongst the team members. We will focus on trying to uncover what  our team members, as well as key stakeholders within the larger marketing department and IT  department, consider to be ineffective or problematic with regard to the workflow. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment meant to quickly test an  idea and prototype. text:
Reflection – Storytelling – NEW FDG

Challenge: A large team was established from every departments to challenge the processes of PET (positron emission tomography) products such as PDG, FLT etc. We produce and sell FDG for a long time. And there are 3 Rival Firms. The half life of the isotope is 1,83 hours and this so limited for delivering and usage. The efficiency of the productions are not stable. And the most difficulties on the logistic operations. We need to create a new FDG that is different from others. We asked to this team “How will new FDG be in future?”The teammates are chosen from different departments to get a different insights.

Selection: In order to tackle the issue, The team visit every step on the processes to see how FDG is produced and delivered. Team saw the dificulties of ths production, and delievering operations. Sales orders are getting in all time includes midnight and holidays. Export operations and airway operations are done in a short time. And these operations should be in legacy. The effect of the radioactivity on these operations are seen. All team joined to all of these operations.

Insight: this team; It was a very serious and innovative work that he pondered to produce and sell in a different way under all these difficult conditions and long-term habitual habits. Team members developed themselves by having to leave their comfort areas.

Approach:

If I wanted to try this exercise again, I would make the workers go deeper. To change this approach, I'll start with personal story-building and then transform them into real-world situations to show how they interact within career boundaries. For example, businessmen and engineers have completely different paths to their professional positions, but they often interact in the business world. This will help to apply the concepts that careers are not separated by difficult limits, but are all part of a large community.

ASSIGNMENT REFLECTION  Busi Tarek  2019-12      Challenge

Last year, as part of my master’s degree in Digital Marketing, I wrote a professional thesis

about the “what’s for dinner tonight” question. I wanted to understand why, even today with

all the digital tools available, it is still complicated for families to decide easily what to eat at

home on weekday evenings. I learned a lot during my thesis research. But, when I decided

to turn it in a product or service, I felt that my school research was good, but too light to

reflect the true reality of my primary user group. I had plenty pain points on my whiteboard,

but finally no really idea what the real problem was.       Selection

I decided to conduct further individual interviews with a group of ten users, mothers between

25 and 45 years old. I began created an interview guide with a dozen open-ended questions

focusing on my user's behaviors in the kitchen and it was in its first version, the perfect

boring survey. I realized that just asking a question would not bring me the genuine answer.

Especially since in France, it is almost disturbing to say loud and clear that we don't care

about what we eat... this is becoming less and less socially acceptable.   I needed a way to encourage my users to express themselves freely and fully. And that's

when a friend of mine suggested I use images. According to him, images are very useful to

capture non verbal thoughts or emotions. I chose to try this tool called visualization, hoping

that it would unlock any discomfort by placing the user in their daily situations and actions.       Application

The Reading Buddy

The New Orleans public schools realized there was an immediate need to help poor performing  students in low-income schools after Hurricane Sandy. These students had been displaced the  year before, and some did not attend school in their new cities. As a result, the reading skills of  these students suffered. It was decided to partner with college students be reading buddies to  give them extra attention and time to work on their reading. I was one of those college  students.    The vision of the program was to help the students but also to connect the college students to  the local community. As a reading buddy I too had a vision for my students. I wanted them to  improve not only their reading skills but let them know they had someone they could confide in  as the students were still living with the stress of returning to damaged homes and in some  cases lost loved ones. As the Good Kitchen example noted, the seniors served had negative  feelings towards receiving help and did not enjoy their meals. I learned the children did not  have a positive experience with reading because they felt ashamed of their lack of skills. I  enlisted the help of a librarian to help me find age-appropriate books. I also included some of  my favorite childhood books, so that I could share my own memories. I thought by sharing my  memories I could get the children to open up to me. I too lived in a city impacted by the storm  and understood their stress. In order to get into their minds, I added an additional task. Each  week, I asked them a question unrelated to the book. For example, I asked what is something  you want me to know about you? If you had a million dollars how would you spend it? What do  you want Santa to bring you? The answers were heartbreaking. These might seem like silly  questions, but I gained insight into their struggles. I then asked the librarian what children’s  books I could use to address these topics. Design thinking for innovation – Final assignment.

The main challenge for this final assignment is related to the lack on ownership and cooperation my  employees have when we are working and they have to work hard. Basically, they do not  understand that if they don`t do a good job and perform, the company will not generate money  hence they will not be able to keep their jobs.

I am the chief of spare parts at a big cars company in my country. I`m in charge of both, the sales  team and the were house team. Unfortunately, I have not been able to increase the production of the  sales team so far and I see that they do not want to perform, they are working really slow and they  do not care about the customer. This small team is composed by 3 sellers and one manager. This is

the challenge I have chosen for the final assignment.

The tool that I have selected in order to face and solve this challenge is the storytelling one, that we  have seen it on the module number 2. I believe the storytelling is a very important and powerful tool  and if I can apply it right, my message will be more powerful and I will be able to get the best out of  every single member of my team.

So far what my sales team has told me and what I have observed, is that they feel like no one cares  about them. They tend to think that no one is looking at their results and no one is even saying thank  you to them. This has changed the mood of their office in a way that coming to work isn`t fun  anymore.

I should be the one changing this and I should be the first to apologize to them because of this  situation. My employees are my number 1 priority and sometimes I do not say it the way I should. text: Leading the Learning with Design Thinking  Design Thinking for Innovation – Peer Graded Assessment  Antonio Ledezma  March 15, 2018    Challenge  I work for a Pharmaceutical Company, and we follow our parent organization’s  business planning process of developing “Mid-Term Plans (MTP)” that are 3-year  road maps that help us map our departmental goals to the overall corporate  goals.  We are nearing the end of the MTP that covered 2009-2015 for the  Training Department, and will be preparing to refresh our goals for 2019-2021.  In  the past, the Leadership team has completed this exercise on our own, and then  cascaded our plan down to the rest of the department.  I believe that we have an  opportunity to improve upon our plans by including the individual trainers and  support staff in this process.  Applying the principles learned in this course,  specifically the idea generation insights from Week 3, could really provide us with  a robust plan for the next three years.    Selection  My rationale behind choosing to leverage idea generation stems from the  thinking around the questions “What is” and “What if”.  As a Training Department,  our Vision is to Lead the Learning for our customers.  You will note that we do  not say “training” and that is by design.  We strive to make our classroom events  more than traditional lecture sessions with interactive workshops, the inclusion of  technology, and leveraging different room layouts for a more immersive feel.  In  the spirit of keeping things fresh – using “What is” could be a perfect start for  taking a look at our learners, how they learn today compared to how our classes  function, and to really dig into their needs.  Then we can leverage “What if”  sessions to build out a host of ideas that can reinvigorate what we do. Reflection - Visualization

Challenge  The Challenge I have is to initiate a digitalization project in a public library. The  question that needs to be answered is: “What kind of programs, like workshops,  tours, talks, etc. can the library run to create a valuable benefit for the public?”. In  the “What is?”-Phase we are analyzing the current status of the institution, including  the setting and the stakeholders. The goal is to make digital elements accessible to  the visitors of the library and also to educate the staff in supplying those. To achieve  this you have to take into the account the mindset of both stakeholders. Visitors are  primarily interested in analog media like books and newspaper. Employees are  administrative staff that have, putting it in a very simplified way, a mindset  accustomed to linear problem solving, due to the fact that a vast amount of their  work is sorting and filing books using excel sheets.   To launch a transformation in this field with sustainable results I will need to  incorporate the employees in the process. In order to activate the other side of their  brain visualization tools seem a probate and effective tool. A big part of the  challenge is to bring the team together to create a project that reaches out to the  public. The team and the public both need to learn to use new digital devices and  media.    Selection and Application  Since visualization connects to the emotional side of the brain, I chose this  approach, because the learning process is deeply connected to emotions and works  best in a playful and fearless environment. We went through the phases “What- Is”(1), “What-If”(2), “What-Wows”(3) and “what-Works”(4) using different  visualization tools. Name: Rosnani Kiah

Reflection – Mind mapping

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of Mind mapping tool that help me to understand how to use

design thinking to generate innovative ideas during brainstorming meetings and problem-

solving sessions. I use this approach often with my customers and my working plans so that I

can build a perfect project in all aspects. Furthermore, as a Pre-sales engineer who always

research and study to apply new technology innovations and services to customers. Therefore,

I have to draw strategies to introduce and persuade the other people to use my products and

solutions which I prepare and show to them. For these reasons in my work and life, design

thinking methods aims to direct the attendees thinking towards a specific flow in order

to achieve creativity or find innovative solutions for problems, especially Mind mapping

is one of the efficient methods that organize all these in a formation and in a visually

brain-friendly method. In addition, apart from the benefits for myself, Mind mapping

also a useful tool to logical remember everything, particular for students who often learn

by heart some lesson in order to pass the exam.

Application

When I start to make a potential deal, I draw up a strategy so that it includes the attraction and

innovation which are the strong points to help customer understand the true value I bring to

them. However, what the most important for me is time management, I need to show the

deadline to customer so that they can arrange their time to listen my project. Mind mapping

improve my ability to understand ideas and collaborate during meetings. In a research by

Chuck Frey, mind mapping expert, employees who use a mind mapping method believe

that their productivity increased by 25 percent. Therefore, in the project two week ago, I

try to apply what I have learned from the mind mapping course to manage my time and as

the result, I had achieved the following:

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a great tool that I use all the time, and I consider it necessary to Capture Attention, Build Trust, and Close a negotiation or obtain resources. I work with international teams, supporting and coordinating projects that focus on enhancing the experience of being a member of the company I work across international teams, helping reduce cultural shock, helping them feel part of a big company, and giving recognition and improve cross-collaboration.  I use storytelling to obtain approval from senior managers to run a project, get a perk for the employees or set process that may enhance cross-cultural collaboration, some times it gets a lot of time and efforts to obtain approval from senior managers since in company terms, could not be a top priority, this could be challenging.   I use stories from the employees or my personal experiences. I creatively use the information, knowing that senior management spends a lot of time in meetings, so I try to use interactive tools while sharing the story.

Application I have one story that came to my mind. Almost a year ago, the company had to merge international departments into one single Global department; this incorporation was intended to equal opportunities, improve international user and employee experience, and make diversity a priority within the company. This goal sounds amazing and mindful; however it brought a lot of challenges and bottlenecks. After a few months that the merger started, cultural shock arrived within the international members, with that lack of collaboration and unsuccessful processes dropping almost 20% of the international employee satisfaction. I proposed launching an intercultural activity within all the teams, mapping all the cultures that integrated a team to help individuals and teams identify how cultures can impact their work, increase awareness, and be more effective at bringing differences and preventing invisible cultural bar

text: Simona Blasi, Peer-graded assignment, Design Thinking for Innovation    Challenge:    The health care experience is typically straight forward; we expect it to have an outcome that  provides us with a course of action (i.e., an intelligent, honest provider who tells us what’s wrong  and sets us on a course of action). But, what about all the other pieces of the journey along the  way?    We define our patient journey as of discovering, engaging, caring, getting better, managing  costs and living life. Every patient has a story; a place they’re trying to go. Along this journey, it’s  important for us to remember that and offer ourselves to help them get there.     With that, each piece of the journey has potential to add small, but significant, experiences that  build personal, meaningful elements.    We feel virtual reality could be one of those experiences during the caring part of the journey.  But, I didn’t want to offer it and not know what patients thought (e.g., content, feelings, physical  reaction). We don’t really know how patients will react to it so we need to learn more.     Selection:    A learning launch is just what’s needed to help guide this decision and learn more about how  patients feel about a virtual reality experience added to care. As I learned in this course, the  times of the standard business plan are gone. It’s time to experiment and not just base our  actions on guessing and projection.    As defined, a learning launch i​s a carefully designed experiment or prototype designed to test  the key underlying value-generating assumptions of a potential new-growth initiative. A  “business-world application of the scientific method.”    As Sebastian Garcia said in the lecture, “​at learning launch you are launching out there into the unknown.”  And, that’s exactly what we need to do to learn more about patients’ feelings on virtual reality.    “New-growth” for this launch is adding a meaningful experience to patient care through virtual  reality

text:
INTERNAL

Mind Mapping – Enterprise Project

Challenge:

I work as business architecture lead who basically decompose the

functions and capabilities in businesses and maps the values in the right  stream. I was assigned to lead complex project in addition to the current  projects. The project was large legacy system (functioning well) which  needs to be replaced with new system with emerging technologies. I stared  to read the important docs of it, interviewed SME to better understand. It  leads me to solve each module individually without integrating business  solution to other modules.

Selection:

I realized that I should look at the big picture at map all modules

together some way or another. So, I looked at Mind Mapping tool through  design thinking tools and techniques to help me better understand this  challenge at discover ways to solve it.

Application:

I started building the main modules in the center and write arrows that

leads to the sub-modules from each main module, and so on. Once I saw  all the modules and its related stakeholders and outputs at one look, it  leads me to better visualize the value stream though the functions on the  system. And create useful building blocks of the business.

Insight & Approach:

Having all the building blocks together gives me and the team more

visualization of linking each module with the correct one. While discovering  the mind mapping tool in this challenge, I addressed the opportunity to  utilize storytelling tool in design thinking that might help me in future

INTERNAL

challenges, which gives me better understanding on how to link the  proposed solution to the original problem area.

As a student of Manipal University Jaipur, a couple of teachers present to me a challenge, me  and my team have the task to generate an impact to a very specific group of people, with the  intention to create enough intrigue for this group so they visit the museums in that are in  Monterrey, Mexico. It was a very difficult challenge for me and my other two teammates  because it is very rare for people to visit museums nowadays even if sometimes the entrance  has no charge.

Selection

Storytelling is a great tool that help us to share our experiences, emotions, or values. With this  tool we can generate a memory that connect us with the people that is willing to listen the  story that we are sharing.

When we share a story, we express emotions and we generate empathy, that is an important  goal for everyone that wants to transmit a message, share feeling between the storyteller and  the audience.

Application

In order to complete this task, we had to visit several of the most important museums in  Monterrey, for every tour that we experience we took photos, videos and information of the  things that most caught our attention, we use all this and summarize our experiences with the  intention of share our point of view about the experience that every museum have to offers for  the visitors.

The most important notes that we try to add in this work were that we describe our day in the  museum and we highlight the plays or exhibits that we most enjoy, this help us transmit our  enthusiasm about the museums and visually share a preview of what anyone could expect from  this places, that are easy to forget if you does not visit museums very often.

Successful leaders exhibit a growth mindset; grounded in  one’s beliefs and values, transformational leaders are open to new ideas and perspectives and are  continuously learning and growing. Our firm’s employees are encouraged to share insights and questions  throughout the program. The program is intentionally provocative.

text:
Reflection Assignment: Storytelling for Building Relationships

Challenge:

I work for a small not-for-profit organization that provides home care and personal supports to  seniors so that they are able to live independently at home for as long as possible.  My role is in  corporate communications, which includes public relations and marketing communications. We have  extremely limited resources for communications: the corporate communications budget is $0, while  the marketing budget is a modest $15,000.  Basically, our marketing communications efforts need to  cost little and have a big impact. For us effective communication is about engaging with the right  audiences and, with such limited resources, this has become fundamental.

Selection:

We chose the storytelling tool because we have a good understanding of our audience.  While the  primary users of our services are seniors, we knew that few seniors sought support services (like  home cleaning, companionship, help with personal hygiene or cooking, or home maintenance)  themselves.  For many older adults seeking these services is akin to admitting defeat and they  generally prefer to rely on family and friends whenever possible. Of course, this arrangement may  work well for the senior, but it can put an enormous amount of pressure on the family member who  becomes the care giver.  We know from secondary research that this caregiver is often the eldest  daughter, who has her own priorities, often with a family (children) of her own and a job. Welcome to  the so-called sandwich generation!  The pressures of having to care for both aging parents and their  own children are the main reason why this is our target segment.

In the past we had used marketing copy that was full of jargon and dense language.  It sounded  corporate and unnatural.  We knew that storytelling could add that human dimension we were  missing and could help us have an even better understanding of our clients’ needs.

I am working on an application aimed at developing sales efficiency. Following a survey to users, we  discovered one of our application process’ overall feedback was still very complicated: time consuming,  lacking figures, confusing with too many steps and with a wrong timing in the year as sales users need  to work on big contracts and negotiations at that time of the year.

After all the insights collected we needed to finally validate our  assumptions before starting to go live and communicating about new evolutions, design and new  process. For that we choose to use the “Learning Launch” design thinking tool. Indeed, we clearly  needed to verify if what we had think of could really improve process for sales users. We consequently  use this tool to make them test the process we had prototyped. The prototype was designed on an IT  environment and we decided to show our prototypes to several stakeholders.

Application:

Among all stakeholders that participated in previous survey and workshops, we choose 2 directors, 2  account leaders and 2 contributors and let them test the prototype and give us feedbacks. We first start  mentioning new deadlines to give them some context. Then, we gave them specific access adapted to  their profile and they had one hour meeting to do the process. Reflection - Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

I noticed the elderly people in my family and in my neighbourhood, I observed a-lot of them faced several issues, mainly back and joint pain. This problem made it difficult For them to perform many essential tasks is difficult. They often needed external help To be able to perform them. Among people Facing discomfort and pain due to back pain, several mutual elements were visible. To further understand the problem in great depth I opted for mind-mapping outlining the problems. Mapping them to possible solutions Creating relations between different elects to better define the scope and form a cohesive solution to the Problems identified.

Application

Given the pandemic, I decided to conduct an online google survey among Elderly people to better understand the target demographic, analyse the problem To find the underlying issue  and develop a proper solution. From the insights I gathered from this, along with telephonic interviews. I developed a mind. I noted down the most crucial insights and information using key words, and then made connections between facts and ideas visually- developing a coherent flow of elements. The process really helped connect the dots between different people from the target audience and understand the problem. I analysed that most people suffered from arthritis, Parkinson’s diseases and acidity. I created a mind-map of the same.

Insight and Approach

Incorporating the mind mapping method in the problem identification and research. It drastically improved creativity and helped me understand and retain the user in great depth. It helped me generate new ideas, unique concepts and reduce complexity of the problem by breaking it down into simple terms and forming the structure to conceptualize and broaden perspective. Reflection: Storytelling

Challenge    I am currently working as a supervisor in a process engineering team. When the COVID-19 pandemic  hit our country, the productivity in terms of completion duration of work items assigned to our team  has significantly dropped with tier 1 items, evaluations categorized as easy to medium difficulty, taking  almost twice as long. My challenge was to find out the specific cause of the drop in productivity so as  to be able to properly propose solutions that may be applicable to other teams as well.    Selection    Recognizing that the issue at hand is more personal in nature rather than technical and requires in- depth understanding how the team members perceive the current situation, Storytelling was the  selected tool.     Application and Approach    A survey form was developed to have an initial grasp of the team’s concerns. The initial plan was to  conduct an open forum with all the team members present but this was later changed to a one-on-one  informal talks so as to have more open conversations.     After these, the information and insights gathered seem to still be insufficient and that members were  still hesitant in raising all their concerns so a half day for de-stressing was scheduled for the team  members where they were allowed to use the time allotted to converse and connect with other team  members accordingly. Then they were later asked to raise any concern they see from the other team  member’s perspective without name-dropping. This vastly increased the feedback acquired from the  members.      Insights and Approach    One of the most notable stories from the conversations was with the youngest member of the team.  He shared that there is a growing fear in the company housing compound that some people already  are infected and that the set protocols from the company are very vague. Added to this, he was being  treated unfairly by the other residents since his parent recently went home from working overseas.  Eve

stick notes. The ideas have reflected the opportunities to grow further and to extend the online

teaching with certain courses.

groups. In order to trigger the ideas, I have shown the present digital infrastructure such as computers,

mobile phones, internet connectivity and uninterrupted power supply. The present online teaching

modes and pedagogical tools and techniques have been conveyed. Individually, I spoke with the group

unexpected pandemic.

various difficulties having a productive class during this pandemic. Since all the

kindergartens were closed from February, we had to figure out a new way to ensure

online class approach just like most of the school did. However, children at this age

could hardly concentrate for a long period of time, let alone asking them to sit in front

talking at the same time, or they might even walk away from their computers. I find

this method to be comparatively less suitable and teachers would have no idea how

much knowledge the students were receiving or if they even paid any attention

during the online class.     So later I discovered a design thinking tool, Visualization, to achieve a better

outcome during this period of time. It is because when young kids are asked to be

seated for a certain period of time, they would soon be distracted by other things in

the surroundings. Therefore, they might lose interest to the class easily. By showing

the teaching materials in their face, and letting the students hold the same props as

the teachers do could arouse their interest better, and hopefully I could conduct a

Design Thinking for Innovation in the Air Transport Industry

1. Challenge: As a leading technology provider in the air transport industry,

our company is currently facing significant obstacles due to COVID-19.   Specifically, survey responses from a wide array of both airline and airport  customers yielded a common theme: people are afraid to fly right now.   They are extremely wary of contracting the virus.  This fear has resulted in a  90% decrease in transactional volume in certain business units in a 2-month  span.  In order to get our business on track, we needed to address this  immediate concern in a manner that is operationally sound and cost  effective.  First and foremost, we needed to win back the trust of our  customers by alleviating any reservations they had regarding their health  during upcoming air travel experiences.

2. Selection:  Given the dramatic impact COVID-19 has had on the business,

our executive leadership team knew that swift action was necessary.  Their  first course of action was to consult major airline and airport customers.   These major customers had in turn sought feedback from their passengers  to determine what would comfort them enough to fly again.  Collectively, it  was determined that a learning launch would work best.  As Lopez from  the University of Virginia alluded to in his lecture, we needed to perform a  small experiment to test a new idea in the marketplace.  Specifically, we  would deploy existing biometric screening technology to perform a quick  health screen for passengers just prior to boarding.  This would allow the  test to be implemented rapidly and at minimal incremental cost.  Our  hypothesis was that this new product would ensure the health and assuage  the fear of all passengers during the pandemic. Challenge & Selection

The tool I selected is Visualization. I use this approach often with our students, who are still in the  initial learning stage. I have used many times the subcategory of visualization which are known as  charts, graphs, various tree diagrams to convert the textual form or the various geographical or  demographic and statistical aspects in visualized form. Sometimes there is hurry of conducting  meetings or the listener or the speaker has a less time to communicate or …the speaker or the  presenter sometimes gets short on his vocabulary …here the visuals a play a major role. Visualization  is there in work since the stone age man existed, rather I would say Visualization was the primary  language because visualization was primarily observed as the paintings carved in the caves of stone  age man, the stone age people used to communicate through those drawn paintings. They conveyed  their feelings; they conveyed the happened incidents etc and if you see in this 21st century we are  using pie charts, graphs, tree diagram, not only in education industry but also everywhere else.

Project Title: Upgrading Educational Halls

These rooms are part  of an educational institution and contain old equipment, while a decade has  passed since the last renovation. We start from the central idea,  add basic axes and, in each of them, we put the individual ideas that come to  mind. Advantages of mind mapping are the better structure of thoughts, the  better overview of a topic as well as the enhancement of the flow of new  ideas. In addition, mind mapping not only helps to put our thoughts down and  in order. It helps a lot to communicate them to others so that they understand  them and watch them. This is the main reason I chose the mind mapping tool  as it needed fast and efficient project development and completion.

Application: I started the process by trying to gather views and ideas  regarding the improvement of the provided education. So I created  appropriate questionnaires which were given to people (students and  educators) who at that time were using these training rooms. Next, I gathered  the staff of the department with which we do brainstorming, in order to draw  opinions from the staff with whom I would organize the renovation work of the  rooms.

Reflection - Mind Mapping

Challenge

In research and development activities, perhaps one of the most difficult tasks next to identifying a  research topic is the creation of research methodology which is not only original but also innovative.  For instance, when a methodology is decided and once review of related literatures is done, we usually  find out that the methodology we have decided on is not anymore original or might be that many  other works have already been doing the proposed methodology. If these things happen, another  meeting will be done to brainstorm again on other research methodology that will work with the  research project. Now how do we fix this time-consuming stage of the research and development?

Selection

The design thinking tool that we use for this problem is mind mapping. Mind mapping for us is a tool  that captures the things that we think of specifically in designing research methodologies. Mind  mapping helps us generate, visualize, structure, and classify ideas to look for patterns and insights that  provide key design criteria. We select this design thinking tool because it saves us so much time and  we also see some gray areas that later becomes especially useful in our studies. The outliers in our  mind map are usually the ideas that helps us proceed with our study and mind mapping is immensely  helpful in finding these outliers.

In our mapping, we usually require the members of the research group to have already read  journals, patents, and other relevant research materials that we can use prior to attending the  brainstorming activity. We also ask them to bring their review of literature notes with them. We  then start to discuss the research methodology starting with one central topic that branch out into  several subtopics. DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenges & Selection

My passion is working with orphans and the vulnerable in our society. My country being one of the highest  hit by HIV/AIDS epidemic, found herself in a state where orphans outnumbered those with parents.  HIV/AIDS has claimed more lives than any other causes of deaths. Having grown up without parents as  well, I always felt that my experience and what used to be pain, can bring them hope. It is difficult to deal  with these people especially if you have not been there yourself. These people feel lonely, have low self- esteem, and have a lot of anger towards life in general. For these reasons I always use Storytelling tool.  This tool prove to be useful because it connects with their emotions and in turn brings healing. From those  that I have worked with, one thing that instantly come out is, it is not easy for them to open up. They need  something to trigger them to respond and that thing is something that relates to their current state. I  often use their response to have an insight of their behavioral patterns and also develop ways and  strategize on how well I can address and bring them to new life.

Application

Naturally, he wanted to give his mother a dignified  burial and the only way to do so, according to him was to bury her on a weekend, something that his  uncles didn’t agree with. Storytelling

Challenge & Selection  Storytelling is a great tool that I use all the time. I work with vulnerable populations, developmentally  disabled individuals, senior citizens, and economically disadvantaged people. Many of these people deal  with oppression and dysfunction in every aspect of their lives, they need to be empowered and  inspiration is a path to empowerment. I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to  inspire them to improve their circumstances. When I work with seniors, we share stories for different  reasons. Often, they're lonely and are so happy to share stories of their lives with me to connect and  they find meaning in sharing these experiences as a form of teaching and/or legacy, in a sense. With my  developmentally disabled clients I share stories of my life in order to help them visualize a state of  independence, I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their goals, and  sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this  information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to gain more  independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives. Covid-19  and  working  from  home  has  radically  changed  footwear  demand,  where  feet  go   and  don’t  go,  how  quickly  shoes  are  worn  out,  and  many  other  factors.  Do  you  need  shoes   when  you  now  spend  work  time  at  home?   Shoes  aren’t  visible  in  a  zoom  meeting,  are  they   relevant?   What  are  they  wearing  or  want  to  wear  while  working  from  home?     When  they  do  go  out,  people’s  habits  and  patterns  have  changed.   Will  there  be  a  need  for   formal  shoes?  Will  sneakers  grow  to  be  even  more  popular?   Is  going  out  a  chance  to  dress   up  a  bit  and  celebrate  fashion?     With  a  horizon  of  only  two  years,  what  footwear  opportunities  are  there  for  La Puerta Falsa?   What   do  customers  need?   What  do  they  want?   How  will  they  use  footwear?   What  should  PURPLE ACADEMY – WEMA BANK PLC’s  new  line  look  like?   Can  TMC  sustain  livelihoods  for  our  stakeholder  artisans  by   changing  what  footwear  it  sells? text:
Co-creating value through design

Challenge

We had to redesign the packaging of the leading sugar brand in the country, with more than 30 years in  the market and penetration of almost 98% in homes. For a long time the brand, Triple play, had been  almost exclusively the only white sugar available in the market, without having any strong competition.  However, the economic impact of the pandemic opened the possibility of importing sugar, and  consequently, cheaper brands began to arrive with the potential to steal market share from Triple play.

Although it was the brand “of a lifetime”, the loyalty of its consumer was impacted. In the end, sugar is a  commodity and in times of economic recession, the weight of the trajectory and the local origin was not  enough to guarantee the purchase.

That is why the need to renew the image of the brand was imminent, especially to attract the new  decision-making generations of household purchases, who did not have a strong bond with Triple play  as the older consumers who had grown up with it.

The packaging is the first communication vehicle for any product, so we decided to bet on its redesign to  communicate the new values of the brand, and project a more renewed, empathetic, and relevant image  for the consumer.

The challenge was that we did not know what these values, attributes, and emotions were, which Indus Business Academy could credibly appropriate and that generate a powerful connection with the consumer, capable of  resisting the price differential.

The solution took a truly consumer-centric approach. That is how we decided that the new packaging  would not leave the mind of the brand manager or the agency designer. Rather, we would co-create it  together with consumers as a team: brand, agency, and consumer.

text: Istanbul Mobile Application  – Learning Launch  Challenge    As an automobile industry employee living in Istanbul where has many transportation  issues  to  be  improved or solved, I was a team member for providing mobile apps for city’s Dolmuş System. Dolmuş is  a microtransit solution created by the city itself as a self-improvisation decades ago. Those are public  minibuses  operates in pre-designated and planned routes, leaves the station when it is full. The full price  is equal to a taxi price yet it is divided into 8 as the vehicle has 8 passengers. It is faster and more  comfortable than other public transportation solutions.     As the vehicle starts travelling when it is full, there is no chance to get in the vehicle in case you are not  on the departing station, especially for long routes. We thought creating a mobile app would help people  to make reservations, embrace the utilization of Dolmuş, and dispose the obligation to go to the  departing station by making a seat reservation and pre-payment.    Selection    We have conducted very intensive design thinking activities which ended nowhere as we received  multiple and various information that contradicts each other. Thus, we have created a clickable  prototype and provide social media and personal advertisements on the stations. Learning Launch then  commenced as a step.    Application    Our learning launch was to identify the potential customers that do not use Dolmuş as the vehicles  departs with no empty seats . Those potential passengers are the dwellers living at mid-roads, thus unable  to utilize the Dolmuş vehicles unless they arrive at the first station.  Thus, team prioritized the longest routes that has no passenger circulation on the road. Those routes also  are expensive ones, and drivers do not want to risk any rooms on the vehicle. We organized the drivers to  reserve seats for the applications made via clickable prototype application. Apart from the application,  every step was manual
