text:
Moving to a new municipality – getting insithts from new  inhabitants to make better services

Challenge and selection

I work in a municipality and every year about 1200 new inhabitants move from other areas to  our municipality. We know something about our new inhabitants; age, where they move from,  if they have children and so on. We want to know more about how they orientate ang gather  information about their new municipality and the services they need when they move to a  new municipality. Do they need school for their children, kindergarten, health services if they  have chronical diseases for example.

To get more and better understanding of the user need I want to use the tool Storytelling.

Since we know who the newest inhabitants are I want to recruit some and invite them to tell  their moving story from when they decided to move to the municipality and the whole process  until the daily life in the new municipality/community.

Their story will give new insights from a human perspective we can use to make better  services to the new and existing habitants. Since many different people move to our  municipality we have to invite people with age and background to catch different needs  according to age, life situation and need for services. I will use storytelling in the faze of  problem framing.

Storytelling

This stage comes early in the design process. It aims to explore the problem to build an  accurate understanding of the main issue that needs to be solved. In the problem framing  stage, the storytelling can be used in this explorative initiative. It helps the design team to  engage with the user to define the problem using a qualitative data from the consumers.

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge & Selection

Visualization is a great tool in that it gives a clear idea when sharing your thoughts to others.

When sharing your thoughts with others, you usually confront several problems. Even though you

think you have told everything to explain about a subject, the degree of understanding would be

different according to the level of information others have. However, visualization gives you an

idea what the subject is all about because you can visualize. For example, people may come up

with different images even though they read the same book whilst they all can come up with

exactly same image when watched the same movie.

I work in a financial industry where I have to provide clients with the best portfolios of financial

products consisting of stocks, funds, fixed income and etc. It’s quite challenging to tell what

portfolios would best suit for the client because every client has different background in financial

product. Some might have high level of understanding while others have only basic ideas. So I

began to explain by using the visualization tool to better explain.

Application

Even though the investment can be best explained in numbers(how profitable you are in

percentage(%)) as its purpose it to gain as much profit as possible, I decided to draw images of

financial products on a power point program by using some friendly images which I thought best

explain the financial product and uploaded on an iPad screen. In this way, not only was I able to

better organize portfolios for each different client and they were very satisfied to see their

portfolios in the form of image.

I wanted to be sure that all of the client understands what their portfolios would look like so I

Challenge and Selection

The tool I selected was Storytelling, helping to better connect with the problem at hand before we test  ideas. Working in engineering it is sometimes hard for people to put themselves in the field working on  the equipment they are doing the design work on. This can create a challenge when designs on paper do  not practically align in the field. Storytelling allows me to create an image in the engineer’s heads as  they are coming up with design to better factor in field restraints and requirements that may otherwise  not be considered.

Application

To begin I develop a story of a normal day operator or mechanic working on that piece of equipment.  The story develops into several different situation and common issues that may arise. The problems are  not always complex and can be very basic in nature; unable to reach a certain component or the  function interferes with another component.

I then encourage the engineers to play a role in the story, how we can solve the problem at hand. Ideas  and suggestions are put on a board to later be built into design consideration. Through the session ideas  are weeded through and the story continues. New problems maybe faced and input from other to come  up with more protentional problems. The activity not only helps place the engineer in the field but also  establishes a flow of idea and thought among the group.

The Storytelling tool helps reinforcing that the new design has a life after our desk. That this will become  someone else project and responsibility. The tool allows the group to break out of their normal roles  and partake in someone else’s. This helps create an imaginative aspect in its own which I believe also  contributes into coming up with a better design.

text:
Design Thinking Assignment: Improve  Feedback Hackathon

1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.  My workplace has an untimely and convoluted feedback process. To receive feedback,  employees must wait until the end of a project, or formally request feedback from  colleagues.

I participated in an internal hackathon to improve the feedback process. Our team discussed  the current process with other employees and found this process limits the amount of  feedback employees receive each year and discourages peer-to-peer feedback. We also  found that colleagues could feel awkward giving constructive criticism to peers.

2. Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g.,  what it is and why you selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate  video lecture references)  To create a better feedback system, I chose the visualisation tool. Initially, I was worried  about using visualisation as I see myself as quite a bad drawer. But after watching Angela  Myer’s video on visualisation, I realised that when it comes to design thinking, visualisation  isn’t about drawing pretty pictures rather using visual tools to enable a team to collaborate  on ideas. As Ms. Myer said, visualisation enables us to “tap into a single picture” and  “achieve a sense of agreement and consensus”.

3. Application: Describe how you applied the tool you selected to your challenge  (e.g., what you did and how the tool was applied effectively or ineffectively).  I used visualisation to create a peer-to-peer feedback tool. I first tried to describe my idea to  other members of my team, but I found that each person had a different understanding of  what I was saying. I then drew this simple table:

My positive feedback for you

Your positive feedback for me

My development points for you

Your development points for me

Creating this table enabled my team to work on something concrete together. In homage to  Legally Blonde 2: Red

text:
DESIGN THINKING  AND INNOVATIONS.

vISualization tool:

Challenges:

When we're dealing with very complex  problems, we're enacting a different kind  of problem solving that has to bring in  more than just logic. Visualization is  really important for the process of  Design Thinking because it's actually a  way of unlocking a different part of our  brain.

Selection:

I selected the tool “Visualization”  because it taught me how to visualize a  problem or any aspect in a problem  solving manner and think laterally.

It all depends on our vision and our own  perceptions how a problem is. the way  we visualize it and tackle it in an  appropriate way itself defines how  innovative we are. This tool  “visualization” plays a major role in our  personal life and enhances our thinking  and it helps us to go forward in life with  proper visualization.

https://youtu.be/h9YTxzr_HPS

The above given is the reference link to  help you learn more detailed about  “visualization” concept in design  thinking and innovation.

Application:

This can help us in many daily life  applications practically.

1.  Visualize Your Problem. Whether

you're solving critical global problems  or tackling micro-level projects,  visualization reveals key themes and  patterns.

2.  Challenge Common Assumptions.

3.  Reverse Your Thinking

4.  Empathize With Your Audience.

5.  Embrace Risk and Failure

Insight:

Visualization is about using images. It's  not about drawing; it's about visual  thinking. It pushes us beyond using  words or language alone. It is a way of  unlocking a different part of our brains  that allows us to think nonverbally and  that managers might not normally use.

Approach:

1.  Visualize with the 'Mental

Rehearsal' Technique.

2.  Create Goal Pictures.

3.  Create a Visual Picture and an

Affirmation for Each Goal.

4.  Index Cards.

5.  Use Affirmations to Support

Your Visualization.

6.  Expect Results.

text:
Challenge

Adolescence is a particularly difficult time and teenagers go through many rites of passage. For  most people, their final high school exams are the first high stakes, life-impacting exams.

As humans we forget around 50% of what we learned yesterday and by the end of the week  70% has gone (Ebbinghaus, 2013). To combat this we study, but most study habits used by  students are high effort, low efficiency and not brain friendly (eggion, 2017).

There is relentless, and growing pressure on senior high school students to perform, but it  comes at a cost. Around 40% of Australian Year 12 students have clinical anxiety issues around  exams (North, 2015).

I believed that an app that provided a highly personalised study/revision experience would help  these students achieve their academic goals with less stress.

Selection

Confident in my technical knowledge of behavioural and cognitive science and the high-level  secondary research but resource constrained, like many start-ups my challenge was whether an  app could be designed that was visually engaging, simple to use and likely to materially benefit  students and to learn this without expending all of my resources. Given my context I chose the  Learning Launch tool to help bring the visual product designs to life and learn whether the  identified customer needs and underlying key assumptions were true, or not as the case maybe.

A Learning Launch is a process whereby a hypothesis can be tested by:

§  Specifying the current key assumptions, across

§  Identifying and understanding the key pain felt by students and their parents

§  Test whether our key assumptions matched the students’ and their parents’ truth

§  Ascertain whether key design perspectives would be simple, engaging and effective

§  Gauge to under what circumstances customers would act to resolve their pain

I applied the Learning Launch to gain deeper quality data and insight from students, parents and  senior high school teach

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge & Selection     My primary goal as a Facilitator/Mentor is to create a classroom environment in which students from all  backgrounds can achieve their potential and learn to think as an Entrepreneur/Innovator. To accomplish  this goal, my teaching philosophy relies on active learning strategies.   I believe the traditional lecture is an important component of any class I teach. However, I also believe  lecturing must be combined with other teaching pedagogy, because not all students learn best from  lectures. Especially, if you are teaching Entrepreneurship, then you have to be very dynamic in teaching  patterns. Design thinking is my new research area and nowadays I try to use its maximum tools in my class.    Visualization tool is the most favorite technique of mine while in the class of Entrepreneurship. I use this  tool to share valuable insights about a problem among a diverse group of students. My students gets easily  connected through this technique and they identify possible solutions to the specific problems. We play the  game of drawing your imagination in the class without any previous artistic qualities. I instruct them to  draw whatever comes to their mind when they see a problem and identify its possible solutions. This  approach benefitted us many times. We draw a problem on the chalkboard and then try to solve it through  brainstorming and drawing tools to make it more visible, simple and lucid.    Application     Every year we conduct an Event “Product Over Weekend”. As a facilitator we are assigned few Students  Entrepreneur. We develop final prototype of their product in this event. They come up with their ideas and  we try to transfer that ideas into visualization, so that best possible solutions can be drawn for a specific  problem. Reflection visualization

Challenge & Selection

Visualization is an important tool to understand the real problem and start to

analyses the situation. I select this tool because it is the first step to get a great

result, you must visualize, understand and, if it’s possible, live the situation to can

truly know the impacts and the individuals’ pain.

During this challenge, people can understand better each other and different

person with different points of view can converge to the same reality. When you

can get this experience, you’ll be able to see the real problem. This tool will unlock

a part of your brain and you’ll be able to expand your horizon, your knowledge of

the world.

My challenge to solve with this tool is to understand why my product doesn’t sell

very well in the supermarket.

Application

I work in a food company and to apply the visualization tool and I accepted the

challenge of go to the supermarket and talk, observes and analysis the consumer.

This approach allows understand what is important to consumers, what they’re

looking for in foods.

You can also understand their needs, difficulties and preferences between other

brands products. This attitude offered a strength contact with consumers and

allows you to solve some doubt about your products and consumers can learn

about their food habits.

Insights

The insights of this approach were that communication with consumers must be

clearer and give them knowledge about what they are buying. For employees in

the company, mainly innovation and R&D area, is very clear what the product

offers, but we shouldn’t forget that the consumers don’t have the same knowledge

of us. We have to consider that consumers don’t have knowledge and,

sometimes, curious to search about some ingredients, but even in this situation,

they have to be able to objective understand about what they are eating or buying.

So, the opportunity to use visualization tool gives some important insights that we

Monica Avila AUTHOR:

Student of University

DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION

Storytelling

Storytelling is a fundamental tool to connect the brand’s story with the values of the people. I am a volunteer of an NGO which works with vulnerable population, dependent people, immigrants and people with mental illness. All of them need physical, emotional and spiritual care support as a health maintenance. The members and volunteers of the association are doing a great job because they seek to create a comfortable environment which responds to the needs of each individual. Sharing stories of life in order to help them is so important to improve and recover their self-esteem.  We realize that patients typically have a strong connection with young people so our challenge is increasing the number of young NGO’s members for the purposes of having an active and motivated community.  Our team has already gone through several design thinking tools, so we are ready to use the storytelling tool to persuaded young people to be part of the team.

Challenge & Selection

Applications

We start the process by holding brainstormed messages to be aware of the resources that are available or necessary to connect with our young target. Young people should know that they could contribute to the social benefits of the target communities and society in general. It’s important to say that they have the capability to help vulnerable people and the NGO needs their help. I explained the importance to use social media to accelerate the dissemination of information. Young people tend to spend long hours at social networks, so we could take advantage of using this online channel to communicate with them.

Visualization

Reflection – Visualization Challenge & Selection The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or

Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of  stakeholders before attempting to identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I use this  approach often with our customers, who are government agencies working to apply technology

innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their services to their customer, which may

be U.S. citizens, businesses, and non-citizens. I have used the technique of using a straw man  visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for discussion to allow a  diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining the scope,

boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying pain

points and opportunities for improvements or solutions. Application I start the process by creating a  straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw man graphic, I will draw from any  existing material available to understand the environment. The existing material may be operational  or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, GAO or other auditing reports. If  materials are not available, then I conduct informal interviews with one-three of the stakeholders

who serve as my main points of contact on the initiative. If appropriate to the situation, I will borrow  the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from previous research, and discussed in David Gray’s book,  “The Connected Company”. The front-stage/back-stage approach helps to reinforce the notion that  every service – even an internal service – has customers with whom the service provider interacts

C1 - Internal use

Work disruption – Learning Launch

Challenge

In my organization a key issue has been the interruption of work due to several approaches being made  during the day to assist other co-workers or additional ‘urgent’ tasks being added to the existing  workload.

This has created a great deal of stress within the division and has led to the need for several key  deadlines having to be extended.

In order to tackle this issue, a committee was set-up including individuals from different functions in the  division to incorporate everyone’s input and set up a flow

Selection

This committee considered several options to design a solution to test the effectiveness of solution  suggested to be implemented. After careful consideration, we decided to use the ‘learning launch tool’  in Design Thinking. The learning launch is used to list steps to test a workflow for an idea or a product  design before its implementation or ‘go live’.

Application

In order to tackle the aforementioned challenge, we decided to implement a checklist adherence in line  with the managers and a daily status update to review the tasks at hand and to remove or add tasks as  needed based on the progress during the week. The second part of the solution was to have a ‘No  meeting day’ every Wednesday to reduce the time spent in meetings.

As a first step, we decided to introduce the strict use of checklists in one team to find the initial  learnings from such an implementation.

The key learnings gained from this implementation were that in most cases there was relatively low  adherence to the daily checklists and greater time allocated to unplanned activities.

To further enable our teams to manage themselves better, we arranged ‘Time Management’ sessions  for all staff across the division. A post training survey gave a positive response to this training and  highlighted improved management of the tasks at hand for the staff.

Challenge:

In my college time, I took a project titled “Safety aspects of a vehicle”. We were  basically analysing the all the aspects related to vehicle safety. We took example  of normal passenger car to analyse its crashworthiness. We considered all the  aspects and parameters related to crash and vehicle collision. I was leading my  team. But simple manual calculation of forces and time consideration was not  giving the best and realistic results. So we took it as a task to identify the  problem and come with a solution for that problem, so that it won’t happen in  the future. So the challenge for us was to find the exact force and time during  the crash and vehicle collision.

Selection:

To find the exact force and time during collision and crash we had to analyse  frontal portion of the vehicle. So the crash testing was basically the testing of  frontal crash system, that how much load it can withstand. So I thought of  choosing visualisation tool of the complete process and the steps where we  were doing the calculation mistakes. So we selected a computer aided design  tool to visualise the design and used a computer aided analysis tool to do the  structural analysis of the component. We choosed ANSYS software for structural  analysis so that we can have a better 3D visualization of the force analysis.  Before, we were doing the analysis using manual considerations and not using  the actual conditions of the collision because of which every time we were  getting the faulty force and time again and again.

text: Jessica Riyad    Challenge:   A cosmetic pharmaceutical company has in hands a problem with taxes, for reduce tax they  have to innovate their production line for a more green products and less trash generation in  all the productive chain (prime manufacturing to client use). To do so, they don’t want to  abandoned theirs current formulas and fabric structure. Value to say, this company has  bigger online sales then in store. Its clients profile are young people, usually looking for  smart products and less impact    Selection:  Our team choose Mind mapping tool so we could visualise all the steps in the productive  chain and what are the possible points of changing.    Application:  Looking at each step of the process, and marking possible changes, with that we see all the  process and the principals aspects of the impact in environment    Isumes: looking for green seel companies, buying non toxic insumes (would that change the  formula?)  Production: machines more ecological, less wast techniques  Innovation: change packing for more ecological (reuse plastic, non-plastic), change the  transportation system for online shopping (use only paper and no plastic bag in the delivery,  aprimorate the system so the transport itself is more efficient)  Trash control: treatment of the disposal material, if possible, destiny to upcycling.    Insight:  After this big view we were able to see that, the more efficient changes in the company were  insumes and innovation, they respect the currently need of the company, but still make a big  impact in the final disposal created by the company. And as an additional it makes the brand  greener for the shopper, because the packing change is something visible for them.    Approach:  Next I would like to add to this solution, so therefore, in the future would be needed the  results for this acomplishment.

Example Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

As part of the organization’s digital strategy the senior management was looking at identifying processes  that are manual and repeatable in nature and that can be progressively semi-automated or fully  automated depending on the complexity of the process there by deriving operational efficiency. This  added constraint being, this would have to be done without any additional budget and by showing an  improvement to the bottom-line, with an overall reduction in cost on a year on year basis

Selection

As part of the technology function, there was an increasing focus on going digital. There was focus on  time to market for the new ideas and incrementally adding value so that more and more users can be  engaged with the tool which becomes part of the learning, feedback and improvement process. To  accomplish this, we decided to adopt Agile practices to achieve this objective of adding incremental  value with short cycles of development

Application

Out organization had historically followed a waterfall-based development, testing and release approach.  The idea of setting up Agile was fraught with many challenges. To help achieve this objective we decided  to do a learning launch with a sub-department within technology that had all its users within  technology. The team was reorganized and was assigned an Agile coach for a period of 8-12 weeks. The  team was requested to go through the entire pilot with an open mind and emphasis was laid on the  learning and adapting to a new practice. As part of the transformation, all the team members within the  team were certified on Agile best practices. The team went through the agile transformation journey in  12 weeks followed by team adopting to the new approach for a period of 12 weeks.

Challenge:  To introduce my challenge, allow me to first give some background that may establish some context. My  baby brother was born a healthy happy baby, but around the age of 4 fell ill, and spent years going to  doctors, being poked with needles and misdiagnosed time and time again, with no clear explanation as  to what exactly was wrong with him. He was constantly on medication for something or another, and  always taking vitamins to help strengthen his immune and digestive systems. Time had gone by, and  things were getting worse, as each doctor jumped to a new conclusion, listing devastating possibilities  and telling us we need to start making choices as to which treatments to attempt, knowing with some  certainty that there was no clear diagnosis, but only a series of guesses that may be partially correct, but  could also be completely incorrect, and we should just go ahead and hope for the best.

At a point in time, we noticed he was starting to get better, his immunity was stronger and his health  seemed to be returning to normal, something we hadn’t seen in years. We didn’t understand the cause,  and the doctors couldn’t explain it, but we were very pleased. But this improvement was temporary. A  few months later we noticed things were digressing, so we started to think about what had changed in  that period, and what had changed again more recently. The only notable difference was the vitamins  he had been taking. So we looked into this further, and did some research to understand what  ingredients were in the vitamins he was taking when he was better, that were not in the other vitamins,  then we traced back to reach a diagnosis based on this new information, which seemed to fit. We  consulted with doctors who agreed, and finally, we had reached our diagnosis.

Challenge

The challenge is to find a minimum number of people required to take an employability  course that I’m teaching this month for a project that I’ve been working on during the  past year. This project revolves around helping others develop their soft skills towards  the change in paradigm that we’re currently seeing when it comes to labor. Under this  new scheme, it is estimated that automatization will take over and many jobs currently  being executed by humans will be replaced by robots. This will not only expose us to the  possibility of massive displacement, but it will also mean that many of the jobs that we  currently do will disappear and other new jobs that don’t currently exist will replace  them.

This requires for a change in mentality and leads us to a new age of “talentism” in which  we’ll have to pay less attention to technical knowledge, standard degrees and formal  education and more to the areas of soft and interpersonal skills that won’t be ever  replaced by robots. Only the “human touch” will sets us apart, and this translates in  things like having empathy and emotional intelligence.

The people who are lending me the space to perform the course are demanding a  minimum of 12 people to enrol, this is why “selling” it is a challenge. The course  specifically provides a hands-on methodology through which participants will be able to  uncover their talents, competencies and values that will later allow them to follow some  steps to develop an action plan, work on some strategic canvases and come up with a  concrete strategy to follow when it comes to landing their “dream job” or at least  coming closer to dedicating their lives to something that’s truly meaningful to them  whilst ultimately putting their talents to work.

BOOK-LAND (Story telling)

Hello I am normal 1st year b-tech student studying in a university In  Hyderabad. As there was a pandemic this year (2020-2021) we had a  lockdown and we had to go for online education over offline so that  our health doesn’t get affected and also our education continues.  Due to pandemic and online education we didn’t have any access to  offline/hard copies of textbooks or handwritten notes of subjects  which made it difficult for us for studying. We were told to search  the books online so that we can study. But we didn’t get all text  books at one website or app or something. It made things real hard  for us. Also, many text books weren’t available in the internet. So, I  came up with an idea of saving copies of different textbooks in a  drive and share it with my friends for free at first. Then I realized  many people had the same problem and we can’t give online copies  of all books without buying copyrights of it. So, I came up with the  idea of Book-land where we pay minimum cost for getting a copy of  the book by buying the copyright of it. Basically, we created a  website which is more of an e-library with minimum costs for  students to get access to different books at one website without  struggling. I showed this to my mentors and potential customers  (fellow students) which they approved.

Reflection – Storytelling in Food Industry

By Leidy Kabiri

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a content strategy from the latest trends in marketing. In order to be effective this  resource should be use carefully and with verdict data. The consumer should be able to identify  in the story, the company's value ladder. A good story can cover diverse aspects that connect  with the consumer or client, such as: personal value, emotional benefit, functional benefit, and  product attributes.

As an example, I can mention the brand Nespresso and their publicity.  Product attributes: “The perfect expresso in a beautiful capsule with good design and a variety  of aromas”  Functional benefit: “Perfection convenience originality practicality and superior taste”  Emotional benefit: “A unique and superior espresso experience, that prepares effortlessly,  that revitalizes you and improves your mood, while it allows you to take a special moment for  yourself out of your daily routine”.  Personal value: “It makes you feel special, complete very well treated in each sip, you feel an  exclusive part of an iconic experience.”

The objective is to create an emotional connection with the consumer. The story facilitates the  understanding of complex ideas and help people to relate to product through emotions. In same  cases, the consumer will not be able to differentiate if he continues to buy the product because  of the story or because of the product itself.

Application & Food Industry

Not all food brands can develop great stories to promote their products. But all brands, without  exception, need to explain to their clients who they are and what they do, and this is the core of  the brand story. Since in the food industry, the developments once the reach the market, can  be copied by the competitors rather easily, the story of each brand is unique and unrepeatable.

text:
Reflection-Learning Launch

Challenge  I’m student of engineering faculty,who is a member of the game development  team as part of the Software Engineering course.Our project based on Unity  engine.​Our project is a horror game made with a setting of the 18th century.In  general, the work on the project consisted in creating the plot, developing the  interior and exterior of the game map, implementing lighting suitable for the  genre, animation, filling the scene with all kinds of liveliness and creating  artificial intelligence for them.  Selection  In addition to the interior and exterior, the remaining parts of the project are too  flexible, so the effect on one part will have an effect on another. Which  ultimately leads to unpredictable consequences.​Therefore, the use of Learning  Launch is rather not a choice, but a necessary measure.  Application  Listing the main experiments, the first of them was completely failed due to a  conflict in the code.After editing, we made sure that the code works flawlessly.  The next step is editing and testing the animation of objects. Like in the first  run, an error was detected in the coordinate system (discrepancies in the  animation).The last experiment, which included work on lighting, fortunately  turned out to be performed on the first try.  Insight  This approach allowed us to take risks saving a lot of time. Since in general the  conditions allowed us to make many attempts to implement it (it can be rolled  back if necessary).  Approach   Of course, in the future, when carrying out a similar project, the likelihood of  repeating errors will be reduced since valuable experience has already been  gained.I think that with this specific work, Learning Launch is the only one  possible to use.

text:
Design Thinking Tool -  Storytelling

Challenge

I work in the automotive sector. I lead the learning area at the Corporate University of my organization and I’m  in charge of monitoring the progress of the training route (courses, workshops, webinars) of the customer service  positions. My goal is to get key positions to complete all the courses they have scheduled for the year (virtual  and face-to-face) so that they are trained to perform their role and meet their performance goals. A large part of  this training route consists of pre-recorded courses hosted on our virtual platform and during the past year I was  able to observe that more than 75% of them had not been completed, the employees only participated in the  face-to-face courses of their route.

Selection

Doing some interviews with the employees, I realized that most did not complete the virtual courses because  they thought that it did not help them much in their daily work or that they were very general topics. Some also  commented that due to the stress of the day, they didn’t have time to complete them. I needed to find a solution  in which I showed them that all the courses are extremely important for any worker and that they also have  specific objectives according to the path of each position. That’s why I decided to use Storytelling to tell my own  story of how the courses helped me to achieve my goals in the company.

Application

I entered the company without knowing absolutely anything about the automotive sector and at the beginning it  was difficult because I had to speak with managers and maintenance technicians in technical terms that I didn’t  know; until I was introduced to the Corporate University and I immediately began taking courses about  mechanics, products and other skills that have served me a lot, but also helped me grow within the company  and get to the position I am in. I organized my ideas and put them into a story in which the participants can easily  identify themselves.

text:
Example Reflection – Mind mapping

Challenge

In our business incubator for craftsmen, clients ask to help them

choosing brand’s names according to their crafts. With new clients, we  can’t use -logically- names or hints that we used before for people in the  same field or craft, so chances to get new ideas for names or logos are  decreasing.

Selection

I selected mind mapping tool, to explore more ideas provided by

team members, clients or costumers, and search engines. This powerful  tool helps to collect data and reveal what is deeply in common, and what  wows  and  works  the  best  at  the  same  time

Application

We started by writing the craft’s name in the middle of a blank

paper, then we wrote every word that have a relation with this craft, and  matching them with single headed arrow. Each word can be  independently explored: it’s composition, meaning, root and translation  to other languages.

After creating the final map, we started cancelling any word that is

not appropriate to be in a brand’s name. that process facilitates clearing  non useful ideas, and matching the words in the best way.

Once the modification is finished, we start combining words, roots,

and even translations. Sometimes the crafter wants to add a hint to his  first or last name, we add it, and search which is the best match.

Insight

The best thing I am thankful to learn and to know through this

course, especially using mind mapping tool is exploring and generating  new ideas, in an organized way, which means increasing the chances to  achieve more goals.

Before that, the team members, me, the client were distracted, we

had a lack of ideas, for inspiration and for hope, to generate an  appropriate project or brand’s name.

Approach

Next time I would use mind mapping tool to generate ideas for logo  design, business name, and why not for organizing project ideas.

text:
Storytelling for a trainee program pitch

Challenge

As a technical guy which has been studying electronics and electrical topics since my high school, the  ability to communicate and tell a great story was not one of my strongest skills. I’ve worked in the  engineering team of a company that develops products related to urban mobility, and during this job  experience was the first time that I really needed to communicate and express my ideas efficiently. As a  member of the research and development team, I could improve my communication skills through the  discussion of ideas for a new product. During one year, me and the engineers involved in a specific project  have done weekly meetings to show the project status for the company managers, and it had been the  most challengers “presentations” I have done so far. text:
Example Reflection - Learning Launch

Challenge

I am currently a student of business administration and for the course of projects we

were asked to develop a business model that we could test in the market. At the

university we were unfortunately taught the classic methodology of previously

elaborating a business plan, however, I was determined to apply the concepts of

design thinking to achieve our goal, which was to develop an online educational

platform to sell courses. We had a two-month deadline, so I had to act quickly, and

the difficulty increased because our resources were very limited because of the

pandemic

Selection

After talking with my team, analyzing different tools, we decided to use the learning

launch tool. As we know from the course, it is an experiment designed to quickly test

an idea and prototype.

Application

Thanks to the technology and information we can find on the Internet, we developed

a pilot course quickly focused on digital marketing, which we sent to our

acquaintances who were in the age of our target audience and interviewed later.

Insight

As we talked with people, we discovered that part of our hypothesis was true, that is,

the course content is an important factor, however, so was the aesthetic aspect, so

to speak, which is why we had to contact some friends who were studying

communication to improve the lighting of our videos.

Approach

After making adjustments, we launched the online platform with only one course,

which was surprisingly successful that the university decided to support us to

implement improvements and work together to reach more people, of course, with

what we learned, I know that this is only the beginning of the road, and that we will

certainly perform more tests in the short term

text:
Anne Steiner  October 15, 2019

Design Thinking Reflection – Visualization

Challenge   I have a business concept for a sustainability product that will help reduce single-use packaging.  The vision is to create a circular economy around a line of reusable cups, water bottles and  containers that can be borrowed on-demand, then returned for cleaning.  Similar to the  business model of car co-ops, e-scooters and bikes for transportation, I propose a membership- style system that would allow people to access these items at strategically placed vending  machines when they are on-the-go.     The challenge is that this idea has never been fully fleshed out and there are significant gaps in  terms of how the concept can be implemented in real life, both on the consumer side, as well  as the implementation side. Additionally, a big question looms as to whether this is a product or  service.    Ultimately, I need to better understand how this product/service might work so that I can move  forward research and development.    Selection   According to designer Angela Myer visualization helps unlock another part of our brain to  access parts of our creativity for complex problem solving.  These visual tools aid us with  imaginative thinking when more than just logic is needed; when extrapolation, inductive  reasoning and solving future problems is required.    Due to the complexity and type of thinking that’s required for my business challenge, the  design thinking tool I select to assist in this challenge is visualization. This is because there is an  immediate need to map out the experience from end-to-end. The purpose of mapping the  process out is both to help me create a more fulsome picture of the user experience myself, as  well as to communicate the business concept effectively to a group of collaborators. text:
Overcoming Barriers - The Story of the Movie at a Fuel Distribution Plant

Challenge

The certification program for fuel distribution plant management systems owned by oil company was in  process. I was responsible for coordinating the project. The certifications were conducted by an  international auditing company and were intended to meet requirements defined by the oil company's  industrial customers. Until that moment, a large number of fuel distribution plants had been achieving  certificates of compliance. However, there was a particular plant where management system  implementation process was not reaching the target. The deployment process had been tried more than  twice unsuccessful. Plant employees were demonstrating resistance to the implementation of the  management system. In order to get the process done, the plant manager had made some decisions  that confronted the employees, which made the situation worse. Given this fact, it was necessary to  understand the reasons for the failure of the attempts and to implement the management system in an  innovative manner, in order to meet the goal set by the direction of the oil company.

Selection

The situation required careful exploratory action on what was happening at the plant. It was more than  obvious that measures of force, objectionable, would not solve the problem, especially since the  organizational ambience had been tried and made worse. Thus, as coordinator of the Oil Company  program, I chose to personally conduct research on the source of the problem and to conduct  innovative actions to achieve the certification goal. In this way, I chose to use the Storytelling tool to  establish an empathetic relationship with the plant's staff, so that they could expose their dissatisfaction  in stories, define the problem most perceived by people, contextualize the problem and act,  transforming the dissatisfaction of the team in satisfaction with the achievement of the results. REFLECTION: STORYTELLING

Challenge & Selection

During my time with a Welfare Organization, I was working with a team who set up a camp in a village. I  was given the task of connecting with villagers and explain to them the importance of education for  their children. In villages, parents prefer their children to help them in daily chores instead of sending  their kids to school. It was my task to help them realize that sending their kids to school is much more  beneficial for the children rather than working in the fields. The strategy used to communicate and  understand them was that I first started with the story so that they can know what I am trying to tell  them. After the story ends, I gathered the feedbacks to understand their problems and help them in  understanding how they can overcome those problems and situations. By doing this, I help them in  creating a bright future for their children.

Application

I have a story to share about using storytelling in this situation. While helping the villagers in  understanding the importance of education for their children, one of the points I wanted them to realize  that knowledge can help their children to make better decisions and choices even if they're going to  farm in the future. I told them a story about a friend of mine who was born into a family of farmers. His  father always wanted him to take over after him. The father didn't receive any formal education.  Traders and merchants always fooled him in selling the crop at a lower price or in buying bad crop  seeds. He always felt that not getting a formal education was a significant disadvantage, and he didn't  want his son to suffer the same way as he did.

text:
MIND MAPPING

 Challenge & Selection

Planning a wedding cum reception for my uncle was a

nightmare. A total of 2.5K guests were expected.

Planning a big fat wedding was a mammoth task made

easy by the mind mapping tool.

We spent a lot of time jotting down the important

aspects of the entire wedding ceremony centered around

the main motif of successful accomplishment of the

ceremony.

 Application

We spent a lot of time going through every little detail

of wedding plan and what needs to be done- from the

order of service to the wedding ceremony.

Just talking through everything and mapping it out on

a single mind map managed to ebb the tide of tears

and soon we were looking at the monster in the eye

and saying, “Well that’s not so bad!”

Various tasks were distributed among various family

members & even the minute details like the time and

date of tuxedo delivery/decorating the car for the

groom were accounted for in the mind map.

 Insight & Approach

Well this technique was an eye opener for me. Managing

complex and cumbersome tasks can easily be

accomplished by the mind mapping method.

The only area I will prefer to improve upon is the

distribution of tasks.

Clubbing various co-related tasks, would reduce time and

effort & provide with ease of operation.

I have attached a copy of our mind map.

I hope you’ll like it!

1. Challenge: The challenge is to help a someone enhance their gift giving experience. It

could so happen that one is unhappy with/ faces challenges while deciding what they  could gift to their loved ones be it family, friends or partners. The aim is to come up will a  plausible solution to help the customer and come up with a strategy which could help  them selected suitable gifts.

approach since the customer can exactly relate or picture what they are being offered as  solution. The process of visualization is important since it's truly a way of unlocking  exclusive part of brain. The splendour of using visualization is that we can tap into a  unmarried picture. The extra you start to use pictures, the more which you start to  diagram while you communicate and create a visual picture for humans of how you are  questioning. The, the more likely you are to achieve a experience of settlement and  consensus with human beings, the extra you are likely to draw out communication. In an  environment wherein your, your capability to, to get things executed and to solve issues  is depending on different people being capable of recognize you and align their thoughts  with yours.

3. Application: To implement the tool I selected followed the five main phases of design

thinking. Through the empathy phase I conducted a couple of individual empathy  interviews to deeply understand the problem of the customer. The aim of the empathize  phase was tp Observe users and behaviors in context Engage with customers. Immerse  yourself in the user’s experience. Example	reflection	-	Storytelling

Challenge

My first job was a job of the strategy consultant in the international audit&consulting company, and this

is where I actually learn about the great power of the storytelling.

Our client wanted to take part in the program sponsored by the government. The aim of the program was

to create new businesses in the selected country’s region. As a consulting company our team (including

me) had to do the research and the presentation, stating what kind of businesses should be opened in

the region, so the client would apply for the sponsorship from the government and open the business.

Of course, the main aim of the consulting company is to persuade the client and government that the

chosen business will run successfully in the region and will bring fruitful results to all the parties involved.

This is when we use the storytelling technique.

Selection

We decided to use a storytelling tool to create a story that would explain and persuade our client why the

business idea we suggest for the region is the best one possible.

As it is mentioned in the video lectures (Week 2 materials – Storytelling tools) the good story should

convey a message that creates logic. In our case, we had to persuade the audience that the idea would

work using based on our research. Storytelling tool allows to create the sequence of the events that would

describe how you arrived to the logical conclusion.

Storytelling allows you address the target audience, to find the common ground with the customer, not

only to describe him the problem in details, but also to show the cause, the reasoning, how to solve the

problem and engage the customer in the story.

text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge

A while ago, I accepted the Manager position at an accounting team in charge of doing the tax accounting  for US inbound and outbound assignees. Getting the job required a deep technical expertise of the tax  methodology and accounting structure used by the company. However, when I came on board my  Manager explained me that the team was having execution issues and therefore had low credibility with  the stakeholders due to their lack of technical knowledge. On the positive side, I worked on that same  organization years before and was familiar with the type of work and knew some of the stakeholders. The  leadership challenge was to transform the team into a Center of Excellence by engaging both the team  members and the stakeholders.

Selection

Storytelling is a powerful tool to capture people attention and engage people on a good discussion.  Similarly to the beginning of a good movie or book, storytelling requires you to demonstrate there’s  something at stake, this will capture your audience’s attention right away. Then, you need to start building  upon that opening and make sure to provide sense of direction for the plot, explaining all the obstacles  along the way, maintaining suspense as explained in the video, presenting the story characters and  adding action to the plot in order to generate emotions. Most people will relate more to emotions, rather  than just data, so you have to embed the data within your story. At the end you have to articulate how  your proposal or recommendation could generate a positive outcome to the challenges presented and  explain what the learnings were.

This is why I believe storytelling was such a good fit to my challenges, as it was possible to present it in  such a way that I could not just present a business plan to improve the team’s performance, but to share  with my stakeholders and team members a story of transformation that will capture their attention and  engage them, which make

text:
Reflection – Visualization

Challenge & Selection

I work for an organization which is aiming at developing capabilities of employees with which we could  become an organization where an employee would meet the needs of the job and perform at an  optimal level and at the same time also aligning this to the objectives of the organization so that the  organization as a whole will meet the existing and upcoming capability needs in the industry. We’ve  used multiple design thinking tools to develop a platform to meet all the learning needs both within  the job role and outside the job role. Now as we have traditional practices of learning in our  organization and we want to digitize the learning and provide a good experience for any employee  visiting the platform.

As a team, we’ve worked towards building a platform that meets the learning needs of employees at  various levels. As part of this we’ve explored few vendors using design thinking principles such as  brainstorming, journey mapping etc. And after this we wanted to test this on some real time users.

Application

As part of this we’ve created a test on two platforms and brought in few real time users and asked  them to experience both the platforms. The next step is collecting the feedback on both the  platforms where we wanted to understand the accessibility, navigation, ease of use and how this  platform is meeting the needs of the end user, etc. during this phase, we’ve interacted with the end  users who comes with various backgrounds and how the platform is meeting their requirements.  With this activity we could visualize the journey and get a complete view on how to make effective  use of the platform and also the problems that would arise in future.

Insight

This exercise helped us in shortlisting the most suitable platform. Also helped us in understanding  how an end user will make use of the features available in terms of accessing the content, creating  journeys, leader boards, gamification etc. thi

Reflection - Learning Launch

Olivier Saidi

Challenge

I was leading a project to build and implement “Technology Competency Framework” for my  organization’s large software programmers’ pool of 0 to 4 years of experience in the company. We have  identified 6 different Lines of Technologies (LOTs) which are prevailing for the business to categorize the  target population within. I wanted each LOT to have definite curriculum and associated evaluation at 3  different levels (L1, L2, L3) with increasing expertise and complexity to enable employees gain higher skills  and competencies as they progress year-on-year. We also wanted to map this framework to employees’  career progression within the organization, so it was far more important to have an accurate technology  competency framework in place. Especially “Evaluation” mechanism at every L1, L2, L3 levels for all LOTs.

Employee evaluation framework was decided to be thru’ online assessments in every LOT, based on the  curriculum set for every level (L1, L2, L3). Online assessment was to be using variety of Multiple Choice  Questions (MCQs) of low, medium, high complexities in each level’s assessment. Sizable question bank  was generated and uploaded in the assessment engine. Parameters like Questions’ complexity,  randomization, points for correct answers, passing percentage have been configured in the assessment  engine.

Challenge & Selection: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information. In your  own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you selected it for  your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).

I was working on improving our company e-commerce website so we start the project by doing  a proper design thinking - journey mapping, understanding our customer expectation and pain  points, collecting user stores and so on in order to identify the areas that need to be improve.  When we were on that stage of “what if” that we required to start the idealization of the  solution/improvement we were having challenges to explain/communicate the idea, the  concept we designed to improve our website.

We need to communicate the idealization idea to many stakeholders – so a challenge was to  select the proper language to communicate. How technical, how deep, high level, which point  of the store to tell. The idea is to communicate the idea in a simply way so everyone  understands but without losing contend.

An elevator speech was to narrow – a business summary or one-page business case was to  technical and for many people it was hard to picture how this idea would look like in reality.  So, I decide to use a visualization tool to communicate the concept to make it simpler, but to  keep the complex interaction of the process – be able to have a high-level understanding with  some dive deep highlight points.

Challenge & Selection

I have been using the technique of visualization or visual thinking for a long time. This

technique helps a larger group of people working together to understand the nature of problem

in a much impactful and less ambiguous manner. It leaves people working together with no

scope for interpretation and hence there is uniformity in understanding the problem. Problem

is understood by everybody working on the solution in the same way it must be understood.

What I mean to say is that there is uniformity in terms of understanding the problem.

I work in the area of learning and development and leadership in my organization. In my role

I need to design learning programs and journeys for the employees of the organization. The

learning experience is a critical part of the entire design process. Learning program design or

the instructional design as we call it goes through multiple iterations. There are multiple steps

involved in designing or learning program like analysing the problem designing developing

implementation and evaluation I use visualization technique during analysing the program to

suggest a learning intervention, designing the program and development steps.

Application

In my work while designing a learning program I need to interact with a lot of with multiple

stakeholders. My stakeholders include learners, talent managers, instructors and business &

HR leaders. At the analysis step when we are deciding or working on to understand the

problem and what kind of learning intervention is required to solve that problem, we use a lot

of visual techniques to understand no problem.

We use strawman graphic to draw on the board. We ask the line managers and HR leaders

to make us understand their problems true pictures. I also ask all the stakeholders to draw

I work together with a team that challenge colleagues throughout  the whole organization to participate in the KPN Value Case Challenge. A Value Case is a conceptual idea to solve a  societal problem. Within the Value Case Challenge the participants need to create a storyline for their pitch in  front of a live audience and jury. The Value Case looks beyond profit and also takes into account people, planet  and purpose. Nicely visual represented in the table below.

I find it challenging to support the participants during the creation process so they can find the right visual support  for their Value Case pitch presentation.

Selection:   I’ve selected the Visualization tool for the fact that I really love to use my imagination. In the ‘What if?’ faze within  the Design Thinking process I love to bring into mind things that are in the present and on that basis hypothesize  on things that could be but have never been. I experience that Visualizations help to broaden the thinking in the  ‘to hypothesize’ stage (What if) which leads to original ideas.   I believe that this is one of the essential elements in the design thinking process. Visualizations help to make a  concept for a solution more tangible, more concrete. To bring it a few steps further than language and words  alone. By means of symbols, diagrams, drawings  new discussions or hunches to new ideas are created.  Visualization helps to make the design concept ‘more real’ and could say more than a thousand words could do. The project scope includes the  Information Security department composed of seven employees, as well as the larger IT  department, with whom we work closely. The project is limited to internal and external  infrastructure networking involving a large number of technological devices. The project  should not exceed 3 months and the solution should include perform penetration testing and  vulnerability analysis. We will focus to prevent hacker attacks that could compromise the  company's image and reputation as well as online sales, which may result in financial losses to  shareholders.

Selection

Our team evaluated several design thinking tools, where we opted for learning launch tool.  After many meetings and strategic planning, the learning launch is an experiment meant to  quickly test an idea and prototype.

Application

The company is very concerned about maintaining an up-to-date technology environment,  prioritizing the security of its data. Vulnerability scans and Penetration tests are intended to  prevent unauthorized actions by exploiting faulty vulnerabilities or more coding practices in  applications, security breaches, in addition to database information, information manipulation,  and unavailability. In addition, they aim to measure the effectiveness of corporate protection  systems against targeted attacks via the internet or other private networks against their users. Challenge:

I work for an International Organization within a team of around 12 people, as part of our internal  communications activities we have one-hour weekly meetings to provide updates and relevant  information about our work.  These meetings have been in place for around 2 years and some of the team  members have been expressing that these meetings were not very useful and that this time could be  better invested in other type of team building activities.

I have realized that some actions needed to be done in order to identify what would be the best  communication and/or team building activities that could fill the expectations of the majority.

Selection:

I decided that Mind Mapping tool, could be a good option to help with the mentioned challenge, as mind  mapping will help us to generate ideas,  group these ideas, establish  common links and needs from our  team through a collaborative and cocreative process.

Application:

As part of the process, I initially did an online survey to get initial feedback from team members on the  way our meetings were being handled and to use this dat, a as based for our mind mapping process.

The survey included information about the objective of the meetings, length, content, agenda,  participants, etc . The survey was anonymous so people could feel free to express their opinions

The information obtained allowed me to identify the key areas to address during our mind mapping  process, which were: the objective of the meeting , the  content and the time and frequency.

I decided to do internal meeting to discuss the findings of the process and identify the patterns of the  team. I have used flipcharts and post it notes and asked the people 3 questions:

•  What would you expect from these meetings?

•  What could you suggest to improve these meetings and fulfill your expectations?

•  What other suggestions do you have to improve team communications and effectiveness

text: Storytelling    Challenge & Selection    In my day to day work i use storytelling to enable the people we are targeting in the society to open up  about the situations they are undergoing.  We work with young women who have unwanted pregnancy  especially those who are in school also those who are pregnant through rape. Many of these women  deal with a lot of stress from societal stigma and they need to be counseled and to be assured that there  are still who they were before the pregnancy. To relieve them from the burden of stigma ,loss of self- worth and stigma, I have to find a way for them to open up about how they feel and think about their  situation this helps to relieve them off their stress ,trauma and stigma. text:
Information visualization is the process of representing data in a visual and  meaningful way so that a user can better understand it. Dashboards and  scatter plots are common examples of information visualization. Via its  depicting an overview and showing relevant connections, information  visualization allows users to draw insights from abstract data in an efficient  and effective manner.

Information visualization plays an important role in making  data digestible and turning raw information into actionable insights. It draws  from the fields of human-computer interaction, visual design, computer  science, and cognitive science, among others. Examples include world map- style representations, line graphs, and 3-D virtual building or town plan  designs.

The process of creating information visualization typically starts with  understanding the information needs of the target user group. Qualitative  research (e.g., user interviews) can reveal how, when, and where the  visualization will be used. Taking these insights, a designer can determine  which form of data organization is needed for achieving the users’ goals. Once  information is organized in a way that helps users understand it better—and  helps them apply it so as to reach their goals—visualization techniques are  the next tools a designer brings out to use. Visual elements (e.g., maps and  graphs) are created, along with appropriate labels, and visual parameters  such as color, contrast, distance, and size are used to create an appropriate  visual hierarchy and a visual path through the information.

Information visualization is becoming increasingly interactive, especially  when used in a website or application. Being interactive allows for  manipulation of the visualization by users, making it highly effective in  catering to their needs. Challenge

I am a development professional and work with 200,000 the most vulnerable, marginalised and

very low income group of people. My purpose of engagement is to enhance their income by

building their capacity, supporting and handholding in livelihood selection, livelihood

generation, and overall holistic development including education to their children, health &

sanitation, nutrition, and continuous saving for the rainy days. Working with ultra-poor people,

I realised that capacity building not only to the ultra-poor households, but also to cadres

involved in their handholds and staﬀ ensuring ﬁeld level implementation is the key to success.

And designing uniform and easy to understand capacity building material was a huge

challenge before us. It was quite necessary to build empathy among cadres and staﬀ and reach

to the beneﬁciaries emotionally.

Selection and Approach

After completing design research to understand the aspirations,needs and desires of the

targeted beneﬁciaries, we used your insights to tell a story about who the users are, what they

need and how the staﬀ and cadres provide those services and solutions. This storytelling made

it easy for everyone involved in the project to empathize with the users and ensure that their

work matches the story. Having a story throughout your project means marketing the design at

the end of the design process is also straightforward, as you already know exactly which story

to tell to show how your product provides value. We use the following formula:-

1. Pilot - What are user goals and problems which they are trying to overcome or achieve?

2. Character - Using the Insights, clear understanding on what the users characteristics are?

3. Theme - Establishing trustworthy presence

4. Dialogue and melody- What will the design say to users and how? Does a

Confidential with no Personal Information

Eliminating Gap between Components – Visualization

Challenges & Selection:

I have utilized visualization for eliminating the gap between components in existing design of machine.  Gap between the component created perception in mind of customer that either the part is missing or  this gap weakens the design structure. With structure being in current production over years and no  problems identified, utilization of straw man diagram seemed more feasible. Considering the aspects with  no problem identified with current design, straw man diagram helped to put forth the need of change,  possible solutions, scope, possible challenges ahead, cost and more.

Application:

Intent was to have solution to problem through cost effective way without change to existing part  functionality. I started creating the straw man diagram through problem statement, current design,  possible solutions, challenges, cost, scope of changes.

Within group of people working on same components, presented this diagram and had discussion on pro’s  and con’s of possible solution. Defined the scope of changes and selected the best possible solution and  cost.

Insights & Approach:

With approach of straw man diagram, this enabled to provide insight of possible solutions and also  understand the change impact and identify scope as well. This provided direction and alignment with  management.

Disclaimer : I have provided the above example in general terms without including part component  names, part location or any of images for references due to concerns of confidentiality. Request you to  understand confidentiality concerns of not sharing while reviewing.

Reflection-Learning Launch Tool

•  Challenge

I am an intern at an architectural firm who are trying to expand in the landscaping business in order  to enter into this upcoming market called as green architecture. The project scope consists of just 5  people and a head of the project. The project should not exceed 2 months and the main goal was to  create landscape gardens for houses as well as apartments. Our firm’s focus was turn away from  traditional architecture/interior designing and shift towards green architecture.

•  Selection of Tool

We purposely selected learning launch tool as we wanted to test this green architecture ideas and  whether they will work or not.

•  Application

For this tool to work, I started searching what is green architecture and how it functions, how it is  different from the traditional architecture. We were testing ourselves to whether we could adapt to  this style of architecture. Then later, we divided green architecture into two core categories which  are kitchen gardening, landscape gardening. To gain some more insights I visited various plant  nurseries and list down the prices of various plants which can be used at home and which ones are  the most suitable for landscaping. As we could not outsource plants we needed to connect with the  local plant nurseries and have an appropriate contract for regular supply of needed plants.

In the second phase we needed to know who our customers will be. Will it be anyone who owns a  big house or will it be a person who just loves plants in his house no matter what the space is. So  after brainstorming a couple of ideas we came up with kitchen gardening or simply home gardening  where people can grow certain vegetables and fruits at home. This will save their daily expenses and  this method requires less maintenance. To make this idea work we conducted surveys which  included our proposition of our idea, how will they react to it and this was conducted within 2 weeks  of time-frame.

It is also difficult to introduce the proposed idea to people who are unaware of the terms  you are proposing and to those people who are already engaged or used to the process that they are  dealing with since from the beginning which is the use of the invasive device in determining their blood- glucose concentration level.    Selection    Visualization had been used first in developing our concept. By visualizing how users feel when they use  the invasive device, we perceived an idea on how to ease their pain by using another method which is the  noninvasive approach. Through visual  technique they can relate and appreciate the process easier. From this, the customer will understand  exactly how the project is intend to work as was said by Angela Myer in the video entitled “Visualization  Tool” on the first week of the session. Mind Mapping

Challenge

I am the Team leader of my organization’s developer department and our challenge is to  improve the testing methodologies within the department to improve the quality of the  software releases. The project should not exceed 30 business days and the solution should  include an even distribution of working hours amongst the team members. We will focus on  the workflow and the documentation required for our customers.

Selection

Mind Mapping is a visual representation of all information collected during the research  process of the Testing workflow and it is best to analyze all possibilities in a creative and easy  to follow format.

Our team is ready to try the mind mapping tool to organize ideas and analyze all situations  through breaking things down into smaller parts.

Application

After having been inspired by customer challenges or problems through gathering data, it is  time to mind mapping and generate insights and as many ideas as possible as potential  solutions. For this stage we require a lot of planning and preparation to ensure that the results  are rich and interesting. For ideation, we need to designate a team that can generate potential  solutions.

First, we focused on the current testing workflow and explained to the participants what we  are trying to improve, and we wrote in the center of the map this topic.

As mind mapping is a creative activity, each member may produce many ideas as possible  which are writing into the map and connected to the topic with the main keyword.

Then, we organized these ideas together to have a proper connection between each other and  the main center point or idea.

We expected to produce a mind map with a clear representation of our new, more agile  workflow.

text:
APPLICATION OF DESIGN THINKING CONCEPT TO ASSESS THE USE OF RENEWABLE ENERGY IN RURAL

AREAS OF LAGOS

Over the past 30years, energy access has been a major challenge for most dwellers in the  rural area of Lagos, Nigeria due to increasing energy demand, increasing population, and  demand for enhanced standard of living. The issue of energy access in Lagos mostly affects  rural settlements as the areas are usually far from the national electricity grid connection.  This research was conducted using the Design Thinking (DT) approach to investigate energy  availability and management in rural settlements. The DT methodology consists of six phases  namely, understand, observe, define a point of view, ideate, prototype, and testing. Through  the ‘understand’ phase, an intensive literature review was undertaken to assess the feasible  renewable energy resources. In the ‘observe’ phase, interviews were conducted in rural  settlements of Lagos. It was found out that cooking is the main energy need and the rural  inhabitants travel up to 10km to collect firewood. A ‘point of view’ (POV) statement was then  created to initiate the ideation stage. The ‘Ideate’ phase involved using viable technologies  to generate solutions targeted at the profile defined in the POV. A selection matrix was then  used to obtain the best energy solution. Through the ‘prototyping’ phase, a concept model  biogas digester was designed for rural settlements. This paper reports on the first 4 stages  of DT methodology.    UNDERSTAND & OBSERVE  The initial phase of the Design Thinking process ‘Understand’, conceptualizes the energy problem  facing in rural communities in Lagos. This phase identifies the core energy needs of the people  by establishing the perspective of human-centered problem solving. Challenge

First, I had not got the full information about this crucial element “Visualization” until I got  through this course which widened my horizon greatly to discover the importance of many  hidden things. Visualization techniques have been used by successful people to visualize their  desired outcomes for ages.

The practice has even given some high achievers what seems like super-powers, helping them  create their dream lives by accomplishing one goal or task at a time with hyper focus and  complete confidence.

In fact, we all have this awesome power, but most of us have never been taught to use it  effectively.

Application

I can tell that now I have been changed completely. My mind and thought can easily analyze  data and go beyond to think deeply not only about what’s seen but more importantly about  what’s not seen and what I desire to see in the near future. Now, I am working with a friend on a  project using what I have learnt and try my best to apply it.  The daily practice of visualizing my dreams as already complete can rapidly accelerate my  achievement of those dreams, goals, and ambitions.

Our brain is constantly using visualization in the process of simulating future experiences, but  this process happens so naturally that you generally aren't even aware of it, the same way  you usually aren't aware that you are breathing. If you aren't aware of it then you aren't actively  directing the process. I can learn to use visualization to actively create future simulations that can  help me  improve the goals that you set for yourself.

You can create two types of simulations, outcome and process. An outcome simulation is a  sensory-based representation of the final outcome you expect, and a process situation involves  simulating the steps that get you to the final outcome.
