Miguel Perez                                        University of Virginia

Due to the quarantine, supermarkets only accept

a limited number of customers to shop inside their

buildings to promote social distancing. Some

supermarkets are forced to close, accepting no

customers at all. People who do shop tend to buy a

month’s worth of groceries in fear that if they shop

weekly, the chance of them catching the virus

increases. The large amount of items purchased leads

to other people getting robbed of the chance to

shop, and for the ones who do shop, they bring home

a heavier load that requires another person to carry

which violates social distancing.

The design thinking tool I will be using is mind

mapping.For me, mind mapping is a representation of

your mind and it is used to look for patterns and

insights.

I used to use mind mapping as a substitute for

lecture notes since I am still a high school

student, so using it in design thinking was very new

to me. It is a creative way to organize information

in clusters. I used it to answer the question “What

is?”. My mind map included branches of who the

customers are and their problems are. Based on

empathy and observation, I noticed my mom would be

very tired when she comes home from shopping. She

makes sure to spray everything with alcohol after

throwing away a disposable face mask. After that she

takes a bath to make sure she’s clean when she

breastfeeds my brother. Everything my mom does is

for the family’s sake. She wanted to shop for us,

but she’s tired of carrying heavy bags by herself.

She is also scared of our safety. Mind mapping was

very effective in defining the problem.

text:
Visualisation

Challenge and Selection:

Being tasked with a project of coming up with a ‘blue ocean’ idea for the company I work for  presented me with an opportunity to apply the design thinking approach for the first time. The  industry I work for is a very price competitive environment where services offered are extremely  difficult to gain a competitive advantage on, this is what is also known as a ‘red ocean’ environment  due to all the ‘blood’ in the water from aggressive price cutting and high level of competition. A blue  ocean idea would bring up something our company could offer that no one else is doing in the  industry hence being referred to as a ‘blue ocean’ idea – where no one else would be competing. I  had been given a young team of 8 members and a timeline of 1 month to come up with some  possible suggestions to present to our directors.

As being in the ‘what is?’ stage of the design thinking process I decided to use the Visualisation tool  with my team to try and get a deeper understanding of the task/challenge presented.  I designed a  chart to allow us to gain a better understanding of what is currently being offered in the industry  and what we are offering in the industry. Each would be put into its respective section of the chart.  This would allow us to know better what it is we are trying to differentiate ourselves from.

Application:

I split the group up into two groups of 4 each with their own chart to fill in their views and insights of  what is currently being done by my company and our competitors in the market. I allowed each  team to come up with as many views as possible for the 1 hour time frame including a 10min break  in the middle to allow a fresh perspective in case things got boring or sluggish after a while. To  further mitigate this risk I also mixed up the groups after the 10min break in the middle. I also  decided to do this in an outdoor environment to try and increase creativity and comfort.

Mind Mapping

1. Challenge:

As a Sales Enablement (training) Manager for one of the world’s largest tech  companies, my role is to ensure that our sellers are equipped with the knowledge they  need to be successful in winning in the market. The discipline of Sales Enablement  works closely with two teams in any organization, one, the sales team, and two, the  product/offering/services creation team. Our role is to take the information which the  product creators have, package that information is easily consumable content (PPT,  Videos, Case Studies, Online learning session) and ensure the sellers are aware of  these latest offerings which our company has.

The top challenges we face in sales enablement are –

• Sellers are busy running after quotas, so they have very little time to spare for

enablement activities.

• People who design products tend to get too technical while explaining it to other

people  which can get boring.

• The business unit I work for has over 8000 sellers globally. So, it is obvious that

getting everyone together in one place for face to face learning, is an extremely  costly and time-consuming affair.

• The evolving IT landscape is changing and many of our sellers are have limited to

no understanding to the latest products and services our company offers which is  making them inept in the market and we are losing business.

PWC ProEdge – Design Thinking Assignment

Challenge & Selection

One of the tools I use on a regular basis is Visualization, or Visual Thinking. I am often analyzing data sets  and putting together presentations on my analysis. These presentations are made for various  stakeholders at my clients such as accounting, finance, engineers and IT individuals. As a result, it can be  difficult to convey the results of my analysis to such a diverse group of individuals with varying  backgrounds. Additionally, these data sets are very large and the findings can be difficult to interpret.

The visualization tools I typically use when presenting my analysis to a client are pivot tables, tableau  dashboards, pie charts, typically presented in power point presentations, and whiteboards when  brainstorming or working through a complex issue. I find it very useful to use these tools to ensure  everyone can clearly understand the findings and that all members have the same understanding.

Application

When putting together my analysis, I typically start with the raw data-set. I then use pivot tables to  narrow down the data into a more manageable format, which makes it easier to identify trends. I  typically slice the data in multiple ways in order to get grounded on the information and ultimately find  trends and root causes of issues. I will also leverage existing visualization tools at my clients such as heat  maps from Tableau. I find it useful to use tools that the client is already familiar with or currently using.

Once I have analyzed the data and identified trends and root causes for the issues I am working through,  I will typically add quantitative and qualitative figures to add more depth to the analysis. The company I work is a manufacturer and maintainer of elevators, and its core business is  maintenance. Mind Mapping would help us to  get all the ideas out there, and link them in a way that would lead us to a possible plan.

Challenge: Connect patients with trusted professional pharmacists who can advise on the best  available medicines for patient needs at the best price and order delivery.

Choices: I chose the storytelling tool. I have a development team that needs to develop a product.  I chose this tool to help developers better understand the problem. https://www.coursera.org/learn/uva-darden-design-thinking-innovation/lecture/PAXCd/ storytelling-tool

Application: I gathered all my developers, put them at the same table and began to tell them a  story. I told them that everything is moving to the Internet and it is more convenient for the  younger generation to receive consultations online as easily as they communicate in instant  messengers with their friends. Also, the older generation should use the new product and took an  example from my grandmother, who writes to me on WhatsApp.

Understanding: My team felt all the emotions that I wanted to convey to them. They immediately  began to come up with ideas on how to do it simply and intuitively for everyone. They drew a  prototype and showed it to me. I was amazed how well they understood me!

Approach: Storytelling is a great tool and I use it a lot in my life and work. People listen carefully  and better understand what they want to convey. They also experience the emotions of the  heroes of my story, get used to the role and oﬀer me cool ideas. Design thinking is really cool!

text:
DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION

TOOL: MIND MAPPING

The challenge that I faced which required mind mapping was a fundraiser in my school. I  couldn’t decide what program to conduct for the fundraiser in order to get maximum  participation for my final goal to be achieved, which is to procure a good fund. The fundraiser  went towards educating under privileged children; therefore, it was absolutely obligatory to  obtain a considerable amount. The reason mind mapping turned out to be necessary in this  situation was due to the various programs attracting different customers. My final option was to  choose between a bake sale, talent show or prom night. I also had to get all the required products  according to the program chosen which required a mind map as well.

A mind map is a tool for the brain that captures the thinking that goes on inside your head. Mind  mapping helps you think, collect knowledge, remember and create ideas. Most likely it will  make you a better thinker. The reason I chose to use mind mapping as a tool to overcome my  challenge is due to the information being presented visually. It will help me structure information  well and analyze it better. The following links can be used to understand mind mapping further:

➢ https://www.mindmapping.com/  ➢ https://www.mindtools.com/pages/article/newISS_01.htm  ➢ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5nTuScU70As

I used mind mapping in order to evaluate the most cost-effective program that raises the most  funds. I also used the tool to map all the necessities for a successful program (bake sale was  chosen according to the tool). It was applied effectively and I was able to avoid unnecessary  complications and doubts.

I gained insight through this management tool and increased my capacity to think effectively and  quickly. It helped me be more organized and manage my time effectively. Mind mapping in  relation to design thinking gives a clear organization and structure, straightforwardness and  simplicity.

Tool: Storytelling

Title: Reinventing oneself through changing one’s story

Challenge Volunteering as a mentor for disadvantaged immigrant teenagers, I was working with Ali (not his  real name), a 21-years-old son of Turkish immigrants. At our ﬁrst meeting, I asked him to tell me  his story. Ali told me that he failed to graduate from general secondary school multiple times and  that subsequently, after he ﬁnally did, all higher education institutions and companies rejected his  applications. The NGO I was working for had eventually helped him to get into vocational school  where he was now to be trained to become a social worker. The classes were to be starting in a  few weeks ahead. The story Ali told me was one of frustration and shame: Always surrounded by  much younger fellow students, he saw himself as a failure, not just in school, but also in life  generally. Moreover, he feared to fail again at the new school and lacked the conﬁdence to ever  succeed alone without help from others. But talking to him I could see that Ali was in fact an  aroused and smart person with a great sense of humor. The major challenge I was thus facing was  to change Ali’s mind-set. More than to help him overcome his paralyzing frustration and to start his  studies more conﬁdently. Apart from just familiarizing him with some learning and organization  techniques, it seemed necessary to change his perspective and to keep him focused on his goals.  During our subsequent meetings, we went through what within the framework of this course  probably would be called the „What is?“- and the „What if?“-phase: We talked about problems that  existed in the past, weaknesses, strengths and the challenges lying ahead. We then moved on to  talking about his larger goals, ideas and the type of person he would ideally like to be. Reflection – Visualization

Challenge

I’m working in IT department of one of global leaders of FMCG industry. During all my career in IT function  I led multiple projects of software deployment as well as developing tools and applications enabling  requested business capabilities in the company. At certain point of time I started observing that almost  every project has a ‘requirements are not clear and not complete’ statement in a list of lessons learnt.  The problem is explained by a fact that business requirements normally captured in a text that explains  the business need from a business perspective and as good described as business requester can. Then  software developer or supplier reads the text and understands requirements as good as can being  grounded to own knowledge and past experience. And usually there is a difference between what  requested and what understood. Just because both requester and developer have different functional  and professional backgrounds. Of cause typically application developer or IT supplier asks extra questions  trying to clarify what is requested. This improves situation but not dramatically. At the end of the game  this drives extra cost to rework and overall frustration on both sides.

Selection

To improve situation further I demanded to add a visualization (or visual design in particular) to every  medium and high complexity requirements as a mandatory component. In addition to verbal visual design  or thinking allowed project team to think and communicate in nonverbal way and tap into a single picture  of what is requested. Depending on the type of project it could be a visualization of either process map  reflecting a vision of how future business process should flow or sketch of dashboard or visualization of  user interface (UI). For the last one (UI) I found mockup tools available in internet that simplify building  visuals every time when new UI should emerge or existing UI should be updated.

text:
STORYTELLING

CHALLENGES AND SELECTION

Designers use storytelling to get insight into users, build empathy and reach them  emotionally. i want to work towards the elderly citizen with dementia and Alzheimer's As  the number of baby boomers who are also seniors grows rapidly, the number diagnosed  with dementia, including Alzheimer’s disease, also grows While it is the only disease with  no prevention, real treatment and no cure, there has been an increase in ongoing  research looking for a cure. People with dementia find it difficult to access memories, both  new and old. This memory and recall impairment begins slowly and progresses to the  point where it becomes hard to recall events, names, and conversations that they would  have easily remembered previously. Good stories can engage seniors so that they will  pay attention, empathize, and even cooperate. It is a matter of science

APPLICATION

I want to use storytelling as a way for the elderly people with such diseases to let their  thoughts out and make them mood better with good communication skills and social  interaction. in old age homes or healthcare institutes where they become frustrated and  can not control their emotions this practice of storytelling can go a long way and improve  their condition. Caregivers who use this process at home can have fun, show an image,  and talk about it with your loved one. Healthcare professionals who use storytelling find  that it opens older adults up to memories, encourages verbalization and promotes self- esteem. Each listener will glean a different emotional response and meaning to the same  story based on their own ability to imagine.

INSIGHT AND APPROACH

We can sit with them in groups and play a game with them where each member can have  a picture of something that will act as a starting point for any story from here they build.  The participants use their imagination taking turns deciding what happens next. This  allows them to express themselves creatively an

Reflection – mind mapping for a new intranet  Design Thinking for Innovation | Assignment | Abdul Thomas

Challenge  I am the manager of online services for a government department. After several years without any  major changes to the intranet, we recently felt it was time for it to be redesigned, reinvigorated and  to become more of an engagement channel for staff. The challenge for us was to create an intranet  that met the needs of staff as well as senior management. In particular, to provide an intranet that  helped people do their job. To achieve this, we knew it was important for the new intranet to be co- designed, something that never happened previously.

To start our ‘what is’ investigation, we carried out a survey of staff to get their feelings about the  intranet. Analysing this data provided some useful insights. What we found was that most people  were generally happy with the intranet, though there were some common themes in the responses:  there were a number of common day-to-day tasks that needed to be made easier, the design was  tired and could be modernised, search could be improved, and the content could be reviewed for  currency.

Selection  While the survey provided some useful data and insights, I felt there was a need to re-affirm the  current reality and, as discussed by Cheryl Flores in the lecture material, ‘establish  criteria for the what-if idea generation phase’. The ideal design tool to use for this purpose was mind  mapping. Mind mapping is a method used to find common themes, patterns and insights from data  collected during the ‘what is’ phase, to help you to generate an idea or innovation that meets the  need of the customer. Mind mapping was important in this project because it allowed us to really  understand what staff wanted from their intranet, and notably what they didn’t want. It also was an  excellent tool to use to encourage engagement and ownership of the new intranet.

1.Challanges:The malfunction of network cables in the system room of the financial sector where I work.

The system room of  any financial sector is the power house that communicates and passes information  to all other individual systems of both operators and relationship managers

2.Selection:Several units came together to discuss on the way forward.The units included the Operator,  Business development unit, The branch manager and the IT representative and Telecoms who are the  provider of the networks. After several shared ideas using the mapping tool the branch manager  cascaded the information to the relevant authority and then every unit played their role.

3.Application: Using the mapping tool several ideas/ images became a reality and was shared and  tackled effectively and efficiently with prioritization giving to the each member of team for prompt  resolution.

4. Insight: The insight gained in application of the mapping tool gave rise to different  creative design  techniques and prompt resolution was achieved. It helped in data collection, patterns and individual  ideas collated with collaboration to yield better results.This process helped streamlined from what it  was to what it become which is the reality.

5.Approach

•  A more robust view  of the problem gives a more robust solution

•  Each team member should have been more detailed.

•  The most acceptable view should have been the end user review .

written by Rui Mendes

Design Thinking for Innovation

Design Thinking for Innovation page 02

all about the challenge

The challenge consist on explain de

diferents valors of the blood pressure

and his classification to the general

public. Blood pressure (BP) is

the pressure of circulating blood against

the walls of blood vessels. Blood

pressure is usually expressed in terms of

the systolic pressure (maximum pressure

during one heartbeat) over diastolic

pressure (minimum pressure between

two heartbeats) in the cardiac cycle. It

is measured in millimeters

of mercury (mmHg) above the

surrounding atmospheric pressure.

Normal resting blood pressure, in

an adult is approximately 120 points

onsystolic over 80 points on diastolic,

denoted as "120/80".

application

selection

The tool used to explain this parameters

is the tool of Visualisation; Data

visualization is the graphical

representation of information and data.

By using visual elements like charts,

graphs, and maps, data visualization

tools provide an accessible way to see

and understand trends, outliers, and

patterns in data.

The process began with the collection of

patient data, where blood pressure was

measured throughout the week. Then a

study was carried out on the samples,

classifying them in high, normal or low

pressure. Once the study was carried

out, Visualization techniques were used.

Design Thinking for Innovation page 03

all about the insight

What I have learned from the

application of visualization techniques is

that one of the most important factors is

chromatic harmony, therefore, one of

the most important factors to explain

blood pressure is that the colors were

adequate so that the patient did not

lose the attention.

approach

In the next approach I will try to

summarize the graphics and simplify it

so that its study is more agile and

efficient.

Big   technology   companies   like   YouTube   and   Facebook   are   competing   for   the   same   advertising   revenue   budgets.   To   remain   viable,   media   owners   like   national   newspapers   and   public   service   broadcasters,   are   increasing   their   pace   of   digital   innovation. Reflection – Mind Mapping Tool

Challenge:

I have been working as an assistant professor in a school of industrial design in a  well known Indian design institute. As we all know integration of design and  technology is very important for a better product development.  My challenge was  to teach them various technologies which help student to convert their design  thinking into reality. As design students go through the entire design process from  ethnography, empathy to the prototyping and testing. During this entire process I  observed that, their major focus is on esthetics, styling and sketching, due to which  their prototypes or mockups did not have an essence of the end product (or final  product which could be used). Lack of technical touch in the mockups creates  hypothetical image on a customer (while learning launch). In a nut shell our  challenge is to provide technical knowledge to the design students.

Selection:

There were lots of ideas available to complete this challenge, but all the ideas were  scattered. Me and my some collogues had lots of brainstorming with directors and  some experts from management. Then I and one of my collogue suggested to apply  Mind mapping tool for this particular challenge. As Mind mapping (or concept  mapping) involves writing down a central idea and thinking up new and related  ideas which radiate out from the centre, we decided to apply it. I explained them  how Mind maps can help us in the early stages of our essay by summarizing our  research and providing us with a picture of all aspects of the question. We can then  move from our non-linear mind map to a more structured essay plan.

Application:

As our main challenge is to provide them technical education, we put this  challenge as a central idea. text: Challenge & Selection The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers, who are government agencies working to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their services to their customer, which may be U.S. citizens, businesses, and non-citizens. I have used the technique of using a straw man visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for discussion to allow a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions. Application I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw man graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, GAO or other auditing reports. If materials are not available, then I conduct informal interviews with one-three of the stakeholders who serve as my main points of contact on the initiative. If appropriate to the situation, I will borrow the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from previous research, and discussed in David Gray’s book, “The Connected Company”. The front-stage/back-stage approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service – even an internal service – has customers with whom the service provider interacts and internal processes that enable the organization to provide the service. text:
Mind Mapping Tool

CHALLENGE:

After 25 years of work in FMCG company, I have just started my new job as a Product Manager in  outdoor company. I was responsible for Citylights ad network – several thousand of advertising’s  panels (1,2 x 1,8m) located on cities streets, bus shelters, shopping malls, airports etc.

My first challenge was: make the existing advertising network called ‘ITFAQ’ start selling.

This advertising network consisting of 600 citylights, located near shops and on the parkings of the  largest retailers like Tesco, Carrefour etc, was dedicated to FMCG* advertisers.

The case was that at the beginning many clients (media houses) have included ‘ITFAQ’ to  campaign's media-mix but at the end - nobody bought it. No one in the sales team could explain  the reason, why? Price discounts or extra panels for free didn't work.

SELECTION:

I have decided to use Mind Mapping Tool, because the pivotal stage in my challenge was gathering  a deep understanding of customer needs and broader perspective on how this product should work  to be desired.

This tool allowed me to involve my colleagues, much more experienced in this industry than me, in  order to develop a common mind among them regarding the current reality of my challenge.

This tool was also used due to the very large amount of data I have collected and we had to draw  the most important facts and observations that would lead us to deeper insights.

APPLICATION:

In big conference room I have prepared the ‘ITFAQ - gallery’ – where people could saw and  feel how the citylights dedicated network looks like (pictures of localization), who is our target  (FMCG companies logos), who buy (media houses logos), folders, charts, etc.

I have invited 15 people from sales, marketing, media planners (customers) and stakeholders like:  sales & HR & finance – directors.

I asked them for their intuition. Please go around the gallery on your own and make notes you  believe might inform new ideas.

INCREASING CUSTOMER PATRONAGE

Challenge  I work as an assistant marketing manager for a business development firm situated in one  of the most reputable tertiary institutions in Ghana. Our mandate is to promote innovative  entrepreneurship among the youth. In spite of all efforts aimed at getting them, students  from the various colleges within the university barely recognize nor patronize our services.  This possess a great challenge to the marketing department and ultimately to the  organization as a whole, mainly because the student group forms the major component of  our target market.

Selection  After adopting the design-thinking model as an approach to solving the problem, I lead a  team to investigate and suggest sustainable solutions to the problem. We were able to  develop a prototype aimed at solving the problem and readied it for a learning launch. The  learning launch is a low cost solution that was rolled out to ascertain what works and what  needs to be “re-worked”.

Application  The realization we made from establishing the current realities and what a solution should  look like lead us to develop several solution concepts. Some of the concepts developed  were benched and others channeled into developing a prototype. For the learning launch,  we focused on targeting a small student group and adopted a short timeline. We realized  from the earlier stages of the process that, students placed great value on the  recommendations of their lecturers, and that the curriculum did not factor in  entrepreneurship training which made the students not appreciate the need for it. We also  noticed that the colleges had mentorship programme that engaged the teaching staff to  serve as mentors to the students.

We therefore organized an info session for the teaching staff of a particular department  with a student population of approximately eight hundred (800), and the leadership of the  student association within the department.

Learning Launch

Challenge

As I’m currently at home due to Covid19, I will take on the project of finding new methods  of revenue generation for the Zoo in my country. It has been recognized worldwide as one of  the best zoological parks in the world and has been known for the quality of care it provides  to the animals. However, for the first time in almost 50 years, the zoo had to shut its door  because of the spread of Covid19. While the lockdown in our country is speculated to open  within a month, it is unlikely that the borders for leisure travelling will open up anytime  soon. A country so heavily dependent on tourism will take a hit, and businesses dependent  on providing experiences will have to come up with new and creative methods to generate  revenue and stay relevant in the changing times.   The method best suited would be for the management to take the experiences online and  turn animal care into virtual tours that individuals or groups can pay to be a part of.  Zookeepers can impart knowledge via Zoom to a group of 5-10 people in one session. They  can also tie-up with schools to provide virtual tours for students, instead of field trips that  won’t be happening at least until the latter part of 2020. Selling merchandise online with  personalized messages would also be a great source of kickstarting income generation while  capitalizing on that as a social media movement simultaneously. This would help to not only  reach out to local customers but also a vast clientele globally, including a potential to reach  out to schools all over the world, thereby creating, virtual tourism. But the challenge would  be that the risk appetite in such times isn’t extremely high since there is no revenue being  earned right now and so the right balance is extremely crucial so as to not incur any losses. Challenge

The challenge being tackled was introducing a new Customer Relationship Management system  our company. It had been noted that there weren’t proper records of clients who had visited any  of the company’s branches looking to be served or to make enquiries. It was thus difficult to  assess the nature of clients that were served, whether their issues had been successfully resolved  and how long this had taken. It was therefore important for the company to introduce a new  system that would tackle these challenges.

This system, called CRM, was important since it would enable the recording of all customer  interactions by the company’s staff, including the client’s personal details, their enquiries and  how long it took to resolve each issue that a client raised. In the long run, this would be helpful  in determining what the key touch points with clients are, which would in turn help the company  in:

• Staffing - Allocating staff to areas that handled more clients.  • Improving Turn Around Times -  The system would show how long each customer’s

enquiry or instruction took to resolve and what areas would require further training for  the staff.

• Mode of contact – How the interaction with the client was made, e.g. through email, walk

in, an intermediary or by phone.

Selection

Leaning Launch tool was the tool of choice for this challenge. A learning launch ideally means  conducting a small experiment to test a developed idea in the real world. It is an experiment that  involves introducing a product or service into the real world to gauge how it integrates into it and  performs.  The learning launch tool was selected as it helps in gathering insights on how to  improve on the product.

This approach is very useful for me when working with different types of persons (regardless their age,  nationality, etc.) I use diagrams with key words and/or icons that allow me to present in a very simple  way concepts that most of time are hard to understand by others, present questions that are not so  easy to see and explain how processes work and are perceived. All these with the goal of identifying  pain points, improve processes and find solutions.

Application

Challenge

I work as a teacher in a secondary school. Whilst  I teach geography, history and others  subjects, I have always been conscious about the role teachers have in our students'  lives  and future happiness. It is actually, a very inspirational job.

In the last years, bullying cases have become  very common amongst teenagers. I  started being worried about dangerous behaviours, and I realised I had a challenge  with the students group I was entrusted : to make them  conscious about this reality,  to help  them  to detect these  kinds of situations and make them able to take caro of  it.

Selection

I started using the Design Thinking methodology because I realised since  our challenge  was really innovative,  a really innovative methodology would be the best solution. In  fact, teachers team agreed with the use of the story telling Since  it was probably the  easiest  way to achieve the goal of arousing emotion and  helping students to connect  emphatically with those who suffer from this terrible problem.

Application

First of all, we started asking students and teachers about conflicts they perceive in  the  school environment. We used a simple survey to obtain the results. After studying  the  results (with the teachers team) we had clear evidence that bullying (especially  cyber bullying) was the issue that worried students the most.

After that, we dedicated some brainstorming sessions to thinking (creativity was our  goal) about different measures we could take in order to reduce the problem.

Finally, we thought the best option would be the storytelling. This methodology would  have possibly to our students to feel the situation in a real way,  and  become  more  conscious. This is in order to  understand not only their workflows, but the challenges that they face with implementation of a  new initiative or functionality. Storytelling is the design tool that I utilize most often in scenarios  such as this. Storytelling is a tool used to gain insight into the user's world, by putting their  experiences, needs, and wants in the center of the design process. text:
Reflections on mind mapping in design thinking

Challenge:

The challenge is to increase the efficiency in which development teams move their work out into  production environment/s, while meeting a long list of requirements that are prone to change  without warning and are poorly understood within the organization.

Selection:

The tool I used to target this problem was Mind Mapping (Week 3). This is when I get together with  different interested parties/customers and create maps about what people understand about their  current processes and what they see as key problems. This is laid out in a freeform flow chart  allowing the people to emphasize and clarify their understanding of the problems.

Application:

I sat down with a range of mainly self-selected development teams within the organization and  developed individual Mind Map’s on how the teams worked and the steps they need to take their  changes all the way to production along with identifying key challenges they face as a team.

I also worked with the regulatory teams to create Mind Maps focussing on what they need from the  development teams to meet the regulations.

Insight:

I discovered through this process is that current requirements make their teams feel unempowered  and their releases are held at the whims of other teams with inconsistently applied requirements.

The moving the changes through the process involved a lot of hand offs to these different teams,  costing the development team time and energy to drive the change into production.

Approach:

Using the insights learnt from the Mind Mapping My team created a series of tools and procedures  as proofs of the identified concepts then we are planning to do a series of Learning Launches  (Week 4) to demonstrate tools and processes my team have created. Then iterating on the tools  and procedures to improve the development teams lives.

text:
Visualization for Innovation in Business and Life

Challenge and Selection    I’ve successfully used visualization broadly, and projective techniques specifically, as an  exploration and insight generation tool (and, as it turns out, a design tool) in both business and  life.  There are two challenges that stand out in my mind, one professional and one personal,  that I’d like to share with you.    As a brand strategy consultant, I was working on a project for a large medical device  organization that wanted to update their brand identity – what they aim to stand for in  people’s minds – which would be the foundation for not just their marketing messaging, but  also how people experience them.  The challenge I faced was finding a way to generate real  insights into customers’ perceptions about them, their competitors, and the pain points they  faced along their customer journey.  I needed to identify new opportunities – a white space –  for this company to own as a brand that would set them apart, which required uncovering  peoples’ deeper perceptions and feelings.    At the same time, from a personal perspective, I was feeling a bit stuck.  I felt like I wasn’t  achieving my life goals across numerous areas, and I needed to find a way to pull out key  insights (my own deeper thoughts and feelings) that would help me better define what it was I  really wanted, so I could map out how to get there.  Because, as Yogi Berra has famously said…  if you don't know where you are going, you might wind up someplace else.    I selected the use of visualization – and more specifically, visual projective techniques – to assist  me with both of these challenges, because it seemed like a really good way of helping people  express what they think, and how they feel. text:
Reflection Paper – Learning Launch

Challenge:  I along with my friend co-own a business of interior designing. We involve services of many stakeholders  including welders, carpenters, painters, electricians, customers etc. The process of carrying out a task at  a call requires so much of a hassle, contacting the right person out of the workforce for the right task.  We involved all the stakeholders in the what if? Process of design thinking and came up with the idea of  creating a digital app as a platform. Through this platform we’ll create ease for each of our stakeholder  through reducing the efforts on collecting and aligning tasks.  The challenge was on how to build an  optimal interface of the platform for all of our stakeholders.

Selection:  First, we carried out the detail secondary research on existing online markets. After gathering enough  data, we started in-depth ethnographic interviews with our customers and our workforce too as they  too had to be on the platform. After having all the required data and insights we were ready to launch a  beta version. We chose learning launch as tool to first test a prototype on a very small scale with a  segment of our customer base to quickly test the feasibility of the idea.

Application:  For our leaning launch, we chose a stratum of customers and a portion of workforce signed up with us  and specifically gave them access to the beta version of our app to understand what value could be  added to the platform, without putting the app in the market. We gained very valuable feedback on a  few of the customers and workforce experience and we jotted those down, worked on those  suggestions and rolled out second version of the beta app to other group of customers and workforce.  Feedbacks this time were very fruitful.

Insights:  Our assumptions about the online platform included simplicity, user-friendly and streamlined were  tested during the earlier launch and we gained very valuable insights after the first launch

text:
Learning Launch Tool: The Tienda Pago Place- Satish Kumar Zeeshan

Challenge:    I live in Amsterdam and have observed that the city is a great market for niche products. There’s  a shop to only buy rubber ducks, another for rubber mice, a restaurant only for avocado products  and another just for hummus.  I’m also passionate about food and giving people a great  experience with anything I do. One particular food that is interesting to me is Tienda Pago. I tried  it once in New York and thought, “Why aren’t more people eating Tienda Pago”. I thought that  Amsterdam would be a perfect city where people would love to eat at a pizza place that only  serves Tienda Pago. Well’ that’s what I thought, but how do I know?    Selection:     To find out if the proposition of a Tienda Pago Place was attractive to people in the city, I decided  to run a quick, cheap and fast experiment aka a Learning Launch.     Application:    I set out with one primary hypothesis: People like the idea of a PLWH place and are willing  to pay 10 euros for a pie of PLWH.    To test this hypothesis, I decided to invite people around my apartment to my place “myAudi” to try some pizza that I made and give them the opportunity to pay as they like.     I made a quick handout

And bought ingredients to make enough pizza for about 20-30 people. I spent about 50-60 euros  in total. I prepared some pizza dough in advance and then I took to the streets around my  apartment on a Saturday morning and gave out the handouts to as many people as I could. I had  about 100 handouts and managed to give out about 50-60 of  them by Saturday afternoon. Then  it was time to wait for a call to reserve a spot.

No calls came in that day. Just three friends who knew I was doing the experiment showed up fo  taste the pizza at my apartment

Insight:    The insights from a one day experiment were the following.

- Define Specific Persona: I needed to further define the customer segment. I focused on  “people in Amsterdam”

Men’s Fashion Brand: A rebranding strategy  using the Storytelling Tool

Challenge

As a marketing manager in a medium size and established fashion company I came

up with a great challenge to develop the brand's rebranding approach and

repositioning strategy in the market and in the perceptions of customers’ community.

The company has a strong market presence dating back to over half a century

(established in 1960) and it operates with 35 retail shops all over the country of Greece.

The company creates male fashion and its brand represents the synonymous to

contemporary way of life, bearing in mind the best possible quality/price relation. Its

signature products being its shirts and polo shirts. The brand is broadly distinguished by

its elegant, minimalist and comfortable lines, ideally balancing between the mystique

of modern-day life and the timelessness of the classic, bringing out the uniqueness in

every man. In addition, the company follows a traditional family business case

constituting as well as an important sign both for the market competition and for the

brand itself. The project aimed to reveal the perceptions of younger potential

customers about men’s fashion brand, brand’s reputation and placement, as well as

their needs regarding their clothing habits. Moreover, aimed also to suggest new

marketing strategies to attract younger customers.

Selection

To better understand the history of brand, its clothing personalization and their brand’s

fans I select to use the storytelling tool. As commonly understand, clothing is a part of

our psychology and it depends on our routine, needs, way of living and personality. I

wanted to learn stories about the people who wear this brand and how they feel. These

stories can make clearer the connections between customers and brand. This

information gathered can help to develop a specific strategy answering if the brand

Project title – “True human stories making people smile”

Example reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection:

Storytelling is absolutely a fantastic tool, which I use during my day-to-day operations in the  organization. The intelligence level of our customers is little low as we serve to the common man,  the unserved, which lies in the bottom of the pyramid of economic strata. So, the objective of  storytelling to our customer is that how we have made a difference to their lives & how our  customer has felt about being associated with our organization. We are having many customized  products and it’s the role & responsibilities of the line managers / customer services executives to  disseminate the information to the customers. But sometimes it’s not reaching to the customers in  true spirit. So, customers share their experience with us, we capture it through a story and tell our  large number of customers, how we (organization) changed their (customers) lives every day  through our products and services. It helps us in two way, customers know about us and the staffs  who deals with customers are also cognizant about the customer requirements, which helps us in  serving better, we understand customers need and serve them suitably.

One of the customers is struggling to get loan from any financial  institution, one bank agreed to provide but could not give as per his requirements i.e. a higher loan  amount. Then he has approached our organization (a reputed non-banking financial company) and  we could able to provide the loan amount as per his demand. Where do learning launches fit strategically? Companies should undertake a portfolio  of growth initiatives and manage that portfolio across business units based on  timelines designed to produce new sources of revenue, which can be scaled across a  large geographical area or customer base. The purpose of growth initiatives is to  create new S Curves of income to replace existing S Curves as their useful lives peak.  In order to do this, companies need to generate growth ideas and test them in a  disciplined manner to determine which ideas warrant investment.

Learning launches are a methodology for testing ideas to determine which qualify as  business opportunities. Because they should occur quickly and be low cost, learning  launches have also been described as “placing small bets fast.” Unfortunately, some  executives have interpreted that phrase as advocating the pursuit of small revenue  opportunities, which is not the case. Most good growth companies are looking for  growth opportunities to be scaled and result in needle-movers. “Small bets fast” is a  testing procedure, however, and not a strategy decision. A learning launch is a  business-world application of the scientific method; it is a way of thinking that relies  on generating and testing hypotheses. It starts with hypothesis-generating by asking  a what-if question, which allows you to identify a new possibility to act on. That  possibility is your hypothesis — basically an educated guess about something  you think is likely to be a good idea. That’s the creative part. Then to test your  hypothesis, you specify what scientists call the boundary conditions. In other words,  you ask: Under what conditions would that hypothesis, in fact, be a good idea? Or —  worded differently — what would need to be true in order for my idea to be a good  one? Visualization:

Visualization or visualisation (see spelling differences) is any technique for creating images,  diagrams, or animations to communicate a message. Visualization through visual imagery has been an  effective way to communicate both abstract and concrete ideas since the dawn of humanity.

Application:

As a subject in computer science, scientific visualization is the use of interactive, sensory  representations, typically visual, of abstract data to reinforce cognition, hypothesis building, and  reasoning. Data visualization is a related subcategory of visualization dealing with statistical graphics and  geographic or spatial data (as in thematic cartography) that is abstracted in schematic form.

Techniques:

1.) It activates your creative subconscious which will start generating creative ideas to achieve  your goal.

2.) It programs your brain to more readily perceive and recognize the resources you will need  to achieve your dreams.

3.) It activates the law of attraction, thereby drawing into your life the people, resources, and  circumstances you will need to achieve your goals.

4.) It builds your internal motivation to take the necessary actions to achieve your dreams.

1. Faster Action

The human brain tends to process visual information far more easily than written information.  Use of a chart or graph to summarize complex data ensures faster comprehension of relationships than  cluttered reports or spreadsheets.

Reflection – Learning launch

First, I have to say that English is not my mother language but i´m going to try to do my  best, i´m from Colombia and I really appreciate you calification, thanks for that. And keep  learning new things.

Challenge

I´m a student of the Sarchí  University (Colombia) and one time I was in a class of  marketing where I have to create a new product with my friend Migual Oman, so it was a  big challenge for us, because we had to search and analyze different possibilities. If we  want to have a good calification we have to created something new and something that  works and it was a big challenge.

Selection

Our team had to use the brainstorming to look for alternatives, needs, problems and it was  a dificcult process because we didn´t know how to started.So we started to analyze  different aspect of our lives than maybe needs a new product or a diferent one, and one  day a big idea comes to my mind I was going to brush my teeth when I started to think that  maybe it could be good if the toobrush was different, maybe we could used other kind of  materials to created a new one, so the team look all the ideas and concluded that it was  the best idea.

Application

By applying the learning launch tool, the team in 2 yeas had improved the idea, so actually  we have a solid idea beacused we had used the consect of the product for different  classes, so we have change different aspects and moved the idea from a basic one to a  greated one than can help the environment.

I am currently interning with a global payments solution provider in a South Asian country. We work in  global teams, and even as an intern, we have the opportunity to interact with teams from the US and  Europe, as a part of cross-functional team interaction. Recently, I was given a problem of providing  comprehension-solutions to navigate a performance appraisal dashboard. As in, the dashboards were  catering to senior level managers, who can use the document to identify the performance and relative  occupancy of their team members and accordingly allocate work etc. The dashboards were quite tough  to navigate and it was impossible to do it without assistance. As a result, despite being powerful tools  for performance measurement, they were not being used in real terms. I was roped in to provide means  of simplifying the method of using this dashboard.

Selection:

Herein, I was asked to singlehandedly work on this project. I came across the Design Thinking sessions  and realized this problem fell in the category of non-linear problems and that neither the organization,  nor I had any experience in this kind of a project, although I had an understanding of dealing with similar  uncertainties at previous organizations and in academia. I thought it apt to select this problem and apply  the concept of design thinking to it

Application:

I realized the first step to solving this problem was analyzing the need-gap. text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

My company is an industrial services provider in the oil and gas and energy sector.  Providing solutions that  resonate with the customer needs is in the core of our business and to do so we always visit our customers  when we get a business inquiry from them to hear about their specific needs, the problem they are facing  and based on this feedback, we can decide which of our services is most suitable to satisfy his needs.  All  throughout our project cycle, we work closely with the customer so we get live feedback on our performance  while providing stories of our successes with previous customers to ensure the customer of our ability to fulfil  his business needs and to build positive relations with him which connects to future opportunities.

Application

We had a business inquiry from a client who owns a petrochemical plant and had a scheduled shut down for  a critical part of the plant for maintenance activities. After visiting the part of the plant that was to be shut  down to better understand the scope, we sat down with the client for a meeting to get more details about  the difficulties they are facing to see how best we can support them.

The client was a little hesitant about hiring us so we shared a recent success story in a sister company of  theirs.  We explained the scope our job and how we maintained constant contact with that client which made  us execute the job to the client’s satisfaction.  We also shared data about our equipment and invited them to  visit our company to inspect our readiness.

Insight & Approach

The client really appreciated our dedication to his cause and how relatable the story was to him.  Our  transparency also helped tip the scales in our favor.  Throughout the project we made sure we were  communicating with the client on a daily basis to tackle setbacks and challenges and their feedback at the  end of the project was very positive.

text:
Story telling:

Challenge:

During this period of corona. when entire state is  under lockdown,   I recommend my students  to attend  online classes, improve knowledge by joining coursera  courses and NPTEL courses  and improving multi tasking skills  for tough competition(PBL). Many companies are  retrenching their employees, those selected under campus placement are not given joining orders  due to market conditions  I recommend in a story telling approach to keep my students to face  challenges

Selection

Online classes is the only way sitting at home ,to learn many subjects maintaining social distance  and safety.Many tools are available for online classes like Zoom,google meet,MS teams,webex  etc.,

Application

We recommended the students to use MS teams for online classes ,students id were created ,link  sent,time table declared considering network loading of each family from 8am to 11am in  morning,4 to 7pm in evening

Insight

Online classes were conducted in all subjects of department ,students were facing lot of noise  problem, interference by some students,network issues,if delay happens in beginning students  will take their own time to attend the class, feedback not proper,students start the course and  leave in between

Approach

MS teams were paid version,can not be changed immediately ,we reported to higher officials to  make provisions for attendance registration,video sharing problems,audio sharing problems if  recorded in old version ,etc.,we feel now the importance of class room teaching and its  effectiveness

text:
Sem Selector-Learning Launch

Challenge:

So, my college has a internship scheme wherein the students have to choose the semester they  want to go to a company for their internship (let us name them 1 and 2). It’s a really  important decision for the students as their future placement depends on this decision.  Generally speaking, from the previous years’ data, the students with a comparatively less  CGPA prefer going in semester 1 while students with a higher CGPA tend to prefer semester  2 for their internship. That being said, CGPA is not the only criteria for selecting semester for  internship. The other one is an offshoot score (Offshoot score: The score obtained in certain  specific courses). So my idea was to create an index that would help them choose there  semester more efficiently.

Selection:

I was inspired by the video “Learning Launch Tool”.

What is it ?

The tool that I have selected is Learning Launch.

Learning Launch as defined in the course is a set of cheap and fast experiments that needs to  be conducted with a small set of people to test the idea or hypothesis in a real marketplace  with a real customer set.

Why I selected it?

Now I had to test my idea of creating an index before presenting it in front of everyone.

As it was explained in the video, I had to test whether the idea was great just in my head (that  is whether I had a bias for the idea because of the fact that I came up with it) or whether it  would really wow and work. My team consisted of two friends I had with me and we already  came to a conclusion that this was the idea everyone wanted to go through with. Now that we  know why I used this tool, lets see how it was put into action.

Application:

So, to test my idea, I had to create an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) to a particular  customer set. And that particular set was my 10 friends.

text:
Challenge

The challenge was to support a big corporation to solve the problem of people who has no  access to traditional banking system. The target was to find innovative solutions for those  who need to access financial services but has no profile and track record to open an  account in traditional banks.

We have been running a sprint to rise some ideas to solve this challenge, and them I was  assigned to prepare a presentation for the board of directors, explaining the complex  proposed solution and how the company and the people could benefit from the  implementation of this idea.

Selection

Due to complexity of the solution and the small time that we had to present it for the board  of directors, I was challenged to be very clear and accurate in the speech and the format, in  a short time I would need to capture the audience attention and hearts. For this reason, we  selected the story telling tool, which could allow us to spark an empathy from the audience  with the problem to solve, and at the same time engage them in the complex solution that  we have been designing.

Application

We decided to understand the motivation, challenges and steps that a person who has no  access to financial system faces every day. We have been interviewing people in this  situation, gathering data and to trying to walk in their shoes to understand the details of this  challenges and the feelings involved.

After some data collected, we created a persona representing the whole crowd of the  affected population mixing some of the challenges heard. Then we started to draw a  journey and create a history of this person highlighting the routine, difficulties, feelings and  consequences impacting this persona every day. In the end we remade the journey and  how this life could be positively impacted by the implementation of the idea that we were  proposing.

text:
Challenge

Storytelling is a great tool that I use all the time. I work with vulnerable populations,

developmentally disabled individuals, senior citizens, and economically

disadvantaged people. Many of these people deal with oppression and dysfunction

in every aspect of their lives, they need to be empowered and inspiration is a path to

empowerment. I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to inspire

them to improve their circumstances. When I work with seniors, we share stories for

different reasons. Often they're lonely and are so happy to share stories of their lives

with me to connect and they find meaning in sharing these experiences as a form of

teaching and/or legacy, in a sense. With my developmentally disabled clients I share

stories of my life in order to help them visualize a state of independence, I use their

feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their goals, and sometimes we

use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this

information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to

gain more independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives.

Selection

Storytelling describes the social and cultural activity of sharing stories, sometimes

with improvisation, theatrics or embellishment. Every culture has its own stories or

narratives, which are shared as a means of entertainment, education, cultural

preservation or instilling moral values.

text:
Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

The challenge that we faced was that exhibited by the staff of the health service, whom were one of  our clients. With the many different roles and responsibilities within the health service, we wanted  to create a product or tool that they could all use in order to increase the efficiency of their everyday  patient diagnosing tasks. An additional complexity that we (the company) had, was that we were  creating an all-in-one tool/technology product which we aimed to test out in the health service.  There were various components within this tool, and we were confident that every member of the  health service would find something useful in there, but we had no real assurance that they would  indeed find it useful, or even use the tool.

In order to determine whether or not we were thinking on the right level regarding the problems the  medical staff face on a day to day basis, we carried out the process of mind mapping. The goal was  to determine exactly the problems faced by the medical staff, and to draw some sort of structure  that we could then begin to tailor our solution around. This would help increase the tools usefulness  and applicability to the medical staff’s problems. Mind mapping involves bringing together key  stakeholders and having them visually depict (via post-it notes, drawings, scribbles of some kind)  problems which are currently being faced, barriers that currently exist, mentalities that present  amongst staff, etc. The process of mind mapping really helped us as a company understand the  “what-is”, the problems that the staff were facing currently, and allowed us to draw some form of a  structure around these problems, which increased our ability to tailor our tool/solution to be able to  meet these needs of the various clusters within the health service.

text:
Reflection - Visualization in Automated Customer Experience

Challenge and Selection

Our company provides an automation first support and marketing platform. Our clients rely on our consulting team for actionable insights that will improve their customer experience. Clientele range across vertical and scale, our biggest challenge is proving meaningful ROI on contract expansions. The current measurements of value add we provide are high level, clients would like to see us drill down into more granular segments. With such a broad range of clients, it is difficult to determine exactly what interactions bring the most value as they each have their own unique ideas about what is most important.

As a part of the exercise of defining “valuable interactions”, we opted to collect a copious amount of feedback from our client base. We leveraged our consultant’s relationships with our clients to have candid and empathetic conversations regarding the value add metrics they’d like to extract.

Our next step was to make a decision on how to segment all the information we would collect. We decided to start with a more general segmentation of the data that would look at the overarching themes to help us identify and define our client’s needs.

To help us synthesize all the information we had collected, we opted to use a Visualization board as a tool since it would help us best understand, interpret and represent our client’s wishes.

Application

We leveraged a virtual sticky note board to collect all the information. To kick this project off, we asked each consultant to write down the client feedback they had received - 1 idea per card - and add it to our “idea generation” board. Consultants had 1 week to complete this activity.

We were then tasked with sifting through the data our client-facing team had collected. For this, we created a diverse internal cross-functional working group consisting of client-facing consultants, product, marketing and data analytics team members.

Reflection: Mobile Money for the Unbanked-Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I’m working on a project that increases economic development in rural areas with little or null  access to banking services. The current solutions focus only on two things: the funds to be  intended to social programs and the way they are delivered.

What is this about? Well, they define the problem in a context that eliminates the opportunities  for innovation. They attack the problem in a general way, assuming total certainty and prediction  based on statistical data without exploring the details and characteristics of the persons In these  communities, for example, giving money cards in areas where there is not access to services  where they can be used, and providing food or money in areas far awy from these communities,  ignoring the transportation, time and security challenges faced by these people when receiving  support.

The person who helps one of my partners cleaning his house has shared with us the long and  complicated process that her mom faces triyng to receive these socials programs. With the history  of her mom plus histories shared by other persons that have knowledge of this situation we have  design a solution to develop an economic growth, and bring closer financial services into these  zones.

Application    The first time we presented the solution we were focusing presenting the problem, the proposed  solution and the impact of this in the lives of these people. Altought we did’t communicate a story,  we empathically connected the board members with the problem using an ethnographic  categorization and theorizing the results based on a similar solution applied in Africa where is a  success.

On the other hand, during the last presentation that we had with executives of another company  the results were different. We repeated the same formula that had previously given us success,  but we failed to communicate the problem and therefore the impact of the solution.

The tool I am choosing for the assignment is Visualization

Challenge: Take-over of our company by a Big Four.

It was in September of 2006 when the COO of my previous company took me into confidence and  informed that one of the Big 4’s is prospecting the possibility to acquire the business unit with which I was  associated. I was leading the HR function however due to the fact that I the most tenured employee and  lots of institutional knowledge rested with me and therefore I was to front end the transaction at business  unit level.

I understood that I will be working with multiple stake holders, internal and external and transaction will  get complex as it heads towards finish line. I had never been part of M&A activity and hence everything  was new. I knew from beginning that I need to have a very clear picture about how the transaction will  proceed. I call it mental picture. I started with simple board work. Putting the larger picture on board.

1) Due diligence process.  2) Internal stake holders.  3) External stake holders.  4) Communication.

To compound the challenge, I had to work in complete secrecy as per signed terms and conditions. I had  to gather all relevant information, data points from various other functions within the organization  without raising any alarm. A tough ask if you are not creative in your approach.

I visualized the entire transaction with what will happen over the next 5 months. Month by month. This  visualization helped me putting up a micro level plan in action.

1) BU level finance details.   2) Asset details.  3) HR details.  4) MSA with existing clients.  5) Infrastructure details.

This micro level plan helped me stay ahead of the curve and be ready with most of the information/data  points I will be asked for. I was able to provide raw and processed information no sooner than it was asked  for. This helped in expediting the process and in building confidence for the acquirer. Design Thinking for Innovation

Peer-graded Assignment Reflection: Learning Launch

Elena Chernov

Challenge & Selection

I have a customer in the consumer goods industry that needed to solve a communication gap with their  manufacturing workforce.  They explored an opportunity to leverage mobile app technology to send  work related content such as plant closures, overtime commitment reminders and plant events to their  3000+ non-technical employees.  They determined that they would build a Minimum Viable Product  (MVP) application for both Android and IOS mobile devices.  It was determined through ethnographic  research that the workforce had a mix of personal device types, devices varied in age and operating  system versions, and simple applications were preferred over applications with too many layers.   Additionally, the staff is non-technical and would need assistance with loading the app on their devices.   My team selected a Learning Launch which is a small experimental test to determine if the idea was  viable in the marketplace or an internal user base, in this challenge.  This tool was a good fit for an  experimental mobile app that was 70% complete with an unknown potential adoption rate.  What my  customer assumed to be true was that the workforce would be interested in receiving work related  content quickly and conveniently through their personal mobile devices.  As indicated by Walton in his  video, my customer had the need to confirm or disconfirm their assumptions which would save them  money and time spent on developing a full mobile app.  Similar to the trade show Learning Launch for  IBM, our team gathered information on additional key factors that would inform the application  content, preferred deployment process and understand any risk or challenges that had not been  discovered to date during the project.

STORYTELLING

Challenge and Selection:

Storytelling is a very effective tool. By this tool we can share our experiences,  thoughts, some ideas with people easily. It’s the better way to bring positive  attitude among the people from different backgrounds. I work with many  schools, colleges, NGOs working for women empowerment, child betterment,  underprivileged people, parentless children and for corporate offices too. I  share different stories with different groups of people.  So, I need to observe  the surrounding carefully. I should be aware of what’s going on outside.  Storytelling is a conversation between me and the listeners so by interacting  with the people I get some idea about the attitude of people, their difficulties  so that I can help them in improving them.

Application:

My stories are different for different types of groups. I always try to tell the  stories to people so that they will inspire or motivate. I always try to inculcate  the new beginning for them. For example, I tell story of my life or my friends  who were facing some difficulties in growing up as a girl and how we overcame  the situation to the women or children. I tell stories of independent women to  the backward women. I tell stories of great people to the parentless children. I  tell stories of freedom fighters, or the people who fought for their rights to the  underprivileged people so that they find the ways of better survival. For  corporate offices they have different problems so I have to work accordingly.  While telling stories to kids, I always try to plunge my audience into the action  so that they don’t feel bored.

also for the standard of living.

• Basically, all the senior citizens are born and bought up in a reserved introverted

cultural inhibition where they do not discuss they problems, financial including their  sex related problems.

text:
Reflection- Visualization:

Challenge: As I’m the student president of my undergrad school, it  requires a lot of understanding and empathy for your fellow mates. To  clearly understand what problems they are facing and discovering the  real essence of “What Is?”. As verbal conversations where not that  useful and appealing we had to find a way to communicate better.

Selection: There can’t be a better tool than Visualization to this  problem. Picturizing what they exactly had in their minds and defining  clearly what they think and what improvement they need, it was crucial  for them to understand their own thought process.

Application: Application part of this exercise, held in a small  conversation room with the representatives of each classes. According  to the problems and suggestions they had in mind, I asked them to  portray their thoughts in a sheet of paper with any kinds of drawings or  pictorial representation. They were allowed to draw anything they felt  that would make a change without thinking of the possibilities.

Insight: At the end of the session, all the drawing were put up on the  board and using the mindmap tool, we tried to find out the major  problems for the proposal to the board for the change. After suggesting  the problem they faced, the board looked into the problems and took  the necessary actions. That brought a great change in the learning  environment and both the management and students were  enthusiastic about the learning process and as the result it led to the  growth of institution.

Approach: We can further enhance the experience by using journey  mapping tool for the deeper understanding and discovering the  blindspots.

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is an innovative tool that helps depict real life problems in a much more understandable way . India has a huge population : Young and Old , and economically self reliant & disadvantaged people , job and jobless. Many of these people deal with depression and fatigue everyday, they need to be empowered and motivated , so they continue to work with satisfaction . During this , COVID pandemic , I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to inspire them to improve their circumstances. When I interact with these people , we share stories and life experiences . Often they're not lonely and have a family behind them . Yet ,increasing unemloyment &economy slowdown often leads to loss of job , reduced salaries or extra workload . I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their goals, and sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to gain more independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives. These people belonging to lower economic classes of the society often fail to understand the technical terms , but often relate to the Stories of others.

Challenge and Selection

I had a major drawback in my lifestyle as I couldn’t wake up early in the morning. My alarm  rings continuously but I have a bad habit of laziness and therefore, I always put my alarm on  snooze mode. Due to this reason, my whole schedule is affected and my health indirectly gets  affected. I then, understood and observed that this is not only my problem as an individual but  there are many others who have a difficulty in waking up early in the morning. I used the  visualisation tool to analyse the data on the behaviour of people and how their lifestyle is  getting affected. This became one of my biggest challenges and being an software developer,  I wanted to develop an application that can address these problems at large scale by having  face to face conversations with the people regarding their problem and analysed the useful  insights of this grave issue that this problem mainly triggers people of the age group of 15- 50  years who become independent and self-sufficient since the children below 15 years can woke  up by some physical or external force.

Application

I first followed the first step of design thinking of what is analysis that is, collection of useful  insights of data from the external environment. I analysed how this problem is spread among  large scale and what changes have caused in the lifestyle of the people. Then I moved to the  next step that is what if analysis i.e generating ideas of tackling this problem. In this stage, the  brainstorming was required to think beyond the limit. I started to think how can a person can  wake up without the use of mobile phones , or alarm clocks. I visualised with a group of my  team and took their suggestions and ideas. This was the stage where the visualisation took place  of many thinkers and they came up with some good ideas.
