Learning Launch

Challenge

I work in the Marketing team of a global company that allows people to try our products before buying  them. We sell medical devices and therefore a lot of time in the first appointment is dedicated to the  client's medical history and medical examinations.

The challenge I have to manage is to create the new omnichannel customer journey to include digital  services. It seems to be a great opportunity for all people involved: customers could receive a better and  customize service, sales people could be more effective and earn more money, the company could improve  revenues, productivity and customer satisfaction.

At the same time, it requires a complete review of our journey because it adds time to our appointments  have a very long duration and involve elderly people, who therefore have a low attention span over time.

Selection

The goal is to create a customer journey that meets the needs of our consumers and amazes them.

A cultural change of this kind in such a large organization makes it even more necessary to be sure that you  are going in the right direction, testing the various ideas that have emerged and be ready to adapt them in  case you realize that the initial idea was not quite. perfect (which certainly cannot be, given that it is the  first time in 70 years that the company approaches the world of digital services).

Video 04.03 – Learning Launch

The first thing we did was a mapping of all customers and stakeholders and their related pain points to the  current purely physical customer journey.

We have identified 2 main clusters of people (customers and healthcare professionals) who currently suffer  from these pain points. Eva Rivera  Design Thinking for Innovation  Simona Gamal  April 5th, 2021

Course Reflection

1) Challenge & Selection

At my current job, I was approached by a UX manager for whom I provided administrative support; he  had heard that I was passionate about the environment and asked if I would help him in standing up a  Green Team in our office. He and I connected with the Green Team leads in the Philadelphia office, and  we learned that the local office teams that already existed were the result of grassroots organizing. For  our office in Princeton, this meant that developing a team wouldn’t be as simple as getting buy-in from  our Office Manager and Office Managing Principal (OMP). The real challenge was understanding the  needs and priorities specific to the individuals in our office and figuring out how we could get maximum  engagement by catering our group’s sustainability efforts to suit those needs.

Our core team (me, the manager, and two other folks in the office) chose to use Mind Mapping for this  challenge. According to the guest video lecture from Eva Rivera, mind-mapping is a  strategy where you take the data you amassed during the “what is?” phase and look for patterns and  themes that emerge, as these patterns and themes can help inform the “what if?” phase. We chose  this tool because we wanted to see if any of the reasons people cited for wanting to participate in the  Green Team could be grouped into themes that could then inform how our core team planned events,  allocated time and resources, and recruited more team members moving forward.

2) Application

Our core team presented a slide deck for our office forum, introducing the idea of a Princeton Green  Team and asking people to help make it a reality. Chinyere Adam

PORTABLE WATER SUPPLY IN MY COMMINITY

Challenge

I live in a part of the word where residents are charged arbitrarily by service providers (government and  private organizations) for services rendered. We don’t get to know the basis and how much of such  services we enjoyed. All we see is bills at the end of the month and we get disconnected if not paid or  we are made to make payments in advance while deductions are made termed ‘pay as you use’.  Residents crave to know how they are billed so they can make plans in advance to match their income.

One of such services with arbitrary bills is water supply. The people in my community resisted these bills  and chased out the service providers. The wealthy ones in the community dug up bore holes to meet  their water needs while the poor ones move about in search of water. They use any available source  whether clean or not and in recent times, there has been outbreak of cholera in many homes with  children dying.

To address this, I formed an association of youths in the community. We planned on presenting a  proposal to one of the private owned organization and hope to partner with them in restoring portable  water supply in my community with a transparent billing system.

Selection

We selected a collaborative approach that will meet the needs of the residents without compromising  the profit objectives of the service provider. We adopted the co-creation approach. We hope to  collaborate with them and share ideas that will be beneficial to us all.

Application

The community representative had dialogues with the water service provider. Suggestions on billing  parameters, water needs and income level were shared by the youth representatives because they have  firsthand knowledge of the needs of the community and exchange of ideas were made. These meetings  were held between both parties until an agreement was made and water supply was restored in the  community.

text:
Visualization

Visualization is any technique for creating images, diagrams, or animations to communicate a  message. Visualization through visual imagery has been an effective way to communicate both  abstract and concrete ideas since the dawn of humanity.

Many people aren't aware of how powerful visualizing can be in their lives. In fact many of us are  doing plenty of visualizations every day. The problem is that most of us are doing visualizations  to create the life we don’t want; we are often using it to imagine the worst outcomes of things or  worrying about the future. If you can remember the time when you worried so much about  something that it actually happened, is probably a good example of using visualization to create  the life you don’t want.

Visualization isn’t something fluffy used by people who aren’t living in reality. It's quite the  opposite; it's used by a whole array of people who know how to use it to bring about positive  outcomes in their life. Many athletes including Olympians use it to excel in their sports. The  benefits of visualizing is also there for children; research from Beijing Institute of Physical  Education and University of Ottawa found that child table tennis players between the ages of 7 to  10 performed better when they used visualizations (mental imagery).

Interestingly, research has also found that people who imagine themselves performing a task,  improve their performance in that task without physically doing anything.

In order to visualize and manifest the kind of life you want, it's very important to have a clear idea  of what you want and why. This can be achieved by understanding what you value and what brings  you the most joy in life. Have you ever had that moment when you were doing something and felt  joyful doing it? If yes, then that is a good sign of something you might want to have in your life.

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a good tool which I use any time. I work with vulnerable populations, developmentally  disabled individuals, senior citizens, and economically disadvantaged people. Many of these people deal  with oppression and dysfunction in every aspect of their lives, they need to be empowered and  inspiration is a path to empowerment. I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to  inspire them to improve their circumstances. When I work with seniors, we share stories for different  reasons. Often they're lonely and are so happy to share stories of their lives with me to connect and  they find meaning in sharing these experiences as a form of teaching and/or legacy, in a sense. With my  developmentally disabled clients I share stories of my life in order to help them visualize a state of  independence, I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their goals, and  sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this  information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to gain more  independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives.

In discussing policy changes with a social service agency, I was  trying to explain to them the benefits of taking a more client focused approach, among other things, and  in particular, of recognizing each person as a unique being, and addressing their individual needs first  and foremost. The agency was in the grip of a “compliance culture” and its clients were failing in this  non-empathetic, rigid structure. I was also explaining how sometimes addressing the needs of one  individual can impact everyone for the better, even if it seems extreme or out of the ordinary. Challenge & Selection

I am with the HR department in my organization and I realized most of the comms that  HR sends out there(to employees) were mostly in text format when I started working  with the firm. Communication is vital in an organization and sometimes communicating  effectively for results tend to be a challenge. Especially when the employee is under a  lot of work pressure and stressed, it sometimes becomes quite difficult for the receiver  to focus when the message being communicated is lengthy. Some employees rarely  open these messages whenever they received them on the employee portal. I then  decided to learn some tools on video making (infographics, animation and editing) to  help with the comms that are pushed to employees. The visualization tool was one that  could work perfectly in that case hence adopting that tool.

Application

So I started with taking the learning on the video making step by step. So for 2 out of 5  comms that had to go out there, just a little write up was required to introduce the  message which was followed by the video itself. So before I come up with the videos,  the internal communication team would send me the content (in a word format and  some pictures) detailing the key message which definitely has to be clearly indicated in  the video.

Communicating without results does not really help in an organization so making the  key message clear was pivotal in the process. The videos were not only shared on the  portal but also via respective departmental WhatsApp groups to cover especially those  who rarely open the portal.

text:
Deepak Das (Storytelling)

Storytelling is the process of using fact and narrative to communicate something to your

audience. Some stories are factual, and some are embellished or improvised in order to

better explain the core message. While this definition is pretty specific, stories actually

resemble a variety of things.

(1) Challenge:

When I work with seniors, we share stories for different reasons. Often they're lonely and

are so happy to share stories of their lives with me to connect and they find meaning in

sharing these experiences as a form of teaching and/or legacy, in a sense. With my

developmentally disabled clients I share stories of my life in order to help them visualize

a state of independence, I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain

their goals, and sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and thought

processes. I use this information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that

works for them to gain more independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives.

(2) Selection:

Storytelling is a great tool that I use all the time. I work with vulnerable populations,

developmentally disabled individuals, senior citizens, and economically disadvantaged

people. Many of these people deal with oppression and dysfunction in every aspect of

their lives, they need to be empowered and inspiration is a path to empowerment. I spend

a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to inspire them to improve their

circumstances.

text:
Storytelling

Challenges

I was in a mini Design Thinking Hackathon. The whole process lasts for two hours. There  were four people in our group, and we were supposed to deliver a minimal viable product by  the end of the two hours. We did not know each other before, and therefore, it is super  challenging to come up with new ideas, challenge each other’s ideas, and express our  thoughts with teammates we barely know.  Our challenge is to design or create an  optimization strategy for our product line to better serve better home officing trends. I want to  share one step in the process with you, where the Storytelling tool comes along and serves as  a big favour for our group.

Selection

We have used other design thinking tools during the whole process, such as the visualization  tool, the mind-mapping tool, the brainstorming tool, etc. However, the storytelling tool is the  tool, which serves from the beginning (introduction of the topic) to the end (elevator pitch). In  short, storytelling is the easiest and the most challenging tool to manage. It builds the bridge  where we can connect and share emotional visions.

Application

I realized that the storytelling tool is the tool that all of us use to introduce the other team  members into our imaginative world.  Due to the time limit, we do not have the time or  resources to gain little details of our customers. Therefore, we decide to treat ourselves as  customers. We are all home officing in the past one and half years. We want to design a  procedure or a product to solve our problems. After that, we were all on the same page as the  customers; we immediately started to recall situations where we would like to change or  improve when we are home officing. Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a great tool that I use all the time. I work with Oil and Gas industry clients who’s prime  agenda is to improve their business efficiency and profits. Many of these client folks are not tech savy  and hence often have their reservation on any new technical design I propose to achieve efficiency or  refine the process. Hence, I spend a lot of time in convincing them or giving them knowledge transfers  to get them on the same team before changing any business process. With my tech experience, I often  share stories of my other clients to help them visualize the proposed transformation and its impact.  Also, after building a prototype, I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their  goals, and sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use  this information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to make more  user-friendly design in the areas required.

Application

I have a story about using storytelling. In discussing design changes with a particular O&G client, I was  trying to explain to them the benefits of taking a more user focused approach, among other things, and  in particular, of recognizing each process team as a unique being, and addressing their individual needs  first and foremost. For their warehouse inventory, there was a requirement to create a solution which  can scan the bar code on the different items which will be later used for assessment and maintenance.

Insight & Approach

REFLECTION-LEARNING LAUNCH

CHALLENGE&SELECTION

The tool that I first chose to work with was Learning Launch in order to put our ideas in practice in  an experiment context, to be able to understand and analyze the results of it.

As a worker/assistant in my father’s company, I perform an important role for the development and  improvement for the future of the company. Our business is mainly focused on textile including  wedding dresses and clothing materials. The communication between my father and I isn’t so open  due to the fact of my father being a person with a fixed mindset. I see myself as a growth mindset  person and so I understood the importance of marketing, advertisement and networking in order to  improve the profit of our company through the increase of sales, not only locally but as well as  nationally and internationally.

We intend to establish partnerships with different stakeholders and marketing agencies as well we  intend to create a team that will work with the business analyzes and budget expenses.

Selection – After some design thinking activities and after understand the problem and find  solutions for it, our team is finally ready to implement the Learning Launch tool to have a more  accurate result from our experiment.

Application

When it came the time to apply the Learning Launch tool, we focused on the structure and  execution of the ideas coming from the marketing partners as well from our accountant  team. More specifically, we wanted to make sure if our company could respect our budget  limit but at the same time work with an online marketing sector effective and worthy.

The first days of the experiment were somehow balanced between expectation and  tension because is important to see the results becoming positive but is probably more  important to understand that being patient is a virtue and in this case we were just hopeful  about the day we could see our results and online marketing investment becoming  profitable.

text: Mind Map    The mind map is an excellent technique and one of the most powerful ones of a designer,  which consists in a first phase, “what is?”, where we will achieve a lot of data that we have to  transform into information and perceptions that can be communicated easily, and a second  phase, called “what if?” that will help us to create creative and innovative solutions.     Application    As we know, Covid-19 and the situation that this virus provoked came to change our  lifestyle. For example, a lot of enterprises, organizations, and businesses, as the case I am  going to share, had to update and accept virtuality as a new method to continue with their  daily labors.    In my case, I will tell you how I used the mind map technique in my church, since it,  redarding the topic of virtuality, was outdated and, because of orders of the Ministry of  Health, it had to close its doors, which means that our community would stop participating in  our weekly activities and the biblical message would not be taught.   The problema was clear, and the solution that we found was using social media to continue  with the weekly activities but, since the church did not have equipment for live streaming, we  had to develop a plan to record. Here’s where the mind map comes on the scene.    First of all, it was reviewed what it is usually done in our meetings and until what extent each  of those things could be virtual. Later, we analyzed which things we would need to make this  true. Once everything was defined, we did an schedule to record, and thought about a  campaign for our community to follow us in social media and participate of our virtual  activities. Finally, we developed activities for our community to feel connected with us in this  new virtual stage.

Learning Launch: a way to the natural solution. 1

Learning Launch: a way to the  natural solution.

Challenge

Despite my engineering background, through the past years I have been  managing our family's business, a large size camping and village resort in  Tuscany. As a small company, owning flexible organisation and adaptable  resources for internally producing products and objects, our goal has always  been to reconnect people (our customers, stakeholders) with the natural  environment we oughted to provide them during their stay with us. Therefore  innovation travelled through the question "how might we provide a more  natural touristic village experience, yet retaining a perception of comfort?".

Selection

The prototype gained its initial shape based on feedbacks provided by our  customer base (via questionnaires): a small wooden structure with cotton tent,  a small retreat for couples in the woods.

Natural materials and a smart yet simple design of the interiors.

The question had been articulated to a certain degree of refinement but we  soon realised we were missing insights and, therefore, parts of the problem to  address. We realised we had very small experience on the "Glamping" (stands

for glamour, nature oriented) business and decided to proceed based on

insights, not guesses that could build up presumptuous hypothesis. Having a  dynamic organisation, where different hierarchical roles merged regularly

together to discuss about everyones ideas, we soon realised that the only way  to gain profound understanding of the challenge was to let the stakeholders

speak for themselves. The option was here to set up a learning launch,

allowing people to live the prototype, created in a single unit. A process that  would have helped us gain more insights and prove our idea quickly and

cheaply.

Challenge

I was recently interning with a company in energy sector. Company carries a legacy of more than 100  years with itself. Overall development and care of the employees is the top most priority for the  company. There were multiple learning initiatives which helped employees to learn and grow. Most  of the learning initiatives we had were in the domain of classroom training/workshops and e-learning  modules. There was nothing specific, structured and formal in the space of peer to peer learning. So,  the challenge for me was to design the sustainable social learning / peer to peer learning framework  and lay down the implementation plan in 2 months. I will try to cover who all were the important  stakeholders involved in solving the problem at hand.

Selection

As there was no proper historical data available for this problem, hence design thinking came to be  very handy in solving the problem and develop a new concept of peer to peer learning at the company.  I have used learning launch tool to solve and come up with the solution as it involves experimenting  different ideas and prototype as mentioned in the IBM story.

Application

I started of with first understanding the concept of peer to peer learning and how it is used in  corporate. With the help of external benchmarking I could identify different initiatives used by some  renowned industries in the field of social learning. Then I conducted in depth interviews with  managers and supervisors to understand their level of understanding of the concept and how they  feel about participating in this initiative.

MIND MAPPING  Student · Omar Gonzales

Coursera · Peer-graded Assignment · 11/28/2020

REFLECTION: MIND MAPPING

1. Challenge

I’m working on a redesign project of the exterior of an automatic cutting machine for  Ogilvy the Advertising and  Communication. Before starting the redesign, we had to better understand what were the  client’s needs, so we had a meeting before the briefing and the briefing itself.

2. Selection & Application

When designing, we need to gather a lot of information from research and also from  meetings with the clients, so we can design better products and achieve better  results. To overcome the challenge of being lost having too much information to deal  with at the same time, I always end up using mind maps. They’re a great tool if you  want better organized data in your project, like said in the course “Mind mapping is  one of the most powerful tools in the design thinker's toolbox.”     All the information gathered from a briefing with a client, like Ogilvy the Advertising and  Communication, can be better  organized utilizing sections, subsections and topics, for example, and you can also use  illustrations, drawings, images – everything that’ll make you visualize the information  in a better way. My team used Miro to create the mind map, an awesome site if  you’re a creative person that also likes practicality. There, we checked if all the data  gathered from the client’s meetings were organized in a simple way that everyone  could understand. Like David Kelley, the founder of IDEO said, “When I want to do  something analytical, I make a list. When I'm trying to do something creative, I make  a mind-map”.

3. Insight

A mind map is a great tool to look for patterns, insights, relations between  information, how they’re all connected in your project. All that leads to more creative  solutions to your designs. Drawing Insights from Researches more effectively

Challenge: -

A lot of times the organization was arriving at conclusion and business decision from a one two  datasets and this has been a growing a concern. We were not sure what we were missing, but the  entire team concluded that a grave error is embedded in the process. We wanted to fix this by listing  out the pros and cons of the methodology and also arrive at a meaningful conclusion that can  provide value to the business.

Selection: -

The Design thinking methodology that we used was storytelling. One of the key reason for going this  route is because storytelling helps to connect to the audience, it gives you a story board and you can  create a beautiful and meaningful story once you join all the pieces. We wanted a method where in  we can list the pros, cons and cause and also design an solution by taking into consideration who the  audience is. As mentioned in the course, even though it may not make sense to us, we can define a  method that can help the audience understand and attach to the problem of interest.

Application: -

We started by making a list of all the positives and negatives of the current approach. As we thought  the negatives weighted heavily over the positives. One key positive following the current approach  was the timeliness. Since we were drawing business decision from a finite set of sources, even  though we had multiple other sources which went unattended, we were able to give quick summary  to management on timely basis. Negatives obviously included the key pieces we were missing or  overlooking by not included other consideration and economic environment before drafting  summaries.

We then listed down all the available sources that can add value and started making a plan to  summarize learnings from all the sources. This made us making a better plan on gaining rich  knowledge without impacting any timing or delay in business decisions.

text:
Learning Launch     Challenge & Selection :- The project was about bringing transparency to the internal recruitment

process. The current process is the candidates apply for the vacant position and the hiring

manager interviews the candidates. Selected candidates are offered the role. There was lot of

frustration among the candidates who did not get the role and felt there was no transparency in

the selection process. The HR head challenged the project team to come up with a solution

within a months time.    Since the challenge was to be complete the project within a short period of one month, the

project team did not have the luxury of time to go in for multiple discussions & chose to utilise

the design thinking tool, Learning Launch .     The project team immediately proposed to gather the requirements by meeting a group of 10

candidates who could secure the role & 5 candidates who secured the role and 5 different hiring

managers to understand their needs & showcase the progressive solution every week.    Application:- Learning Launch is a better tool to jump start the design the solution. This helps us

demonstrate a progressive solution every week to the stakeholders, gather the feedback &

improve the solution. This helps us to see if the design is meeting the expectations & do a course

correction to avoid costly rework & time.    Insights:- During the project we realised that the requirements are not cast in stone at the start

of the project. It continues to evolves during the course of the project. During the second week

stakeholders wanted to consider the privacy of the candidates which was not even mentioned as

a requirement in the initial phase. This helped us to complete the project to the fullest

satisfaction of all stakeholders and avoid costly rework of the solution architecture.    Approach:- we will continue to use Learning Launch tool to manage the evolving requirements of

any project to reduce rework or delays.

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge and Selection:

Storytelling as a concept has existed from centuries, from the time when cavemen would  gather around and listen to ancestral stories. It is indeed a form of art which is passed via  different means for various purposes. I am a volunteer at a special needs school and usually  work under the administration team, but due to certain circumstances, I was asked to  conduct a session on basic values like, peer pressure, arrogance, honesty, kindness, love etc.  with children. I was entrusted with the task of inculcating various values in one session and  this task baffled me.

At first I wasn’t sure how I would go about the session but then I decided to engage the  students with a story. I wanted the kids to have a good time but also learn something  important. I did not wish to exhaust them and hence decided to use the tool of storytelling  to inculcate certain values. “Storytelling is the most powerful way to put ideas into the  world”, as rightly said by Robert McKee. Stories have an emotional connection which makes  it more relatable for the listener and hence easier to grasp on the content.

‘Mahabharat’, which is an Indian epic, was the first thing that came to my mind. It entails  the story of the fight between two groups of cousins (princes) for their respective right to  the throne. On  their return the Kaurav prince is adamant on giving up the throne and also molests the  Pandu wife (apparent queen). To avenge these wrongdoings, the Pandu princes wage a war  where they come out to be victorious, however at a large price. text:
Why Should I Mind Map?

The soul never thinks without a mental image.

Aristotle

There are many reasons why mind mapping is used by millions of professionals, creatives and students  all over the world. Here are the top 4:

Mind maps structure information.

Mind maps can store and structure vast amounts of information. They display hierarchy, show  relationships between individual ideas and enable you to see the “big picture” at a glance. These  features also make mind maps an ideal tool to present information to others, create knowledge pools  and solve complex problems.

Mind maps improve comprehension.

In both school and university education, mind maps have proved to be popular and effective learning  aids. By structuring information in a way that is more compatible with visual learning styles, and by  filtering long texts into shorter mind map topics, learners can absorb large amounts of information  faster.

A 2013 study¹ published in the Modern Journal of Language Teaching Methods (MJLTM) examined how  students in Iran reacted to mind mapping as a tool for learning English as a foreign language. From the  sample group, 83.4 percent of students had a positive view of mind mapping in reading comprehension,  while only 16.7 percent responded negatively.  Tellingly, in a questionnaire issued after the study, the  statement “When I use mind maps for a reading passage, I’m more able to solve post-reading activities”  scored most highly.

Mind maps enhance productivity.

The benefits of mind mapping are not limited to education; they can be useful in a commercial sphere as  well. Mind mapping enables you to learn faster, communicate more efficiently and brainstorm more  effectively, which is why ever more businesses are using tools like MindMeister to get the most out of  their teams.

Challenges:

I am 22 years old south Indian hence defiantly you will correctly guess me as an engineering  graduate. Yes, you have correctly guessed it, am an electrical engineer. It can decrease pollution and increase farmer security. It has a lot of potential as  it has huge advantages over traditional agriculture. It is definitely the agriculture of the future. The goal is to establish criteria for the what-if idea generation phase. Mind  mapping provides a segway from what is to what if. text:
REFLECTION - VISUALIZATION

1. Challenge: ​My challenge is to improve the experience and coexistence of the tenant and owners

in the condominiums of family homes in urban areas. The Stakeholders are the tenants, owners,

maintenance service and marketplace.

2. Selection: ​The tool chosen for my challenge was visualization as it allows a better assimilation,

understanding and memory of a concept or problem, especially in this challenge involving several

stakeholders to develop a good customer experience. Attached the links

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B131Tm9Iex1

http://beck-calhoun.biz/bloghome.jsp

3. Application: ​The application of the visualization is carried out as follows.

- The visualization was centered on the owner and the tenant

- Photographs of various situations of pain experienced by the owner were used.

- A mental map of the activities that the owner has on a day-to-day basis was created

- An owner was invited to the viewing session to obtain valuable information first hand.

- Gif and emojis were added to make it more playful.

- A customer experience prototype was made based on a possible mobile solution that can

improve the coexistence of family homes.

4. Insight: ​What you learned from this exercise:

- The visualization catches the attention of the participants.

- It promotes empathy, collaboration and allows me to organize my information about the

challenge so as not to think in a linear way.

- One of the strengths of this tool is the communication that is generated in an atmosphere of

continuous decision making.

5. Approach: ​For the following visualization exercise, I have considered inviting stakeholders to have

more information about the challenge and to quickly correct the sketch, make a correct

extrapolation and find suitable solutions.

Learning launch got translated into a pilot initiative for us through social media launch of our initiative to gather pro-bono consultants to deliver the services and also enable people to apply for our services.

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge    As a pre-sales solutions engineer I am constantly faced with the tasks of understanding my  clients’ business drivers and being able to translate those drivers into digital solutions that  drives business outcomes. A part of my job role requires me to be able to plan my year in  order to predict how much business I will do with my clients over the course of a financial  year. This planning involves working very closely with one, or sometimes multiple account  managers. I’ve found that planning strategies for a large set of accounts can be extremely  challenging, especially when it involves decisions that need to be made by multiple people  who need to agree on what is possible for a specific client.     Traditionally, this type of planning would be done by looking at historical sales data for each  client and by trying to predict future sales by numbers alone. This has not been as effective  as I think the business would like it to be, primarily because it reduces the clients’ needs to a  number and the sales process to a monetary goal.     Selection    I decided that there had to be a better way of visualizing the problem and simplifying the  scenario surrounding each client. Spending time with each client was a good start to  understanding their needs, but I also needed to be able to translate those needs into a  roadmap for the digital transformation efforts that would come. This could not be done  until I had a better view of what the digital estate of each client looked like and also be able  to share this view with others such as the account managers and regional sales managers.     Mind mapping seemed like a great way to visualize the situation. More importantly, it  provided the ability to look for patterns within the large quantities of sales data and the  engagements that were constantly occurring between the account teams and the clients. Every year we engage in marketing out products and services which for the potential clients to apply. We definately understand that there are other organizations that offer the same services to the same market, hence we do alot of marketing so that they can find a good reason for them to choose us. As we do that we ensure good marketing through advertisements done in various ways and channels, but we always ensure that we give them the right information on the real products and services we offer and avoid giving wrong image to the public about us. However, we always ensure that we give polished and attractive content; and storytelling has always been a great way of marketing our organization. We create a thrilling story that covers who we are, what we offer, what we believe in and the quality we offer, hence story telling has always made it easy for us to pass the message and engage with potential clients.

Application I came across using storytelling as a tool and I found out how very successful it can be. We use our website alot, where we collect information about our services, our clients ,their satisfaction of the services and how they feel about our organization. We put together their stories and share with the public. The last challenging project was linked to a particular category centralization (at that time  decentralized) and involved members of different internal departments and external  stakeholders, with the focus on implementation of centralization in 1 smaller regional  market within the 3 months. The purpose of Learning Launch is to get to the truth – identify  all internal and external challenges within the B2C workflow and the current ways of  working. The truth saves money, time and should the assumptions be correct, the benefits  for the category and the business would be substantial. I work in a special sales unit inside a big multi-national manufacturing business.  Our Sales unit is specialized in Travel Retail channel (Airports, cruise ships, boarder  stores, etc). The unit is semi-autonomous in terms of structure, strategy, internal  processes and business objectives than the rest of the company.  The unit structure consists of three departments: Sales, Marketing, and Finance.  The other resources (example: HR) are leveraged from the total group.  The challenge that the unit is facing is in internal communication between the three  departments.   The current communication is intense, casual, and repetitive in many cases. This is  causing considerable time to be wasted in answering communications and providing  information.

According to Fatma Ivanova and Sandeep Jones’s book “Designing for Growth”, this tool  transforms information into images and is used to make sense of our observation of  customers and their journey, in our case the customers are actually personnel in  each dept.

3. Application:

The ambassadors agreed to be included in cc in any info or feedback request sent by  someone in their department to another department.  For example, if a marketing personnel sends a request for retail prices overview to a   sales personel, he or she needs to put the marketing ambassador in cc in this email.  Then all ambassadors will collect data over a certain period of time and all  information will be demonstrated in one visual. TOOLS USED FOR THIS COURSE IS VISUALIZATION

Challenge:

Here I am going to describe the challenges, which I faced in my research.  I did my research in the field  of Air pollution, I also predicted the Movement of air pollutants in the atmosphere with reference to  the existing Meteorological conditions.  In my research I can simulate the Meteorological conditions  by using a MET model and also I can use a Dispersion model to predict the movement of air pollutants.  The real challenge in my research is how the peoples living in that areas are affected because of the  air pollution.

Selection:

The selected tool for the research is AERMOD (AIR DISPERSION MODEL- US EPA), The model uses  Gaussian plume model as the base. AERMOD was developed by American Meteorological society/  Environmental protection regulatory. It is a steady state model and widely used in the plume  dispersion studies. AERMOD model is used as a regulatory tool in policy making for many air pollution  management programs. AERMOD dispersion model consist of two Pre-processors namely AERMET (A  meteorological pre-processor) and AERMAP (A terrain data Pre-Processor). Aermet is a pre-processor  software used in the AERMOD dispersion model exclusively used to analyses and predict the  METEOROLOGICAL conditions.  Dispersion of pollutants especially in the gaseous form purely depends  on the meteorological conditions like Wind Speed, Wind direction, ambient temperature and the  mixing height. Both Meteorological parameters as well as the emission parameters will be considered  as the Input parameters for the AERMOD model.

AERMOD is an advanced dispersion model developed by American Meteorological society and I  selected this model because accuracy of prediction is very high in case of AERMOD model.

Application:

I used the AERMOD model to predict the movement of pollutants in the environment and also the  Meteorological scenarios with respect to the pollutants behaviour.

Reflection: Flip Your Mind

Challenge

During the past months, I had enrolled on a Design Methodologies’ course in my university, in  which we are assigned many real-life problems in the industry, and we have to present innovative  and new ideas for the problem-solving. We were “hired” by a manufacturing company, who  needed the help of very creative engineers to design a mechanism or machine capable of flipping  or rotating 180 degrees a really large metal hoop used in their processes. No further information  was given rather its material and that the ring has big enough for it not to be flipped or rotated  by hand, and that the sky was our limit for possibilities for the solution.

Selection

The first tool I selected from this Design Thinking process was mind mapping. As I tend to be very  visual and creative, I believed this skill was going to be very well used. Mind mapping, as seen on  its corresponding video on week 3, is a tool that leads to creative solutions, many of them very  well perceived outside the box. This tool allows us to create patterns, establish goals, and creating  totally new outcomes. It is more intuitive than other tools and allows you to be as colorful and  visual as you please, making it the perfect tool for when designing a product that need a visual  representation.

Application

The process or application of this tool is rather simple but can evolve to great things. On the  center we find our goal, the mechanism or machine. Finding the first branches of investigation  really depends on the focus of each designer. For instance, mine revolved a lot around the  materials I had in hand, due to the pandemic, many materials were not available in my household  and could not just go shopping so easily. text:
USE OF MIND MAPPING TO ORGANIZE A SYMPOSIUM

The challenge here is to organise a symposium at college level. It includes the participation of every  College in the region. The students in and below third year can participate in this symposium.  Students, professors and all other Students in the college are welcomed to this symposium.

Mind Mapping is the tool I have used to help me organise this symposium. Mind mapping tool allows  the user to organise his/her thoughts through drawing a simple mind map, so that the user could  know about the challenge. Here the mind mapping helped me see through the things which should  be done before and during the symposium.

I have applied the Mind Mapping here to know about the preparations to be done in the  symposium. I have drawn a mind map connecting students with their projects and with their  professor so that I could arrange the symposium with a count of members and projects.

This mind mapping allowed me to think of various ideology to organise the symposium and helped  to prevent me from doing any mistakes. It allowed me to think in various aspects so that I had  various choices.

Next time I would like to use the tool VISUALIZATION for organising the same symposium. Since I  had feedback from various members participated in the symposium I would use it for the next time  in the Visualization.

Classified - Confidential

Reflection on Mind mapping

I chose to reflect on mind mapping because having learnt that it can help people organize and stablish  connections and relations between elements that would have not been identified otherwise. Besides, It  can shed light into the way someone’s mind work and function as a shared ground to make sure  everything is understood. I used this approach to create a systematic understanding of the new  consumer group we are approaching for a future marketing campaign for a global brand. This target is  just recently gaining importance for the market and there have been several studies trying to uncover  the hidden truth behind their interests and choices, but most of them are based on a global audience  and we needed to tailor those findings to the local market.

Application

The first step was reviewing all the literature written on the target audience and compare and contrast it  with the data from the local market. Upon completion, it was clear that the findings could be easily  organized through a mind map that comprises information from every document available. All sources  described the same characteristic aspects of their personality and the different data that each study  provided a new part of the whole picture. In order to describe the target’s personality, I discovered the 6  pillars that rule over the decisions of our target. This couldn’t have been possible without the aid of the  mind map that put ideas clearly into the paper for others to visualize and understand.

It depends on the  multiple factors like natural calamities, pandemic situations, company policy changes, etc.  So, we here are trying to make one tool/platform in which by analysing all the factors with  the help of Machine Learning the price of the stock can be predicted to some extent. Also,  we will provide the trading options so that investor and   seller can make their trading at the  same platform. We are going to provide different login option for the brokers of the share  market. Also, we are going to try to provide the insurance based on the predicted price by  our tool. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment  meant to quickly test an idea and prototype. In particular, we wanted to build a platform where all  the users can do the trading of the stocks with some guidance by price prediction. The  desired application will be mobile application through which users can trade their stocks.    This tested our assumption that the structure and execution were the main causes of our  workflow challenge. Challenge:

I am a Team Lead in a Finance and Accounts department and our department got a request from the  business head to streamline the process of sales of By product/ Scrap materials as they are getting  several calls from new small /medium level customers for an opportunity to buy our by-products  /scrap materials in place of existing customers and also they are ready to take at competitive rates.  Since there is a practice of selling scrap materials to existing customers in our company, the chances  of getting opportunity for new customers are very less. On the other hand, since the existing  customers are very old and continuing to buy our materials from a long period, management does  not interested to lose the relationship with existing customers.

As a Finance team, we took it as an opportunity and we started to think as an entrepreneur to  maximize the profits and also to free up the storage facility in order to avoid storage handling  charges, interacted with other departments and understand the issues and customer sentiments.  After having couple of workshops with cross functional teams and after brainstorming sessions, we  decided to change the scrape sales process from traditional method to auction method where each  customer needs to participate in auction and submit their biddings. text:
Reflection on Design Thinking

David Perez

June 7, 2020

The challenge:  In order to persuade prospects for a warehouse membership purchase, Sam’s Club uses  various incentives.  The company has found that many consumers will move from the consideration  state to the purchase state faster if incentives are offered.  While the purchase price would remain the  same at $45, additional incentives after purchase help hundreds of thousands of households annually  commit to an annual membership.  However, no incentives have universal appeal.  Equally important is  the fact that warehouse clubs sell products at a price that covers the overhead of club operations;  organizational profits are derived from membership fees.  Costly incentives essentially defer any  membership income to year two members up on renewal.  The challenge is to develop incentive  programs with a lower cost and in a new manner that do not require half a year to get measurements  on effectiveness.

The tool I have implemented is Learning Launch.  It’s important to note that this is not a hypothetical or  theoretical test.  An actual learning launch was launched a few weeks ago.  This tool was chosen  because it is an approach our team has not tried before.  In the past, we have executed large-scale  national campaigns making assumptions provided from our team.  The appeal is in the concept of “not  knowing what we don’t know.”

Instead of a large, national, multi-million dollar ad campaign, we have identified a test market and a  random audience and just launched a new program for the sake of learning.  We are testing five vastly  different offers with two different messaging themes.  For application, since we don’t know what would  be most appealing, we are pushing a variety of incentives and campaigns and starting off by giving each  of them equal funding in the test market.

Design Innovation with Rubric Evolution on Mind

Mapping Ideology

Assignment Type: Mind Maps     What is it   Mind mapping is a creative and logical means of note-taking that "maps out" your ideas in free-form. They  are non-linear representations of how you connect ideas and concepts. They are useful for creative thinking  and brainstorming. All mind maps have some things in common. They have a natural organizational  structure that radiates from the center and use lines, symbols, words, color and images according to simple,  brain-friendly concepts. Mind mapping converts a long list of information into a colorful, memorable and  highly organized diagram that works in line with your brain's natural way of doing things. The illustrate  associations between ideas or topics that radiate from a central theme, topic, or concept.     Why use it   Mind mapping assignments can increase student’s achievement and knowledge retention because students  are constructing knowledge. Mind maps help students learn information by forcing them to organize  information and allow them creativity by the addition of color and images. These types of maps have been  shown to lower extrinsic cognitive load because students are creating a two-dimensional space to tie ideas  and concepts together. They allow students to create visual images to make information more meaningful  and allow for deep learning to occur.     How to use it

  Mind maps can be used for a variety of purposes including:

  Note taking

  Brainstorming (individually or in groups)

  Problem solving

  Studying and memorization

  Planning

  Researching and consolidating information from multiple sources

  Presenting information

  Gaining insight on complex subjects

  Jogging your creativity

Mind Mapping

Challenge and Selection:

My challenge was to develop a new IT solution for my organization, the solution  aim to aggregate all scattered services and combined them in one solution and  simplify the underlying processes of these services. I and my team decided to  use mind mapping as a tool to due to its capability in discovering common  pattern and organizing the information which will be easier to be visualized and  analyzed, using the mind mapping as tool will help us to identify all possible  services that can be added to the system and the one that need to be grouped  in on service to optimize the solution and to deliver the best service and user  experience to our customers.

Application:

First, we started by collecting the required data about the current services to  identify the current situation through holding several meetings with our  stakeholders within the organization to identify what services they are providing  and underlying process for these services and document all information.

After collecting massive amount of data, I met with my team and started  consolidating and analyzing the all the information, throughout the analysis we  used a white board and engaging team discussion to cluster and categorize the  services based on the identified common patterns and characteristics between  those service.

After categorizing the services, we evaluated each group of services then we  eliminated the duplicated services, merged depended services and  brainstormed new enhanced based on the discovered opportunities during the  stakeholders’ interview that will lead us to provide the high-quality services with  simple and easy steps and achieve the maximum customer satisfaction.

By applying the Mind Mapping tool, I and my team discovered many  opportunities to increase our customer satisfaction and provide better services.

text:
Story Telling

Challenge & Selection  Story telling tool served my purpose, gave me insights about my customers which gave me a  clearer picture of the problem and was more confident with the proposed solutions. I loved using  this method as it gave me the feeling that I’m not only solving a problem but I’m creating a cause.  My selection was based on a problem that everyone almost experience, which is the scarcity of  healthy affordable food.     Application  The application started with stating the main issues people are not happy with their life style,  they’re depressed, they’re fatigued most of the time, they’re unhappy with their body shape, and  lots of the effects that’s caused by unhealthy processed food. The main issue was people don’t  have time to prepare their food so they go to the available alternative: junk fast food which is  the main cause of all the mentioned problems, as they don’t eat healthy, they’ll have malnutrition  and that causes fatigue, depression, anxiety which highly effect their mood and even when they  have the time, they don’t have the energy to prepare their food. We started by interviewing  multiple people asking them about their preference and the story behind their lifestyle, made  some recommendations and suggestions.     We started ideating and we came up with multiple solutions: meal prepping agency, healthy grab  and go, healthy vending machines, and many more. The options were communicated back with  the customers to get their feedback and from their stories and their emotions, we’ve realized  that they don’t just want healthy, they want homemade hearty healthy food, so we started  fetching up more ideas, getting elders inputs as well, recipe creators and we came up with the  best idea, food agency that works on getting grandmas recipes with a twist to make it healthy as  well as making it affordable, easy to grab and hearty, customers were happy with the solution. MOOC DESIGN THINKING /REFLECTION : LEARNING LAUNCH

With my team of five experienced travel  consultants, we design tailor-made tours to unusual destinations for our clients. Our tours are not packaged or  « ready-made », each tour is individually crafted to suit our clients’ needs.   Over the years, the competition between tailor-made tour operators has increased greatly and travellers have  increasingly played with this competition to get the best prices. At the same time, they have get used to booking  online simple services like one night accommodation or plane tickets and they now turn to tour operators like us for  more and more complex services (like tours implying multiple service providers not available online), requiring more  and more time from us to build. Traditionally, making an enquiry for a quote and a detailed itinerary to a travel  specialist has always been free for the customer. The result is that clients copy paste their enquiry to many travel  companies, looking for the best prices and the best attention to their request. On our company side, as a result, we  now transform only 10% of the enquiries into bookings ( versus 20% 3 years ago). We thus had to increase our prices  and reduce the time devoted to each enquiry, going on the opposite directions of the clients’ needs. text:
Learning Launch - Automotive Center of Excellence

Challenge

I am the current president of the Automotive Center of Excellence research organization, which has more than 100  members grouped in 5 research teams in the field of industrial engineering. This student  organization has various activities such as training in the field of research, general meetings, talks,  lectures among others with the aim of consolidating the technical and soft skills of its members  and of the students of the Industrial Engineering career in general.

One of the biggest problems caused by virtual work given the context of COVID-19 is the high rate  of inactive members, more than 30% of the members are participating minimally in the activities  of the organization, specifically, in general meetings, so it is necessary to act in the face of this  challenge.

In order to face this problem, there will be the support of the Human Resources area and the  coordinators of the different research teams, since they are in charge of holding the general  meetings.

Selection

The human resources team and coordinators have already been trained in the Desing Thinking  methodology. Likewise, its first three stages ("What is", "What if", "What wows") have already  been carried out, resulting in two prototypes that are to be applied in the final stage ("What  works"). For this, the “Learning Launch” tool will be used, since it will help to carry out the  experimentation and subsequent validation of the possible solutions.

Application

For our first learning launch, the team will focus on the structure of the general meetings. To this  end, a change was made in the order of the activities of the general meetings and a set of topics  was included that were the ones that were most accepted in the surveys carried out. text:
Example Reflection – Story Telling

Challenge & Selection

I am connected with the Banking Industry specifically Housing Loans Department. We know that not all  individuals are financially literate and familiar with the bank terms and processes.  To be assigned In  Housing Loans Department you must be able to fully explain properly all the processes and terms to  your client. We offer different types of Housing Loan Products thus one must be knowledgeable with all  of it to be able to fully explain it your clients. Some of our clients don’t have any background or  knowledge in terms of Housing Loan Application thus we have to explain to them in the most detailed  way while preventing the use of jargon words that they might not understand. We often use to define  the meanings of these words along the way of our discussion to fully explain to them the whole process.

In line with my industry and expertise, story telling is an effective tool to use. To be able to run down the  process of Housing Loan Application to our clients

Application

I start by making sure that a proper KYC is done to the clients to be able to package which product and  requirements we can provide to them. Second step will be able to discuss the needed requirements of  the client and the reason why we are requiring them. Third step will be explaining the monthly  amortization and bank charges that is included in their Housing Loan Application. Fourth is to run down  the process from birth to death of the account.

Insight & Approach

I learned about the different types of design thinking tools that we can use in our work place or even in  our daily lives. We are different individuals with different ways of learning. One must be able to identify  which proper tool to use for a specific type of individual or industry to able to properly convey your  message.

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge

I am a member of a service team for students at a university, currently offering us services such as  cafeteria, parking, transportation, courses, workshops etc .; One of these services requires a lot of  effort and coordination is the delivery of the parking license. The process is slow and uses very  outdated processes, we analyzed everything that was wrong and what we needed to improve and  update.

Selection

We found that we needed to make 1 minute and not 5 minute parking card delivery processes, we  also realized that we needed a more optimized process, something that is less manual practices, as  an example we can mention that the entire user registration process We did it manually, that is,  everything was written by hand with pen and paper and not digitally, so we also considered this as  something that we had to implement.

Application

For our learning lunch we focused on attention times, our first step was to take the database of  students who would request a parking license and we sent a form to their university email where  we asked them to register all their information, with This, we would be able to have the information  of all of them digitally and we hoped that when they went to the service window they would only  collect their parking license and thus reduce at least 3 minutes to the time of the process.

The delivery of the parking cards flowed correctly, according to what we had thought even better,  our times were from 30 seconds to 60 seconds, what we did discover is that now we had to focus  on logistics, on how to avoid confusion, crowds, and that the delivery is less confusing for the  students.

Insight

Our goal is to have a process without a parking license, we want to achieve a totally digital process  that students can enter the parking lot with their cell phone with an App, we are currently working  on the development of the App and we hope to start in August

Challenge and selection:

One of the most powerful tools in the design thinking process is the Visualization tool

because it allows us to think in a non verb way and materialize our ideas and feedback

through symbols, colors, drawings, photos and so on. It’s a core component of the way we

communicate, capture and share information with the stakeholders relevant to our project. I

used this tool in the development of new entrepreneurship. In the “what” stage we identify

the main problem in most small and medium companies in Lima, Peru which was a low

efficiency of the storage capacity of this companies. Most of them, spent lots of money in

storage and couldn’t manage it properly. In 4 small focus groups, we applied this tool to

gather together all sorts of information and insights of our stakeholders to satisfy their

needs, materialized our concept better and start the process of building a prototype and

scale of our service.

Application:

In a meeting with our potential customers, we divided them into 5 groups of 4. Each group

shared a common characteristic according to the industry they were in, for example,

technological devices, clothes, etc. We created a straw man and gave them to each group.

Each group had a white board where they put the drawing and with material we gave them

they started to visualize and materialize our concept. Our main goal was to enrich us of

information and insights to have a more solid concept and to improve the quality of the

service that we were offering which was to be an ally to those companies and managers of

supply chain and storage documents and information related to their industry. We decided to

Design Thinking for Innovation

Reflection

Final Assignment: Visualization

Challenge and Selection:

I am currently pursuing my final year in BBA. So, we had a lot of group projects in these two years. The  most challenging one that I faced was ‘design thinking project’. In that as a group our job was to find a  solution for a faulty product (in design) that we could see in our day to day life. We did find one design  and it is ‘shoe rack’. Being a hosteller, my room had a lot of spaces and we didn’t have a shoe rack itself.  So, my group just decided to take this as a product that we could design it and show to our professor  and colleagues.

As a group we were discussing how to confront this idea and show to my peers. Well, there we got an  idea to use one of the design tools which is ‘visualization’. We took this because only by showing our  idea into model or more like prototype will give best reviews.

Application:

We applied this visualization technique by creating a prototype for a shoe rack which saves the  maximum space in a hostel room. We made this prototype using cardboard and used paints to decorate  for good appearance. We used a good technique called ‘SMART’ (Specific Measurable Achievable  Relevant Time bound) goal to achieve this project successfully.  Using visualization, as a design thinking  tool was extremely effective for me.

After finishing the prototype, me and my team was ready to answer all questions from our guests while  presenting our product design. The reason behind being effective was I received few feedbacks from my  guest as well as fellow peers which eventually helped me in a better manner. We quite did a mind  mapping also to generate innovative ideas while making the prototype.

Smartphone Selling Method – Learning launch    Challenge & Selection   The first tool I used was the tool of learning launch, to achieve deep understanding of a selling method of  smartphone for a gsm company. I use this approach by choosing potential customers which may have the interest  to buy smartphone. I have used the technique of letting people to use phones as their own cell phone inside the  shop in order to show how smartphones can help them in their life (social, work, ..).    Application   Firstly, I have changed the structure of smartphone selling points in their shops. This allows customers to go and  try any smartphone they want, they also have the chance to use them as their phone, therefore they have the  opportunity to make a video call to their child in different country, manage their bank account, play  games…Basically they have the chance to understand how they use smartphone as a part of their life and how  smartphones makes their life much more meaningful.  For the experience, I will divide the customers into groups of 2-3 participants, each group has one selling  specialist which helps them to use smartphones for any of their needs. At the end of the day, I will put them in a  short practical quiz about their smartphone, this allows them to have a deeper understand for the phone. In  addition to that, I will marked the quiz and gave them discounts by depending on their success. For instance, 5/5  means %100 success in the quiz which means 25% discount on the smartphone they prefer. Discounts only valid  the day which they have experienced the smartphones.

1- Know your customer

In order to understand the factors affecting consumer choice of mobile phones.

2- Make them try

In order to show how a phone could improve a consumer's lifestyle.

Challenge

Indus Towers Limited is a clothing brand and we face a huge loss during the pandemic because of the lockdown

the brand revenue decreased our challenge is to improve our sales and find alternative ways to

sell our product. Improving the marketing & sales teams in our organization and prepared them

for the change the organization will go through. Improve the workflow within the marketing &

sales department in order to increase sales in the online channel and to spend marketing

budgets on the right campaigns. The project is limited to internal resources such as budget and

employee time. IT department got short of time they have to deliver the project as soon as

possible.

Selection

Our team has gone through several design thinking tools, and they decide to go with the

learning launch tool as they saw it as the perfect tool for the project. in general, the learning

launch is an experiment meant to quickly test an idea and prototype.

Application

For our first learning launch, we focused on designing and establishing our website and run

several tests to make sure the website fit to launch. Our team run a demo to a group of

stakeholders and took their feedback on the website to know what needs to change before the

launch. This tested our assumption that the structure and execution were the main causes of

our workflow challenge.

For our second learning launch, we focused on training our staff on the changes and include

them to be part of the process.  Also, we focused on gaining clarity about our tasks and

priorities. This tested our assumption that our prioritization of tasks was the main cause of our

workflow challenge.

test these assumptions. This tool clearly helps both of our team and the stakeholders would be

fairly open to the new prioritization of tasks and processes. Testing our assumptions offers as

text:
Reflection- storytelling

The tool I choose is storytelling to achieve a good understanding between team members and create  good moral values in the group. I use this approach because it is easier and more efficient was to convey  the message. It also makes the topic interesting and points out the importance of the discussion.  Storytelling can often be used in convincing the client and making them understand the concept better. I  have used this method to introduce new ideas and deliver a moral value. This process has helped me  build a good relationship with my team members.

Application, Insight and Approach

I start the storytelling process when my team and I are contradicting over a point or struck without a  conclusion. I would always consider making it easier for my group meets to understand, so this process  has helped me convey the message that I want to my members.

It is a simple process; all it takes is to come with a new story to deliver the message of the discussion  and make it easier for them to understand. For this process, I will take a small story to make the  conversation effective and active. Bringing up a good story that would match the discussion can make  the interaction process effective and make the learning process easier. While delivering a story, I would  always consider the points like 1. What is the need?  2. What can be beneficial output? And 3. How  effective can it be? After this process, my team meets are well aware of the topic and transparent with  their doubts, and we are finally ready to move to the next context.

text:
STORY TELLING

1. Challenge:

Storytelling is in the heart of our DNA as a human being, it helps us connect events is a  holistic experience through time. This unique nature of stories makes it one of the  essential tools during the design process of both products and services. What does  happen when asking consumers about using a product? They usually start to tell about  their experience in the form of a story. They describe the events they went through and  the lessons that they faced at each stage. As a designer, I used to find this method an  interesting one to learn about the consumer experience and then reflect it into an  outcome solution of the design process. There is nothing better than hearing about the  product from the mouth of the consumers or see then use in real life.

2. Selection:

Storytelling in the design process can be implemented using various techniques and  methods such as the following:

Digital and Visual storytelling, Scenario generation; Storyboarding; Plays; Animation;  Talk and images.

3. Application:

Problem Framing  This stage comes early in the design process. It aims to explore the problem to build an  accurate understanding of the main issue that needs to be solved. In the problem  framing stage, the storytelling can be used in this explorative initiative. It helps the  design team to engage with the user to define the problem using a qualitative data from  the consumers.    Multiple storytelling sessions can be held with the consumers who meet with the  persona characteristics. Then, the data can be collected and analysed to build a  generalised idea about the problem. The advantage of using the storytelling tool is that  it helps to create empathy with the problem as the consumers tell their stories from their  own perspective describing their pain points in the process. It helps to build a persona  empathy map about the consumers’ feelings and experience.    Solution Framing  In the solution definition and prototyping stages

REFLECTION-Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling has an important place in any activity that requires good strategies and a great

design thinking tool that we can use in many circumstances to achieve our goals.

For example, I would like to use it in the area of sales marketing, installing solar panels and promoting  renewable energy. We are therefore now witnessing an important energy transition and we are  supposed to convince and persuade a general public for the use of renewable energies, in particular  our solar panels.

And for this, advertising campaigns are organized by the company to convince people to migrate to  such a source of energy.

When we are in the field, people are open but they are afraid of change, they prefer this comfort zone  (fossil fuels) while neglecting the vast consequences on the environment and living beings in general  including man. By exchanging with them, we will be able to use their different ideas and their points  of view on the subject to adapt to the context of the subject in order to find strategies and solutions  to better convince them and persuade them to buy our products and to adopt for this transition.

Application

So, I'm going to use storytelling, which is a very powerful design thinking tool and the most

suitable in our case. A tool that can make everything enjoyable, make the subject or theme interesting  by touching the sensitivity of our interlocutors. Storytelling turns bland content into sparkling,  sparkling content that stands out. In our case, we will try to show them the disadvantages of energy  fuels.

Have you ever felt it? This feeling of frustration over the resurgence in the number of cases of covid19  preventing certain activities and the number of deaths caused by this disease. information (attention to claims, etc.), resolution of doubts, customer service in general,

objective would be to establish a mechanism that allows all people to be assisted in the

shortest time possible and those who have to wait, do not do so for a long time. Likewise,

identify the periods in which the quantity of people requesting attention is minimal or null

and it becomes necessary to consider changing the number of agents attending.

because there are a series of interactions between the people who need to be cared for

administrative procedures, but in most cases personal criteria must be used to resolve

raises the level of uncertainty because the time that each person will need to resolve their

not usually constant and can vary constantly not only in the same day, but in entire weeks

or by days (morning or afternoon). The information available is mainly related to the days

when there is the highest traffic of requests and peak hours.

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a very useful tool that can be used especially during studies to animate the students.  I'm studying digital economics at a university in Germany. Many term papers and exams are an  important part of our curriculum and as a result our lecturers have to read through and evaluate  dozens of different texts from over two hundred students. There is not much tension. Even for the  students, it is usually very tedious and boring to write, for example, thirty pages about the history of  the design of digital assistance systems. Interest in studying is waning. That shouldn't be the case,  because after all, the course is there to develop interest in the various modules. The course is the  basis for our future profession. If you associate something boring like housework with this subject at  the beginning, you quickly lose patience and interest. Storytelling helps, for example, to make a  lecture exciting. A professor who himself makes the subject of mathematical fundamentals of  business administration interesting with lots of stories and background knowledge will get far more  attention from his students than a professor who boredly writes some formulas on the blackboard.  This has a positive influence on both sides: The students enjoy learning the content and get more  specialist knowledge and good grades and the professor can distribute his knowledge to many  interested people
