Ahmed Elnemr // Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

I am founder and president of an art and culture association in Milan, Italy. Since its foundation, this association has  had the goal to engage foreign students and expats living in Milan and the Italian society in a dialogue through cultural  events. For this purpose, we design and produce numerous cultural events (mostly concerts) during a year and this  requires a comprehensive knowledge of the audience. Initially, to understand better our market, we relied on  traditional market research methods. Thus, we sent out surveys to define our target audience’s taste and preferences.  However, the results were not satisfying. Non-Italian respondents were interested in cultural events that would not  attract the Italian audience, therefore, they could not result in the desired interaction between these two  communities.

Moreover, we wanted our cultural events to be of high quality and have a positive impact on the cultural taste  of our  foreign community. Cultural events which precisely matched this community’s taste could not result in their cultural  growth, and thus did not satisfy us as cultural activists. Our confusion and lack of experience resulted in a dramatic  failure of our first project. We organized a high-quality jazz event in one of the best music halls in the city. This event  cost us a lot of money and energy, but, unfortunately, our ticket sales were not even close to satisfying and the  expected interaction between foreigners and Italians, of course did not happen. Following this defeat, we decided to  take a different path and try a new approach.

Selection

After an extensive discussion in the association, we decided to try the Learning Launch or the experimentation  approach. We decided to follow the suggestion of Dennis Lehmann that he made in his lecture: “The key is to do experiments  that are fast and cheap”.

Reflection - Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection:

As a board member of a non-profit student consultancy firm I was confronted with a strategic positioning  challenge. Historically, our organization linked students of the local University, who were eager to exhibit  their recently gained academic and theoretical knowledge into practice at local small and medium  enterprises (our clients) on a project base. The challenge was triggered since our key stakeholder/ partner,  the local University, decided to organize consultancy projects themselves instead of outsourcing this to a  semi-independent student entrepreneur organization. Since we were a spin-off of the local University our  very own existence was at stake unless we were able to reinvent our proposition. The only question was  ‘how’? We’ve always assumed that the main driver to do business with us for local small and medium  enterprises and the students themselves, was the fact that we were affiliated with the University. This  way the project scope included the strategic positioning of our non-profit student consultancy firm with  limited resources based on the added value to the several different stakeholders including a high urgency.  The goal was to unravel the intrinsic motivation of our current clients and students to do business with us  in order to reposition ourselves into the market and outsmart the new competition provided by the local  university (former key stakeholder). We expected to cluster the different stakeholders based upon their  motivation to do business with us.

Our challenge was to understand the current reality/ ‘as is’ of our organization by collecting high

amounts of data from several stakeholders and to look for patterns, insights etc. in order to develop  design criteria for the ‘what if’ of our organization. There were several hypothesis concerning the specific customer needs we had to validate  and there were several doubts concerning the pricing (what these specific customers would  be willing to pay) and different customer segments.   We wanted to test a beverage subscription service that “learns” over time from consumption  preferences, habits and favorite ingredients. The concrete customer need we identified is the  logistical nightmare of shopping beverages and serving all different needs within the family  (taste and nutrition and occasions).

Selection   Based on the huge number of different hypothesis we decided to run small experiments  based on the learning launch method.

1. Idea

2. Specific customer.

3. Specific need.

4. Solution / idea that meets the customer need.

5. Better than current alternative   = Hypothesis

Visualisation

Challenge and Selection

I selected visualisation because its an important tool for every  firms to create an image not just by drawing but by visual  thinking to think non verbally and to push ourselves beyond  words or language. Let’s see how Dove used visualisation to be  successful. They mainly targeted women and the challenge they  found among women was about their appearances. Its true now  a days Women don’t have confidence about their looks they hide  their flaws through make up. They feel that their ugly in their  own natural way or afraid that society would judge their looks  however Dove helps and proves the women wrong let’s see how.

Like in the video of The Good kitchen story mentioned in the  lectures  where employees were embarrassed about their jobs  but Hatch and Bloom just changed they way they think about   themselves by making them think they are chefs working in  restaurant and customers are the senior citizens just changed  the whole scenario.

Application

Well they used this tool by creating a video which focused   on women asking  them about how they feel about

themselves in which many answered they lack confidence  in their  looks they are not  able to embrace their flaws  and they feel incomplete without makeup. It was all  about self doubt and self critics. So the team brought in a  forensic artist  to draw  two portraits of women to  compare a women’s self perception by visually drawing   to that of how others saw her. The results were  surprisingly amazing. The portrait drawn in the   perception of a stranger seemed attractive when  comparing to the self perception one. Which in turn  clearly defines that  women are bombarded by  unattainable standards of beauty via magazines and  television in which they compare themselves to that of  others and undervalues themselves. Thereafter I met department  representatives from each of the above mentioned departments to gain their perspective on challenges  they faced in the existing process. The updated version of the process was shared with the all the  stakeholders highlighting the areas that were changed. Example Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge & Selection

I’ve not done any dessign thinking before the training but I think me and my team could use it in a  near future regarding the new software we are working on. The challenge would be to get a  feedback on how the customers experience it.

In my company, the first version of this software is already used by customers and the feedback is  good. This second version runs as a service in the cloud whereas the first one is delivered on  physical servers. So the philosophy and the way to use the new software are very different so we  need to know if it suits the customers needs.

For that, we could use the learning launch tool which will allow to conduct a small and quick test of  the new software with key customers. The data will get from the learning launch tool will make us  feel if the customers embrace the new software.

Application

As the new software is running as a service in the cloud, we would just have to give an access to  the User Interface to the customers participating to the test.

The choice of customers is very important : the idea would be to get the feedback of 5 customers  already using the first version of the software and to ask them to use the new one to do the same  tasks as the first one. These 5 customers should have several profiles to ensure that the data we’ll  get will represent the targeted customer: 2 should be part of the biggest clients of the company, 2  should be new ones and 1 should be one of the tough customers using the software.

To get a good quality of feedback, the customers should be able to test the new software for two  weeks. And by the end of these 2 weeks, a meeting should be organized with the customers and  the following questions should be ask to them : 1) does the new cloud base architecture of the  software answer some of their needs? 2) what is a real plus in the new software? 3)what is missing  in the new software?. The tool that I used is Visualization. At first I thought it was about drawing. But the truth is,

PowerPoint display, photography, and video are all examples of this. Basically, it's something

that brings us beyond the use of vocabulary or phrases.

Application

I started using this instrument in a very basic way, imagining very simplistic objects like

geometric figures. As the author mentions that the more you use images, the more you will

start to make diagrams when you speak to give people a graphic representation of what you

are saying. The more inclined you are to initiate a dialogue with others, the more likely you

are to arrive at a sense of understanding and consensus. I think all of these strategies

helped me to be much more efficient.

What I have learned from doing this exercise especially with my teammates is that what we

struggle most with is being able to understand the ideas of others, which is why it is

important that everyone has the same knowledge. It is important to me that everyone on my

team will practice this tool so that we can communicate in a better way.

Reflection – Mind Mapping

1. Challenge

While working recently at a student association, I gained exposure to large scale sales  processes for a wide range of different stakeholders. We were in contact with customer  groups with various needs and thus required carefully targeted messaging in order to convert  leads into long-term buyers. Due to the nature of tenures within student associations, with  significant turnover every year, it was difficult to build and sustain deep customer knowledge  and insights.

2. Selection

I believe that mind mapping as presented in week 3 of this course could constitute an efficient  way to generate customer insights and to observe changing trends with each new student  cohort. The goal here would be to gather existing customer data, market intelligence and  learning of previous year by the management team and introduce the results in a visual  format to new team members as well as representatives of each customer group.

3. Application

The first step would consist of data collection. This would include a combination of data from  our proprietary data sources as well as new data collection initiatives. Regarding the former,  insights could be derived from CRM data, previous customer surveys and prior focus groups  with relevant stakeholders. Regarding the latter, new initiatives should be centred around  identifying and substantiating blind spots in the existing research. It could also be an  opportunity to generate new data points through more creative research methods such as  dedicated workshops or events.    Secondly, this data needs to be condensed and synthesized into digestible and visually  appealing presentations. It is important to combine different media in order to allow for a  wide range of complexity in the representations presented. Example Reflection – Imagine

Challenge & Selection    The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding  of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define  possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers, who are government  agencies working to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their  services to their customer, which may be U.S. citizens, businesses, and non-citizens. I have used the  technique of using a straw man visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for  discussion to allow a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining  the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying  pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.    Application    I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw man  graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing  material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, GAO or  other auditing reports. If materials are not available, then I conduct informal interviews with one-three  of the stakeholders who serve as my main points of contact on the initiative.    If appropriate to the situation, I will borrow the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from previous  research, and discussed in David Gray’s book, “The Connected Company”. The front-stage/back-stage  approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service – even an internal service – has customers  with whom the service provider interacts and internal processes that enable the organization to provide  the service. Coursera : Design thinking

Assignement :   Mind Mapping     Challenge:     After finishing my freshman year in an international business school, I now have three

months of free time in front of me that I would like to put in use. My challenge is to find a  business idea, to model it, and present it to one of my family members in order to possibly  create a family business. Another dilemma I am facing is in which country I would like to start  a business as well as the Covid situation. I could possibly incorporate my business in Belgium  (where my family lives) or in Spain (where I study), I did a SWOT and PESTLE analysis in order  to get better insights of the markets. Finally, it represents a challenge at a personal level, I  want to know how self-disciplined I am and how I could put in use the knowledge I have  acquired this year.     Selection:

The tool I have chosen to use is a Mind Map, it forms a part of the “What is? “process

and helps communicates the insights, data and information gathered during this phase.  It  helps distinguish patterns and links between key elements and its goal is to establish criteria  for the “What is? “idea generation phase. It represents a pivotal point in the design thinking  process. I’ve chosen this tool because in order to help me organised all the data I have  collected from the Spanish and Belgian markets as well as customer behavior and entry  barriers. Furthermore, it a great way to presents my idea to my family member in order to  communicate my vision in the clearest way possible.     Application:

I have used the tool by sequencing key elements such as Belgium, Spain, Ideas,

Differentiation, Customers and Barriers. I linked all of them and distinguish which part were  missing bits of information’s and where I was well informed. It helped me to distinguish  certain links that I couldn’t establish before and putting my ideas down helped me get better  at explaining them in a logical and clear flow.      Insight:

text:
Using the Learning Launch in the production of “chorizos”

Challenge:

“AJ” is a family business dedicated to the production of artisanal “chorizo”, which is a kind of sausage  traditional in Colombia, in this particular case made with pork. The product is characterized by its  excellent quality and delicious flavor, fundamental factors for customers. The company wants to start  producing and selling other products in order to expand its portfolio and be able to cover other  markets.

Selection:

For this purpose, the design tool select is the Learning Launch, which consist in make small  experiments that test the new idea or ideas in the real marketplace. I selected this tool because  I think is the perfect one to analyze the impact that a product could have on the market and get  different opinions of costumers. All this data will provide a lot of useful information to improve the  products and reach alternatives that are preferred by customers.

Application:

In the search of ideas of new products, it was evaluated the idea of a “chorizo” made from  chicken, that is very common and could be easy because we already had the equipment and  knowledge to produce this kind of sausage. So, we started to search different recipes to have  an idea and started to create our recipe with the different ingredients, trying not to be such a  greasy product. Then, the chicken sausages were prepared.

The Learning Launch was used when we had the product, because we gave some test of this to  different people, mainly relatives, in order to have some first opinions for improvements and in a  near future, we can do another Learning Launch with some of the costumers of the product.

In this occasion, the tool was applied effectively and since the product is food, it was easy to  make the tests and get some useful information for the next steps of the plan, where the tool will  be more effective because will be use in the real marketplace.

Mind Mapping (Module 3)       Challenge & Selection     The first tool I used was the tool of mind mapping. To understand a problem  and find the ways of  storing vegetables in different methods. This was done to explore, identify and redefine the problem  areas and its solutions. Mind Maps really come into their own when it comes to encouraging  creativity and enabling to generate new ideas in brainstorming sessions. The spatial layout of a Mind  Map helps gain a better overview, making new connections more visible so it can create an infinite  number of thoughts, ideas, links, and associations on any topic. Mind mapping has been used here  to map out all the ideas related to cold storage. This was done so that I can find many possible  solution to it.

Applications

I started the process by putting the main topic of discussion in the centre of the paper. As the  discussions with many stakeholders started to initiate, we started to add elements to the mind map.  This helped us to keep tract on the ideas, which has been discussed. If the ideas repeated, we gave  them priority. The application was to make a cold storage, which can be portable and cost effective.  We started discussion of different ways that can be possible of making a cold storage. Then we  started adding connections, which were not very apparent at the start, but started to revel itself  once the mind map has been create.

Insight & Approach     I learned a lot from conducting this activity with several stakeholders including our team. And what I  understand using mind maps for brainstorming is, It helps easily retrieve information from our  memory, gets our thoughts flowing freely so we can come up with new ideas, Identify connections  between individual ideas, helps to see the bigger picture. Challenge

I am working on a project aiming to specifically reduce the time and discomfort associated with  grocery shopping. Essentially to create a better user experience during the regular shopping trip.  This challenge targets the most uncomfortable of customers- the elderly. Lifting heavy objects such a  milk, eliminates the option of a hand-held basket. The alternative, a traditional shopping trolley can  solve the issue of weight. However, it is only a borrowed item and all products placed into the trolley  must be removed and placed into another vessel (car boot or backpack) to return home. A  significant portion of the elderly customers observed, relied on public transport to and from the  supermarket. A ‘Shopping Jeep’ or ‘Nanna Trolley’ is the most sought-after solution for this  demographic.

Selection

The tool of Visualisation has been selected for this early stage in the problem-solving process. This is  as we are still at a point of defining ‘What Is’ the problem and how we visually identify the  surrounding repercussions of the average shopping trip for the elderly before they are addressed.  The Visualisation Tool also aides in working with human centred design, particularly through  identifying points of strain on the human body (effect) and visually linking them to the cause of pain  eg. Too much weight being carried from the checkout to the car boot without a trolley.

Application

The first test was to examine the current practices with the Shopping Jeep. I took this to a grocery  store and documented the entire experience door to door with a photographer and videographer  following me. During the experience I had noticed back and neck strain when lowering objects into  the shopping jeep. The second, most notable flaw in the process was the self-checkout. More  bending had to occur to remove everything and return them after scanning.

1. Challenge: There are many challenges which one can face as a teacher. The basic job of a

teacher is to teach the young minds and inspire them, and this job is best done when the first  student from your class to the last student is benefited from what you teach. Even if one  student is left out the task a teacher is assigned to do is not accomplished. This challenge  came to me when I had 2 students in my class who were differently able. These 2 students  were a part of inclusive education program of my college and they both were sponsored by a  big financial company, as a part of their CSR activity. Now let me tell you about the  background of these 2 students. One was visually impaired up to 98% and the other was  suffering from cerebral Palsy and could not walk and always needed a wheel chair. Both the  students came from a poor economic background and were the first ones in their family to go  to such a reputed expensive college. The challenge I faced was that both of them were not  accepted well in the class. I observed that both are sitting in the first bench alone and no one  is talking to them. These 2 students were also scared as they were from a regional language  background and English was not their forte. The other regular students came from effluent  families and were impeccably dressed just like their English, no one bothered to talk to these  2 differently abled students, forget about helping them in their studies. I as a teacher was  deeply troubled as I felt that not intelligent students but the weaker section of students need  a teacher more. Another challenge was that in future more such students will be joining and  so the college students should accept and understand inclusive education. My college had a  tie up with this financial giant and there were more students with special abilities expected in  the coming years. Storytelling  The Me & You Way  Challenge

I work in oil & gas organization at a plant site level and my organization has a vertical hierarchy at  work level. Hierarchy, in most businesses is explained using a two-dimensional pyramid drawn on a  board but  we fail to realize that  work level hierarchy is not just a pyramid drawn on a board or on a  piece of paper but it is a pyramid made up of people holding hands together at all levels. Now, what  will happen if people leave each other’s hands, The People Pyramid will fall? Hence, it is very  important for all levels to work together, have empathy and a sense of ownership. To achieve this  sense of togetherness, ownership it is very important to keep everyone motivated else the system  can’t work. Every person has a different mindset and it is an extremely difficult task to motivate  people such that they keep holding hands and the pyramid of people does not fall.     Selection

Storytelling is an important tool that can work wonders as it brings compassion, emotional  connection, empathy, and motivates people. Storytelling says it's not about the list of things we have  to do; it's about the connection that we give to people about a piece of information. Keeping and  making people work together is very difficult but “A cause” is something that ignites people, and  unites people and that is what good storytelling does, is it creates a cause. When people are told a  story they try to find themselves in that story and if a story is good one, people will find themselves  in the story and it is only then they will get the essence of the story.    Application

People under me in the vertical organizational level used to avoid doing jobs on plant site. What I  felt that in some way or the other they avoided me and critical jobs by making excuses. Challenge

As a Project Leader in an international IT organization, I design, implement and deploy IT applications  for clients in financial control in the aim of helping them in their decision-making.

The applications we develop are based on an innovating cloud-based solution. Our projects consist in  building specific applications to our customers needs, from a common platform (e.g. of application:  Financial planning, People planning, profitability modeling,…).

Selection

The Learning Launch consists in a prototype to test key customer, execution and defensibility  assumptions. It involves quickly engaging with customers.

I selected the Learning Launch tool because it is very useful for expose part of a development in real  usage conditions and with the presence of stakeholders (including future users). This tool is part of  an iterative development process which allows us to correct and enhance the prototype while the  project is running.

Application

The projects I lead are based on Agile method. With such a method, the first phase consists in  identifying project community, gathering client needs, define objectives and critical success factors.  Then, the project is sliced into lots called “Tracks”. Each Track can be seen as in an iterative and  incremental sub-process with a strong involving of stakeholders which allows a high reactivity.

In our project management, the Learning Launch is used as the final step of a Track. Indeed, a live  demonstration is organized in the real usage conditions with all the stakeholders. Customers and  users are invited to react and interact. It allows my project team to consider all the remarks,  regarding the displaying, ergonomics, workflows,…

The remarks are included as optimizations and enhancements in the following Tracks. At the end,  when the application is deployed, our developments are already optimized and experienced taking  the stakeholders remarks into account.

Challenge    When I entered a new company, I had received the great challenge of optimizing the entire commercial policy  of the company and increasing profitability with this within 2 years and, together with my welcome kit, for  that to happen , I had to approach all areas of the business and understand the flows of each one of them so  that, throughout the project, I had the participation and cooperation of all those involved so that the final  result was as satisfactory as possible. For this task completion, I have chosen the Storytelling tool in order to  put all the resources / people (and their experiences) involved in this process front and center.    Selection    For this challenge I chose the Storytelling tool because, in view of my recent entry into the company, I needed  something that would really unite and engage people in this cause that was not just mine, but a mission for  the entire company that was under my responsibility to ensure the perfect execution and achievement of  results and, for this purpose, this tool would fit very well, after all, it would be much more direct and  convincing to create a cause to unite everyone throughout the company's history (from AS x TO BE) in Power  Point with an excellent plot than any other conventional way.    Application    In order to guarantee the success of the commercial policy review project and increase the company's profit  margin (main objective) with the use of Storytelling, I used a lot of the methodology seen in this course. As a  new entrant to the organization, my first steps were to get as close as possible to all areas of the company  during the first 4 months to deeply understand their background, the company and its areas. Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

I am a member of my organization’s commercial financial department and my/our challenge is  to improve

the workflow (activities and projects) within the department in order to increase the retention  of stores, and renewals of a positive leasing contract (greater than the one currently practiced  in the contracts).

The project scope includes the financial department composed of six employees, as well as the  commercial department, with whom we work closely. The project is limited to internal resources  (i.e., budget and employee time).

The project should not exceed 12 business month and the solution should include and even  distribution of working hours amongst the team members. We will focus on trying to uncover  what our team members, as well as key stakeholders within the larger financial department and  commercial department, consider to be ineffective or problematic with regard to the workflow.

Selection

Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools, so we are ready to  try the learning launch tool. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment meant to  quickly test an idea and prototype.

Application

For our first learning launch, we focused on the structure/execution of the retention of stores  and negotiations there are today. In particular, we wanted to see if we could structure our tasks,  projects, and processes to adapt the methods of Scrum project management for our work (e.g.,  time boxed, daily, specific meetings, reviews, etc.) in an effort to become more agile. Classified - Confidential

Mind Mapping of CPG Categories

Challenge & Selection

I work in Marketing Insights at a large CPG manufacturer.  In the course of my work, we began asking  big, meaty, foundational questions around why consumers were really using our products and how we  might better serve them today, as well as innovate for the future.  In asking these types of questions, we  began with the exact same framework as the Design Thinking questions!  Knowing that we would need  help from consumers to answer our questions, we decided that we needed to create something like a  mind map to better understand jobs to be done for our products and why consumers were using our  product to satisfy those jobs.  Then, we wanted to understand where those most relevant jobs weren’t  satisfied currently and as our next step, design criteria and possible solutions to fulfill those consumer  jobs.

Application

We started the process by identifying existing knowledge around the jobs that consumers are trying to  get done with our products. We have multiple-market awareness and usage surveys that includes many  attributes that we could leverage.  In pulling together those attributes, we created a strawman mind  map to arrange the attributes into functional, emotional and social jobs.  We wanted to look at this  strawman to see how well this captured the complete uses of our products.    In very short order, our collective intuition was pinging.  There were a great deal of functional jobs and  even some emotional, but the social and even identity outcomes were missing.  We had more work to  do.    We conducted primary qualitative research to find the additional jobs across multiple markets globally. Reflection – Visualization

Challenge

I’m part of a process improvement team within our company to help various departments with work  flow and efficiency. Our usual approach to each task is to identify issue(s) and work out a potential  solution. Once the solution is validated and approved, we will move forward with Plan, Do, Check, Act  (PDCA) cycle for a 3 months period. Often times our biggest challenges in this approach are to find out  the root cause(s) of the issue(s) and to come up with effective corrective measures.

Take one recent task as an example: for each statutory holiday, our distribution team needs to put  together a special delivery schedule for over 6000 customers and communicate it with all relevant  parties – customers, order desk, sales representatives etc. The holiday schedule process takes a lot of  time and resources. And often times the accuracy of the information on the schedule is to be desired.  Considering how often this process is repeated during the course of the year, it’s evident that the  process needs to be revamped.

Selection

To identify what caused the inefficiency and inaccuracy of holiday schedule process, we decided to use  visualization to illustrate the current process, which in turn should lead us to problems as well as root  causes.  Other design thinking tools were also considered but passed over for following reasons:  not  enough data/information for mind mapping; no solution yet to test out using learning launch; lack of  emotional connection for storytelling given the nature of this particular challenge.

Application

We set up a half day workshop with key players from all involved departments. Together we used post-it  notes to map out each step of the current process on the wall. Once the process mapping was  completed, we started to add in pertinent details to each step: responsible person; timeline; roadblocks;  error occurrence; frequency and severity of errors etc.

Case Study: MMC - Addressing unmet needs of the Gig Economy

About Gollis University India

Gollis University India is a part of Finca Antonio SAC companies which is a global leader in risk, strategy and people. With  roots dating back to 1864, MMC today is formed of 4 large global organizations – namely Marsh, Mercer,  Guy Carpenter and Oliver Wyman. MMC is a Fortune 200 Company with presence in over 140 countries,  70,000 colleagues and annual revenue of $15 billion and growing.

Gollis University India is the knowledge center for the MMC companies with expertise in employee benefits, insurance  broking, reinsurance broking, analytics, research, consulting, financial management and information  technology. It provides services to Marsh, Mercer, Guy Carpenter and MMC through its operations services,  research, investment consulting, analytics, consulting operations, specialized accounting, fiduciary  accounting, management consulting and IT services.

Problem Statement

The world of gig economy is a fast one, allows flexibility in employment and gives opportunities to talented  part timers to work in evolving industries and segments. The "on demand" workforce, freelancers or  independent contractors  are growing in size as industries struggle with getting access to trained, full time  employees at appropriate salaries. However, gig economy workers don’t necessarily get all the benefits that  full time employees receive. The traditional mould of employee benefits is structured a certain way  irrespective of which part of the world we discuss. The lack of consistent income, less stability coupled with  lack of benefits isn’t a great proposition for new age workers who are increasingly demanding flexibility.

text: The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared  understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to  identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our  customers, who are government agencies working to apply technology innovations to  modernize their mission or the delivery of their services to their customer, which may be U.S.  citizens, businesses, and non-citizens. I have used the technique of using a straw man  visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for discussion to allow a  diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining the scope,  boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying  pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.    In discussing policy changes with a social service agency, I was trying to explain to them the  benefits of taking a more client focused approach, among other things, and in particular, of  recognizing each person as a unique being, and addressing their individual needs first and  foremost. The agency was in the grip of a “compliance culture” and its clients were failing in  this non-empathetic, rigid structure. I was also explaining how sometimes addressing the  needs of one individual can impact everyone for the better, even if it seems extreme or out of  the ordinary. I told a story about when I ran an emergency shelter after a natural disaster.  Everyone was doing really well except for one woman whose stress was making her very  emotionally volatile. I could tell she needed attention; in my mind I decided she would be  “Princess for an hour.” I made her a cup of coffee and sat down with her and let her talk. text:
Reflection - Learning Launch

1. Challenge: I work in an educational institute. As part of the institute I deal with students,

teaching and non-teaching staff. There are a number of activities that require streamlining  and innovative way of implementing to get desired results. It could be activities like  improving bonding of alumni with the students, improving scores of students in certain  government exams, poor participation of faculty or students for certain activities, improve  relation between the teaching and non-teaching staff and so on.  One such challenge we  faced was when the Institute offered two courses which are mandatory for students of  Second year and Third year to attend

i.  Intended to improve creative thinking which stretches over 3 semesters

ii.  Intended to improve research skills which stretches over 1 semester

Both these courses are an initiative by the institute to improve student’s skills. These  courses are not part of the university curriculum and hence the grades of these courses are  not mentioned in the university grade sheet. There are observations made of students  attending and submitting course work of courses that are part of university curriculum but  not for the above mentioned two courses. There is a growing trend of students not  attending the sessions conducted and disinterest in completing the course work. It was a  matter of concern because investments were made for conducting these courses in terms  of resource, time and money and the outcome expected for the courses were not observed  in the projects done by the student in the following year. So the challenge was how to  improve the participations of students in these courses.

2. Selection: Based on the problem data was collected in terms of qualitative data as well as

quantitative data. The collected data gave rise to many assumptions about the cause of the  situation and there was a need to understand if these assumptions were the real the cause  of the problem.

Learning Launch – Insurance Company

Challenge

I am the manager of the Pricing & Underwriting line of an insurance company and our challenge is  to increase Property insurance sales by improving the sales process.

The scope of the project is related to the subscription and specifically to the risk inspection process.  Inspectors, underwriters, commercial executives and clients participate in this process.

Our company works with internal inspectors and with several external suppliers to whom cases are  assigned according to business rules. Each inspector coordinates a visit with the client, where a risk  report is prepared that is subsequently reviewed by the underwriter, who decides to approve or  reject the insurance contract.

We focused on which part of the process we could improve, or which part of the process was the  most problematic. The project was accomplished with the available resources, with no additional  financing, only the time and commitment of the project team members were available. As a goal,  there was a maximum period of 30 days to implement an experiment and have conclusions to  continue advancing.

Selection

Our team has had several experiences developing innovative projects without a formal  methodology. Over time we have created our own way of doing things and we trust that “Learning  Launch” will be a very good contribution to create a simple, fast and cheap prototype that tackles  the problem in a good way.

For our first “Learning Launch” we focused on the different phases of the inspection process. We  recently had a training on the AGILE methodology that we decided to use. We defined 1 weekly  sprint, where we were able to review in detail tangible progress that helped get the experiment  going.

assistance to the insurance buyers if they suffered any complication (like heart attack) due to high

of design thinking approach were already answered – “What is” and “what if”. Following were the

like low education, poverty, stressful job, obesity amongst other

b) Apart from financial assistance, customers wanted help to overcome or control the condition

a daily basis was a key need of the customers and they would be willing to pay more if they get such

journey of switching to a healthy lifestyle. Our task was to test the prototype in the market and confirm

MIND MAPPING

CHALLENGE

The tool I used here is mind mapping to define how I made my project successful.

Our project is totally on collecting data using sensors and making them to communicate  between different systems to get the desired output. The challenge we faced is we have to  deal with lot of electronic items which are really difficult to handle 3 sensors, GSM module,  WIFI module and arduino.

Each device holds various data and each have to be programmed and checked

separately and then has to be interconnected with a single program. We used mind  mapping knowingly or unknowingly  as a tool to match the people’s knowledge, attitude  and skill for assigning people to the particular task in our project.

SELECTION

Mind mapping tool is creating meaning to the data that are collected.   It is the

ultimate stage of  “What is” and which takes to the “What if”  phase. In our project we have  clear idea on end to end process. The difficulty is to manage the work among ourselves. We  framed the concepts and processes in a structured manner virtually so that they can be  easily available. Mind mapping helped us to finish our project effectively. Here all the ideas  are linked by lines to the major and minor siblings ,thus we created meaningful content and  that could be remembered for long time.

APPLICATION

Our project is to run or shut off the electric motor based on the output from sensors.

First, the process has been sequenced from top to bottom. And also the alternate ideas  were also taken into account. We have used projective techniques to rate our ideas , where  the objective is at the centre and the various tasks that has to be performed forms the  petals of pinwheel and those tasks have been prioritized. We attempted to get the hidden  or deeper thoughts from everyone. At the same time, one of us is making note of important  and valuable thoughts. Learning Launch

Challenge

I work in a consumer product company in the logistics department and my challenge is to revamp  their existing distribution network to reduce product distribution costs. It involves monitoring the  key performance metrics for examining supply chain performance. Distribution in most of the  consumer product companies happen through roadways and thus, freight shipping companies play  an essential part in delivery. The project is expected to be finished within four weeks.

Selection

After going through multiple design thinking activities, two possible ideas came up. Learning launch  was the best design thinking tool to test those ideas and gain insights.

Application

The first learning launch focussed on negotiating with our existing customers regarding their product  ordering policy. The idea was to convince the customers to order less frequently but in higher  quantity for per unit shipment charges to go down. The team selected a sample of customers for  whom the shipping charges were higher than average. These customers were sent a trial shipment  with higher quantities so that we could get real-time data and identify the possible issues in it. This  lasted about two weeks and it tested the assumption that higher volumes will reduce the shipping  and thus distribution costs.

The other learning launch was to identify the activities in the existing distribution system, where  unnecessary time and costs were incurred. Once these non-value adding activities are identified  then making changes to the current distribution system to optimise and fine-tune it. This idea, also  known as value chain analysis took two weeks and it tested the efficiency of the supply chain  through various metrics for getting insights into the possible issues.

I’m currently a 5th-year level student right now and in order to graduate, the major  requirement is to pass the subject Design Project. Our team’s design project focuses the design of a  hydroponic system of farming. Hydroponic farming is a method of growing plants using nutrient solutions in  a water solvent instead of using soil. Because hydroponic systems have already many existing designs  according to our research, doing our prototype will be like copy-pasting of the existing designs. Hence, our  design project will not be culminating and unique in any sense. Our adviser challenged us that aside from  making our design economically cheaper than the current alternatives, we should include feature/s in the  design that will make it culminating and unique to other designs.    Selection    Our team thought of using design thinking to solve the problem. After brainstorming of different design  tools, we thought of using the Learning Launch tool as the best tool for this challenge. Learning Launch, as  what I’ve learned from the video presentations, is a design tool in a form of a small experiment that tests  the new idea in the marketplace. LEARNING LAUNCH TOOL

CHALLENGE

Agriculture is the main occupation in my country. Unfortunately, farmers here still live in

poverty conditions. This is because they lack information on where to get market for their products

and on market prices for which they must depend on exploitative middlemen who take advantage

of their ignorance. There is also a long distribution chain that dilutes their revenue. As we are

working for an online platform that links small scale farmers to buyers using mobile and web

technology. Our challenge here is to create a simple technology that can be easily accessed by

famers considering that most of the farmers live in the rural areas with little access to internet

services. The project scope includes IT personnel and the marketing team together with our key

stakeholders, where they will help us in structuring the first prototype of the technology. The

timeline for this project should run for at most 60 days, for the software development team to

create a prototype of the technology. Our marketing team will help us with the first go-to-market

research once we come up with the prototype.

SELECTION

Our team decided to go with the learning launch tool. Learning launch is a small experiment

that tests our new idea in the real marketplace quickly and inexpensively. This tool will help us to

go through an iterating process that will improve our solution. In accordance to a full new product

roll-out, a learning launch is a learning experiment conducted with low expense to gather market-

driven data to determine whether a growth idea has enough merit to warrant detailed investigation

with the commitment of further time, people and resources. Working with the prototype will help

us experiment the idea with a larger group of farmers.

Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge and Selection

For several years I worked at a small luxury hotel in Vermont. It was a castle like hotel where  people got the chance to spend the night in very elegant rooms and then go to skiing in a near  center. As I was working, I realized that people did not have breakfast at the hotel. The dining  room was beautiful, the space, the tables, the windows with trees outside, it all seemed perfect  but for some reason people did not stay and have breakfast there. The service (we thought) was  ok. Coffee, some pancakes, pastries, yogurt, cereals, fruits, eggs, all served in this huge room but  with no guests to eat or drink them. Of course, we needed to improve this service in order to  make the stay of our guests even better.

After doing this course I realized we used the learning launch tool without knowing that was its  name. We got together with the team and drafted our hypothesis: the guests do not find our  breakfast appealing and they rather have breakfast elsewhere.

Application

For our first learning launch, we focused on the price of the breakfast. We issued some discounts  and coupons for free breakfasts. We wanted to see if the fact that the room had some clients  would attract others. If you see the room empty you think the service is bad, even if you never  tried it. But if you see people having eating and chatting and having a good time, you might  consider staying and have breakfast there too. This was a very small change but we were able  to see its effect very fast. After the first week of discounts and coupons the breakfast room had  more clients than before.

For our second learning launch, we focused on the food and beverages we were offering. CHALLENGE & SELECTION

My company is facing a decline in sales and patronage due to the emergence of new startup companies,  that have disrupted the market we operate in. Now as the product designers we conducted surveys,  product insights, and some data analytics to find out whether to develop new, modify the existing, or  maintain the existing products.

I choose the Mind mapping technique in order to identify the patterns and insights in the data I  collected during the research. This is done to find which is the best idea.

APPLICATION.

Firstly, I together with my team created a gallery of the ideas and data we gathered during our research,  these ideas were divided into clusters and each is displayed on screens in various sides of the meeting  room.

The stakeholders were then invited into the meeting room and each after briefing them about our  design criteria, each was given a clipboard, sticky notes and a pen. They were then asked to move  around the room to have a look at this ideas and data, also to come up with their own perception and  insights about what they see. This lasted for 30 minutes.

Next, we asked each of them to go through their notes and to filter and group these notes in terms of  similarities in the theme and context. We gave out 10 categories on which to they can classify their  notes. This activity carried on for 10 minutes.

After arranging their ideas, to our greatest dismay all their notes centered around 4 categories out of  the 10 we provided. Design Thinking Reflection – Visualization

Challenge and Selection:

I‘m working in the IT project management team of a Consulting company that offers web based  assessment solutions to optimize recruiting processes of our clients.

The company has grown very quickly from being a start-up and just became part of an international  corporate company. New client and product development projects are getting more and more  complex due to client requirements as well as technical and legal requirements. Especially when it  comes to very technical projects that will result in infrastructural development of our IT solutions the  IT department approaches the work single-handedly which makes it very difficult to take care of the  project management and make sure everything is done in time and tested properly before going live.  Furthermore, for those types of projects there is no official kick-off meeting.

To help get an understanding of what IT is working on I would like to introduce project kick-off  meetings that will include a visualization of the planned solution. This – in my eyes – will help to get a  shared understanding of the work being done, support to document our IT infrastructure and help  knowledge sharing between IT and IT project management co-workers. This will benefit the  implementation process itself and also the overall understanding of our IT infrastructure which is  beneficial knowledge when it comes to further IT development.

-  All relevant IT staff that will work on this solution or is directly/ or indirectly affected by  potential changes

-  All IT staff that should learn about what we are doing

-  At least one IT project manager

-  At least one Quality assurance manager

Example Reflection- Visualization and story telling

Challenges

I don’t work in a professional jobs nor do I have a business firm to handle. Right now I am

pursuing my degree at Qatar University in GD Goenka. Forest and we had entrepreneurship

course during our 6th semester. I have always been interested in Business including some of my

fellow mates and there has been an interesting activities during this course were we have to come

up with an innovative idea to open up a relevant business suitable of our environment and pitch it

in the class. We were divided into groups and each groups have to come up with a different

ideas. I had interesting ideas jumbling in my head and out of all these astonishing ideas, our

group decided to pitch our business idea on Food Hub. The idea was in fact new and innovative

but we lacked the way to present it and we had a tough time agreeing upon a common decisions.

Selection and Application

We knew the idea were superb but we lacked the ability to present and convince our lecturer and

other mates about the framework and the potential opportunities it possesses. Then another idea

clicked our mind, we planned to present our idea through visual presentation. We started to draw

the basic ideas that we had on the chart paper. We drew a bus and designed it in such a way that

it looks perfectly attractive for delivery services in the central of the chart paper and then around

it we drew our target customers, to whom we want avail our services, the resources that we

would require such as machines, vegetables, pastry items and utensils. We also drew the

sponsorship firms which we would seek help from and the items that we will be serving to the

customer. Through visualization, the audience were able to capture the clear idea of what we

were trying to present to them and we were also able to show them the picture which were

difficult for us explain and elaborate.

Learning Launch

Challenge and selection

I am an administrative member in the retail team of a consumer goods sales company. One of my  superior’s and my own biggest and most constant challenge is to provide sales information and insights,  both to my fellow staff members and field supervisors.

Putting up information for staff members is reasonably simple because we ‘speak the same language’;  we all have fairly similar academic background and share common knowledge through daily interaction  in the office. On the other hand, supervisors come from different backgrounds -most of them started as  store sellers, some were sales representatives from whole different industries, etc.- so their computer  skills vary from one another, and so does their understanding of words and KPIs that might seem very  common for the staff, such as ‘growth’, ‘variation’, ‘profitability’, etc.

In this occasion, we had the challenge to provide daily sales information and insights to supervisors, in  order to help them focus on the stores and brands that had lower performance. This information had to  be useful, thus, it had to be understood by every supervisor regardless their skills.

We selected the Learning Launch tool to assess the understandability and usability of the information,  by testing the solution with 2 supervisors: “P” a fast learner with the highest computer skills, and “M”  who has a much more traditional workstyle.

Application

The information was sent as a simple Excel file because it’s the most common software used by the  company, and it could be browsed on the field with a cellphone. The file had 3 sheets:

- Daily sales by store, supervisor and brand, both from the current and past year  - Monthly sales target, current sales, and percentage of target fulfillment by store, supervisor and brand  - Sales year over year growth by store, supervisor and brand

We sent the initial file to both P and M, asked them to check the information and share their feedback.  The

Hypothesis

Our company was in a plan to create new packaging material that would act as an alternative to

the normal polythene paper packaging bags. Studies show that large populaces of Kenyans are shoppers,  and therefore, need cheap and an alternatively effective solution for their goods and services. In this case,  our company targets mostly small scale shoppers who buy goods for domestic purposes

Our assumption was that biodegradable bags are cheap and durable when compared to polythene

text: Visualization:    Employee appraisal is an integral part of all the companies. It is often done Half-yearly or  Annually. Managers usually do this appraisal and evaluation process for all his direct reports.  This is an extra job responsibility for the managers besides their tons of business-related  responsibilities. Not only that, collecting performance feedback, but target achievement  details, Org. contributions for all his direct reports is also a time-consuming task and keeping  that information available at one place during the appraisal process is another big challenge.    This Fiori Appraisal app will enable the managers to complete the appraisal process easier on  the go and anytime from anywhere. The apps will show all his direct reports on a master list  and the details section will show the Performance feedback, Target achieved, Org. Contribution  and other relevant details for them. Managers can review all the feedback for all his direct  reports, can provide his feedback and an overall rating for his direct reports. Along with that  managers can recommend for promotion for his direct reports who had an outstanding  performance throughout the year.    Main Goals:    Manage the project effectively to deliver it on time within budget with minimum defects.  Find  out opportunities for the new business area and generate more revenue.  Better manage the  career and skill growth for his direct reports.  Should have all the updates, performance and  feedback for his direct reports readily available to him in a single click.   Needs:  Need to reduce the time and effort required to collect all the information and use them  when required.  To better utilize the travel time and doing something productive, it is needed to  have the business processes like timesheet approval, vendor invoice approval and  Performance assessment and rating for his direct reports to be mobile device enabled so that  can be accessed and completed anytime and anywhere.   Pain Points:  I

Launch of new education

Challenge. I am a professor of labor law at the Faculty of Law and Social Sciences. My  challenge is to improve the learning method of my students since my classes are in the first  year. Being a public university, I have students of all social levels and the truth is that not all  students are prepared to begin such deep studies. Their academic standards really need to  improve. My classes consist of a period of six months and it is the time I have to be able to  adapt them not only to the university but also to the introduction of law. I will focus on trying  to figure out what teaching and learning styles are effective for my students.

Selection. I am thinking of trying various design thinking challenges for my students and found  that the most suitable tool to apply is the learning launch tool. Since my goal is to discover  teaching and learning styles that are effective for my students, I can use the learning launch  tool to quickly experiment and test an idea.

Application. I focused on discovering what are the problems that lead my students to not  understand the lessons. Finally, I was able to determine that most concepts, require prior  mastery of civil law. For example, they cannot easily learn the rights of a worker if they do not  know that it is a right in itself. Because of this discovery, I made sure that before introducing  new concepts, I teach them the prior knowledge in that specific lesson. I stopped assuming  they already know it, because they should have learned it in their previous academic years.  Whether they can still remember it or not, the lesson always begins with the review of learning  the concepts needed for that specific lesson. I also established that all the students must go  together on class. Before moving on to the next concept, they must first master the current  lesson. I also be more opened up for them. After each session, I give them a free consultation  time where they can ask me whatever they want

text:
Challenge & Selection

I consider visualization to be one of the most important design thinking tools. I see the im- portance of this tool in its versatility. We can use the visualization at any stage of thinking. In  this essay, I want to look at how this tool helps to solve communication problems between the  designer and the client. In this case, we apply design thinking directly to the design problem,  however, these tools and skills can be useful in any other area.

Application

The problems that the visualization as a tool solves are directly related to the problems of  empathy. In a situation where the designer must show some empathy towards the client, vis- ualization becomes our best friend. You can try to explain an idea to another person for an  infinitely long time, but he generally imagines the final result in a completely different way.  Therefore, it is often necessary to visualize the idea that is being discussed in order for the  communication to take place. When we want to get a clear explanation from the client of  how he wants to see the final product, we do not have to immediately put a sheet of paper  and a pencil in front of him, it is the designer's task to correctly visualize the idea after all.  This is similar to drawing a portrait of a person according to his description. Even when the  person from whom we want to see the visualization of some idea does not have sufficient  skills or desire, we can sketch his concepts or the final result. This approach to the analysis  of the brief helps to shorten the subsequent edits and to immediately catch that elusive con- nection between the often abstract desires of the client and the way the end product might  actually look like.

REFLECTION ASSIGNMENT: Storytelling & Visualisation

Challenge

In the past, I did an NLP training course. To complete the training, all trainees were to do an exam  consisting of various tasks. One of these tasks was to interview a person and to analyse one of  her/his competences in depth by using the skills we learned in the course. The results were to be  presented to the trainer and the group of trainees. After I did the interview and the analysis as  requested, the presentation was still ahead of me. The competence I analysed was courage, involving  complex mental and emotional processes like overcoming fear. So, the results were difficult to  explain anyway, let alone pack into a short presentation. First, I was stuck and couldn’t think of any  solution to present the results in a concise way. The day of the audit was getting close and just one  day before the audit a sudden thought struck me: A comic would be the perfect solution! It would  simplify the content and the presentation format at the same time. A story is easier to follow then a  complex entanglement of psychological processes. And animating them with cartoony figures would  help even more to increase comprehensibility.

Selection & Application

As a first step, I had to prioritize the results as I knew I couldn’t incorporate all details in the story. I  had to ask myself, who is “your audience, where do they come from, and what do they need?” (as  Juan Lopez mentions in the video). This leading question brought me to the realization, that I had  to create the presentation assuming the audience has no previous knowledge, e.g. they haven’t  heard the whole interview as I did. Thus, I had to break the content down into most important facts  and to arrange them consecutively, so that everyone could easily follow.

Challenge

As a 5th year Electronics Engineering student, we are working for our design project wherein we  need to proposed a certain topic that will help or solve a particular problem that we are facing  right now in our environment. This include paperwork, documents and a prototype. In proposing  my idea, I need to pitch it in front of the audience and some panels. So I practiced hard my  communication skills and be confident for who I am. As an engineering student, we should also  be good in communicating others. Using this storytelling tool, it helps me to boost my self-esteem  and act as a professional speaker. Learning this tool helps me to express more my idea to others  and be an effective speaker so they will not get bored when I am talking.

Selection

The tool that I selected is the storytelling tool. Through this tool, it helps me to increase my  confidence when I am interacting with other people. I can express more myself because it is just  like telling a story to them. This is an important tool because you need to get the attention of  your audience. You need to take the listener along on your journey. This tool really helps me in  presenting something like presentations or reports to my fellow students.

Application

I applied this tool when we are asked to pitch or present our proposed design project title  individually. I explain first the problems about the lack of electricity in the Philippines then  followed by my solution for designing a new portable water turbine. text:
Reflection-Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

I am a graphic and product designer. I work at a fintech startup. As a UX designer, I worked on a

sophisticated application in stock investing. At the first stage of the project, we spoke with

stakeholders, target users, developers and, we had a lot of meetings that had to explain our

project to them.  The explanation of a complicated application in verbal communication is not

easy. Almost every time that we represented our project, there was a lot of question from the

audience. So, I decided to create an overview of the application I am designing, showing how all

its parts work together. Because design is visualization of a solution, I decided to use mind

mapping for this challenge.

Application

First of all, I use a big board to apply all parts of the application. I put the application in the center

of the board and connect different parts of that with a line. For the primary stage of the project,

we focused on the most important parts of it, and after we got feedback from the target users,

we decided to add new features to our mind map. After I finished the poster, I took a picture of

that, and I put it on our pitch-deck.

Insight

After applying the mind mapping tool to our project, we got great feedback. We could very

easily communicate with our team, developers, key stakeholders, and especially the investors.

This caused me to use it in the next stage of the project, and I added new features to the mind

map. This result made me use other techniques of design thinking on my projects.

I learned that I should give it a try the next time in one of these situations:

1-Discover new features of the application I am working on. In this case, I can just try drawing

new connections between entities or adding more entities to the equation.

Storytelling - Sales Asset

Challenge: So, the place where I work is called Tata  Group’s, where I work as an Admissions Counselor helping  people in enrolling into our education programs. Now, as a counselor, my job is to make sure that the  learners are really able to understand the USP of the program, where they can connect it to their career  and can really see its value. But apparently, I used to be like a chatbot(website), just telling the data  which was already present on the website. Thus, my conversion ratio (lead to sales) was less since not  many learners could identify the benefits of enrolling into the program.

Selection: I understood that I will have to change the way I counsel and add more meaning and value to  it. The tool which I used was story-telling. I could understand that for a learner to completely relate to  our program(product), it is important that I share relevant examples which he could easily relate to. And  thus, he would get the underlying value addition of the program.

Application: So, moving forward, in all my counselling, I used to tell two stories where in the first  case(let’s say X), the learner who took the program and then, explained her career growth after few  years, how she could moved up the corporate ladder, how she managed to apply her learnings into  various work activities, how she used to networking for better opportunities etc. In the second  case(consider Y), the learner did not enroll into the program and thereby lead to a flat trajectory of  career growth and where she missed on various opportunities to scale up.

Insight: By doing this, there were three clear insights viz. 1) There is more engagement with the learner  during the counselling. 2) I am able to build more trust with the learner. 3) The conversion of lead to  sales has increased phenomenally.

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge:

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding  of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define  possible solutions to the problem. I used this approach often with my colleagues who are working to  apply technology innovations to modernize their tasks and the delivery of their services to their various  customers both internal and external.

Selection:

I have used the technique of using a rectangular box visualization of a problem domain with a set of  questions or prompts for discussion to allow everyone to learn from each other in the process of  defining the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when  identifying pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.

Application:

I start the process by creating a rectangular graphics of the problem domain. To develop the rectangular  graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing  material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, and  other auditing reports.

Where materials were not available, then I conducted an informal interview with some of the  stakeholders who serve as the main points of contact on the initiative.

The frontstage/back-stage approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service – even an internal  service – has customers with whom the service provider interacts and internal processes that enable the  organization to provide the service. The template I often start with also has a column on the left to  identify vendors and Value Chain Providers and a column on the right to identify downtime that may  add constraints to how the organization operates.

The rectangular graphic is simple, using simple shapes and icons available in Microsoft word/  PowerPoint or on the Internet.

text:
Challenge:

Educating the new comers to server lab is one part of my job to reduce the mishaps.

Even after detailed explanations of the do and don’ts mishaps were happening regularly and  considerable damage were happening in material and man hours to fix the damage during the induction  of the new comer.

Selection:

After going through this design thinking course, it occurred to me that instead of just explaining

the lab manual and the routine dos and don’ts, storytelling would help to drive the point of what is  expected out of them while they work with the lab infrastructure. I went for storytelling since I need to  educate a group of people who are having diverse technical background.

Application:

I picked up specific incidents from the lab log about the accidents created by the previous

people and created a nice story linking all the important incidents.

Insight:

After the narration of the story to the first group I came across, I was able to see people

listening with interest in contrary to sleepy faces during my earlier sessions. The change in attitude of  trainees are more heartwarming for me.

Approach:

I’m going to make this integral part of the training. There were fewer accidents from the new

group and they seems like well understood what is expected out of them in lab and what they should  avoid very clearly with the story telling approach.

Challenge & Selection

The challenge I did is to apply Visualization to teach a group of Grade 7 students about Algebra which  causes failed grades and wasted lessons. For a 5th year college student like me I think this will be a great  opportunity to make younger students who find themselves incapable of doing higher level  mathematics. When I was their age (11-12 years old), I really found algebra hard and uninteresting since  I am not fond of analyzing complex equations in terms of variables that causes my algebra roots to be  weak. I haven’t felt the effect of not fully understanding of algebra since I came to my first year of  college where I am ashamed that I cannot do simple algebra computations when I am asked to. I  struggled to pass the course at that year where I found myself trying hard to study in rush to cope up  with the lessons. Learning in rush is not that efficient and reflected obviously at my grade where almost  all my classmates end up having an average of 1.5-1 while me barely making it to 2.5 after the end of the  semester. Realizing that this is an issue that I can do something for others, I used Storytelling to let them  learn Algebra in a fun and effective way.

text:
Tool Selected: Learning Launch

Challenge:

The question to resolve was “how to get fast the right information needed to conduct a task in the frame  our working space”.  This was the initial questions that my team in Training and Knowledge Management  collected from the different users in recent surveys. Since many years, this question has been addressed  from different perspectives and applied different solutions that, in the end, they failed to fully satisfy our  users. There is too much information that in the end, is not productive as they spend too much time to  select the right information source.

Selection:

We apply in an intuitive way, the four steps of the design thinking process “what is, what if, what wows,  what works”. We collected all the existing ways that we had to provide training/ information to users and  we analyze them in terms of the following criteria: 1) accessibility 2) speed to get the right information 3)  accuracy and updated information. When collecting feedback from users, they confirmed that they would  like a centralized system, with visual, voice and preferable examples given and that they can share and  re-use if necessary.

As mentioned in the Training video “Learning Launch Tool” by Angel Glenn, we decided to experiment rather  than building “theoretical Business Cases or ROI”. We decided to apply an Intelligent Fast Failure  approach where we were going to test/ fail/ succeed (Learning Launch). So we defined our hypothesis  and assumptions:

  in terms of value creation, we considered that users would need to reach the knowledge/  information to conduct their task correctly and fulfill most of their requirements

  in terms of execution, we wanted a quick and fast access to updated information and execution  (eg no need to login/ passwords, etc)

  in terms of dependability, we wanted to be able to manage by our team and no dependency of  other departments

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge    We are making major revisions to our top-selling professional education course, which  historically has involved textbooks, some video lectures, and an online or in-person exam to  complete. Studying takes 2 to 6 weeks to take an exam and the full course, for a professional  designation, is 8 exams on different topics. Feedback from students indicates we need to  change the format to adapt to new learning needs.     Selection    A lot of work had been done prior to my joining the project.  Surveys, interviews with students  and with their employers, review of product feedback, competitive analysis, plus much more. In  addition, those involved in designing the new course and its content are very seasoned  professionals with a lot of experience in what works and what doesn't. In fact, most of them had  taken at least some of our courses as students, so were very familiar with the student  experience.     For example, we think students want more online courses, fewer printed textbooks, shorter  course segments, recorded live instructor segments, audio books. We think they want more  real-life examples, but does that look like case studies, or like industry-specific topics?    The key was to specify all the assumptions, data points, and hypotheses that were driving  decisions and be sure we agreed on what was important and how to proceed. As a market  researcher, my goal was to collect all the hypotheses and outstanding questions in a systematic  way so I could validate and/or understand them better through additional research. I decided  mind mapping was the technique to use.    Application    I started with a small group of key leaders and invited them to two meetings. The first was to lay  out what we were going to do and ask them to help.
